Every once in a while, my heart yearns for a good vada pav. And so when I hear of one, I lose no time in seeking it out. And so it was in this context that I found myself at Puneri Vade, a tiny nook in the wall near HSR layout where I met a shy but friendly young couple, Akshay and Ruchika Shinde, who moved from Pune to Bengaluru a couple of years ago to introduce the vada pav, bhajjis, poha and misal of their city to Bengaluru. I tasted some of their fare, and suffice to say, if like me, you love your vada pav, Puneri Vade is certainly a place to make note of.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/5bcyGF2Xys5U8cJH.summary: This video is a food review of Namma Hallimane, a popular village eatery on the Bangalore-Mangalore Highway in Byrapura, Hassan district, Karnataka. The restaurant is known for its wood-fired biryani and rustic setting. The reviewer highly recommends the mutton biryani, boti gojju & idli, khaima unde, and mutton curry. He mentions that the mutton biryani is the most popular dish, with the rice being particularly flavourful. The reviewer also notes that the restaurant is quite popular and recommends arriving early to avoid the crowd. The unique highlight of the restaurant is its use of traditional cooking methods and local spices, which gives the food a distinct and authentic flavour.

best_dishes.summary: A traditional wedding biryani cooked over a wood fire, known for its simple yet luxurious flavors, tender meat, and aromatic spices.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/aH7rvnS5itWGF2dy.summary: This video features a visit to Taj Hotel in Bengaluru to taste their famous Shaadi Ki Biryani. The host highlights the history of the dish, its connection to wedding feasts, and the traditional wood-fire cooking method. The unique aspect is the use of specific wood types like Casuarina and Tamarind for their slow burn and high heat, impacting the biryani's flavor. The host and guest delve into the meticulous cooking process, the specific blend of spices, and the importance of the 'dum' technique, where the biryani is sealed and steamed to perfection. The visual appeal of the biryani, with its fluffy rice, tender meat, and generous ghee topping, is emphasized, along with the accompanying dishes like brinjal curry, raita, and dalcha that complement the biryani's richness. Overall, the video portrays the Shaadi Ki Biryani as an experience that embodies tradition, flavor, and cultural significance.

In this episode, I taste a biryani tradition that goes back a century at Taj Hotel in Shivaji Nagar, Bengaluru. One of the earliest eateries in the city, it has perhaps also kindled Bengaluru’s love affair with the biryani. Alongside a wholesome chicken and a nuanced mutton biryani, I also taste some of the other popular dishes here - an aromatic ghee rice, spicy kheema masala, robustly flavoured lamb chops, and an akhni that made its way from the owner’s home to my table.

Mutton Seekh Kabab.name: Mutton Seekh Kabab
Mutton Seekh Kabab.summary: Smokey and flavorful, with a slightly granular texture, this kebab is a popular choice among patrons. The red color suggests the use of food coloring for a vibrant appearance.

Sallu Butter Chicken.name: Sallu Butter Chicken
Sallu Butter Chicken.summary: Indulge in this creamy and buttery delight! This tandoori chicken is generously coated in a rich sauce, perfect for sharing with a group. Hints of sweetness and traditional spices complement the moist chicken, best enjoyed with the accompanying kulcha.

Mutton Akhni.name: Mutton Akhni
Mutton Akhni.summary: A hidden gem not featured on the menu! This home-style dish features tender mutton in a flavorful gravy, bursting with the tanginess of tomatoes, the freshness of coriander and mint, and the savory depth of caramelized onions. It pairs perfectly with both kulcha and ghee rice.

Kheema Hyderabadi.name: Kheema Hyderabadi
Kheema Hyderabadi.summary: This flavorful Kheema is packed with aromatic coriander and mint, offering a delightful burst of freshness. The minced meat boasts a satisfying coarse texture, further enhanced by the green chilies. The accompanying flaky paratha serves as an excellent complement, making each bite a true delight.

Mutton Biryani.name: Mutton Biryani
Mutton Biryani.summary: A true testament to the restaurant's legacy, this biryani is a must-try for mutton lovers. The rice is infused with the rich flavors of the meat, creating a harmonious blend that is both mellow and warming. The generous chunks of tender mutton, cooked to perfection, are the highlight of this dish. Each bite offers a delightful interplay of textures and tastes, thanks to the coarsely chopped tomatoes and onions.

Ande Ki Mithai.name: Ande Ki Mithai
Ande Ki Mithai.summary: A unique and unexpected dessert that's a must-try! Despite its name, this sweet treat doesn't have any noticeable egg flavor. Instead, it delights with the rich flavors of khoya and the delicate crunch of caramelized almonds, offering a delightful play of textures and sweetness.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/aH7rvnS5itWGF2dy.summary: This video takes viewers on a culinary journey to the iconic Taj Hotel in Shivaji Nagar, Bengaluru, renowned for its century-old biryani tradition. The host, Kripal Amanna, provides a behind-the-scenes look at the making of their signature biryani, showcasing the meticulous process and simple yet flavorful ingredients.  He savors a range of dishes, from the smoky seekh kebabs to the indulgent butter chicken, each offering a unique explosion of flavors. The star of the show, the mutton biryani, lives up to its legendary reputation with tender, flavorful meat and perfectly cooked rice. A delightful surprise awaits in the form of the Ande Ki Mithai, a unique dessert that challenges expectations. This episode is a must-watch for food enthusiasts seeking an authentic taste of Bangalore's culinary heritage. The unique highlight of this video is the access to the family recipe of Mutton Akhni, a dish not available on the restaurant's menu.

It had been a while since I had filmed a biryani making episode. And so when the opportunity arose to film the complete process of a biryani whose recipe has remained constant for over a century, I lost no time to head to Taj Hotel Shivaji Nagar, an eatery that  dates back to the early 20th century, and today churns out over 500 kilos of biryani each day. I met with the third and fourth generation of the family of the late Janab Abdur Rahman, who are committed to preserving the ancient traditions that go into the making of their biryani, including cooking it over a wood fire only.

Hope you enjoy this very special biryani making episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

The host explains that this biryani is special because it's cooked over a wood fire using traditional methods, giving it a unique and authentic flavor. The biryani is made with lamb that's first seared in a masala and then boiled until tender. The rice is cooked separately and then layered with the meat, saffron milk, and ghee before being sealed and cooked on a low heat. The host describes the biryani as having a luxurious feel, with the meat being incredibly tender and flavorful. He also mentions the accompanying dishes, such as the brinjal curry and dalcha, which complement the biryani perfectly. Overall, the video highlights the cultural significance of biryani in India and the unique experience of dining at Taj Hotel.

popular biryani restaurant, donne biryani, shivaji military hotel, popular biryani, mutton biryani, chicken biryani, mutton dry, chilli chicken, kaal soup, mutton liver, jayanagar, banashankari, bangalore, bengaluru

When Bengaluru emerged from lockdown months ago, Lokesh and Rajiv, the brothers behind Shivaji Military Hotel took a conscious decision to not reopen dine-in until the situation got better. This meant foregoing a substantial chunk of revenues and relying on takeaway business only, but this was something they were prepared to live with, for the safety of their customers and staff. So when they reopened the eatery to customers a couple of weeks ago, we lost no time in getting there to savour their hugely popular donne biryani and also report on the current experience at this 90-year old culinary institution that has a reputation for being jam packed with customers. We arrived to find certain measures in place, even though in precarious danger of being overrun by its patrons. Thankfully though, the taste of the donne biryani hasn't wavered a bit from the time we tasted it last nearly a year ago. Hope you enjoy this episode, stay safe and happy eating!

Kaal Soup
A warming, gently-spiced mutton bone broth, the trotters are cleaned well and cooked to melt-in-the-mouth texture.
Rs. 180 (usd 2.4)
8.5/10

Chicken Donne Biryani
The biryani is served steaming hot and is impressionable in its persistent aroma and spicy, flavourful fervour laced with green chilli heat. We tasted the donne biryani in takeaway mode where it is packed in foil, but it's not quite the same as when it is ladled onto a donne, a container fashioned of leaves. 
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
9/10

Mutton Donne Biryani
The biryani has a slightly smokey tone, and the spices imbued with the weight of the fat and the character of the meat, is rounded in its flavour as opposed to the chicken biryani. The meat is juicy and has absorbed the flavour of the masala rather well. This is the textbook donne biryani, served by this revered culinary institution for the last nine decades. 
Rs. 260 (usd 3.5)
10/10

Chilli Chicken
The chicken is moist, bathed in a green chilli gravy, this is certainly not a dish for the faint-hearted. 
Rs. 180 (2.4)
8.5/10

Mutton Pepper Dry
Tender meat braised in a deep roasted masala with plenty of pepper. 
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1)
9/10

Mutton Liver Fry
The liver has a bit of a bite, its deep flavours juxtapose delightfully against the contrasting freshness of coriander and mint in the green masala.
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2)
8.5/10

https://goo.gl/maps/mZqgz8ZNB4C8e5s38.description:
#ShivajiMilitaryHotel #DonneBiryani #GourmetOnTheRoad

Bengaluru's most popular Shivaji Military Hotel, Chicken Donne Biryani, Mutton Donne Biryani, Breakfast, Bengaluru's Top Restaurants, Biryani

What begins as a visit by Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna, to check out this iconic restaurant’s breakfast soon turns into a never-seen-before-on-video demonstration on the making of Bengaluru’s most famous chicken biryani, the Donne Biryani at Shivaji Military Hotel, a restaurant that has stood tall for over eight decades for its local-influenced Maratha fare.

Needless to say, he also catches a full military-style breakfast that includes a nourishing paaya soup, chicken leg masala, chops, mutton liver, khaali dose and steaming hot donne biryani. 

Lunch at Shivaji Military Hotel video - https://youtu.be/XxatALJz0Ro

Leg Soup
The gelatine has rendered well into the broth and glistens on the surface, you taste the flavour of the fat in the broth and the spicing too, especially the green chilli. The trotter is the sort that melts in your mouth. 
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2) for 2 legs.
8.5/10

Chicken Chops 
A rich, spicy green masala of coriander, mint and onions, studded with green peas. The juicy chicken pieces tame the salty savoury punch of the gravy. The khali dose makes for the perfect companion to taste the chicken chops masala. 
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6)
9/10

Chicken Leg Piece
Plump chicken legs cooked nice and juicy down to the bone. Definitely not a dish for the faint-hearted, you can taste the searing heat of the red chilli powder in this gravy. The onions,  tomatoes and lime provide a mildly sweet-tart counterpoint to the chilli heat though. 
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2) for 2 pieces.
8.5/10

Mutton Liver 
The mutton liver is cooked to perfection in a green masala, has a springy bite and is soft and creamy inside. Absolutely delicious, the intense earthiness of the liver goes well with the salty savouriness of the gravy.
Rs. 150 (usd 2.1)
10/10

Mutton Dry
The fat bits in the meat pieces add flavour. I tasted this piping hot off the stove, but I wish the meat had rested in the masala for a bit post cooking for me to better savour this peppery preparation. 
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6)
8/10

Chicken Donne Biryani 
You can taste the ingredients that have gone into Shivaji Military Hotel’s iconic donne biryani the moment you place the intensely flavourful rice in your mouth. The sweetness of the spices, the star anise, the mild astringency of the cloves, the fresh bite of the herbs, the pointed pungency from the green chillies, the tartness of tomato and the lime. The ghee coats the rice with a film of lushness, you can smell the smokiness from the dum. The chicken is delicate in its flavour, and not as effusive. Savour it with the rice to enjoy the complete range of flavours in this dish. 
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6)
9/10

A few months ago, I featured an episode with a brave lady entrepreneur who despite facing physical hardships after a serious accident had given up an IT job to pursue her passion in food. Your response to it was amazing, and soon Veena’s Kari Dosa street food stall was thriving. Until one day when she returned to her spot to find that the entire lot had been razed to the ground!  

Left with no recourse but to begin from scratch again, this time Veena opted for the safety of a shop. Pooling her savings and borrowing some more, she has set up a small Kari Dosa shop in BTM 2nd Stage, Bengaluru. However, the going has been anything but smooth with poor sales and not enough people knowing of her delicious fare. So, she reached out to us requesting support for her enterprise. I rarely ever do this, revisit a place for an episode in less than a span of six months, but I felt this delicious initiative had to be supported. I hope you enjoy the episode and will also be motivated to support Veena’s Kari Dosa stall.

A few weeks ago, I heard of a lady entrepreneur who despite facing physical hardships after a serious accident had given up an IT job to pursue her passion in food. Resources were limited, so she set up a small streetside stand. Extremely hardworking, Veena’s day begins at 4 in the morning when she wakes up to prepare the dosae batter, curries, thokku and kurmas that go into her delicious kari dosa. After sending her two young children to school, she arrives at her stand in JP Nagar, South Bengaluru, where customers queue up to savour her scrumptious fare that begins as low as Rs. 10 for a delightful plain dosae with spicy peanut chutney and aromatic vegetable gravy, and Rs. 30 for an egg topped version. What lends the stall its name though are the Tamil Nadu style kari dosai, chicken and my favourite, a prawn thokku topped dosae. If you love dosae, especially the non vegetarian kind, head here. And in doing so, you will also be supporting a deserving small enterprise.

Hope you enjoy this find; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

45 years ago, a young lad found himself at a difficult crossroad.He was interested in photography and cinema, but the financial situation at home compelled him to give up his education and take up a job in a restaurant. Working 18 hours a day, life was tough, he spent many nights with no roof over his head. Things got better, when he and his family set up two restaurants in Chennai. Unfortunately, the restaurants failed and they had to begin all over again. This is hardly the kind of backstory one would expect to hear of Chennai’s iconic Sangeetha vegetarian chain of restaurants. But these are exactly the kind of challenges Mr. Suresh and his family endured to build 50 restaurants over the years. I caught up with him at their flagship Adyar restaurant, where I relished a delightful Tamil Nadu meal which in addition to highlighting the cuisine of the land is also accommodative enough to encompass flavours beyond the borders of the state. 

I hope you enjoy my last saapad from this Gourmet On The Road, Chennai tour. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

https://goo.gl/maps/kqUtDU14PkpJV4gT6.title: ANAND Dum Biryani Vs. MANI Dum Biryani! Which Famous HOSKOTE Early Morning BIRYANI Should You Try?
https://goo.gl/maps/kqUtDU14PkpJV4gT6.description:
#hoskote #biryani #bangalore

mani dum biryani, anand dum biryani, popular hoskote biryani shop, early morning biryani, popular biryani shop,, hosakote, hoskote, bangalore, bengaluru, mutton biryani, biryani trail, inspiring stories, karnataka

The Hoskote early morning biryani draws hundreds of faithful fans who wake up at an unearthly hour every Tuesday, Friday and Sunday to make the 40-km trek to queue up at biryani shops in this town just outside Bengaluru. 

However, for those not completely in the know, some of the most commonly asked questions with respect to this long-standing biryani tradition are: What’s the fuss about the Hoskote biryani? Which biryani should one try, should one try the Mani Biryani or the Anand Biryani? How different are these biryanis? Or are they similar? Which one is spicy, which one is not? What goes into the making of these hugely popular biryanis? Which one came first? And more… 

In this special Gourmet On The Road episode, we revisit these biryanis and compare side by side Hoskote’s most popular early morning biryanis, undoubtedly, in an attempt to answer many of the questions posed. Hope you enjoy this one; take care, stay safe and happy eating! 

Anand Mutton Biryani 
The dominant flavours in this biryani are that of the fresh ingredients, the naati ginger, garlic, coriander,mint etc., followed by a veil of the aromatic spices. Every grain of rice is imbued with its flavours, and the meat is a combination of some soft, juicy pieces and some on the bone, that calls for a bit of effort to get to every bit of it, some fat included. The spicing is gentle and warm. 
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1) 
9/10

Mutton Biryani
The only dish made at Mani Dum Biryani, is unique in its aroma that is redolent of an amalgam of spices combined with meat. Each grain of the rice has absorbed the procession of spices that go into the pot and the fat that is rendered from the meat, this is the sort of biryani that leaves behind a spicy impression on the palate. You can taste the heat of green chillies, and the flavour of the secret spice mix that’s made in Mani’s home. Some of the meat is laced with fat that melts in the warmth of one’s mouth, some pieces though can have a bit of a bite. This is a spicy biryani, and the mosaru bhajji, onion and cucumber raitha helps cool things down.
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1)
9/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

Note: It can get crowded, especially on Sundays. Get early to beat a long queue.

After trying his hand at a number of professions, Mani decided to pay heed to his parent’s advice and set up a tiny vegetarian eatery in a hut in his hometown on the outskirts of Bengaluru. The year was 1992 and his hometown was Hoskote, then a mere highway halt enroute to Madras. Soon Mani began preparing and serving a rustic-style mutton ‘biryani’ inspired by his amma’s recipe. His early patrons, workers from nearby factories, truckers and drivers, for whom the biryani was a satisfying early morning meal to help sustain them through the day, having relished Mani’s biryani not only carried its taste but also news on this biryani shop. Year after year, the throng of customers to Mani’s eatery grew, and this also spawned the tradition of the early morning Hoskote biryani ritual with other biryani shops opening in its wake. Today Mani Dum Biryani Hoskote caters to hundreds of customers every Tuesday, Friday, and a few thousand on Sundays, but the rustic soul of the biryani remains, be it in the setting or the flavour of the dish, prepared only by Mani’s sons with a secret spice blend made by his wife. I drove out at dawn one Tuesday to watch the sons, Manjunath, Kiran Kumar and Chandrashekar prepare the biryani that first put Hoskote on the food lovers’ map. 

Mutton Biryani
The only dish made at Mani Dum Biryani, is unique in its aroma that is redolent of an amalgam of spices combined with meat. Each grain of the rice has absorbed the procession of spices that go into the pot and the fat that is rendered from the meat, this is the sort of biryani that leaves behind a spicy impression on the palate. You can taste the heat of green chillies, and the flavour of the secret spice mix that’s made in Mani’s home. Some of the meat is laced with fat that melts in the warmth of one’s mouth, some pieces though can have a bit of a bite. This is a spicy biryani, and the mosaru bhajji, onion and cucumber raitha helps cool things down.
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1)
9/10

Gourmet On The Road,

Coconut Shell Idli.summary: A unique and flavorful idli steamed in a coconut shell, infused with herbs and spices, and topped with coconut oil. The idli has a soft and pasty texture, and a distinct aroma of fermentation.

Kotte Kadubu.summary: A traditional South Canara classic, Kotte Kadubu is a steamed rice dumpling that is served with a spicy chutney and a light and flavorful sambar.

Khara Mangalore Buns.summary: A spicy twist on the classic Mangalore buns, these buns are speckled with green chilies and have a crispy exterior and a slightly doughy interior.

Ghee Ragi Halbai.summary: A seductive and wobbly dessert, the Ragi Halbai is made with finger millet, jaggery, and ghee. The Halbai is sweet, nutty, and has a melt-in-your-mouth texture.

Coffee.summary: A robust and flavorful coffee with a dark roast and a 80:20 blend of Arabica coffee and chicory.

The reviewer tries a variety of dishes, including the coconut shell idli, kotte kadubu, khara Mangalore buns, ghee ragi halbai, and coffee. He highly recommends the coconut shell idli, describing it as soft, pasty, and flavorful, and the ghee ragi halbai, which he calls "seductive" and "melt-in-your-mouth." Overall, he seems to have enjoyed his meal at Jagli Tindi.  The unique highlight of the restaurant is the use of traditional South Canara cuisine and ingredients to prepare their dishes

Masala Coconut Idli.name: Masala Coconut Idli
Masala Coconut Idli.summary: Steamed in a coconut shell with curry leaves, coriander, cumin and a drizzle of coconut oil, this idli is a burst of flavors and aromas. The grated coconut pieces add a delightful crunch, while the fermentation brings out a pleasant sourness. Enjoy it on its own or savor it with sambar and chutney.

Kotte Kadubu.name: Kotte Kadubu
Kotte Kadubu.summary: Similar to idli but steamed in a cup made of jackfruit leaves, this dish offers a unique flavor experience. The batter is fluffier and drier, resembling a cake-like texture. The jackfruit leaves impart a subtle greenness and a distinct aroma, making it a must-try.

https://goo.gl/maps/wyn3Eai5PAu5f5wc8.summary: Mark embarks on a culinary adventure at Jagli Tindi in JP Nagar, Bengaluru, guided by the enthusiastic Kripal Amanna. They explore unique idli variations, including the Masala Coconut Idli steamed in a coconut shell and the Kotte Kadubu cooked in a jackfruit leaf cup. The Masala Coconut Idli, infused with coconut oil, curry leaves, and spices, offers a burst of flavors and aromas, while the Kotte Kadubu surprises with its fluffy texture and subtle greenness from the jackfruit leaves.  The highlight of Jagli Tindi lies in its dedication to traditional South Indian flavors and the innovative use of ingredients like coconut shells and jackfruit leaves for steaming.

It is no secret that out here in Bengaluru, we love our coffee, especially the traditional South Indian filter coffee kind. However, what is not much known is the fact that there are a variety of distinct coffee traditions in the South, based on geography, brewing and serving customs. But that’s about to change, as a mother and son duo, Anusuya and Ranjit Prakasam, have just opened a cosy filter coffee café in Jayanagar, South Bengaluru, where they brew and serve a range of 10 filter coffees that incorporate unique blends, paired even to the milk that goes in - from hand churned to A2 milk of desi cows. I pay them a visit to taste five coffees and also some of the local bakery snacks that are served alongside. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

yercaud, sri venkateshwara veg restaurant, yercaud street food, where to eat in yercaud, tamil nadu, yercaud famous street food, yercaud food tour, idli vadai, onion dosai, ghee dosa, podi dosa, yercaud food walk, yercaud food trail, tamil nadu food tour, yercaud food series, support local, support small business, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food 

It is rare these days to find old world eateries that haven’t succumbed to the compromises of time, in their approach, way of life, and most importantly the flavours they present. 62-year-old Sri Venkateshwara is one such place where time seems to have stood still. Yercaud’s first restaurant has seen many dignitaries pass through its doors in its early existence, since then much has changed, but the second generation family holds on to its good old fashioned approach to serving tasty, honestly priced vegetarian fare. I stopped here on my last evening in Yercaud to relish a tasty tiffin that also included three of their must-try dosae.

The video concludes with a unique dessert combination of rice, curd, and gulkan, a testament to the restaurant's commitment to preserving culinary traditions.

If you have a sweet tooth and find yourself in Chennai, this 108-year-old sweet shop in Zam Bazaar, Triplicane is a must visit. Especially for its dum ka roat, a delicious baked dessert of semolina, khoa and ghee that has all of Chennai flocking here. My other favourite from a quick tasting here was their ande ki mithai, a rich cake-like-texture creation that belies its core ingredient in its subtle flavour and aroma. The popularity of this Chennai institution has spawned imitators, so make sure you head to the original store in Zam Bazar, Triplicane to get your share of their iconic sweet treats.

I’ve eaten in Kappa Chakka Kandhari, Bengaluru, and it was a great meal all right, but when I found myself in Chennai recently, I had to visit its first restaurant, which also gave me an opportunity to share a table with my dear friend, Chef Regi Mathew after 25 years. For those who don’t know him yet, this culinary doyen, a master in many cuisines, has made it his life’s work to promote regional cuisine, especially that from his homeland Kerala. The dishes that I tasted at this lunch were the sort that left an indelible impression on my palate. Made to age old home recipes, sourcing the best ingredients from God’s own country - tender jackfruit, breadfruit, chinese potatoes, pearl spot fish, mussels and more -  Chef Regi’s menu is a triumph in showcasing regional Malayalee cuisine. And has also, deservedly, earned him a recent accolade as India’s top chef.

The next time you find yourself in Chennai or Bengaluru, definitely book a table at his restaurant. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay tuned for more from Gourmet On The Road, Chennai. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

https://maps.app.goo.gl/uKGRoe6u3h8SNZ1J.summary: Kappa Chakka Kandhari in Chennai is a culinary tribute to Kerala's diverse cuisine, spearheaded by Chef Regi Mathew. The restaurant prides itself on using fresh, local ingredients and traditional cooking methods, particularly slow cooking in clay pots to enhance flavors.  Chef Regi's dedication to preserving authentic Kerala flavors is evident in the dishes, each bursting with unique aromas and tastes. The menu boasts a wide variety of seafood, meat, and vegetarian options, all prepared with minimal spices to let the ingredients shine. A must-try is the Chatti Meen Curry, a pearl spot fish curry cooked in coconut milk and buttermilk, offering a harmonious blend of creamy, sour, and sweet notes. Another highlight is the use of Nenthra Pazham, a sweet dish made from pineapple and Nenthra banana, showcasing the diversity of Kerala's culinary heritage.

yercaud, yercaud tribal cuisine, tribal food, food cooked in claypots, coconut shells, bamboo and banana leaves, where to eat in yercaud, tamil nadu, yercaud food tour, claypot chicken, banana leaf fish fry, bamboo biryani, coconut shell prawns, mudavattukal kilangu soup, yercaud food trail, tamil nadu food tour, yercaud food series, support local, support small business, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food 

A few months ago, I heard of this culinarian in Yercaud, Kathiravan Karthikeyan, who had spent considerable time researching the lost tribal cuisine of Yercaud, and had made an attempt to revive age-old food traditions. Cooked only in natural mediums - clay pots, coconut shells, bamboo and banana leaves, the dishes presented to me were rustic and flavourful, a delicious ode to the tribal cuisine of the land. If you find yourself in Yercaud, this is certainly a cuisine to take in.

Mudavattu Kilangu Soup.summary: A traditional soup made with mudavattu kilangu, a special tuber known for its medicinal properties, particularly for joint pains. It boasts a unique flavor profile that resembles mutton soup.

Kattu Kozhi Soup.summary: A rustic and restorative soup crafted by pounding a whole country chicken, including bones, and simmering it to extract maximum flavor and nutrition. This soup is believed to have healing properties.

Parai Fish Fry.summary: Fresh Parai fish from the Yercaud Lake, marinated with simple spices like ginger, garlic, lime, salt, and pepper, and cooked to perfection on a hot stone. It offers a crispy exterior and a juicy interior, highlighting the natural flavors of the fish.

Kaliman Chicken Varuval.summary: Chicken cooked with a blend of spices in a clay pot. It has a thick, robust masala that coats the chicken pieces, giving it a unique and flavorful taste.

Coconut Shell Prawn Fry.summary: Succulent prawns cooked and served in a coconut shell. The coconut shell imparts a subtle sweetness and enhances the flavors of the prawns and the accompanying spices.

Bamboo Mutton.summary: Tender mutton pieces cooked inside a bamboo, infusing the meat with a smoky flavor. The bone-in mutton adds to the taste and authenticity of the dish.

Bamboo Chicken Biryani.summary: Aromatic and flavorful biryani where the chicken masala and rice are cooked separately and then layered together in a bamboo. It's cooked over charcoal, giving it a unique smoky aroma and taste.

Vanabanam.summary: A traditional digestive drink made from beet leaves, coconut milk, rose petals, honey, and other herbs and spices. The drink is served in a bamboo for a traditional touch.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/dcaGdjFmb2Apfnwz.summary: This video takes you on a culinary journey to La Four Seasons Resort in Yercaud, where the General Manager and culinarian, Kathiravan Karthikeyan, has revived the lost tribal cuisine of the region. Cooked using natural mediums like clay pots, coconut shells, bamboo, and banana leaves, the dishes are a testament to the ingenuity and resourcefulness of the Yercaud tribes. The highlight of the video is the emphasis on the unique cooking methods and the use of fresh, local ingredients. From the Mudavattu Kilangu Soup, known for its medicinal properties, to the flavorful Bamboo Chicken Biryani, each dish tells a story of tradition and culinary heritage.

https://maps.google.com/?q=11.785557,78..summary:
This shop has been serving its famous Sukku Coffee for over 30 years. The coffee, made with dry ginger, palm jaggery, coriander seeds, and garlic, is prepared without any sugar and is known for its warming properties, making it an ideal drink for the chilly Yercaud weather. 

Highlight: The shop uses a unique hand-pounding technique to crush the ingredients, giving the coffee a distinct texture and flavor.

https://goo.gl/maps/zrCuARY8qXzBJM4q6.summary: In this video, food critic Kripal Amanna takes renowned actor Ashish Vidyarthi on a culinary adventure to Gowdara Mudde Mane in Bengaluru, a restaurant specializing in rustic Gowda cuisine.  They savor a meat-centric feast featuring Gowda staples like Ragi Mudde, mutton dishes, and a unique mutton pulao made with coconut milk.  The highlight of the video is the palpable enthusiasm both Kripal and Ashish share for the food, making it a delightful watch for food enthusiasts.  Kripal eloquently describes the dishes, highlighting the use of fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods that bring out the authentic flavors of Gowda cuisine.  Ashish, in his characteristic jovial manner, expresses his delight at experiencing this unique cuisine for the first time.

https://goo.gl/maps/zrCuARY8qXzBJM4q6.title: Most Popular GOWDA Cuisine At GOWDARA MUDDE MANE | Non Veg Feast | Raagi Mudde, Mutton Korma, Palav
https://goo.gl/maps/zrCuARY8qXzBJM4q6.description:
#gowdafood #gowdaramuddemane #bangalore 

bengaluru’s most popular gowda cuisine non vegetarian restaurant, kanakapura road, bengaluru, non veg paradise, meat lovers, kaal soup, mutton korma, spare parts, offal, chakna, kheema gojju, chicken fry, mutton chops, karela, leg fry, mutton lollipop, mutton palav, pulao, veg meals

Having burnt his fingers in a string of failed ventures, Chandrashekar, a pharmacist by education, set up a small eatery 20 years ago as a last resort on some land gifted by his father and with the recipes of his late wife, Chandrakala. Little by little, the restaurant grew, not just in size, but also in its reputation for stellar Gowda food. Though located in a nook of South Bengaluru, loyal patrons flock to Gowdara Mudde Mane for the meaty fare that Chandrashekar and his family dish out. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay safe and happy eating!

Kaal Soup
A nourishing, spicy light broth deep in the intensity of the spices.
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5) without the trotter
8/10

Mutton Korma
The mutton pieces have a delicious bite and have stewed well in the flavours of the korma. There’s a bit of fat that sheaths the meat that heightens the meaty flavour.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
10/10

Kheema Gojju
The kheema is coarse ground, one can taste the freshness of coriander and curry leaves. There’s potato and green peas too, the green chilli in this preparation is quite assertive on the palate.
Rs. 190 (usd 2.5)
8.5/10

Chicken Kendasampige
Sliced breast of chicken marinated and grilled, tasty but does not make as much of an impression as the traditional fare here.
Rs. 190 (usd 2.5)
7/10

Mutton Chops
You can taste the flavour of the meat in the gravy, the meat is soft and juicy, the sort that requires minimal effort to chew. 
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1)
9/10

Chakna
Offal that’s cleaned well and cooked in a spicy coriander based masala, this is a must order if you’re a ‘spare parts’ lover.
Rs. 220 (usd 3)
8/10

Mutton Lollipop
Soft meat on the shin, that’s marinated simply in spices and then deep-fried to a meltingly-tender soft-as-butter texture.
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2)
9/10

Karela Fry
This deep-fried shin is generous in its meaty flavours enriched with fat and gelatin. Definitely, a must-order here.  
Rs. 180 (usd 2.4)
10/10

Mutton Pulav
Made only on Sundays here, this is a gentle pulav, the masala is laced with coconut milk. The rice, though a bit starchy, is redolent with the flavour of the hard spices like the clove, cassia, etc. The meat is soft and subtle in its flavours, the sort that combines well with the rice.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
8.5/10

Veg Meals
A simple yet sumptuous meal if you’re looking for something vegetarian at this otherwise hardcore ‘meaty’ destination.
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2)
8/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

From the refreshing Dahi Puri to the signature Bengaluru Masala Puri and the flavorful Pani Puri, each chaat offers a unique explosion of textures and tastes. https://goo.gl/maps/bZat92ZaSkeRCVyJA.summary: Mark Wiens and Kripal Amanna start their Bengaluru food tour at Brahmins’ Coffee Bar, a legendary establishment known for its South Indian breakfast. They relish the incredibly soft idlis served with a flavorful chutney. The vadas are equally impressive, crispy on the outside and incredibly airy on the inside.  The secret to their unique taste lies in the perfectly balanced flavors and double frying technique. When it comes to soft, melt-in-the mouth idlis, all roads lead to Brahmins’ Coffee Bar idlis, or at least it did until the current situation. I visit this modest South Bengaluru eatery that’s big on its reputation to see how they are coping with life post covid, and take back a parcel of their entire menu consisting of all of four items only! Are the idlis still as soft? Well, you’ll have to watch this one to find out. Stay safe and happy eating!

Note: This episode was first released in May 2020 and is being rerun to support Bengaluru eateries with takeaway orders in the current situation. Please support local eateries.

Takeaway Dish Review

Idli
A coarse-grained porous idli that allows for the chutney to seep in, you can taste a slight tartness from the fermentation. With the spicy ghatti chutney, that is made of hurukadale, roasted Bengal gram, coconut and  the idli takes on a bold, flavourful avatar. Pour the ‘telu’ or ‘flowy’ mint-coconut chutney over the idli to make for a bite that melts in the mouth.
Rs. 34 (usd 0.45) for 2 idlis 
 
Uddina Vade
It’s a tough act for the vade to follow the idli in takeaway mode, given that the vade is best savoured hot and crispy. However, a saving grace here is the vade is studded with curry leaves, green chillies, peppercorns, fresh coconut, thereby making for a flavourful bite. Soak up the past-warm vade with the chutney to relish the warming heat from the green chillies in the chutney. 
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) per vade

Khara Bath
BCB’s khara bath is a flavourful one, embellished with curry leaves, toasted lentils, mustard seeds, grated coconut, coriander, tasty enough to be savoured sans the chutney. But if you like it spicy, go ahead and introduce it to the zesty gatti chutney. 
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) 

Kesari Bath
End your takeaway tiffin with the kesari bath! There’s tonnes of ghee that goes into this sweet semolina and vermicelli concoction and you can taste it in its lush richness. The flavours draw from the tangy fruitiness of the pineapple and the warming cloves. The plum raisins add a sugary pop when you bite into one. 
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) 

Note: I haven’t rated these as I feel it would be unfair to rate South Indian breakfast items in a takeaway format. Since this is a rerun episode, prices of the dishes may have changed since.

Brahmins’ Coffee Bar is open only in the mornings from 6am to 1030am presently.

A couple of weeks ago, I watched a beautiful Kannada play that not only chronicled the iconic Vidyarthi Bhavan but also brought alive the emotional connect that patrons have with this institution over the decades. Amongst the brilliant characters portrayed, a pivotal performance was that of famed actor and food legend, Sihi Kahi Chandru, who gave voice to the Vidyarthi Bhavan masala dosae, the heart of a tiffin experience at the 77-year-old eatery. In the course of our conversation backstage, Chandru Sir and I quickly decided we should savour a full tiffin at Vidyarthi Bhavan soon. This isn’t your typical Gourmet On The Road episode, but it makes an attempt to capture our experience at the breakfast that followed. Hope you enjoy this one. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating.

Join Kripal Amanna on Food Lovers TV as he visits the iconic Vidyarthi Bhavan in Bangalore, accompanied by renowned actor and food personality Sihi Kahi Chandru. This episode offers a unique perspective, delving into the emotional connection patrons have with this 77-year-old eatery. Witness the bustling atmosphere, the aroma of crispy dosas, and the anticipation of eager diners. Discover the secrets behind their consistently delicious, traditional South Indian breakfast, from the perfectly crisp Masala Dosa to the comforting Uddina Vade and fluffy Poori Sagu. This isn't just a food review; it's an exploration of the legacy and culinary heritage that make Vidyarthi Bhavan a beloved Bangalore institution. 

Highlight: The episode beautifully captures the essence of Vidyarthi Bhavan, highlighting not just the food but the emotions and memories associated with it. The conversation between Kripal and Sihi Kahi Chandru provides a unique insight into the history and significance of this iconic eatery.

Rajamma and her husband, Basavaraj, set up a pushcart in a street corner of Jayanagar to fry and sell hot bajjis. Thirty years have passed since, the neighbourhood has evolved beyond recognition but Rajamma’s Madhavan Park Bajji Angadi, or shop, has stood constant at the same spot. Her husband has since retired, and today, she is helped by her sons, as they continue to serve delicious vegetable bajjis at honest prices to customers who visit not only for the scrumptious fare but also for the comforting nostalgia of yesteryear. Hope you enjoy this episode; take care, stay safe and happy eating! 


The bajjis here are served fresh and are rather enjoyable, my favourites were the capsicum, baby corn and also the masala vade. But it is the sort of place that you can't go wrong no matter what you order.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/3boRN1VsEHACUknz.summary: Mark Wiens and Kripal Amanna are on a street food tour in Bengaluru, India. They visit a stall called Uncle Egg Rice, which is known for its delicious egg rice and egg curry. The egg rice is cooked with egg masala, and every grain of rice is coated with it. It has the right amount of spices and soy sauce, making it very addictive. The egg curry is made with a thick sauce and the right blend of spices, giving it a creamy and rich texture. The yolk disintegrates into the gravy, making it extra rich and giving it a lot of body and texture.  They also have capsicum and onions to tame down the spice. Uncle Egg Rice is a must-try for anyone looking for a delicious and affordable meal in Bengaluru. The owner is friendly and passionate about his food, which shows in the taste.

When I polled viewers on restaurants to cover in Chennai, Mathsya in Egmore came much recommended. Not surprising though, with a culinary legacy that spans decades to when Mr. Shama Bhat, a native Udupi set up Udupi Shri Krishna Bhavan in 1947, which eventually morphed into this popular vegetarian eatery in 1980.

I caught up with the fourth-generation, present-day custodians of this iconic Chennai institution, and in the course of doing so, also relished many of their much-ordered tiffin treats, including the rasam vada, kotte kadubu with kootu, menaskai and ghee roast dosae.

This video takes us on a culinary journey to Buhari, a legendary restaurant in Chennai, India, famous for inventing the iconic Chicken 65 dish in 1965. The restaurant, established in 1951, boasts a rich history and numerous firsts, including the introduction of espresso machines and imported bone china to Chennai's dining scene. 

We explore the restaurant's signature dishes, starting with the simple yet delightful Bun Butter Jam, made with homemade bun, mixed fruit preserve, and a unique white butter. Unlike other versions, Buhari's Chicken 65 features tender chicken marinated in a yogurt-based marinade without curry leaves, resulting in a moist and flavorful experience.  

The Mutton Biryani, a classic dish, presents a medley of fragrant rice, tender mutton, and a subtle blend of spices that gently tantalize the taste buds. The Ceylon Parotta, another specialty, offers a delightful contrast of textures with its crispy top and soft bottom, perfectly complementing the flavorful mutton mince. 

Beyond the iconic dishes, Buhari's charm lies in its old-world ambiance and the simple yet flavorful approach to its cuisine, reflecting an era where quality ingredients and time-honored techniques took center stage. Buhari stands as a testament to culinary heritage, where classic dishes and a nostalgic atmosphere continue to captivate food enthusiasts even after 75 years.  

**Highlight:** The video highlights Buhari's claim to fame as the birthplace of the iconic Chicken 65 dish, invented in 1965. The dish's unique preparation, using a yogurt-based marinade without curry leaves, distinguishes it from other versions, adding to the restaurant's allure.

When I asked viewers for recommendations on my recent drive back from Mangalore, a few recommended that I visit Shenoy Restaurant in Guruvayanakere. Open since 1932, this modest eatery is run by the very hospitable Shenoy family who dish out a range of vegetarian delicacies breakfast through lunch and evening snacks. The food is the sort that’s homely, wholesome making use of produce in season. On this visit, I sampled a few of their snacks including the best biscoot rotti I have ever eaten. The flavours were the sort that hit home, also compelling me to make note to return here for a more substantial meal.

This is definitely one of those hidden spots that needs to be on every travellers list when driving towards Mangalore on the Charmady route. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

This video is a food review of Shenoy Restaurant, a 92-year-old family-run eatery located in Guruvayanakere, Karnataka. The restaurant is praised for its homely vegetarian delicacies and use of seasonal produce. 

The reviewer highly recommends the Biscoot Rotti, describing it as the best they've ever had. Other notable dishes include the Aloo Bonda and a unique version of Bajil, a Mangalorean breakfast dish. The reviewer also appreciates the light and mild flavors of the palya (vegetable side dishes) and the refreshing coconut chutney. 

What makes Shenoy Restaurant special is its history, familial atmosphere, and commitment to traditional recipes that have stood the test of time. The reviewer highlights the heartwarming sight of the family working together, with the lady preparing teas, the man serving customers, and the daughter managing the cashier. 

The video concludes with an invitation to viewers to visit Shenoy Restaurant and try their offerings, especially the Biscoot Rotti, Bajil, Bonda, and lunch. The reviewer expresses their intent to return for a full meal and encourages viewers to support Food Lovers TV through their membership community or Patreon.

New Shivabhag Café is not just another eatery but a way of life for the denizens of Manguluru. Founded over 80 years ago by Mr. Madhav Kamath, this bustling, culinary destination is now tended to by his grandsons. A stellar reputation built on the back of some solid culinary fare that’s light on the pocket and good old fashioned hospitality is what draws loyal customers here day after day. No matter which part of the world they may live in, logging a visit here is de rigueur for most Mangaloreans when they return home. I drop in impromptu for a chat with the amiable owners and also partake of some of the dishes that are a favourite with regulars at this iconic café.

On a recent visit to Mangalore, I came across this egg stall that though relatively unknown is quite the hit with regulars for its punchy egg wraps, chilli and stumbler, a quintessential egg dish from Kudla. Its owner, Devdas, is rather shy and prefers to let his food do the talking. However, I learnt from regulars that while making a living as a waiter during the day, he would tend to his egg stall at night, and it is by dint of his hard work over a decade and pleasing demeanour that Devdas’s motte angadi (egg shop) is fast emerging as the spot for a late evening ‘eggy’ snack. Hope you enjoy this street food episode from namma Kudla.

Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

I discovered Janatha Lunch Home quite by chance on this Mangalore visit, thanks to the buzz around its seafood thali that comes loaded with a smorgasbord of dishes for all of Rs. 350 only. Around 50 years ago, Mrs. Lucy D'Souza began a tiny mess to cater homestyle meaty meals to a handful of customers in the coffee town of Mudigere, Karnataka. The reputation of her homely fare comprising mutton, fish and pork delicacies prepared to an interesting confluence of Mangalorean, Kodava and Mudigere culinary influences, grew over the years making Eddies Mess a mandatory lunch stop for meat lovers in the know, locals and travellers alike, Today this mess is tended to by her son Eddie and his wife, Lavin D’Souza. If you love your non-vegetarian oota, this place is a definite must-visit when in the area.

Hope you enjoy this lunch stop. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Drive 30 kilometres outside Shimoga, past areca nut plantations, serene forest scapes, and the roar of the mighty Tunga river, to Mandagadde, a village known for its bird sanctuary and equally popular eateries that proffer a variety of freshwater fish delicacies. In this episode, I visit Bhavani Fish Hotel, a rustic dining spot set in a home that began the Mandagadde fish tradition 27 years ago. I met the owner, Ramesh Rao and his family to learn what makes the Mandagadde fish special, and also savour some of the delicacies on offer. When in Shimoga, definitely make the trek here; the fry and curries certainly are worth the effort.

Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

https://maps.app.goo.gl/xTuniMbPdWAP8Jxc.summary: This video is a food review of Hotel Bhavani, a rustic dining spot located in Mandagadde, Karnataka. The restaurant is known for its freshwater fish delicacies, especially its fish fry and fish curry.  The reviewer tries a variety of dishes, including the Gujole Fish Fry, Owlu Fish Fry, Katla Fish Fry, Gowri Fish Fry, Fish Curry, and Surgi Fish Curry.  He highly praises the masala used in the fish fry, describing it as supremely enduring and giving it a 10/10 rating. He also enjoys the akki roti and the coconut-based gravy of the fish curry. He notes that the service is functional and the atmosphere is rustic, but the food more than makes up for it. Overall, he highly recommends Hotel Bhavani for anyone looking for a delicious and authentic South Indian seafood meal. Highlight: The unique thing about Hotel Bhavani is that it was the first restaurant to start the Mandagadde fish tradition 27 years ago. The owner, Ramesh Rao, and his family have been serving up delicious freshwater fish delicacies ever since, and their recipes have been passed down through generations. The restaurant is also known for its rustic ambiance and its use of fresh, local ingredients.

What began 20 years ago as a highway stop to provide breakfast sustenance to truckers has now morphed into a must-visit on the informed traveller’s itinerary for its comforting, earthy kappa rotti, a fluffy rice flatbread cooked on a clay pan minus sans any oil. The thing to do is to taste it with the thick curries, chicken or vegetarian, that are dished out by Ashok Anna and his family at this eatery, Hotel Laxmi Janardhana, located in a town called Yermal, about 30 kilometres from Mangalore. The setting is quite rustic, and the crowd an eclectic mixed lot. But it is the food that rules here, as I discovered during a busy morning here. 
Hope you enjoy this one. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

What makes Grand Hotel in Kochi a bastion of traditional Kerala delicacies is its retinue of experienced cooks led by Chef Joseph who has helmed the kitchens here for the last 30 years. When it comes to authentic preparations like the karimeen pollichathu, koonju (tiger prawns) roast, Alleppey fish curry and suchlike, the dining room here has found much favour amongst the city’s denizens for 60 years now. On this short Kerala visit, I stopped by for a delicious lunch and also caught the making of its most famous dish, the karimeen (pearl spot fish) pollichathu. If you have time for only one traditional meal when in Kochi, this place is it!

When I walked in for breakfast and perused the menu at this 60-year-old eatery located right opposite Ernakulam’s historic Siva temple, I couldn't help but wonder if there was a connection to Udupi. A fact that was corroborated by the owner, Mrs. Meena Mohan, whose husband’s family migrated from South Canara nearly a century ago to perform religious duties in Kochi. And Gokul Ooottupra, too, seems to cater to its patrons in the same attitude of service and tradition, I discovered over my leisurely meal here. From staple classics like the vada, dosae, kadla puttu curry, yelle adda to a few inspired creations like the peri peri idli, the vegetarian fare here is the sort that draws in customers by the hundreds each day. If you find yourself in Kochi and are craving a vegetarian meal, look no further. Hope you enjoy this watch. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

https://maps.app.goo.gl/Xwoj4AHwzbtSVEDi.summary: This video features Gokul Oottupra, a renowned vegetarian restaurant in Kochi, Ernakulam, known for its Udupi roots and traditional Kerala cuisine. The restaurant, established in the 1960s, holds historical significance and boasts a loyal clientele. The video highlights the eatery's commitment to serving authentic South Indian breakfast staples like idli, dosa, puttu, and kadala curry. The owner, Mrs. Meena Mohan, shares insights into the restaurant's history, her family's migration from Udupi, and their dedication to providing quality food. The highlight of Gokul Oottupra lies in its unique approach to treating its staff, offering them the same food served to customers, a practice rarely found elsewhere. The video emphasizes the restaurant's welcoming atmosphere, its flavorful dishes, and its commitment to preserving culinary traditions, making it a must-visit for an authentic Kerala breakfast experience.

I thought I had tasted all possible dosae until I walked into Pai Brothers Dosa, Ernakulam, a 30+ year-old eatery that makes a mind-boggling 266 varieties! The offerings here are vegetarian, with the inclusion of eggs that seem to be a huge hit with the locals. I tasted two spicy creations, one with quail eggs and the other with chicken eggs. Needing some respite from the heat, we found our way to Mattancherry, where we tasted the thickest avocado shake at Rinoos Cool Bar. Hope you enjoy this street food amble in Kochi.Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

https://maps.app.goo.gl/it7EC8Xqax1JoMkf.summary: Pai Brothers Dosa in Ernakulam is a legendary eatery that has been serving up an astounding variety of dosas for over 30 years. With a menu boasting 266 different types of dosa, they offer a unique and delicious take on this South Indian staple. The dosas are vegetarian, with the option to add eggs, and are known for their generous fillings and flavorful chutneys. Some of their must-try dosas include the Gundu Dosa, loaded with cheese and a spicy chutney, and the SP Vardhan Dosa, a flavorful explosion of veggies and spices. Whether you're a dosa enthusiast or simply looking for a delicious and satisfying meal, Pai Brothers Dosa is a must-visit.  What makes this place unique is the sheer variety of dosas they offer. With 266 options, there's a dosa for every palate!

summary: Ragi Mudde is a dough-like preparation made of ragi flour, finger millet flour, or both, and water, and is traditionally eaten with saaru (made of greens, meat, or vegetables) by rolling it into a ball using one's right hand without using any cutlery. It is the staple food in Karnataka.
A spicy and flavourful curry made with minced meat, a variety of spices, and herbs.

When Mr. Chandrappa moved to Mathikere, then a remote corner of Bengaluru nearly half a century ago, he set up a vegetarian eatery to cater to the local populace. This met with limited success, however things clicked when he added in the non vegetarian dishes that he and his wife would cook at home. Eventually, his sons joined in to support this family enterprise that in a span of 46 years has come to be the de facto eatery for naati (local style) non-vegetarian oota in the area. However, there are still many outside the immediate area who are yet to discover the homely taste of the fare here. I was one of them, until I paid a surprise visit one afternoon. In doing so, I caught up with the second and third generation of Chandrappa’s family and also his culinary legacy in a smorgasbord of meaty dishes.

Chandrappa Hotel, a hidden gem in Mathikere, Bangalore, has been serving authentic non-vegetarian Karnataka cuisine for 46 years. This family-run eatery, passed down through three generations, is known for its commitment to fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods. The highlight is their use of fresh, locally sourced meats, cooked from scratch with a perfect blend of spices. The Brain Pepper Fry, Pork Pepper Fry, and Mutton Chops Fry are must-tries, showcasing the rich flavors and textures that define their culinary legacy. The warm and inviting atmosphere, reminiscent of a homely setting, enhances the dining experience. Chandrappa Hotel is a testament to the enduring appeal of simple, flavorful food made with passion and authenticity.  

What’s unique: The restaurant uses fresh, locally sourced meat and cooks traditional dishes from scratch using family recipes passed down over three generations

Naati Koli Saaru.summary: A creamy and flavorful curry with a hint of fenugreek, best enjoyed with Neer Dosa or Akki Roti.

Mutton Fry.summary: Tender and juicy pieces of mutton cooked with onions, tomatoes, and a blend of spices, leaving a delightful crunch in every bite.

https://goo.gl/maps/Ez44RS39DBViUas6A.summary: Vaishali Restaurant, a popular highway eatery on the Bengaluru-Mangalore highway, offers a delightful culinary experience with its delectable meaty fare.  Known for its Naati-style dishes, the restaurant serves up flavorful curries, tender mutton fry, and aromatic biryanis.  Their signature dish, Naati Koli Saaru, is a must-try for its creamy texture and authentic flavors, best paired with Neer Dosa or Akki Roti. The restaurant's mutton fry is another highlight, featuring tender pieces of meat cooked to perfection with a blend of spices and a satisfying crunch. For kheema enthusiasts, the Kheema Gojju and Kheema Dosa are highly recommended.  While the biryani is flavorful, it tends to be a tad dry and slightly salty. Overall, Vaishali Restaurant is a great stopover for travelers seeking a hearty and satisfying meaty meal.  The restaurant's commitment to using high-quality ingredients and traditional recipes is evident in every dish.  Whether you're craving a comforting curry or a flavorful fry, Vaishali Restaurant is sure to satisfy your taste buds.  Don't miss their Kaal Soup, a flavorful and well-balanced starter.

Brothers Basavaraju and Shivakumar are huge fans of Dr Rajkumar and family. So much so that their 36-year-old eatery has no name board, but is simply known to locals as Rajkumar Idli hotel in Tumkur. In my tasting of their old-fashioned thatte idli, a harkback to the 'acrey' idli of yore, when idlis where steamed on large plates prior to the advent of modern idli steamers, I discover that their devotion to Kannada cinema’s most iconic family is also mirrored in their pursuit to preserving an age old idli tradition. This unpretentious shop is definitely worth a stop when on the route.

The restaurant, run by brothers Basavaraju and Shivakumar, is a tribute to Kannada film icon Dr. Rajkumar. The Thatte Idli, a highlight of the menu, stands out for its old-fashioned preparation and airy, fluffy texture, reminiscent of the 'acrey' idli.  The accompanying usli, a flavorful and healthy dish, complements the idli perfectly. Another must-try is the Special Khali Dosae, thicker than usual and packed with a flavorful palia.  Beyond the food, the video highlights the restaurant's simple ambiance and the dedication of the owners to preserving traditional recipes.  It's a must-visit for those seeking an authentic South Indian breakfast experience in Tumkur.  The unique aspect of this restaurant is its dedication to serving traditional, old-fashioned Thatte Idli, a rarity in today's times, making it a true culinary gem for those seeking an authentic taste of the past.

I had heard much about this tiny eatery located in a bylane of old Mysuru, especially of its biryani that back in the day would be cooked over a wood-fired stove. And so when I received recommendations in response to a recent “where should I lunch in Mysuru” post, I lost no time in making tracks to Nasheman. The place is drab, and that’s putting it mildly, a handful of tables sit cheek by jowl in a modestly-sized room, and the service is industrial at best. But it is the mutton biryani here and other meaty delicacies, especially a delicious twice cooked mutton phaal that draw customers to this 50-year-old restaurant. In this outing, I tasted most of what was on offer for lunch, after an insightful kitchen tour.

Masala Puri.summary: A mellow and flavorful dish with a gentle blend of spices and fresh ingredients. Its not too spicy and has a creamy texture from the peas.

Dahi Puri.summary: A delightful combination of creamy dahi, sweet chutney, and crunchy puri. The flavors are well balanced, starting with the creaminess of the dahi and ending with a hint of sweetness and spice.

Diet Bhel.summary: A lighter option without fried components, it offers a simple yet flavorful blend of chutneys, spices, and puffed rice.

Cutlet Chaat.summary: A must-try dish with a crispy cutlet as the star. It is served with a medley of chutneys, spices, and fresh ingredients like carrots, coriander, and onions, creating a burst of flavors and textures.

Sukha Puri.summary: A dry chaat option with a satisfying crunch. It features a mix of puffed rice, sev, chutneys, and spices, offering a burst of flavor in every bite.

Pani Puri.summary: A highly recommended dish with the perfect balance of sweet and spicy flavors. The puri is filled with a flavorful pani and a mix of chutneys, leaving a refreshing and satisfying taste.

The Masala Puri is described as having a gentle blend of spices and fresh ingredients, while the Dahi Puri impresses with its creamy dahi and sweet chutney. The Diet Bhel provides a lighter option without compromising on taste, and the Cutlet Chaat stands out with its crispy cutlet and flavorful chutneys.  The Sukha Puri offers a satisfying crunch with its mix of puffed rice. The highlight of the experience is undoubtedly the Pani Puri, which Kripal describes as having the perfect balance of sweet and spicy flavors. What sets Atithi's Chats apart is the well-balanced flavors of their chaat, which gently tease the palate without being overwhelming.  If you find yourself in Malleshwaram, Atithi's Chats is a must-visit for a flavorful and satisfying chaat experience.

Raghavendra was employed in a bakery 33 years ago when he decided to set up a small business on his own. His original thought was to set up a stationery store requiring minimal capital, but given his interest in food, he began experimenting with all sorts of snacks and condiments and soon hit upon combinations of chaat. Thus was born Harshini Condiments in a tiny bylane of Ravindra Nagar in Shimoga. The fare here is chaat but in a healthier avatar. Think ingredients like fresh fenugreek, banana stem, cabbage, pomegranate, corn, et al tossed together with savoury elements of crunch and punchy homemade chutneys. Creations that are not only wholesome but also hit home in the flavour department. A must try for street food lovers when in Shimoga! Happy eating!

https://maps.app.goo.gl/Na6x3LTDZMsgpRAv.summary: This video features Harshini Condiments in Shimoga, a hidden gem serving amazingly tasty yet healthy chaats for the past 33 years. Owner Raghavendra's passion for food led him to transform his initial plan of a stationery store into this beloved eatery. They offer a unique twist on traditional chaats, incorporating fresh ingredients like fenugreek, banana stem, and pomegranate for a healthier take. The highlight is their exceptional homemade chutneys, adding a burst of flavor to every dish. Must-try items include Nippat Masala, Menthye Soppu Masala, Bread Masala, Corn Masala, and Mirinda Masala, all affordably priced between Rs. 50 to Rs. 60. Harshini Condiments is a must-visit for anyone looking for a delicious and healthy street food experience in Shimoga.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/gGpWUkmeegS8HqR5.summary: Aubree is a bakery that could be on a High Street anywhere in the world. They make a variety of plum cakes, including a rich plum cake with rum and wine and a rich fruit plum cake without rum and wine. All of their products are eggless. The owner says that they use the same recipe for their plum cakes but have modernized it on the ingredient front. For example, they use three types of nuts in their plum cakes: almonds, cashews, and hazelnuts. They also use ghee and soak the dry fruits in apple juice and fruit juices. The host tries both the fruit and rich plum cakes. He finds that the fruit cake has a more assertive spice flavor because it doesn't have any booze in it. He also notes that the fruit cake is quite moist for an eggless cake. The host prefers the rich plum cake with rum and wine. He finds that the flavors are deeper and more intense. He also likes the fact that the cake is quite dense. Overall, the host is impressed with Aubree's plum cakes. He thinks they would make a great gift, especially in the boxes they come in.

They use premium ingredients like refined flour, three types of nuts (almonds, cashews, and hazelnuts), and ghee. Their plum cakes are modernized versions of traditional recipes, with the option of a rich plum cake soaked in rum and wine for three months. They also have an eggless fruit plum cake soaked in apple and fruit juices. Both cakes are moist and flavorful, with the boozy version having a deeper, more intense taste.

This plum cake trail is inspired by the thousands of responses I received to a recent tweet on Bengaluru’s most popular plum cakes. In part one of this tasting trail, I sample plum cakes at three Bengaluru institutions, Thoms, perhaps one of the most recommended, a 100-year-old Excelsior bakery that is still unknown to many, and a special matured cake at All Saints. I hope you enjoy this tour, stay tuned for part 2.

I also take this opportunity to wish you and your loved ones a wonderful Christmas season. Happy eating! God bless!

Kripal Amanna

Rich Plum Cake.name: Rich Plum Cake
Rich Plum Cake.summary: This plum cake is rich, moist, and has a perfect balance of flavors. It is not overly sweet or boozy, making it enjoyable for everyone. The cake features a generous amount of fruits, including raisins and plums, and is enriched with cashews. The fruits are soaked for six months, resulting in a deep flavor and a moist texture. The cake is not overly alcoholic and has a subtle sweetness that makes it irresistible.

Chicken Puff.name: Chicken Puff
Chicken Puff.summary: The puff pastry is flaky and airy, providing a satisfying crunch with every bite. The chicken filling is flavorful and well-seasoned, with a good balance of chicken, onions, and peas. The ratio of filling to pastry is perfect, ensuring that each bite is bursting with flavor.

Vegetable Puff.name: Vegetable Puff
Vegetable Puff.summary: The puff pastry is flaky and airy, providing a satisfying crunch with every bite. The vegetable filling is flavorful and well-seasoned. The ratio of filling to pastry is perfect, ensuring that each bite is bursting with flavor.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/nXbc6k2vqUWpr2xu.summary: Thoms Bakery, known for its popular plum cakes, offers a delightful culinary experience with its rich and moist plum cakes. The bakery, run by a family passionate about their craft, uses a traditional recipe dating back to the 1970s. Their plum cakes are known for their perfect balance of flavors, not too sweet or boozy, and generous amounts of fruits and nuts. Apart from plum cakes, Thoms Bakery also offers delicious chicken and vegetable puffs that are popular among patrons.

This plum cake trail is inspired by the thousands of responses I received to a recent tweet on Bengaluru’s most popular plum cakes. In part one of this tasting trail, I sample plum cakes at three Bengaluru institutions, Thoms, perhaps one of the most recommended, a 100-year-old Excelsior bakery that is still unknown to many, and a special matured cake at All Saints. I hope you enjoy this tour, stay tuned for part 2.

I also take this opportunity to wish you and your loved ones a wonderful Christmas season. Happy eating! God bless!

I hope you enjoy this tour, stay tuned for part 2.

I also take this opportunity to wish you and your loved ones a wonderful Christmas season. Happy eating! God bless!

When I survey a new city for a Gourmet On The Road series, I usually invite recommendations from viewers, and post due diligence and research, these form the basis for what one eventually explores. When I called out for Shimoga, this restaurant received the most recommendations. And those in the know may not be surprised given the fact that Sri Meenakshi Bhavan has been an integral part, actually a pioneer of the city’s culinary landscape for over a century now. The space that it occupies was once the owning family’s ancestral abode and that energy also seems to permeate through the homely old-fashioned decor and the South Canara inspired fare here. The food is tasty, sumptuous and satisfying, made to traditional recipes by cooks, many who have served in the kitchens here for decades. Whilst the benne masala dosae may come as the most recommended dish, the vade, avalakki mosaru, paddu too are as rewarding as I found during a breakfast visit where I also had the opportunity to converse with the restaurant’s third generation owner, Mr Chandrashekar and his daughter, Ganavi.

If you are in Shimoga, or are making plans to visit, this is one eatery you must not miss. Hope you enjoy this breakfast episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

A former corporate executive, Pooja Patil realized her heart was in food, more specifically the regional specialities and dishes of her family, originally from Solapur in Maharashtra, but Bengaluru residents for decades. Honing recipes, adding her touch, she opened Maskaa, a small, cosy café in Koramangala, to serve comfort fare - from vada pav, thaalipeeth, sabudana vadas, misal pav, pav bhaji, omelets, paneer bhurji, even a couple of interesting chicken dishes, and in sync with the eatery’s name, a butter-laden bun that pairs deliciously with a masala tea, brewed with a secret blend of 17 spices prepared by her father.

I dropped in for a ‘snacky’ lunch one afternoon to chat with this enterprising lady entrepreneur, and also taste some of her dishes. Definitely check out Maskaa when in the neighbourhood and support this unique initiative. Hope you enjoy this one; take care, safe and strong. Happy eating!

Vada Pav.name: Vada Pav
Vada Pav.summary: A fairly simple vada pav with a tinge of green in the batata vada that comes from the green chili. The potatoes are nice and creamy, with a bit of mustard and lime.

Misal Pav.name: Misal Pav
Misal Pav.summary: A unique take on Misal Pav with moong beans, farsan, and a warming, spicy gravy. The farsan adds a nice crunch and the pav soaks up the flavorful gravy.

Chicken Kheema Pav.name: Chicken Kheema Pav
Chicken Kheema Pav.summary: A spicy and smoky chicken kheema with a homemade kala masala. The kala masala is made with roasted onions, coconut, and chilies, giving it a rich and intense flavor.

Green Chicken Pav.name: Green Chicken Pav
Green Chicken Pav.summary: A refreshing and flavorful chicken curry made with fresh coriander, mint, and coconut. The gravy is thick and creamy, and the chicken is tender and juicy.

Maska Bun.name: Maska Bun
Maska Bun.summary: A soft and sweet bun slathered with generous amounts of Amul butter. A simple yet satisfying treat that pairs perfectly with the masala chai.

Masala Tea.name: Masala Tea
Masala Tea.summary: A flavorful and aromatic masala chai made with 17 different spices, including cardamom, cinnamon, and pepper. The perfect way to end a meal at Maskaa.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/nPqfdGkCHfdx8k8m.summary: Maskaa is a cozy cafe in Koramangala, Bengaluru, run by Pooja Patil, a former corporate executive turned food entrepreneur. The cafe serves a mix of Maharashtrian and Irani comfort food, with a focus on snacks and light meals. The menu features dishes like Vada Pav, Misal Pav, Chicken Kheema Pav, Green Chicken Pav, Bun Maska, and Masala Tea.  The highlight of Maskaa is their use of fresh, homemade ingredients, including a special kala masala made by Pooja's father in Solapur. The masala chai is a must-try, made with a secret blend of 17 spices. Maskaa is a great spot for a quick and satisfying meal, with reasonable prices and a welcoming atmosphere.

A couple of years ago when we were all stuck at home during the pandemic, I was craving for a donne biryani. That’s when I chanced upon RNR donne biryani on a delivery app. I had never heard of them before, and so Intrigued, I ordered. And was pleasantly surprised with what I tasted, so much so that I even filmed an impromptu vlog. 

Now whilst most businesses that opened during this period to cater to consumers at home were unable to make it beyond the pandemic, RNR has not only survived but scaled across multiple kitchens (at last count there were 18!) in the city and also a couple of restaurants on the back of the popularity of its donne biryani that is made to a family recipe. In this episode I visit their newest restaurant in RT Nagar, Bengaluru, where I catch up with Ramya Ravi, co-owner of the chain, who articulates that “their vision is to take Bengaluru’s donne biryani offering across the country!” And going by what I witnessed during the step by step making of their signature chicken donne biryani, and also what I tasted, they certainly seem to be on the right path to doing so.

I hope you enjoy this biryani making episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!  

Kripal Amanna

When it comes to chaats, every city has its own style, and Shimoga is no different. Be it the masala puri, sev puri or paani puri, each one hits differently as I discovered during this outing to DVS Circle Pani Puri, a chaat shop that has held sway over the city’s penchant for its spicy fare for nearly four decades. I was told these unique flavours were a result of Shimoga’s purveyors not being influenced by chaat traditions of the North and therefore developing a unique palate of their own. Hope you enjoy this streetfood outing; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Sandeep Bhosle had to give up his gaddo (cart) a couple of years ago and move to a tiny stall on Dr Atmaram Borkar road in Panjim. But that hasn’t diminished the popularity of his ros omelet in any manner whatsoever. When the lights in his shop come on, the street food scene here comes alive. Dining off tables and stools arranged on the sidewalk, Sandeep’s clientele is a democratic mix of Goa, from the elite to the daily wage earners, for whom a plate of his xacuti gravy laden egg dish is bliss and the sort that Sandeep says,  “guarantees a good night's sleep.” Hope you enjoy this street food episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

My last visit to Udupi Sri Krishna Bhavan in Balepete for an early tiffin coincided with the conclusion of their lunch service. I watched some of the lunch crowd relishing their thali meals, and made a note to return for the same someday. And so when on a recent visit to Chickpete, a lunch opportunity suddenly opened up, I lost no time in heading to this near-100-year-old eatery to taste their South Canara lunch. It’s a simple affair - couple of vegetable preparations, lentils, rasam, poori and rice, even a sweet - quite homely in its taste and sumptuous enough to fill one’s belly for a very affordable Rs. 110 only. And consumed in the restaurant’s heritage setting, it is also the sort of meal that transports one back to ‘good ole yesteryear’! Definitely plan a lunch here when in the area.

The host highly recommends their South Indian thali, praising the beetroot palya and raw mango chutney. He describes the food as light, flavorful and prepared with care. The ambience of the restaurant is praised for its old-world charm, transporting diners back in time. He concludes by recommending this place for those looking for a simple, traditional South Indian meal in a nostalgic setting.

pure vegetarian restaurant, oldest restaurant, bengaluru, south canara cuisine, sambar, rava idli, vada, vade, sagu dosae, masala dosa, south indian tiffin, dumrot, badam halwa, gulab jamun, filter coffee, popular bengaluru restaurants, balepet, chickpet, must try restaurant, historical restaurant, heritage eatery, bangalore food tour, eating out in bengaluru, vegetarian, eateries in bangalore, support local

Although established at its present location in 1926, its culinary provenance dates back to the early 1900s. One of Bengaluru’s oldest eateries, Udupi Sri Krishna Bhavan has not received the kind of recognition other eateries of its ilk have perhaps due to its location amidst the hustle and bustle of Balepete. The food here is prepared the old-fashioned way, not the sort that swims in rivers of ghee or is buried under mounds of butter, khoa, or other such dairy decadence. Which is good, especially if you want to indulge, sans any guilt, in its tasty South Canara fare, like many of its regular patrons, some who have been visiting for 50 years! I soak in some charming old-world vibe as I make a tasty meal of some of their must-try dishes including a scrumptious, very popular sagu dosae and perhaps the most impressionable sambar you will find in this city. A sambar that we also watched the making of. 
Hope you enjoy this episode; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

https://goo.gl/maps/LUzZyTxcG3Mbwf9RA.summary: This video takes us on a culinary journey to Udupi Sri Krishna Bhavan, a hidden gem in the bustling streets of Bengaluru. Established in 1926, the restaurant boasts a legacy dating back to the early 1900s, serving authentic South Canara cuisine. The highlight is undoubtedly their Sambar, a flavorful and thick concoction with a perfect blend of spices and vegetables, a testament to their commitment to traditional recipes. The Sagu Dosae, a crispy dosa with a wholesome vegetable filling, is another must-try, known for its balanced flavors and guilt-free indulgence. Udupi Sri Krishna Bhavan offers a nostalgic dining experience, with its old-world charm and time-tested recipes, making it a must-visit for those seeking an authentic taste of the past.

It had been a while since I’d savoured a good military (local) style oota (meal). I had heard on and off about this 10-year-old eatery located at Devanahalli on the outskirts of Bengaluru, but never ventured out given the distance to be traversed for a meal. And boy oh boy was I pleasantly surprised when I finally did. The place may be rustic, but the food that’s dished out by Suresh Gowda and his family in the kitchen here is the sort that makes the 50-km drive here worthwhile. I savoured their biryanis, meaty fries and the curries that have earned this military hotel a strong fan following.

Hope you enjoy this one. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!
