A couple of years ago I was at an eatery in Mysuru, when a few lads walked up to me and in the course of our conversation told me that the Mysore Pak to try was in their hometown, Shimoga. I was amazed at their courage and conviction, standing in Mysuru and praising a Mysore Pak from their hometown. Nonetheless, I made note of their recommendation. And so when I recently did a tour of Shimoga, the Venkatesha Sweet House Mysore Pak was top of my list. Not only did I taste this hugely popular sweet alongside a few other treats, I also caught its making with third generation owner, Prasanna, and his sweet makers of decades. When in Shimoga, definitely visit this 60 year culinary institution.

Champakali.summary: A traditional South Indian sweet with a crispy texture and a sweet flavor that’s not overpowering. It’s made with gram flour, sugar, and cardamom, and it’s sure to satisfy your sweet tooth.

Mysore Pak.summary: A rich, decadent sweet made with gram flour, ghee, and sugar. The Mysore Pak at Venkatesha Sweet House is known for its unique texture. It's not as smooth as some Mysore Paks, but it's incredibly flavorful and will melt in your mouth. It’s a must-try for anyone who visits the shop.

Milk Halwa.summary: A rich and creamy milk-based sweet. It’s made with milk, sugar, and nuts, and it’s cooked to perfection. It's a must-try for anyone who loves milk-based sweets.

Dappa Khara.summary: A savory and crunchy snack that’s perfect for any time of day. It’s made with rice flour, peanuts, curry leaves, and spices, and it’s deep-fried to perfection.  It's a must-try for anyone who loves savory snacks.

Sweet Mixture.summary: A delicious mixture of sweet and savory ingredients. It’s made with sev, peanuts, raisins, and spices, and it’s a perfect snack to enjoy with tea.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/TX4jZjG5GqGp2xdc.summary: Venkatesha Sweet House in Shimoga is a culinary institution renowned for its traditional sweets and snacks, particularly its Mysore Pak. Established in 1964, this family-run shop has been delighting customers for over 60 years with its commitment to quality and authentic flavors. The star attraction is undoubtedly the Mysore Pak, a rich and decadent sweet made with gram flour, ghee, and sugar. What sets Venkatesha’s Mysore Pak apart is its unique texture – a delightful contrast between crispy and melt-in-your-mouth goodness.  This distinct texture is achieved by hand-roasting the ingredients, a testament to the shop’s dedication to traditional methods.  Beyond the Mysore Pak, Venkatesha Sweet House offers a tantalizing array of sweets and snacks. From the crispy and flavorful Champakali to the rich and creamy Milk Halwa, every item on the menu is made with the finest ingredients and a whole lot of love.  If you're in Shimoga and craving a taste of authentic Karnataka sweets, Venkatesha Sweet House is an absolute must-visit.

When Mr. and Mrs. M. Mahadev Rao moved to Peenya on the outskirts of Bengaluru, this area was a remote industrial outpost where a few factories lay scattered amongst fields. With a family of seven children to feed and educate, this couple rented a shed to run a small tiffin shop that fueled workers and staff in the manufacturing units around. Over time, the popularity of their homely vegetarian tiffin fare and meals grew, also earning for the humble eatery the moniker ‘Bhatru Hotel’, as the couple were constantly cooking and feeding customers. 34 years on Gurukrupa Bhats Canteen stands strong as a cornerstone in this now bustling suburb, a daily ritual for many of its patrons, for whom a day is incomplete without coffee, tiffin or a meal here. Now in his nineties, Mr Rao has left the running of the eatery to his sons who are involved in every aspect of the operation - from the cooking to the serving and speaking a kind word or two with their customers, many who share decades-old relationships with the place. I dropped in for a quick tiffin, but felt compelled to linger on and savour many of the dishes on offer.

Thatte Idli.summary: Unlike plain idli, this variant incorporates Sago pearls for a stickier, more substantial texture. The addition of butter enhances its richness, making it a more indulgent choice.

Gulab Jamun with Banana & Ice Cream.name: Gulab Jamun with Banana & Ice Cream
Gulab Jamun with Banana & Ice Cream.summary: This unique dessert is a must-try. The combination of ripe banana, sweet syrup, and creamy ice cream creates an unusual yet delightful flavor profile.

Special Gajar Halwa.name: Special Gajar Halwa
Special Gajar Halwa.summary: This halwa stands out for its balanced sweetness, allowing the character of the carrots to shine through. It's a refreshing change from overly sweet versions.

Tuppa Mysore Pak.name: Tuppa Mysore Pak
Tuppa Mysore Pak.summary: This Mysore Pak is well-roasted, with a soft center and a delightful nutty flavor, making it a classic South Indian dessert.

Coffee.name: Coffee
Coffee.summary: The coffee here is a unique blend of 30% chicory and dark roast, giving it a distinct taste and texture. It is strong and flavorful, perfect for coffee lovers.

Maddur Vade.name: Maddur Vade
Maddur Vade.summary: This Vade is another popular choice. It is crispy and flavorful, perfect as a snack or accompaniment to a meal.

This family-run eatery, known for its home-style vegetarian fare, has become a daily ritual for locals, offering a taste of tradition and a sense of community. The dishes, prepared with a focus on lighter flavors and fresh ingredients, cater to the daily needs of the workforce, providing satisfying meals without feeling heavy. Their commitment to quality and consistency has earned them a loyal following, with customers returning day after day, year after year. From their signature Idli Chutney Sambar to the unique Gulab Jamun with Banana & Ice Cream, the menu reflects a balance of classic South Indian staples and innovative twists, all made with a focus on freshness and flavor. Whether you're a local worker or a curious foodie, Hotel Gurukrupa Bhats Canteen offers a glimpse into the heart of Bengaluru's culinary scene, where food is more than just sustenance—it's a celebration of tradition, community, and the simple joy of a satisfying meal. The unique element of this eatery lies in its ability to adapt to the needs of its community, creating a space where food fosters a sense of belonging and comfort. It's a testament to the power of simple, honest food made with love, a legacy that continues to nourish both body and soul.

There are only a handful of culinary institutions in this city that have stood the test of time for half a century or more. Serving their patrons faithfully, not just in their fare that harks back to the days when things were simple, but also conveying the nostalgia of many memories across generations. And so it is indeed a sad day when one of them has to close doors soon. 

I have visited New Krishna Bhavan in Malleshwaram a few times, to film and to partake of their trademark, unfussy South Canara fare. This time at the restaurant felt different though, its imminent closure palpable in the sentiments echoed by the owners, cooks and many customers for whom NKB was part of their life. 

This is an episode I wish I didn’t have to film. But here it is nonetheless. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Not many know this interesting trivia about New Krishna Bhavan, Malleswaram, that until the recent lockdown this restaurant had not closed its doors even for a single day ever since they opened for business in 1954! Quite in contrast to the popularity of this vegetarian eatery.

I recently discovered this restaurant that although open at Bengaluru Airport City for a few months now, is largely unknown to food lovers in the city. Fronted by a veteran chef with a creditworthy reputation for North Indian cuisine, the food at Maa Da Dhaba certainly delivers. From punchy kebabs to silken dals and robustly flavoured curries and kadais, there is a popular selection of Sino Indian fare on the menu too. What also adds to its appeal is the pleasant drive to get here and its location - only a couple of minutes to the airport terminal but yet far removed from its bustle. Definitely check it out, and yes, at prices that are quite honest too.

best_dishes.name: Dal Makhani
best_dishes.summary: This comforting Dal Makhani, simmered for 12 hours, offers a lighter take on the classic dish without compromising on taste or smokiness.  The lentils retain their shape until they melt in your mouth.

best_dishes.name: Chicken Malai Tikka
best_dishes.summary: The Chicken Malai Tikka is incredibly soft and moist, especially the pieces from the center of the skewer. It's perfectly balanced with just the right amount of creaminess, enhanced by the mint chutney's refreshing flavors.

best_dishes.name: Honey Chili Potato
best_dishes.summary: The Honey Chili Potato is a delightful burst of flavors, starting with the sweetness of honey and followed by a kick of chili sauce. The sesame seed coating adds a nutty taste, while the potato itself is soft and creamy inside, contrasting with the crispy exterior.

best_dishes.name: Mutter Paneer
best_dishes.summary: This Mutter Paneer is a simple, wholesome dish that showcases the goodness of desi-style peas and paneer in a flavorful gravy. A hint of sweetness comes from the honey used in the tomato-based gravy.

best_dishes.name: Punjabi Kadai Chicken
best_dishes.summary: The Punjabi Kadai Chicken features tender tandoori chicken tossed in a rich gravy with onions and tomatoes. The dish offers a delicious blend of flavors, from the sweetness of onions and tanginess of tomatoes to the smokiness of the chicken.

https://goo.gl/maps/BVPVHAxhXBt2Bme18.summary: Food Lovers TV host Kripal Amanna takes viewers on a culinary journey to Maa Da Dhaba, a hidden gem located in the cargo complex of Bengaluru Airport. This unassuming eatery, run by Chef Subodh Goyal, may not boast fancy décor but more than makes up for it with its delicious and affordable North Indian fare. Kripal samples a range of dishes, from classic Chicken Malai Tikka and melt-in-your-mouth Dal Makhani to flavorful Punjabi Kadai Chicken and a satisfyingly spicy Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani. The restaurant also caters to different tastes with Chinese and South Indian options. Kripal highlights the restaurant's commitment to providing tasty food at reasonable prices, making it a must-visit for anyone looking for a satisfying meal near Bengaluru Airport.

Almost everyone has heard about and many have tasted the early morning biryani at Hoskote, a pre-sunrise ritual 40 kilometers from Bengaluru. However, few visitors seem to know about a fried kabab evening tradition that is hugely popular with locals. On a drive back from Kolar a few weeks ago, we took a detour into this highway town to savour a quick meal of chicken kabab, egg rice, and a chicken biryani too. The last wasn’t on our plan, but then, we were in biryani country after all. Definitely check out Ravi Kabab Center when in the area, and be prepared to jostle with the crowd to get your share of bisi bisi (hot) kababs.

Hope you enjoy this one. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Chicken Biryani.summary: Aromatic and flavorful Biryani made with a unique blend of spices. Experience the enticing aroma and taste of turmeric, red chili powder, cloves, cinnamon, and cardamom, all perfectly infused into the rice and tender chicken.

Quail Fry.name: Quail Fry
Quail Fry.summary: Farm-fresh quail deep-fried to a crispy texture. The quail is cooked with minimal spices, allowing the natural flavors to shine through. While the meat itself is lean and requires a bit of chewing, the overall taste is satisfying.

When it comes to tiffin eateries in Bengaluru, there are those that are celebrated, even venerated, and splashed across media, both traditional and new. Nothing wrong with that. And then there are those that quietly go about their work, serving customers for decades on end, content to not bask in the limelight. A great example of the latter is Mahalakshmi Tiffin Room in Basavanagudi, South Bengaluru, though open since 1926 is still unknown to most in the city. I visited them one afternoon to meet the second and third generation owners, and to also taste an assortment of their honestly-priced fare, including a deliciously light and fluffy khali dosae and a satisfying sambar. Hope you enjoy this tiffin episode; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Goli Bajje.name: Goli Bajje
Goli Bajje.summary: Crispy and crunchy on the outside, soft on the inside, with a hint of sweetness and flavors of carom seeds, cumin, coconut, green chili and curry leaves. Best enjoyed hot and pairs well with the spicy chutney.

Idli Vada Sambar.name: Idli Vada Sambar
Idli Vada Sambar.summary: Idli and vada served with a flavorful and well-balanced sambar that's not too thick or thin, seasoned with tamarind, jaggery, chili and coriander. The sambar is designed to penetrate the idly, and the vada has a slight crunch with flavors of fried urad dal.

Khali Dosae.name: Khali Dosae
Khali Dosae.summary: Light, airy, soft and fluffy dosa with a slightly toasted exterior. It's made without oil or ghee, giving it a dry texture, and pairs well with sambar, chutney, sagu (vegetable stew) or aloo (potato) filling. The sambar is particularly flavorful when soaked up by the dosa's pores.

Toast Jam.name: Toast Jam
Toast Jam.summary: Unique combination of toasted bread served with a homemade banana, tomato and sugar jam, and a vegetable stew (sagu). The jam offers a sweet and tangy flavor with hints of cardamom and guava, while the sagu adds a savory touch.

Carrot Halwa.name: Carrot Halwa
Carrot Halwa.summary: Traditional gajar halwa made with carrots, roasted semolina, coconut, dry fruits and milk, resulting in a light and not-too-sweet dessert. It has a creamy texture with the natural sweetness of carrots and coconut.

Coffee.name: Coffee
Coffee.summary: Strong and flavorful coffee with a blend of 80% coffee and 20% chicory, roasted to perfection. It's served hot and pairs well with the Goli Bajje, enhancing its flavors.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/d4TghiDftbR74JXh.summary: Mahalakshmi Tiffin Room, a legendary eatery in Basavanagudi, Bangalore, has been serving authentic and delicious South Indian tiffin for almost a century.  The restaurant, run by the third generation of the founding family, prides itself on its simple, home-style food made with traditional recipes and a commitment to affordability. The food is light and wholesome, with highlights being the crispy Goli Bajje, flavorful Idli Vada Sambar, and the unique Toast Jam.  The restaurant's enduring legacy is a testament to its commitment to quality and customer satisfaction, offering a nostalgic dining experience that transports you back in time.

A farmer by profession, Mr. Rangaswamy opened a small thatched eatery on his property abutting the highway in Gowdagere, near Channarayapatna, 15 years ago to serve tea and snacks to travellers on the Bengaluru Hassan route. As the eatery became popular, his family also introduced their unique village style biryani along with other meaty preparations like the mutton sambar, thale kaalu and chops. He has since passed on, but his family continues his culinary traditions at SLR Biryani. Notwithstanding the recent construction of a flyover that bypasses this humble home eatery and has impacted business here, it still manages to hold on to its loyal patrons. The popularity of their wood-fire-cooked biryani is such that it runs out in a few hours each morning, after which it is the mutton dishes served with ragi mudde, plain rice or khushka that occupy centrestage. I dropped in impromptu for lunch one afternoon and was elated to find, through a tremendous stroke of luck, the biryani that was prepared for a special order.

Over 40 years ago, Mr. Chandrashekar, originally from Sasthan in Dakshina Kannada, had to wind up his long running restaurant in Shimoga during the emergency. Forced to once again begin from scratch, he chose a spot in Birur, then a sleepy village around 240 kilometres from Bengaluru to set up an eatery. Since then Birur has grown to a bustling trading town, the spot where his venture, Preethi Canteen stands, is now a busy highway. And this tiffin restaurant has been elevated to legendary status by its many patrons for whom a halt here is a must when on the road around here. Over time, I have received many requests to taste their iconic masala dosae, and so on a recent drive to Shimoga, I stopped here and caught not just a taste of their tasty fare, but also a conversation with its second generation owner, Mr. Prakash Holla on what makes Preethi Canteen a hugely popular culinary institution.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/e6AjBDSqFkwJskUb.summary: This video features Preethi Canteen, a legendary highway stop in Birur, Karnataka, known for its iconic benne masala dosa. Established over 40 years ago, this humble eatery has become a must-visit for travelers on National Highway 206. The episode highlights the thin and crispy benne dosa, made with generous amounts of butter.  The owner emphasizes the traditional recipe and the importance of using quality ingredients. Beyond the dosa, the video also showcases other South Indian staples like curd vada and mandakki, all made with fresh ingredients. The highlight of the video is the unique texture of the benne dosa, thin and crispy around the edges and slightly thicker in the center, a result of the traditional preparation method.

Naati Koli Rasam.name: Naati Koli Rasam
Naati Koli Rasam.summary: A hot and warming rasam with a piece of tender country chicken on the bone, offering a flavorful broth with a tangy tomato flavor and the freshness of coriander. It's a perfect start to a meal, especially on a cold evening.

Drumstick Chilli.name: Drumstick Chilli
Drumstick Chilli.summary: A unique and flavorful dish featuring tender drumsticks cooked in a spicy chili sauce. The drumstick kernels are moist and pulpy, offering a delightful contrast to the heat of the green chilies. It's a must-try for those who love drumsticks and spicy food.

Chicken Kshatriya Kabab.name: Chicken Kshatriya Kabab
Chicken Kshatriya Kabab.summary: A deep-fried chicken kebab with a crispy and flavorful batter. The chicken is coated in a unique masala and fried to perfection, offering a delightful crunch in every bite. It's a great option for those who enjoy flavorful and crispy snacks.

Mutton Nalli Fry.name: Mutton Nalli Fry
Mutton Nalli Fry.summary: Tender and flavorful mutton nalli cooked to perfection with a rich and aromatic garam masala. The meat is incredibly soft and falls off the bone easily, while the marrow adds a unique depth of flavor. It's a must-try for mutton lovers.

Naati Chilli Chicken.name: Naati Chilli Chicken
Naati Chilli Chicken.summary: A mildly spicy chili chicken with a unique naati style twist. The chicken is cooked with a blend of spices and vegetables, offering a balance of flavors. The spiciness is subtle and builds gradually, making it an enjoyable dish for those who prefer a milder chili chicken.

Chicken Biryani.name: Chicken Biryani
Chicken Biryani.summary: A flavorful and aromatic biryani with tender chicken and perfectly cooked rice. The biryani masala is a blend of aromatic spices, offering a distinct and flavorful taste. It's a classic dish that's sure to satisfy your biryani cravings.

Mutton Biryani.name: Mutton Biryani
Mutton Biryani.summary: A rich and flavorful biryani with tender mutton and perfectly cooked rice. The mutton adds a unique depth of flavor to the biryani, making it even more aromatic and delicious. It's a must-try for mutton biryani lovers.

Crystal Roll.name: Crystal Roll
Crystal Roll.summary: A unique dessert made with candied pumpkin, cream, and nuts. The pumpkin is cooked with sugar, giving it a crystalline texture. It's a refreshing and not-too-sweet dessert that's sure to tantalize your taste buds.

Elaneer Payasam.name: Elaneer Payasam
Elaneer Payasam.summary: A comforting and gently sweet dessert made with tender coconut. It's a refreshing end to a meal, especially after a spicy and flavorful biryani. The coconut adds a natural sweetness and a delightful texture to the payasam.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/Jmp6zZhNqb9pnzJs.summary: This video review explores RNR Biryani, a popular eatery in Bengaluru known for its delicious Donne Biryani. The reviewer highlights the restaurant's commitment to serving authentic Karnataka-style cuisine in a welcoming and tastefully designed ambiance. He highly recommends their Naati Koli Rasam, a flavorful and warming soup, and the Drumstick Chilli, a unique and spicy appetizer. He praises the Chicken Kshatriya Kabab for its crispy exterior and juicy interior, and the Mutton Nalli Fry for its tender meat and flavorful marrow. He finds the Naati Chilli Chicken to be mildly spicy with a gradual heat build-up. Moving on to the star of the show, he tries both the Chicken and Mutton Donne Biryani. He notes that while both are flavorful, the mutton biryani stands out for its richer taste and the depth of flavor imparted by the meat. He appreciates the generous portions, noting that one biryani is sufficient for two people. He concludes the meal with the Crystal Roll, a unique and refreshing dessert, and the Elaneer Payasam, a comforting and mildly sweet treat. The reviewer highly recommends RNR Biryani for its authentic flavors, generous portions, and the variety of dishes available, making it an excellent choice for biryani lovers and those looking to experience the taste of Karnataka.

#rnrbiryani #donnebiryani #bangalore

rnr biryani, popular donne biryani, rnr biryani, rt nagar, rnr biryani bengaluru, most popular donne biryani available across bengaluru, authentic bangalore biryani, authentic donne biryani, rnr biryani recipe, donne biryani recipe, grandma recipe, famous biryani of bangalore, must try biryani, bangalore food trail, karnataka food tour, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

A couple of years ago when we were all stuck at home during the pandemic, I was craving for a donne biryani. That’s when I chanced upon RNR donne biryani on a delivery app. I had never heard of them before, and so Intrigued, I ordered. And was pleasantly surprised with what I tasted, so much so that I even filmed an impromptu vlog. 

Now whilst most businesses that opened during this period to cater to consumers at home were unable to make it beyond the pandemic, RNR has not only survived but scaled across multiple kitchens (at last count there were 18!) in the city and also a couple of restaurants on the back of the popularity of its donne biryani that is made to a family recipe. In this episode I visit their newest restaurant in RT Nagar, Bengaluru, where I catch up with Ramya Ravi, co-owner of the chain, who articulates that “their vision is to take Bengaluru’s donne biryani offering across the country!” And going by what I witnessed during the step by step making of their signature chicken donne biryani, and also what I tasted, they certainly seem to be on the right path to doing so.

I hope you enjoy this biryani making episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Channe Gowda moved to Bengaluru from his native place, Kunigal 10 years ago to eke out a living and supplement his family’s marginal farming income. He tried his hand at many a job and trade, barely managing to make ends meet. A couple of years ago, he set up a food cart in Banashankari, South Bengaluru on the back of non vegetarian recipes gleaned from his well wishers. This too met with limited success, it was at this point that he introduced a thatte keeping in mind the clientele in the area. And that was when things changed. His soft and spongy 15 rupee thatte idli served with butter and two delicious chutneys caught the attention of locals and demand grew to an extent that he gave up the non veg menu to only focus on the idli, vade and a single rice preparation. Unable to cope with the stream of customers, Channe Gowda eventually moved operations to a house in the area, from where he continues to serve hundreds of his now famous Kunigal thatte idli each day. 
From a street cart that would barely support him, he now provides livelihood to a team of fifteen! I set out this evening to meet this hard-working gent, and in the course of doing so, not only tasted his satisfying idlis, but also stumbled upon a flavourful tomato rice that he makes to an aromatic biryani recipe.

I hope you enjoy this inspiring tiffin thindi outing. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

About a year ago, I received a request from a family that had just opened a cloud kitchen to serve dishes made to family recipes handed down through generations. Much as their fare - a smorgasbord of meaty regional Karnataka delicacies seemed interesting - we couldn’t explore it further as we rarely ever cover cloud kitchens. Emboldened by the interest from customers, the family eventually set up a small eatery to seat all of 10 in the setback of a building on New Bel Road, North Bengaluru. And this of course, provided me with just the excuse to make the trek to Kutumba Kitchen, meet the family and taste some of the dishes that have earned this small enterprise quite a few fans in a short span of time.

https://maps.app.goo.gl/S6mKCLe5Y5uGq94u.summary: Kutumba Kitchen is a small, family-run eatery in North Bengaluru serving authentic Karnataka cuisine. The restaurant is known for its flavorful mutton chops, mutton palav, and chicken curry, all made with family recipes passed down through generations. The restaurant also serves Mangalore-style ghee roast and a variety of vegetarian options. The food is affordably priced and the portions are generous. The restaurant is popular among locals and visitors alike. The highlight of Kutumba Kitchen is its commitment to using fresh, local ingredients and its dedication to preserving traditional Karnataka recipes.

old bangalore café, banashankari, adukale foods, traditional foods of karnataka, karnataka café, bengaluru tiffin, snacks, bale yele idli, nuchinna unde, haalu mennasu saaru, majjige huli, ambode, gojju avalakki, tirupati ladoo, south bangalore, bangalore food trail, karnataka food tour, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

Recently, I was invited to inaugurate a store that, though small in the space it occupies for now, has a plan that’s grand enough to take the traditional flavours of Karnataka across Bengaluru and beyond. Out here, I tasted dishes like the haalu mennasu saaru, nuchinna unde, majjige huli, baale yele idli, gojju avalakki, and even their version of the Tirupati ladoo. An initiative of folks passionate about propagating hitherto unseen (in eateries) Karnataka delicacies, and Adukale Foods, I hope they are able to sustain and take forward their delicious vision. Do check them out at Banashankari, South Bengaluru.

best_dishes.name: Haalu Mennasu Saaru
best_dishes.summary: A peppery soup with milk that is surprisingly light and flavorful.  The pepper provides a warmth that builds gradually and is balanced by the sweetness of jaggery.

best_dishes.name: Nuchinunde
best_dishes.summary: Steamed lentil dumplings that are soft, pasty, and packed with the flavors of coconut, lentils, and a hint of pepper.

best_dishes.name: Majjige Huli
best_dishes.summary: A creamy and flavorful pumpkin curry that balances sweetness, spice, and nuttiness. The pumpkin melts in your mouth, releasing the delicious flavors of the huli.

best_dishes.name: Baale Yele Idli
best_dishes.summary: Idlis made with jackfruit leaves that impart a unique aroma and flavor to the dish. The idlis are served with a chutney that complements their distinct taste.

best_dishes.name: Gojju Avalakki
best_dishes.summary: A traditional Karnataka dish made with flattened rice (poha) and a tangy-spicy gojju. The dish features a perfect balance of sweet, spicy, and tangy flavors.

best_dishes.name: Tirupati Ladoo
best_dishes.summary: A sweet treat inspired by the famous Tirupati Ladoo, offering a rich and indulgent flavor.

best_dishes.name: Sakkare Pongal
best_dishes.summary: A sweet Pongal dish prepared in the form of a nedum (a type of steamed dumpling). It offers a comforting sweetness and a soft texture with varying levels of creaminess and bite.

best_dishes.name: Bele Kadubu
best_dishes.summary: A traditional Karnataka sweet made with rice flour and jaggery, known for its soft texture and delicate sweetness.

best_dishes.name: Tuppa Ladoo
best_dishes.summary: A rich and decadent ladoo made with clarified butter (ghee), offering a melt-in-your-mouth texture and an irresistible aroma.

This was an amazing afternoon! To catch up with nearly 150 food lovers - who had come not only from all parts of Bengaluru but also beyond - and learn from them first hand their special connection with our show. I’ve always known that our work connects with a wide cross section of viewers, but here for the first time, we were meeting them. Our youngest participant was just over two and the oldest, in their eighties. Truly felt blessed to meet each one of them over a delicious jolada rotti oota at one of my favourite Uttara Karnataka restaurants, the legendary 60-year-old Basaveshwar Khanavali, here in Koramangala, Bengaluru. Hope you enjoy this leisurely afternoon of conversation and catch-up over a sumptuous baale yele oota. 
Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

new imperial bakery, india’s oldest bakery, 143 year old bakery, kolar gold fields, kgf, karnataka, wood fired oven, veg puff, dil pasand, muffin, coconut biscuit, spicy cookies, vanilla cookies, old fashioned bakes, plum cake, bread, karnataka food trail, kolar food tour, near bengaluru, bangalore, small business, support small business, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

On a recent road drive through Kolar, we made a detour to Kolar Gold Fields, once famous across the world for its gold mines. The mines have long closed, and the town is now a pale shadow of its former glory. What has endured however is a bakery that first opened in 1880 and still continues to dispense its baked wares in an old school tradition that harks back 143 years! I met its fourth generation owner and also tasted many of the scrumptious treats on offer that are still popular with the inhabitants of this verdant town 70 kilometres from Bengaluru.

Hope you enjoy this one. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Note: I enjoyed most of the baked treats on offer. Standouts for me though were the veg puff, muffin (dilpasand), coconut biscuit, spicy cookies and plum cake.
Biscuits are priced at Rs. 30 for 100gm, the puffs and muffins at Rs. 13, and a loaf of bread, Rs. 30.

Sometime ago, I had put out a tweet asking for underrated dosae recommendations in Bengaluru. From the many suggestions I received, I picked this tiny shop in Jayanagar, South Bengaluru. What first drew me to Dose Of Davangere initially was the fact that they still roast the dosae over a wood-fired stove, a cooking tradition that is fast disappearing in cities. And their commitment to procuring unsalted village butter from Davanagere. All in all, I was rewarded with the best expression of a Davanagere dosae that I have tasted in Bengaluru thus far. If you love your butter drenched dosae, especially the original Davanagere kind, this is a must-visit! In fact, I would go as far as endorsing it as a must-try dosae when here in namma ooru!

Amongst the many culinary traditions that prevail in this state, an interesting one is that of Maratha-Karnataka fare. A cuisine that took birth a few hundred years ago when Marathas migrated to Karnataka and settled into the local culture and practices of the land. Over time, their food evolved to assimilate local produce and ingredients. Many of the ‘military’ eateries in and around Bengaluru trace their roots to this style of cooking, although the offerings of some have morphed beyond recognition. To find examples of this unique fare that is comparatively true to its origin, one has to travel a bit out of the city. Like this 70-year-old eating house that we discovered in Malur, a town located 50 kilometres from Bengaluru. Where rustic meaty preparations are cooked with home made masalas over wood-fired stoves.

Hope you enjoy this lunch at Venkob Rao Mess. Take Care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Rohan Bopanna Master Blend.name: Rohan Bopanna Master Blend
Rohan Bopanna Master Blend.summary: A blend of Arabica beans from Rohan Bopanna's estate in Madapur, Coorg. The blend includes beans processed using both pulp sunrise and washed methods, resulting in a mellow coffee with a slightly heavier body.

Whiskey Barrel-Aged Coffee.name: Whiskey Barrel-Aged Coffee
Whiskey Barrel-Aged Coffee.summary: A blend of Arabica and Robusta coffee beans aged in whiskey barrels for a few months. This aging process imparts flavors from the whiskey cask to the coffee, creating a unique and flavorful brew.

Clarified Cappuccino.name: Clarified Cappuccino
Clarified Cappuccino.summary: A unique take on the classic cappuccino. This drink is made by clarifying a regular cappuccino using an age-old technique from the bar industry. The result is a clear coffee drink with all the caffeine but none of the solids from the milk. It is flavored with a hint of rosemary.

Robusta with Homemade Yeast Fermentation.name: Robusta with Homemade Yeast Fermentation
Robusta with Homemade Yeast Fermentation.summary: This coffee showcases the often-neglected Robusta bean. It undergoes a specialized processing method using homemade yeast for fermentation, which enhances its complexity and brings out flavors reminiscent of Arabica coffee.

It was wonderful to meet tennis ace, our very own Bengaluru boy, Rohan Bopanna, soon after his return from Wimbledon and being recently ranked World No. 7 for the second time in a decade. However, his constant travel on the circuit has meant that there are aspects of namma ooru that he hasn’t been able to explore yet, including Mavalli Tiffin Rooms in Lalbagh. And so we took it upon ourselves to introduce this icon to a Bengaluru tiffin legend over a leisurely, indulgent-breakfast conversation where we also caught a glimpse of his passion for coffee, and his role as the ambassador for the World Coffee Conference, to be held in India for the first time in our city in September.

Hope you enjoy this tiffin talk. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

#ctr #mtr #vidyarthibhavan 

most popular masala dosas in bangalore, masala dosae, tiffin, ctr, mtr, mavalli tiffin rooms, lalbagh, vidyarthi bhavan, basavanagudi, bengaluru, bangalore

When it comes to the ubiquitous masala dosae here in Bengaluru, everyone has an opinion, actually many opinions, and clear favourites. Stuck at home during the recent lockdown, I couldn’t help but reminisce tasting three of Bengaluru’s most popular versions, and put together a special compilation for you, highlights of the CTR, MTR (Mavalli Tiffin Room, Lalbagh) and Vidyarthi Bhavan masala dosae from Gourmet On The Road.

Hope you enjoy this short and scrumptious bonus video; take care, stay safe and happy eating! 

CTR Benne Masala Dosa
This butter-drenched gold-hued dose is blessed with the perfect gentle crackle. On the palate, one tastes the lushness of the homemade butter that envelopes every bite of the dose, the palya and the chutney with its delicious veil. If you need one reason to visit CTR, this would be it.
Rs. 57 (usd 0.8)
10/10

MTR MASALA DOSA
The dosa here is iconic and never disappoints. Made with a blend of three rice varieties, including two red rice varieties that lend a toasty colour tone, the dose is crisp outside and soft within. The palya is seasoned just right. 
Rs. 90 (usd 1.3)
10

Vidyarthi Bhavan Masala Dosa
If you need one reason to visit Vidyarthji Bhavan, this would be it. A dose that’s crisp and lacey in parts, soft and fluffy in others, and hides within its single fold a creamy potato palya. The chutney is spicy and vivacious, a bold complement to the gentle flavours of the dose and palya.
Rs. 53 (usd 0.7) 
10/10

#VegetarianBreakfast #BestRestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Full Breakfast at MTR (Mavalli Tiffin Rooms) Restaurant, Lalbagh Road, Bengaluru, nearly 100-Years Old Eatery, Vegetarian Food, Bengaluru’s Most Popular Restaurant, Bengaluru's Most Popular Breakfast Spot, Rice Idli, Medu Vada, Rava Idli, Masala Dosa, Kesari Bath, Khara Bath, Chandrahara, Damroot, Dumrot, Badam Halwa,

This nearly-100-year-old establishment is chock full with customers every hour of the day when they are open. With a loyal fan following that values its adherence to age-old recipes and traditions to serve up consistent, wholesome South Indian fare, Mavalli Tiffin Rooms on Lalbagh Road is perhaps Bengaluru’s most popular breakfast destination.  

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna drops in for a full breakfast and tastes 11 must-try dishes from this timeless eatery’s repertoire. He begins with a kitchen tour with VIkram Maiya, Managing Partner, MTR before sitting down to a sumptuous meal that includes amongst others, a dessert creation that’s the restaurant founder’s ode to French pastry. Enjoy!

RICE IDLI
The idlis are soft and a hot, buttery treat when had with the ghee. The coriander in the idli adds to its flavour. The idli dissolves in the mouth when immersed in the nourishingly thick sambar.
rs. 33 (usd 0.5)
8.5 

MEDU VADA
The vada exhibits a textbook crunch as it yields to the bite! Delicious with the sambar and comes alive with the spicy kick of the chutney. 
Rs. 44 (usd 0.6)
8

RAVA IDLI
Made of roasted semolina, yoghurt and speckled with fresh coriander, toasted cashews, and lentils, the rava idli makes for a hearty breakfast. The creamy potato sagu is a flavourful accompaniment to the rava idli.
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
10

KHARA BATH 
Fortified with carrots, slivers of green chilli and crested with a tomato slice, the khara bath is soft and crumbly, yet holds itself together. The pudina chutney helps tone down the tart notes of the lime and tomato. 
Rs. 62 (usd 0.9)
8

KESARI BATH
This breakfast treat glistens with the lushness of ghee. Embellished with toasted raisins and nuts, the kesari bath here is rich in its texture owing to the shavige (rice vermicelli) and semolina mix. 
Rs. 57 (usd 0.8)
9

MASALA DOSA
The dosa here is iconic and never disappoints. Made with a blend of three rice varieties, including two red rice varieties that lend a toasty colour tone, the dose is crisp outside and soft within. The palya is seasoned just right. Rs. 90 (usd 1.3)
10

PUDI DOSA
It’s soft, fluffy and big on flavours. You can taste the grainy crunch of lentils, the sharp, spicy notes of the chilli and the undertones of asafoetida. Tame its aggression with the palya and coconut chutney. 
Rs. 95 (usd 1.3)
8

DAMROOT 
Made of shredded pumpkin, semolina, raisins, nuts and tonnes of ghee, this MTR sweet is scented with cardamom. 
Rs. 47 (usd 0.6)
8.5

BADAM HALWA
You can ‘almost’ drink this lush, buttery, silken almond halwa enriched with ghee and flecks of saffron. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
10

CHANDRAHARA 
MTR’s ode to French pastry, this ‘sugary-sweet’ pastry is fried in pure ghee, garnished with almond slivers and doused with a khova (milk solids) syrup. 
Rs. 67 (usd 0.9)
8

best_dishes.name: RICE IDLI
best_dishes.summary: The idlis are soft and a hot, buttery treat when had with the ghee. The coriander in the idli adds to its flavour. The idli dissolves in the mouth when immersed in the nourishingly thick sambar.

best_dishes.name: MEDU VADA
best_dishes.summary: The vada exhibits a textbook crunch as it yields to the bite! Delicious with the sambar and comes alive with the spicy kick of the chutney.

best_dishes.name: RAVA IDLI
best_dishes.summary: Made of roasted semolina, yoghurt and speckled with fresh coriander, toasted cashews, and lentils, the rava idli makes for a hearty breakfast. The creamy potato sagu is a flavourful accompaniment to the rava idli.

best_dishes.name: KHARA BATH
best_dishes.summary: Fortified with carrots, slivers of green chilli and crested with a tomato slice, the khara bath is soft and crumbly, yet holds itself together. The pudina chutney helps tone down the tart notes of the lime and tomato.

best_dishes.name: KESARI BATH
best_dishes.summary: This breakfast treat glistens with the lushness of ghee. Embellished with toasted raisins and nuts, the kesari bath here is rich in its texture owing to the shavige (rice vermicelli) and semolina mix.

best_dishes.name: MASALA DOSA
best_dishes.summary: The dosa here is iconic and never disappoints. Made with a blend of three rice varieties, including two red rice varieties that lend a toasty colour tone, the dose is crisp outside and soft within. The palya is seasoned just right.

best_dishes.name: PUDI DOSA
best_dishes.summary: It’s soft, fluffy and big on flavours. You can taste the grainy crunch of lentils, the sharp, spicy notes of the chilli and the undertones of asafoetida. Tame its aggression with the palya and coconut chutney.

best_dishes.name: DAMROOT
best_dishes.summary: Made of shredded pumpkin, semolina, raisins, nuts and tonnes of ghee, this MTR sweet is scented with cardamom.

best_dishes.name: BADAM HALWA
best_dishes.summary: You can ‘almost’ drink this lush, buttery, silken almond halwa enriched with ghee and flecks of saffron.

best_dishes.name: CHANDRAHARA
best_dishes.summary: MTR’s ode to French pastry, this ‘sugary-sweet’ pastry is fried in pure ghee, garnished with almond slivers and doused with a khova (milk solids) syrup.

Over the last few months, I had received numerous requests from our viewers to visit Hotel Aditya in Mahalaxmipuram, a eatery that in just over 12 years has managed to create for its local non vegetarian fare the sort of fan loyalty that some of Bengaluru’s revered culinary institutions have taken multiple decades to garner. The people behind the eatery are extremely low profile, preferring to let their food do the talking, and therefore reluctant to let cameras in. Which is also why you may not have seen a single in depth video or feature on the place thus far. 

We managed to get our cameras not only into the restaurant, but also deep in the kitchen where we took an in-depth look at the making of some of their iconic dishes, from the meaty curries to the terrific biryanis and fries. The best part we found at Hotel Aditya, not only is the food great, but so is the ambience that it is served in. Making it one of the very few local style non vegetarian restaurants where you can savour your meal in peace and air conditioned comfort too.

If you've been putting off tasting some great naati oota because of concerns of ambience and crowd, Hotel Aditya is certainly the place to dive into local non veg cuisine. Hope you enjoy this watch. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Thriveni and Narayana Bairy’s SLV Coffee Thindi sits in a distant suburb of South Bengaluru. But in the nine years that it’s been around, this darshini style eatery has garnered quite the reputation amongst locals for its soft idlis, part of a short menu of only five or six tasty tiffin dishes that are personally prepared and served with much care and attention by the husband-wife duo. On weekends, their children chip in too. The fare served also draws from Narayan’s experience at some fabled eateries where he first worked when he came to Bengaluru from Kundapura 25 years ago, Do taste their delicious tiffin thindi and support this hard working family’s business.

Known for their incredibly soft idlis, this small family business has been serving up delicious and hygienic South Indian tiffin for the past nine years. The limited menu features only a handful of items, all made with care and attention to detail. Regulars rave about the idlis and chutney, as well as the vadas, khara bath, kesari bath, and avalakki bath. The warm and welcoming atmosphere, coupled with the tasty food, make SLV Coffee Thindi a must-visit for anyone looking for a satisfying and affordable meal. Don't miss out on the opportunity to support this local gem and experience the true taste of South Indian hospitality. 

Uniqueness: The unique selling point of SLV Coffee Thindi is the exceptional softness of their idlis, which stems from a secret recipe perfected over years of experience.

Jayaramu was working in the food and beverage department of a hotel in Mysuru when he lost his job during the pandemic. Left with no recourse to earn a living, he began a sugarcane juice stall, but with a twist. Given his experience in mixing cocktails and mocktails in his previous job, he tried crushing seasonal, fresh fruits and herbs in the cane to create an interesting, healthy yet refreshingly delicious take on the humble sugarcane juice. I visited Ambaari Juice stall a few weeks ago and tasted a bevy of his offerings - malabar plum, mango, mixed fruit, pomegranate, muskmelon, et al - in sugar cane juice. Definitely something to try when you are in the palace city next.

Do support enterprising small entrepreneurs like Jayaramu who in the course of earning a livelihood are also bringing something deliciously different. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating.

Note: plain sugarcane juice with mint, lime, ginger is priced at Rs. 30, the fresh fruit and sugarcane juices are priced Rs. 60 upwards. My top picks were plain, jamun and mango amongst others.

Sisters Chandrakala and Shoba were running a successful catering business which was unfortunately brought down by the pandemic. They lay low for 27 months before bouncing back with a small eatery to serve up Andhra delicacies made to the recipes of their parents and grandparents. Curryce Andhra Bhojanam, located in RT Nagar, North Bengaluru is only four tables large, but in my opinion, the food that they serve is destined for bigger things ahead. Join me in this homely episode where I taste a full-fledged veg bhojanam, kodi vepudu, gongura chicken royulu roast and a memorable Hyderabadi style biryani.

https://goo.gl/maps/dNcegdxHUyZFcKyy9.summary: This restaurant is run by two sisters, Chandrakala and Shoba, who started it after their catering business was impacted by the pandemic. They serve authentic Andhra food, using recipes passed down from their parents and grandparents. The food is delicious and the prices are reasonable. The restaurant is small, with only four tables, but the food is definitely worth trying.  The highlight of the restaurant is that it is run by a family passionate about preserving its culinary legacy through authentic Andhra recipes.

A Gourmet On The Road episode that’s dearest to me is the one where I shared a meal with ‘namma priyaru’, Karnataka Ratna Puneeth Rajkumar. How one wishes things had turned out differently, but alas! He wore Karnataka on his sleeve, and part of his vision was to promote young talent in Kannada cinema, a role that is now being bravely carried forward by his wife, Ashwini Puneeth Rajkumar. And when I recently received a call from her inviting me to a conversation on Aachar & Co., a film made by a near-all-women-team led by Sindhu Sreenivasa Murthy, somewhere, I felt this would be an apt continuation of my conversation with Appu Sir. 
We met over a delicious South Canara lunch at New Modern Hotel, an appropriate venue given the film’s setting in Bengaluru of the sixties. We discussed the film, which promises to be a witty family entertainer, rich in its cinematic value, food, pickles, family, a lot more… and also basked in the warming memory of our dearest Appu, Puneeth Rajkumar.

I am looking forward to watching the film, you should too. Hope you enjoy this special conversation. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

support local eateries, takeaway meal, new modern hotel, lockdown, new modern hotel, basavangudi, south bangalore, traditional vegetarian food in bangalore, south canara food, traditional vegetarian food, thatte idli, set dosa, khara bath, kesari bath, rice rasam, rice sambar, anna saaru, lunch, old world restaurant, traditional eatery, bangalore, bengaluru

Mr Padmanabha Adiga, has seen famines, plagues, political unrest and other disruptions in the 60 years he has helmed this old Bengaluru institution, New Modern Hotel, but says the current situation is something else altogether! An optimist though, he and his sons prepare to do what it takes to tide this South Canara vegetarian eatery through. Inspiration aside, I also take away a simple but nourishing anna-saaru meal in addition to some of their popular tiffins and sweets. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care, stay safe and happy eating.
Note: This episode was first released in May 2020 and is being rerun to support the eatery and others like this establishment that need help in the current situation. Please do support local eateries.

Set Dose
There’s a hint of tart sweetness in these soft, fluffy dose that are perfectly suited for takeaway. With the nourishing sambar, vegetable saagu and chutney, it makes for a wholesome light meal. 
Rs. 48 (usd 0.6) 

Thatte Idli
Soft and porous, the thatte idli breaks under its own weight. The sambar, pleasing to the palate with its sweet acidity is perfectly suited to impregnate the idli with its mildly spicy fervour. 
Rs. 29 (usd 0.4) 

Khara Bath
As you place the khara bath in your mouth, the savoury aroma of the onion is what you taste first, followed by the moist crunch of the tomato and the grainy bite of fresh coconut. Spice things up with the chutney. 
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) 

Kesari Bath
Redolent in the flavour of cloves, this isn't a kesari bath that’s dripping in ghee. Which makes for a tasty indulgence minus the guilt.
Rs. 27 (usd 0.4) 

Anna Sambar
A sambar rich in lentils and grated coconut, made well, the vegetable, ladies finger, still has its crunch intact. 
Rs. 43 (usd 0.6) 

Anna Saaru
The tomato plays a dual role in this pleasing South Canara tilli saaru, more popularly known as tomato rasama here in Bengaluru. The tomatoes are the foundation of this tart broth, and also offer a fruity crunch in the diced tomato that is perhaps added when the rasam is near cooked. 
Rs. 43 (usd 0.6) 

Mysore Pak
Rich in ghee, the fresh mysore pak crumbles under its own weight. When you place it in the mouth, it dissolves into a lush, buttery pool of deliciousness.
Rs. 18 (usd ) per piece 

Jehangir
Crisp, crunch and moist, this well-made old-fashioned mithai is a popular sweet at NMH.
Rs. 18 (usd ) per piece

The pandemic was a difficult time for Mahi and her husband Majeed. Their little son fell seriously ill and to nurse him back to health, this young couple had to borrow a fair bit of money. However soon thereafter Mahi lost her job. Left with no recourse, she turned to her love for cooking and opened a small shop near her home in Akshayanagar, a distant suburb in South Bengaluru, where she serves Lucknowi biryani and kebabs made to her grandmother’s recipe at home. There’s only a table to seat four and a few regulars in the area who order takeaways. But business has been tough, and the young couple have been having a tough time trying to make ends meet and repay their loans. I received an appeal from Mahi, and after making discreet enquiries, visited them for a meal. While the tiny size of the shop, it’s no more than a kiosk, with a table outside to seat four, did surprise me, what floored me completely was the taste of the fare that is served out of Biryani Delicacy. I will definitely return for the biryani and the kebabs. And needless to say, you should visit too. To savour a unique Lucknow style biryani that has been tweaked a bit to suit Bengaluru’s palate, and to also support a deserving small enterprise.

Hope you enjoy this episode. Tackle care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

https://goo.gl/maps/xcrZ1xpCUaMxDBZS7.summary: This video features Biryani Delicacy, a small biryani shop in Akshayanagar, South Bengaluru, run by Mahi, a Lucknow native.  The shop is known for its unique Lucknowi biryani and kebabs made using Mahi’s grandmother's recipes. The standout dish is the Mutton Biryani, praised for its smoky flavor and tender mutton. Other must-tries include the Galouti Kebab, known for its melt-in-your-mouth texture, and the Shami Kebab. The video highlights Mahi’s inspiring story of starting the business after facing job loss and personal challenges during the pandemic. The small size of the shop adds to its charm, offering a cozy and intimate dining experience. Overall, Biryani Delicacy is a hidden gem for authentic Lucknowi cuisine in Bengaluru.  What makes this restaurant unique is that they make the biryani in the traditional Lucknowi style using a specific type of rice and a paste made from fried onions.

It had been a while since I visited South Canara, and so when a craving for a good Mangalorean meal hit me, I found my way to this tiny eatery that’s almost hidden in a bylane of Malleshwaram. Run by Ravi Shetty, an affable native of Kundapura who has been cooking since the age of 17, Karavali Lunch Home offers a delicious smorgasbord of coastal flavours from Dakshina Kannada featuring unique dishes like the country chicken uppu koli, that has earned it loyal patrons in its 15 years of existence. What also finds favour here is the freshness of the seafood that Ravi procures each day. and also their pocket friendly fish thaalis that are priced upwards of Rs. 140.

If you are craving authentic flavours of kudla, check them out. Hope you enjoy this episode.  Take care. Stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

sarposh experience kashmir, sarposh restaurant and tea room, bakery, wazwan, authentic kashmiri cuisine, kashmiri food, tabak maaz, seekh kebab, dani phol, meith maaz, rogan josh, marchewangan kormeh, ristae, goshtabae, wazzeh palak, razmah dal, nadur yakhin, kong kahwe, maaz traem, sarposh restaurant, sarposh indiranagar, sarposh foods, sarposh owner, indiranagar, bengaluru, bangalore, inspiring story, lady entrepreneur, small business, support small business, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

My meal at Sarposh was an eye opener into the traditions of true Kashmiri cuisine that restaurateur Azmat Ali Mir seeks to showcase. In ingredients that she procures from the valley, to the brigade of wazas (cooks) from Srinagar who have made Bengaluru their home! To enjoy a meal here, park aside all notions you may have of the cuisine based on the odd so-called Kashmiri dish you may have tasted on a menu here and there. For the fare here is anything but that.
I opted for the maaz traem, a traditional celebratory meal and what followed was a procession of 12 dishes. From the initial methi maaz, soft and velvety tripe, served on a bed of rice, to a ghee-fried tabak maaz (ribs), dani phol (stewed lamb shanks) and a finely minced seekh kebab, to the hearty mains, rogan josh, the subtly flavoured sort you have never eaten before, rista (juicy meatballs), a comforting palak and razmah dal, creamy nadur (lotus stem) yakhni, marchewangan korma, the only searingly spicy dish of the lot, and gushtaba (meatballs stewed in yoghurt and dried mint), each preparation I found exquisite and subtly distinct in its flavour and taste. 
If you’re looking to try wazwan fare true to its roots, far removed from the ginger-garlic-chilli-cream infused heavy dishes that get passed off as Kashmiri elsewhere, definitely check out Sarposh restaurant and tea room in Bengaluru. 

Hope you enjoy part two of my Sarposh outing. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

When Azmat Ali Mir moved from Srinagar to Bengaluru after marriage, she yearned for authentic Kashmiri food, but “there was none to be found”, she says. A casual idea of staging a Kashmiri pop-up for a few friends ‘avalanched’ into a dinner for 1000 guests, compelling her to fly in wazas (Kashmiri cooks) to prepare the meal. Encouraged by the response, and her husband Azeem Syed, she embarked on setting up a space that sought to not only celebrate true Kashmiri cuisine, but also its culture and traditions. Thus was born Sarposh restaurant and tea room in Indiranagar, Bengaluru. Needless to say, the cooks (wazas) stayed back. I visited her for lunch one afternoon and was blown away by the sheer depth of cuisine and culture that this young entrepreneur seeks to showcase in her cozy dining space, which also offers a fascinating insight into the traditions of her land in its decor and artifacts. What was intended as a typical review lunch turned into an engrossing conversation with Azmat and her team, thereby resulting in this rare two-part Gourmet On The Road episode. Hope you enjoy part one.

A couple of years ago, I visited a fledgling highway eatery that was trying to find its feet in the aftermath of the lockdown. I enjoyed my meal there and our ensuing video prompted many of you to visit Malgudi Mylari Mane, Nelamangala. Things have improved for them to such an extent that they have recently opened their second restaurant, right here in Bengaluru. I had to check it out, and find out happily so, that the food still retains its delicious, rustic appeal, and is a wonderful complement to an age-old Mysore inspired dosae. Wonderful to see small businesses succeed. Check them out.

https://goo.gl/maps/4ShsEPMHdoCF8ozP7.summary: Kripal Amanna revisits Malgudi Mylari Mane, two years after their first encounter, this time at their new location in Koramangala, Bengaluru. He finds the same delicious and rustic food, a testament to the restaurant’s success since its highway eatery days. The video highlights the unique Mylari Dosae, a soft and flaky dosa inspired by a Mysore classic, best enjoyed with the restaurant’s flavorful curries. Kripal recommends the tender and juicy Mutton Chops Dry, the flavorful Mutton Palav with its aromatic spices, and the Nati Koli Pepper Fry with its perfectly cooked country chicken. He concludes that Malgudi Mylari Mane, with its commitment to quality meat and traditional recipes, is a must-visit for those seeking authentic Karnataka cuisine.

Ranganatha was only in the fifth grade when he began assisting his brother-in-law at his chat cart after school. Soon, his interest in making chaat overtook any academic inclinations and after completing seventh grade, he gave up school. Soon, his family joined in too, his father giving up his profession as an automotive mechanic, his mother, and much later, his wife, assisting in preparing the masalas, chutneys, etc. at home. Over the last two decades or so, the cart has made way to a tiny shop and Sri Ranganatha Chats Corner has emerged as a favourite chaat spot in the neighbourhood, not only for their homestyle, simple preparations, but also the friendliness with which they interact with customers, many who have been tasting their fare over years.

Meet them when you’re in Malleshwaram next, and do your best to support small neighbourhood enterprises like these. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Masala Puri.summary: A quintessential Bengaluru street food dish with crushed puri, potatoes, chutneys, and a blend of spices. It offers a medley of flavors and textures, from the creamy peas to the crispy boondi and savory onions.

Dahi Puri.summary: Dahi Puri features crispy puris filled with potatoes, chutneys, and yogurt. It is known for its balanced sweet, spicy, and tangy flavors, making it a popular chaat choice.

Bhel Puri.summary: A light and refreshing chaat, Bhel Puri combines puffed rice, sev, onions, potatoes, and chutneys. It offers a satisfying crunch and a blend of sweet, tangy, and spicy tastes.

Pani Puri.summary: Pani Puri consists of crispy puris filled with a mixture of flavored water, potatoes, and chutneys. It delivers a burst of flavors with every bite, ranging from tangy and spicy to sweet and minty.

Chips Masala.summary: Chips Masala is a simple yet flavorful snack made with crispy chips tossed in a blend of spices and chutneys. It's a perfect combination of crunchy texture and savory flavors.

Boti Masala.summary: A unique chaat offering, Boti Masala is made with a special type of boti (cooked chickpeas) combined with a flavorful masala blend. It offers a distinct taste and texture that sets it apart from other chaat varieties.

https://goo.gl/maps/B2iEuEAF2eCY56pN8.summary: Sri Ranganatha Chats Corner in Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, is a beloved street food stall known for its simple, homestyle chaat preparations. Run by a family passionate about serving delicious and affordable food, this small eatery has become a neighborhood favorite over the last two decades. The highlight of Sri Ranganatha Chats Corner is their use of family recipes, passed down through generations, which contribute to the unique and authentic flavors of their dishes. The stall's friendly atmosphere and commitment to quality have earned them a loyal customer base, making it a must-visit for anyone seeking a taste of authentic Bengaluru street food.

Sumathi was content being a homemaker, when her husband Charles, a software engineer, encouraged her to open a small eatery given her passion for cooking. She began one and ran it for a few months, when tragedy struck, and her husband was no more. Left with no recourse to fend for her three children and herself, Sumathi Charles ploughed her entire savings into setting up a modest eatery serving Tamil Nadu style vegetarian tiffin and meals. I visit The Madhras Kitchen early one evening and leave thoroughly impressed with most of the dishes I taste. I have no doubt that if this eatery remains true to its cuisine philosophy, it will certainly emerge as a must-eat-at place on Bengaluru’s culinary trail. Located in the heart of Bengaluru on Castle Street, this clean, hygienic eatery is certainly worthy of more than one visit. Do taste their delicious fare, and in doing so, support yet another deserving small business.

Ask most locals in Chikmagalur where they go for their dosae fix, and chances are they will mention this eatery, also one of coffee town’s earliest. Over the last 63 years, Town Canteen, that sits on the edge of IG Road, has emerged as the place to go for the scrumptiously crisp, buttery, benne masala dosae, chased de rigueur with soft, cardamom sugar syrup soaked gulab jamuns, and their special blend filter coffee. Although I tasted these two years ago, I couldn’t miss an encore when we were filming a Gourmet On The Road series in coffee town a few weeks ago.

A definite must-try when in Chikkamagaluru. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Ganesh may not speak or hear, but he certainly knows the pulse of his customers when it comes to preparing and serving them fresh teas, each one brimming with the goodness of natural ingredients. I am told he began this enterprise when he lost his father owing to some ailment that couldn’t be cured. Ganesh took it upon himself to research and prepare a variety of teas that he believed could help his customers stay healthy and restore them from day to day health niggles. It was inspiring to watch this one-man-army go about his work serving the community when I dropped in unannounced at his small store one evening.

Please do support this small business and share this video to encourage differently abled entrepreneurs like Ganesh who notwithstanding their challenges  are bravely standing on their own, and are in many ways an inspiration to society.

Hope you enjoy this watch. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!


Note: Each tea dispensed by Ganesh is unique. Whilst some of them may taste a bit medicinal, they are extremely beneficial to one’s health, say regulars. My favourites were green tea, lemon tea and jaggery tea. Teas are priced upwards of Rs. 20.

When Dr Gani Ganeshwar was studying medicine in Mangalore, he fell in love with the port city’s iconic Ideal Ice Creams and Pabba’s. Over the years of studying medicine, he consumed many of their creations and pondered over the possibility of bringing these to Bengaluru. Nearly a year ago, the thought finally came to fruition when this enterprising doctor began Scoops of Mangalore, where Ideal ice creams are not only sold in retail packs, but also fashioned into the most popular Mangalore Gadbad’s, Tiramisu’s, Parfaits and the like. https://goo.gl/maps/y84RACjtZ81R6Y1z8.summary: Dr. Gani Ganeshwar, a former medical student with a passion for Mangalore's iconic Ideal Ice Creams, has brought the taste of the coast to Bengaluru with Scoops of Mangalore. This small business serves up classic Mangalore Gadbads, Tiramisu, and Parfaits using authentic Ideal ice creams. Kripal Amanna from Food Lovers TV visits the shop to try out their offerings, including the Old School Gadbad, Special Gadbad, and Tiramisu. He finds the Old School Gadbad to be a delightful mix of textures and flavors, highlighting the strawberry and raspberry jelly. While the Special Gadbad is tasty, it doesn't quite live up to the hype, with the flavors blending together a bit too much. The Tiramisu is a coffee and chocolate lover's delight, with a satisfying mix of ice cream, cream, and brownie pieces.  Overall, Scoops of Mangalore offers a taste of Mangalore in Bengaluru, with their Old School Gadbad being a must-try for its simple yet satisfying flavors.

When Narasimha Murthy’s livelihood as a masala salesman was disrupted owing to covid, he set up a tiny eatery serving seafood. Thrice, but each one failed. As a last resort, he approached Karnataka Fisheries Development Corporation, and they suggested he explore the model of a seafood mobile canteen that he set up a couple of years ago. Murthy still keeps his day job, selling spice mix packets throughout Bengaluru whilst his wife, Sunanda cleans the fish and prepares the masala throughout the day. And in the evening, they drive their seafood fry truck to Rajajinagar, where this hard working couple cook, and serve the neighbourhood. The fish that they serve is fresh, sourced from KFDC each day, and their fries, delicious as I discovered when I paid them an impromptu visit a few weeks ago.

I salute their work ethic, and hope many of you will be inspired to support this small enterprise. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

I first discovered The Vintage in Chikmagalur a couple of years ago when Sree and I, having emerged from the pandemic, were looking to take a break in a safe environment. This villa homestay set in an orchard came recommended. Since then, we have returned twice again to the endearing hospitality of its owner, Charles Baptist, who personally leaves no stone unturned to ensure his guests enjoy a refreshing Chikmaglur experience. On this visit to film a Gourmet On The Road series in coffee town, we camped here and left only after partaking a delicious Malenadu brunch, highlights of which included a tender jackfruit curry, tasty Malnad chicken, kadak fish fry and a surprising bottle gourd payasa. Definitely a spot to consider when you’re planning your next weekend break.

I first came across this 85-year-old coffee institution when I visited Chikmagalur over two years ago. Since then, their Grand Aroma blend has been a staple in our coffee shelf at home. On this visit though, I was pleasantly surprised to find that not only is this heritage coffee roasting and blending house holding on to its traditional blends, but has since made notable strides in creating an assortment of coffee varieties to suit every palate. If you’re visiting Chikkamagaluru, a visit to this old-school coffee retail shop is a must. And when there, do chat up with the Setty brothers and request to take a peek at the making of some of their blends.

Grand Aroma.summary: A blend of coffee with a strong aroma that lasts for months. It's their signature blend and a staple for coffee lovers.

Made in Chikmagalur.summary: A blend that represents the traditional taste of Chikmagalur coffee. It's known for its authentic flavor.

High Voltage.summary: A strong coffee blend with 40% chicory, perfect for those who prefer a bolder and more intense flavor.

90/10 Blend.summary: A blend with 90% coffee and 10% chicory, offering a smoother and more delicate flavor profile.

Peaberry Coffee.summary: A unique coffee made from peaberry beans, which are round instead of the usual twin beans. It's known for its exceptional quality and aroma.

Mysore Nuggets.summary: A premium blend made from AAA Arabica coffee beans. Its light roast makes it perfect for black coffee.

Italian Roast.summary: A dark roast coffee with smoky notes, perfect for those who enjoy a bolder and more intense espresso.

Happy Day.summary: A blend with 80% Arabica and 20% Robusta beans. Its caramel notes make it ideal for milk-based coffee preparations.

Monkey Coffee.summary: A rare and expensive coffee made from beans that have been digested and naturally fermented by monkeys.  It is known for its unique flavor profile.

When Vani, a dietician, and her husband, Harsha, a IT professional, chanced upon an ice cream churner at an exhibition in Bengaluru, they saw in it an opportunity bring to fruition their plans of creating 100% natural ice creams, made only with fresh fruits and nuts, sans any artificial flavours, colours or additives. A trip to Italy to learn the art of making gelato, low fat ice creams, followed by months of honing recipes at home, led to the birth of their ice cream parlour, Churn in a leafy bylane of RMV 2nd Stage. The ice creams here are made fresh everyday using only seasonal ingredients. Although Churn has its share of loyal patrons in and around the neighbourhood, their ice creams are perhaps unknown to most of Bengaluru. I visit Churn to meet the friendly couple, learn the art of making gelato and taste every flavour that’s in the store.

https://goo.gl/maps/tjwFoqf6Lfi9hAW57.summary: Churn, located in RMV 2nd Stage, Bengaluru, is a hidden gem that serves 100% natural, handmade ice creams and gelatos. The owners, Vani and Harsha, are passionate about using only fresh, seasonal ingredients, with no artificial flavors, colors, or preservatives. Vani, a dietitian, ensures that the gelatos are not only delicious but also relatively low in fat and sugar. They make everything from scratch, including their own nut butters, Nutella (called 'Jandaya'), and even the brownies in their Dark Chocolate Brownie gelato.  What sets Churn apart is its commitment to quality and using natural ingredients. They make their own nut butters, caramels, and even Nutella in-house. The gelatos are made fresh daily and have a shelf life of only one week. They even offer unique flavors like Wood Apple and Black Grape, showcasing the diversity of Indian ingredients.  The highlight of Churn is their dedication to using natural ingredients and making everything from scratch. This dedication is evident in the taste and quality of their ice creams and makes Churn a must-visit for anyone looking for authentic and delicious gelatos in Bengaluru.

https://goo.gl/maps/76eVHEjKFU5y4UWu8.summary: Tasty World Food Factory in Chikmagalur offers a unique experience by allowing visitors to witness the hygienic production of traditional Karnataka snacks and sweets. They provide an air-conditioned viewing gallery where you can see the making of various snacks like boondi, chakli, murukku, and their signature soft gulab jamun. The highlight is their commitment to quality, using fresh ingredients and traditional recipes. They have a cafe where you can relish their freshly made snacks and sweets, with interesting concoctions like chocolate-coated murukku with chutney and dahi chaat.  The must-try is their melt-in-your-mouth gulab jamun. Tasty World Food Factory is a must-visit for anyone looking to savor authentic Karnataka snacks and sweets in a hygienic and welcoming environment.

world of coffee, chikmagalur, chikkamagaluru, coffee experience zone, coffee shop, filter coffee, artisan coffees, coffee tours, coffee roasting, coffee estate, 4d coffee, coffee tour, coffee tasting, civet coffee, karnataka food tour, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food


It is said that coffee first found its way into India through a Sufi saint, Baba Budan who, having smuggled seven coffee beans from Arabia in his beard, planted these in the hills around Chikkamagaluru in the late 17th century. Fitting therefore that this coffee town is also home to a unique coffee store that offers customers an immersive walk through the history, brewing and experiential tasting of coffee. I visited World Of Coffee on a recent trip and tasted a host of coffee - new age artisan varieties like pineapple fermented, honey infused, foraged civet coffees, and traditional filter coffee. When in Chikmagalur, you must explore coffee and this store is a great place to start.

Hope you enjoy this heady brew of an episode. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Tasting:
Each of the coffees tasted left a mark. My favourites though, in descending order of preference - civet coffee, filter coffee, cold brew, fruit and honey infused coffee. And to taste coffee in a dessert form, the panna cotta is highly recommended.

The coffee panna cotta is priced at Rs. 170, and the artisan coffees around Rs. 170.

Filter Coffee.summary: A traditional South Indian filter coffee, typically made with a blend of coffee beans and chicory. It is strong and aromatic.

Cold Brew.summary: Coffee that is brewed by steeping coffee grounds in cold water for an extended period. This results in a coffee that is less acidic and more refreshing.

Pineapple Fermented Coffee.summary: This coffee is made by fermenting coffee beans with pineapple. This gives the coffee a slightly fruity and acidic flavor.

This isn’t a typical Gourmet On The Road episode. What appealed to me most about Director, Santhosh Ananddram’s upcoming film, Raghavendra Stores, set in a fictional eatery in Malenadu, wasn’t just its earthy, realistic portrayal of culinary traditions, but also its message. That tackled headlong the social challenges faced by those in the food trade, the protagonist in this film unable to find a bride due to his profession as a cook or ‘adige bhatta’. In this fun conversation, I catch up with Santhosh Ananddram, and actors, Navarasa Nayaka Jaggesh and Shwetha Srivatsav over a delicious tiffin thindi at a Malleswaram icon, Sri Raghavendra Stores.

Am definitely looking forward to watching the full film, if you’re a food lover, you must too. Hope you enjoyed this special episode. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

https://goo.gl/maps/E44GiLwwTHCefB7Q7.summary: This video is a culinary journey to Sri Raghavendra Stores, a legendary eatery located near Malleshwaram railway station in Bangalore.  For over 4 decades, this small eatery has been serving delicious and affordable South Indian breakfast staples to locals and travelers alike. The star of the show is undoubtedly their incredibly soft and fluffy idlis, made with a perfect blend of rice rava and urad dal, best enjoyed with their spicy and flavorful chutney. The video takes viewers through the bustling kitchen, showcasing the meticulous process of preparing their signature dishes, including their crispy vadas, flavorful Chow Chow Bath, and comforting Shavige Bath.  The highlight of Sri Raghavendra Stores lies not only in the taste of their food but also in the textural symphony that each dish offers. From the grainy chutney to the perfectly balanced ratio of rice rava in the idlis, every bite is an exploration of textures. If you're looking for an authentic Bangalore breakfast experience, Sri Raghavendra Stores is a must-visit.

Long before the current Mangalore highway was built, travellers from Bengaluru enroute to Hassan, Coastal Karnataka and beyond took the state highway that would meander through towns along the way. Kunigal was an important stop back then, and I remember pit stops for breakfast here in the nineties when quality eateries were hard to find, barring places like Hotel Parimala that first opened doors over four decades ago. Since then, a new highway has emerged that bypasses most such places. On a recent road trip to Chikmagalur though, I decided to stop at Hotel Parimala and rediscovered for myself a culinary institution that takes great pride in its age-old traditions that places great emphasis on serving quality fare to customers at prices that also seem to be an honest echo to the past.

I hope you enjoy this episode enough to revisit old eateries like Hotel Parimala that have been bypassed by modern highways. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Mr. Srinivas Padiyar, a native of Kundapura, set up a sugarcane juice shop in Seshadripuram in 1977. However, fed up with the flies that would swarm around sugar cane, he shifted to making fruit juices, his attempt being to offer fruit juices with no sugar to the extent possible, by juicing only the freshest produce in the prime of their season. This coupled with his honest approach, “to offer customers full value for their hard earned money’ has earned for Lakshmi Juice Centre a loyal following through the years. I visited the store one warm evening to taste some of his most popular offerings.

Shyam Mishra moved from Allahabad to Bengaluru 35 years ago to set up a small juice shop in a narrow alley of Chickpet. That in itself wasn’t an event perhaps, but it was his recipes for fresh juice blends and rich creamy milk shakes created only with seasonal produce that over time has made Shyam Mishra Juice Centre a destination not only in the area but am told also in the dozen or so outlets it operates in Bengaluru, manned by the extended family that has since migrated to the city to support the trade. I dropped in at their original store to taste nine of their popular offerings, each one special and refreshing. Definitely a juice shop to add to your summer cooler list.

When Amudha’s husband, Manikanta lost his small trade owing to the pandemic, she decided to convert her tiny cook-at-home enterprise into something that would enable the family to earn a livelihood. She came up with the idea of a street side vegetarian barbecue shop as a concept that was healthy and would perhaps also resonate with customers. However, not one to take the easy way out, she took assistance to learn barbecue recipes and practices from a five star chef before launching Sri Sai Veg Bbq in Banashankari, South Bengaluru. Over the last two years, this family has won the hearts of food lovers in the neighbourhood for their delicious warming fare that is prepared with a whole lotta love, care and packs a tasty punch.

https://goo.gl/maps/7f9oEfRekT8z3XvB6.summary: Sri Sai Veg BBQ is a heartwarming family-run street food stall in Banashankari, South Bengaluru, specializing in delicious and healthy vegetarian barbecue. Amudha, the owner, started this venture after her husband, Manikanta, lost his job during the pandemic. She learned barbecue techniques from a five-star chef, ensuring high-quality and flavorful dishes.  They offer a variety of vegetarian skewers, including pineapple, mushroom, broccoli, paneer, baby corn, and potato, all grilled to perfection with unique masala blends.  The highlight of Sri Sai Veg BBQ is their commitment to using fresh ingredients, homemade masalas, and cooking with love and care, making it a must-try for anyone seeking delicious and affordable vegetarian barbecue.
