In happier times, Bhagya Kulkarni’s conversations with her husband, noted television personality, Sanjeev Kulkarni, often revolved around bringing the street food of Hubballi, their hometown to Bengaluru. Their trips back home always included tasting forays to the eateries of Durgadbail and incessant recipe experimentations to perfect the robust masalas of Hubli street fare. When he fell ill, she set up a small business catering Uttara Karnataka meals out of their home in South Bengaluru to support the family. Unfortunately, he passed on, but Bhagya Kulkarni was determined to fulfil their dream, and thus was born Agraane Kitchen, a tiny shop that serves up the Durgadbail girmit, mirchi, avalakki usli, bun bonda, cut mirchi, etc., in addition to typical breakfast offerings and an austere but wholesome jowar rotti meal during lunch. I visit them on a rainy evening to savour the spicy, snacky street fare that I missed on my recent Hubli expedition, and to also support this enterprise that in a manner of speaking, is this brave lady’s culinary tribute to her late husband. Established in 1940, Suvarna Mandir is perhaps Hubballi’s oldest restaurant, if not the oldest. Located amidst the hustle and bustle of Durgadbail market, it’s quite easy to miss the tiny doorway that opens into a courtyard setting in an ancient home from nearly a century ago. Looked after by third generation custodian Mr. Prakash Bhatt, when asked if he was the owner, replied that he was merely taking care of the space like his grandfather and father had before him, this eatery’s charming old school disposition extends to the fare that is served here. And a popular chaat destination is Karnataka Bhel House, which began as one of the earliest stores unlike food carts way back in 1975. Childhood friends, Koushik, Sachin and Sanketh, grew up in Kundapur, fascinated by the teeming variety of marine produce brought in by boats to the fishing ports of South Canara. Upon completing their studies, the engineers returned to Kundapur, built a food truck, roped in a village cook, before driving back to Bengaluru to launch their ‘Mangalore in Bangalore’ sea food enterprise. Orphaned at a young age and in search of a livelihood, Huchappa migrated from his village to Bengaluru in 1950. His son, Kumar continues the tradition under the shade of a temple peepal tree, which also gives his very popular chaat shop its name, Arali Mara, peepal tree in Kannada. Dahi Poori.summary: A popular Indian street food consisting of puri (thin, crispy fried bread) filled with dahi (yogurt), potatoes, chutneys, and spices. It is a refreshing and flavorful snack or light meal.

Masala Poori.summary: Crispy and puffy puris are crushed and then topped with a flavorful mixture of potatoes, onions, tomatoes, chutneys, and a blend of aromatic spices.

Bhel Poori.summary: A beloved Indian chaat, is a symphony of textures and flavors.  Made with puffed rice, sev (crispy gram flour noodles), potatoes, onions, tomatoes, coriander, and a medley of chutneys, it offers a delightful crunch in every bite.

Sev Poori.summary: Crispy puris are loaded with a tantalizing combination of potatoes, onions, tomatoes, yogurt, and a generous amount of sev. The sev adds a satisfying crunch and a burst of savory flavors to the dish

Pani Poori.summary: Round, hollow puris are filled with a mixture of flavored water (pani), potatoes, chickpeas, chutneys, and spices. The pani typically comes in two varieties: sweet and tangy, creating a burst of contrasting flavors.

Bengaluru loves its egg rice, a heavily indigenised variation of the fried rice fortified with an amalgam of punchy spices and fresh ingredients to cater to local palates. Whilst one will find a popular egg rice cart in almost every neighbourhood, there is perhaps none as popular as Snehajeevi Gowdara Adda Egg Rice, that thumps out enormous quantities to queues of patrons who wait patiently for the hot, spicy rice and other egg-y creations at this shop, ironically, located in the predominantly vegetarian neighbourhood of Malleshwaram. I had never been a fan of burgers in takeaway mode. The buns usually suffer the ill effects of the journey, arriving limp and soggy, with the filling inadvertently reorganised depending on how bumpy the ride has been from the kitchen to your home. But we were blown away by the near pristine condition in which this extravagant order of burgers arrived, packed in sturdy cartons equipped with air vents to dissipate moisture. Packaging aside, the flavour and texture combinations too are the sort that work well to please most palates. As we discovered in this leisurely amble through some of Boss Burger’s most popular offerings, from a spicy chicken piri to desi chicken tikka, crunchy quinoa and root veggies to guacamole black bean and a loaded juicy mutton version that mimicked the smoky character of seekh kebab. #ctr #mtr #vidyarthibhavan 

most popular masala dosas in bangalore, masala dosae, tiffin, ctr, mtr, mavalli tiffin rooms, lalbagh, vidyarthi bhavan, basavanagudi, bengaluru, bangalore

When it comes to the ubiquitous masala dosae here in Bengaluru, everyone has an opinion, actually many opinions, and clear favourites. Stuck at home during the recent lockdown, I couldn’t help but reminisce tasting three of Bengaluru’s most popular versions, and put together a special compilation for you, highlights of the CTR, MTR (Mavalli Tiffin Room, Lalbagh) and Vidyarthi Bhavan masala dosae from Gourmet On The Road.

Hope you enjoy this short and scrumptious bonus video; take care, stay safe and happy eating! 

CTR Benne Masala Dosa
This butter-drenched gold-hued dose is blessed with the perfect gentle crackle. On the palate, one tastes the lushness of the homemade butter that envelopes every bite of the dose, the palya and the chutney with its delicious veil. If you need one reason to visit CTR, this would be it.
Rs. 57 (usd 0.8)
10/10

MTR MASALA DOSA
The dosa here is iconic and never disappoints. Made with a blend of three rice varieties, including two red rice varieties that lend a toasty colour tone, the dose is crisp outside and soft within. The palya is seasoned just right. 
Rs. 90 (usd 1.3)
10

Vidyarthi Bhavan Masala Dosa
If you need one reason to visit Vidyarthji Bhavan, this would be it. A dose that’s crisp and lacey in parts, soft and fluffy in others, and hides within its single fold a creamy potato palya. The chutney is spicy and vivacious, a bold complement to the gentle flavours of the dose and palya.
Rs. 53 (usd 0.7) 
10/10


Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,

#ctr #vegetarian #bangalore

central tiffin room, ctr malleswaram, shri sagar, bangalore’s most famous benne masala dose, vegetarian, breakfast, tiffin, south canara cuisine, popular eatery, south indian, karnataka, kesari bath, masala dosa, set dosa, idli vada, chutney, poori bhaji, filter coffee

Bengaluru loves its masala dosa, or dosé as this supremely satisfying treat is called locally, with fans vociferously claiming top honours for their favourite eatery. One such much-loved dosa destination is CTR (Shri Sagar) in Malleswaram, which has catered to customers since 1952. I visit CTR as they emerge from lockdown to taste their benne masala dosé and a couple of other breakfast favourites, and also take a look at how this eatery has geared up for life in a post-covid world. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay safe and happy eating!

Previous CTR video link:
CTR - SHRI SAGAR | Bangalore’s Most Popular BENNE MASALA DOSA, GOLI BAJJI, IDLI & More | Malleswaram https://youtu.be/Ylb6ISVUxLY

Idli Vada
The vada is crisp and crunchy with air bubbles within that make it a great medium to soak up the flavourful sambar. The idli has a bit of a tart edge that benefits from mingling with the thenginakayi (coconut) chutney.
Rs. 52 (usd 0.7)
8/10

Poori Saagu
If you’re looking for a filling snack, this would be it. Three pooris accompany a vegetable saagu, the veggies retain their crisp crunch, if you’re looking to perk things up, combine it with the chutney that has a sharp green chilli edge.
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
8/10

Benne Masala Dosa
This butter-drenched gold-hued dose is blessed with the perfect gentle crackle. On the palate, one tastes the lushness of the homemade butter that envelopes every bite of the dose, the palya and the chutney with its delicious veil. If you need one reason to visit CTR, this would be it.
Rs. 57 (usd 0.8)
10/10

Set Dose
An exact opposite to the buttery masala dose, the set dose is almost austere. It’s spongy texture though makes it the perfect medium to soak up the flavours of the vegetable saagu and chutney. If you’re looking for a healthy dosa fix, this would be it.
Rs. 52 (usd 0.7)
8.5/10

Kesari Bath 
Dripping in ghee and topped with toasted cashews and raisins, the grainy kesari bath almost melts away when placed in the mouth. The cashew provides an element of nuttiness and the raisin, pops of sweetness to this semolina preparation.
Rs. 29 (usd 0.4)
8.5/10

Coffee 
A fitting end to a meal here.
Rs. 15 (usd 0.2)
8/10

Central Tiffin Room, CTR Malleswaram, Shri Sagar, Bangalore’s Most Famous Benne Masala Dose, Goli Bajji, Mangalore Bajji, Kesari Bath, Masala Dosa, Maddur Vade, Rava Idli, Ordinary Masala Dosa, Filter Coffee

When it comes to the Benne Masala Dosa, all roads lead to CTR - Shri Sagar or Central Tiffin Room in Bengaluru. The city’s love for this butter drenched dose goes back a few decades when the present owners took charge of this 70-year old establishment that served as the only eatery in the historic Malleswaram area.

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna catches up with Sandesh Pujari, third generation owner of this landmark eatery and explores what makes the benne dose special, before indulging in a tiffin treat that includes not just their most loved offering, but other equally popular snacks like the Mangalore bajji, Maddur Vade and more. Enjoy!

Rava Idli
The soft rava idli makes for a wholesome, comforting tiffin, bathe it in the kai (coconut) chutney or savour it with the vegetable sagu that is packed with nutrition and flavour.
Rs. 29 (usd 0.4)
8.5/10

Goli Bajji
Scrumptious with a bit of a stretchy pull on the bite, and served steaming hot, the goli bajji is a must-have when you are at CTR for an evening snack. Relish it just by itself, with its slight hint of sweetness, or dunk it into the chutney to make for a spirited mouthful.
Rs. 35 (usd 0.5)
9/10

Maddur Vade
This vade has the texture of a scrumptiously flakey cookie. On the palate, one tastes the deep savoury notes of the fried onion. Relish it while at CTR, or also carry some home, it makes for a great snack on the go
Rs. 29 (usd 0.4)
8/10

Ordinary Masala Dosa 
The dose is roasted kadak (crisp), and smeared with a generous amount of kempu (red) coconut chutney inside that lends a tinge of heat. The creamy masale, potato palya, barely whispers its flavours, but lends a great supporting act to the dose that takes centerstage with every bite.
Rs. 52 (usd 0.7)
8.5/10

Benne Masala Dosa
This butter-drenched gold-hued dose is blessed with the perfect gentle crackle. On the palate, one tastes the lushness of the homemade butter that envelopes every bite of the dose, the palya and the chutney with its delicious veil. If you need one reason to visit CTR, this would be it.
Rs. 57 (usd 0.8)
10/10

Kesari Bath 
Dripping in ghee and topped with toasted cashews and raisins, the grainy kesari bath almost melts away when placed in the mouth. The cashew provides an element of nuttiness and the raisin, pops of sweetness to this semolina preparation.
Rs. 29 (usd 0.4)
9/10

Coffee 
A fitting end to a meal here.
Rs. 15 (usd 0.2)
8/10

#VidyarthiBhavan #MasalaDosa #Bengaluru

bengaluru breakfast, bangalore popular breakfast, south indian breakfast, evening tiffin, vidyarthi bhavan, basavangudi, south bengaluru, popular bangalore dosa, masala dosa, masala dose, uppitu, rava vada, kesari bath, coffee 

There’s nothing that comes close to savouring the crisp crackle of a dosa a few moments after it has left the pan. An experience that we missed much in lockdown. And so when Bengaluru’s most popular dose spot, Vidyarthi Bhavan re-opened dine-in, we lost no time in getting there to savour their iconic masala dose, scrumptious rave vade and a couple of other evening treats. In doing so, I also took a look at the measures that this eatery has employed to ensure a safe dining experience. Enjoy and stay safe. 

Rave Vade
A deep-fried semolina vade studded with chilli, cashewnuts, ginger and curry leaves and served only in the evening, I am told this is quite popular. It’s bite is as crunchy as a cookie, crisp around the edges and soft towards the centre. 
Rs. 27 (usd 0.35) 
8/10

Kesari Bath
A textbook kesari bath that dissolves on the palate in a buttery gush of ghee, the raisins convey a pop of sweetness and the cashew lends a toastiness to the clove-induced flavour of this semolina pudding. 
Rs. 27 (usd 0.35) 
8/10

Uppitu
The flavour of onions headlines this soft semolina preparation that’s studded with fried lentils, green chillies and curry leaves. A flavoursome dish on its own, savour it with the spicy chutney if you prefer to perk things up. 
Rs. 27 (usd 0.35) 
8/10

Masala Dose
If you need one reason to visit Vidyarthji Bhavan, this would be it. A dose that’s crisp and lacey in parts, soft and fluffy in others, and hides within its single fold a creamy potato palya. The chutney is spicy and vivacious, a bold complement to the gentle flavours of the dose and palya.
Rs. 53 (usd 0.7) 
10/10

Coffee
Rs. 17 (usd 0.2) 
8/10

In this exciting Gourmet On The Road episode, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna explores Namma Bengaluru's most popular dosa destinations!

In part one of this two part episode, he begins his trail at Mavalli Tiffin Rooms or MTR tasting a plain dosa and a masala dosa. He then visits Hotel Janatha and New Modern Hotel in South Bangalore for ragi and rava dosas.

Vidyarthi Bhavan had to be part of this list, together with smaller eateries such as Davanagere Benne Dosa and the crowd favourite Taaza Thindi!

the quintessential triangular MTR masala dose served with a tuppa da batlu. Perfectly roasted crust that glistens, stuffed tempered mashed potatoes with a side of thick, spicy chutney.
this dosa is a ritual for many here and when you taste it you certainly understand why!
Rs 86.
10/10

this dose has a spicy green chutney smeared inside for that flavour burst in every bite. a simple dose done well. 
Rs 81.
8/10

Rs 30.
6/10

a paper thin rava or semolina dosa studded with flecks of onion. a really tasty dosa. the saagu makes for the right accompaniment but this dosa doesn't need one! 
Rs 40.
8/10
Hotel Janatha
Plot No.26, Diagonal Road, Sajjan Rao Cir, Parvathipuram, Vishweshwarapura, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560026

Rs 50.
8/10

this dosa looks wholesome. can feel the weight of the ragi as you tear into it. the saagu, a medley of veggies with a tangy taste brings this slightly dry dosa to life.
Rs 20.
8/10

#Breakfast #RestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Bringing its patrons exceptional benne masala dosa, soaked in ghee, heavenly kesari bhath and filter coffee since 1943, Vidyarthi Bhavan is a landmark in Bangalore that is simple yet inviting. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits this highly endorsed eatery. He converses with third generation owner Arun Adiga, understanding what keeps patrons coming back. He also relishes a full breakfast of all the items on the menu, tasting from the iconic dosas to poori saagu and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Idli Vada
A delightful plate of pillowy soft idlis and traditional uddina vada bathed in a tasty, hot sambar. The chutney, although a little runny, is enhanced with a punch of spice and a delicious tempering. 
Rs 14 for one Idli and Rs 26 for vada.
8/10

Poori Saagu
This poori saagu is a humble yet delicious dish at VB. A medley of beans, carrots, brinjal, and sweet pumpkin all harmoniously brought together. The pooris are light and fluffy as you would expect. The chutney adds a flavorful punch. 
Rs 36.
8/10

Khara bath
Spicy and savoury, this semolina concoction with veggies like carrots, onions and the simple tempering has a pleasing texture. A dish that needs no accompaniment.
Rs 26.
8/10

Kesari Bath
This bath is laden with copious amounts of ghee, and tiny morsels of pineapple to give it that sweet, tart flavor. The intense flavour of clove cuts through the richness, making this an irresistible bite. 
Rs 26.
8/10

Saagu masala dosa
This dosa is roasted perfectly with a crackly exterior and a soft interior. That slight tartness of the batter is present in every bite. The delicious saagu is a wholesome change from the typical potato stuffing. 
Rs 50.
9/10

Masala dosa
A traditional masala dosa in every sense, served with chutney. The dosa is roasted to a nice deep brown crisp around the edges, yet soft and fluffy within. The flavourful potato palya is gently tempered.
Rs 46.
10/10

Filter coffee
Strong, robust coffee topped with a frothy cream. Pull your coffee to cool it down and end your meal in an authentic way. 
Rs 16.
9/10

https://goo.gl/maps/SNrNDwCBdLnTaXNSA.title: ANAND Dum Biryani Vs. MANI Dum Biryani! Which Famous HOSKOTE Early Morning BIRYANI Should You Try?
https://goo.gl/maps/SNrNDwCBdLnTaXNSA.description:
#hoskote #biryani #bangalore

mani dum biryani, anand dum biryani, popular hoskote biryani shop, early morning biryani, popular biryani shop,, hosakote, hoskote, bangalore, bengaluru, mutton biryani, biryani trail, inspiring stories, karnataka

The Hoskote early morning biryani draws hundreds of faithful fans who wake up at an unearthly hour every Tuesday, Friday and Sunday to make the 40-km trek to queue up at biryani shops in this town just outside Bengaluru. 

However, for those not completely in the know, some of the most commonly asked questions with respect to this long-standing biryani tradition are: What’s the fuss about the Hoskote biryani? Which biryani should one try, should one try the Mani Biryani or the Anand Biryani? How different are these biryanis? Or are they similar? Which one is spicy, which one is not? What goes into the making of these hugely popular biryanis? Which one came first? And more… 

In this special Gourmet On The Road episode, we revisit these biryanis and compare side by side Hoskote’s most popular early morning biryanis, undoubtedly, in an attempt to answer many of the questions posed. Hope you enjoy this one; take care, stay safe and happy eating! 

Anand Mutton Biryani 
The dominant flavours in this biryani are that of the fresh ingredients, the naati ginger, garlic, coriander,mint etc., followed by a veil of the aromatic spices. Every grain of rice is imbued with its flavours, and the meat is a combination of some soft, juicy pieces and some on the bone, that calls for a bit of effort to get to every bit of it, some fat included. The spicing is gentle and warm. 
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1) 
9/10

Mutton Biryani
The only dish made at Mani Dum Biryani, is unique in its aroma that is redolent of an amalgam of spices combined with meat. Each grain of the rice has absorbed the procession of spices that go into the pot and the fat that is rendered from the meat, this is the sort of biryani that leaves behind a spicy impression on the palate. You can taste the heat of green chillies, and the flavour of the secret spice mix that’s made in Mani’s home. Some of the meat is laced with fat that melts in the warmth of one’s mouth, some pieces though can have a bit of a bite. This is a spicy biryani, and the mosaru bhajji, onion and cucumber raitha helps cool things down.
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1)
9/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

Note: It can get crowded, especially on Sundays. Get early to beat a long queue.

Anand was only 14 when he opened a tiny shop to sell idli and chitranna to support his family in his village, Hoskote, located about 40kms from Bengaluru. Customers requested him to sell biryani too on Sundays. What began as a tiny 2-kilo experiment 21 years ago has grown today to a massive kitchen that sells nearly a thousand kilos of mutton biryani on Sundays. And in doing so has placed Hoskote on the map for biryani lovers who don't seem to mind waking up at an unearthly hour just to get here to stand in a queue for an hour or two for a plate of the fabled Hoskote biryani that runs out by 9am and is sold only on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays. I drive out to Hoskote at 4am to find out what makes this biryani such a craze. Stay safe and happy eating!

Mutton Biryani 
The dominant flavours in this biryani are that of the fresh ingredients, the naati ginger, garlic, coriander,mint etc., followed by a veil of the aromatic spices. Every grain of rice is imbued with its flavours, and the meat is a combination of some soft, juicy pieces and some on the bone, that calls for a bit of effort to get to every bit of it, some fat included. The spicing is gentle and warm. 
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1) 
9/10

Kaal Soup 
There’s plenty of coriander and mint in this kaal soup; one can taste the gelatin that’s rendered into the broth. What it lacked though was depth of flavour from the spices, the sort of nourishing jolt that you expect to register on your tastebuds. 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4)
7/10

Chicken Fry 
A tasty homestyle chicken fry, order a portion of this to add additional meaty protein to your biryani.
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4)
7.5/10

that's rather simple in its preparation it's preparation style in fact one would say it's quite rustic as well i can certainly taste a bit of the flavor of the kasuri methi that probably goes into this dish the chicken is moist and juicy what i also like is the texture of this mince it's quite coarse and because it's coarse it manages to hold on to the flavors of that masala because otherwise when it comes to chicken there's not really too much flavor inherent in the bird itself that bird needs plenty of help from the ginger from the garlic from the coriander some green chili and the other spices that go in to make this radha murk or the radha chicken i think more than the chicken piece i'm enjoying the flavor of that chicken mince because the chicken mince has also trapped some of that oil that this masala has been bound in and that gives it that slight fattiness which is always essential when you're tasting meat [Music] palate cleansed we're now ready to meet the big daddy on the plate the mutton rogan josh the button is so tender that i barely lifted it and the piece split into two go into the effect of gravity that's how tender i'm expecting this rogan josh to be i want to savor that meat with some of that rogan josh gravy because as that meat cooks with the fat over a period of time all that fat all that flavor of the meat breaks down into that gravy that gravy which is largely onions and plenty of kashmiri chili to give it that color and of course there's also a fair bit of yogurt that goes into the making of that rogan george you can see that the meat is rich in the fat and that's something that you most definitely need to get a good rogan josh you need all that fat to lend its character to that meat and then meat is a sword that slithers of the bone it's as soft it's as moist it's as tenderly cooked as that delicious you know when it comes to enjoying the rogan josh you can enjoy the meat as is and then also find some of those meaty notes in the flavor of that curry and i'm looking forward to mopping those flavors up with this khameri naan i love the texture of this bread this bread is thick and almost acts as a sponge to soak up that gravy [Music] and also on the bite the texture is that of bread so that khameri because it's fermented doesn't tug on your bite at all rather it gives in quite easily it's quite porous almost like bread and that's why i think it's a perfect accompaniment to tasting a gravy that's lush rich and thick with the flavor of the meat and the fat like this rogan jorge there's also a bit of the fermented afternoons that i get from the bread which you can certainly taste more when you taste the bread by itself but then this isn't bread that you eat by itself this is bread that you scoop up some delicious gravy with [Music] i love the savory nose of that onion so that onion has been boon out but out to a deep savory flavor and that's what you're tasting in that rogan josh [Music] so that's the one advantage of https://goo.gl/maps/yTntaCuwB9quZJEN9.title: CHAAT, North Indian veg Thali, Mithai Takeaway From BHARTIYA JALPAN 75-Year Legacy | Rerun Episode
https://goo.gl/maps/yTntaCuwB9quZJEN9.description:
#bhartiyajalpan #vegetarian #supportlocal

support local eateries, takeaway, bhartiya jalpan, chats, chaats, vegetarian thali, mithai, namkeen, samosa, chole bhature, dahi bhalla, aloo tikki, north indian, bangalore, bengaluru

To quell a chaat and north indian veg food craving, we take away from the Bengaluru outpost of Bhartiya Jalpan, a 75-year-old mithai and namkeen house from Guwahati, Assam. Now whilst takeaways aren’t the best way to savour desi chaats, we found the flavours spot on if you’re looking to savour some chatpata desi fare. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay safe and happy eating.

Note: This episode was first released in June 2020 and is being rerun to support Bengaluru eateries with takeaway orders in the current situation. Please do support local eateries.

Samosa
The dark spiced stuffing makes this a chatpata samosa, the pastry is flakey and still retains its crunch despite being cold. The date chutney is warming and spicy.
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) per samosa 
8.5/10

Chole Bhature
A popular snack at BJ, the bhatura loses its puffy vigour in takeaway mode, but is still redeemed by the deep flavours of the chole (chickpeas). Definitely a dish that needs to be snacked on when at the eatery as opposed to takeaway.
Rs. 150 (usd 2) 

Raj Kachori
The kachori had become soggy by the time we turned our attention to this yoghurt laden chaat, but the crisp sev and moth beans still offer crunch. The yoghurt is sweet, savoury and sour. 
Rs. 129 (usd 1.7) 

Dahi Bhalla
A dumpling (bhalla) made of rice flour and urad dal, topped with spiced yoghurt, this is the perfect takeaway chaat as the bhalla has soaked up the spicing from the yoghurt and the chutneys. 
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2) 
9/10

Aloo Tikki
A potato patty stuffed with a spice mix and shallow fried on a griddle until crisp, and served with peas gravy. Smash the patty along with the peas to help the chutneys seep into the potato.
Rs. 129 (usd 1.7) 

Bhartiya Jalpan Shaahi Thaali
A tray laden with paneer makhani, aloo mutter, daal, boondi raita, jeera rice, chapatis, a sweet, pickle and papad, this meal option is a sumptuous one. I found the chapatis soft, the paneer soft and creamy, the vegetables cooked the manner they should be and the dal a nourishing accompaniment to the jeera rice. 
Rs. 269 (usd 3.6) 
8/10

Malai Chamcham
The chamcham just dissolves in one’s mouth leaving behind a veil of aromatic sweetness. Highly recommended.
Rs. 38 (usd 0.5) 
9/10

Rabri
Sweetened milk braised slowly over hours and topped with thick cream and nuts, what’s there not to like!
Rs. 81 (usd 1.1) 
8.5/10

Note: I haven’t rated some of the dishes as I feel it would be unfair to rate them in a takeaway format. Since this is a rerun episode, prices of the dishes may have changed since.

https://goo.gl/maps/546tf138essAZYnT7.description:
#mtr #vegetarian #supportlocal

support local eateries, takeaway, mtr, mavalli tiffin rooms, lalbagh, vegetarian lunch, thaali, rava idli, masala dosa, hema malini maiya, bangalore, bengaluru

Step into Mavalli Tiffin Rooms, the city’s oldest eatery, In this throwback episode to see how they have evolved their popular 21-item traditional lunch to a more convenient and packaging-friendly 9-dish mini-meal. 

From revamped, sanitised processes to consolidated menus, this century-old institution is revamping and reworking processes to meet the needs of the current situation. But then, that shouldn’t come as a surprise, because after all, they do have a tradition of innovating through adversities in the past, as illustrated in the invention of the rava idli during the rice famine of the 40s, or the seed for MTR packaged foods that was sown during the 1975-77 emergency. 

Note: This episode was first released in May 2020 and is being rerun to support Bengaluru eateries with takeaway orders in the current situation. Please do support local eateries.

Mini Meals
No longer the enormous spread that would be a delicious gateway to a post-lunch slumber, the mini meals is compact in its post-covid avatar. But that doesnt get in the way of making for a satisfying lunch, puri, saagu, rice, rasam, palya, mosaru anna, poppadom, uppinakayi and payasam, the mini meal has all that you need to savour a taste of Mavalli Tiffin Room. 
Rs. 162 (usd 2.1) 
8/10

Masala Dose
Although packed in a foil-lined box, the masala dose is missing its crunch in takeaway mode, understandably, as opposed to when savoured at the restaurant. You can heat it on a tava with a dollop of ghee to make some amends, and the flavours are trademark MTR, the sprightly chutney smeared inside the dosa and the flavourful, bright aloogadde palya. The chutney is rich in coconut and green chilli spice. All in all, makes for a delicious takeaway dose, once you get past the expectation of eating something crisp.   
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2)

Rava Idli
A dish born of a crisis, the rava idli is said to have been invented in the kitchens of Mavalli Tiffin Rooms, when there was a shortage of rice during the famine of the 40s. This is a flavourful rava idli that is rich in yoghurt, embellished with coriander, mint, coconut and topped with toasted cashew, and does spectacularly well as a takeaway. The aloogadde sagu serves well to moisten the idli with its savoury character. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)

Masala Dose
One can never tire of a masala dose here. Drenched in ghee, crisp to a brown roast, encasing a smear of chutney and the gatti (firm) aloo gadde palya, it’s the sort of dose that sings to your palate. 
Rs. 95 (usd 1.3) 
10/10

Limited Meals
It’s name belies its enormous proportions! On the thaali sit a couple of hot pooris accompanied with a potato saagu and a dry palya (vegetable preparation); one can also opt for the masala dose instead of the poori. And then, there’s the crowd-pleasing bisi bele bath, rich in its lentil goodness, chase this with more rice, soaked up in the sambar and rasam. And to wrap things up, a couple of desserts, a simple nuchinna goddi (broken wheat) payasam and a plump sugar-soaked gulab jamun. If you prefer to not succumb to the calling of a post-prandial siesta, order for their seriously addictive coffee.
Rs. 190 (usd 2.5) 
9/10

#ramzan #iftar #bengaluru

Ramadan Mubarak, folks, wish you peace, happiness and good health, most of all. Join us on this trip down memory lane to an iftar takeaway from Sharief Bhai. Hope you enjoy this rerun; take care, stay safe and strong. 

Note: This episode was first released in May 2020 and is being rerun to support Bengaluru eateries with takeaway orders in the current situation. Please do support local eateries.

Takeaway Dish Review

Sharbath
A light and soothing rose milk sharbat to accompany the iftar delicacies. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.7) per glass.
6/10 

Onion Samosa
I love the sweet crunch of the onions and the crisp, flakey pastry that it is encased in. This is an iftar staple, and Sharief Bhai does a good version of this samosa that is sold at every street corner during Ramzan.
Rs. 70 (usd 0.7) for 4 nos.
8.5/10 

Aloo Cheese Samosa
A well-spiced aloo and cheese stuffing, that lends it a crisp and creamy bite. 
Rs. 105 (usd 0.7) for 4 nos.
7/10 

Gosht Kheema Samosa
The mutton mince is roasted with spices, lending it a deep flavour alongside the onion and peas. On the palate, it is spicy and tangy.
Rs. 130 (usd 0.7) for 4 nos.
8/10 

Paneer Til Kebab
Cubes of paneer, coated in a spicy marinade and deep-fried, the fat in the cottage cheese makes for a moist and spicy bite. If you like your paneer, you will enjoy this snack.
Rs. 100 (usd 0.7) 
8/10 

Gobi Til Kebab
The gobi has a certain sweetness to it as a result of it being deep-fried, it’s missing a crunch in takeaway mode, but other than that makes for a tasty snack.
Rs. 90 (usd 0.7) 
7/10 

Murg Til Kebab Boneless
The chicken, although savoury on the palate, is a tad dry. 
Rs. 140 (usd 0.7) for 4 nos.
6/10 

Murg Shami Kebab
Spiced chicken mince, wrapped around a boiled egg quarter and sprigs of mint and coriander. Makes for a sprightly, comforting snack. 
Rs. 130 (usd 0.7) for 3 nos.
8/10 

Gosht Haleem
Sharief Bhai’s haleem is well-endowed with meat, you bite into meaty strands that have incorporated completely into the pounded wheat, in a flavourful cocoon of warming spices. The brishta, fried onions, lend it a slightly sweetish, flavourful crunch.
Rs. 330 (usd 0.7) for a large portion.
8.5/10 

Murg Anda Kheema Roti
A flakey paratha, topped with a spicy baida (egg) and chicken mince mix, makes for a chatpata, filling snack. Savour it hot!
Rs. 100 (usd 0.7) per roti.
8/10 

Phirni
The phirni is served chilled in a clay pot, a simple dessert made well. You taste the coarse graininess of the rice and the weight of the reduced milk. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.7)
8/10

In this throwback episode, we visit Nagarjuna, a popular Andhra eatery, to order and take away their popular vegetarian carrier meals, post temperature checks, hand sanitisation and electronic payment, time-appropriate practices that we will need to get used to. The food, packed in tamper proof containers and relished in the comfort of our home,  though remains as comforting as one remembers it from the good old days. Hope you enjoy our this one, take care, stay safe and strong.

Note: This episode was first released in May 2020 and is being rerun to support Bengaluru eateries with takeaway orders in the current situation. Please do support local eateries.


Vegetarian Carrier Meals
This weighty meal can feed an army, well, at least 3 to 4 hungry diners. The food is staple Nagarjuna fare with creamy lentils pappu, nourishing sambar, tangy tomato rasam, teh customary koora or vegetable with all the mandatory accoutrements - pappulu podi, curd chillies, payasam, papad, pickle and more served with a humongous bucket of rice. 
Rs. 420 (usd 5.5) 
8/10

Chicken Sholay Kebab
One of Nagarjuna’s most popular boneless chicken appetisers is embellished with loads of curry leaves. The flavours seem a bit sedate in takeaway mode when the dish is eaten around 30 minutes or so after it’s prepared, as compared to the spicy, aggressive bite one encountered when eating this at the restaurant. A tasty bite nonetheless. 
Rs. 305 (usd 4)
7/10

Chilly Chicken
The chilli, spelt with a ‘y’ as opposed to an ‘i’ on the menu is as unique as the dish in itself. Not to be confused with the popular Sino-Indian version, this is Andhra’s ode to its love affair with the chilli. The chicken is moist and juicy, soaking up a gravy made of copious amounts of green chillies, a dish that will have you begging for more punishment if that’s your thing! Definitely not for the faint-hearted though!
Rs. 285 (usd 3.8)
8/10

#supportlocal #vidyarthibhavan #masala dosa

support local eateries, takeaway, vidyarthi bhavan, basavangudi, south bangalore, traditional vegetarian tiffin in bangalore, masala dosa, dose, idli vada, chutney, old world restaurant, traditional eatery, bangalore, bengaluru

In its 78 years of existence, Vidyarthi Bhavan has always served its iconic masala dose within its premises, keeping it strictly outside the purview of delivery services. However the current scenario calls for an entirely new approach in food service, and in keeping with this, this revered South Bengaluru eatery has embraced takeaway as a new way of life, at least for the foreseeable future. I visit Vidyarthi Bhavan to document this change from the past and see for myself how its management is taking all steps necessary to ensure continuity of its delicious culinary traditions in as safe a manner as possible. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay safe and happy eating!
Note: This episode was first released in May 2020 and is being rerun to support Bengaluru eateries with takeaway orders in the current situation. Please do support local eateries.


Masala Dosa
The masala dose is now folded twice as opposed to the VB classic one fold, an allowance that the eatery has made for the dose to be rolled into an aluminium foil in order to retain its temperature when savoured at home. The crispy crackle of the dose is now replaced by a whisper of a crunch, but the buttery flavours are still spot on. The dose oozes ghee, and the aloogadde palya is mildly seasoned and creamy. It helps to crispen the dose a bit on the pan just before eating. 
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7) 

Idli
VB’s idlis are the grainy sort, perfect for ladling over chutney and piping hot sambar, before breaking it down to a delicious, spicy mash. If they’re too cold by the time they get to you, steam for a couple of minutes.
Rs. 26 (usd 0.3) 

Uddin Vade
The vade definitely suffers the most casualty when consumed in a takeaway format. Gone is its crisp crunch, that would yield to a porous bite. The only way to redeem the vada is to dunk it into a bowl of piping hot sambar and savour it with a dollop of spicy chutney.
Rs. 26 (usd 0.3) 

Khara Bath
The kharabath travels extremely well, given its moist texture. This tasty dish is studded with onions, fried lentils, coconut flakes and curry leaves, making for a playful medley of flavours and textures.
Rs. 26 (usd 0.3) 

Kesari Bath
End your meal with this luscious semolina preparation, the flavour of the pineapple and cloves is quite pronounced. The dish is mellow in its sweetness, save for the pop of extra sweetness when you bite into a toasted raisin.
Rs. 26 (usd 0.3) 

Note: Due to the current uncertain situation, please call the eatery to ascertain the timings and what is available. Prices may have changed since when this episode was originally published a year ago.

When Mr Mohammed suffered business losses in Bengaluru 18 years ago, he was on the verge of retreating to his hometown, but his wife, Mrs Asiya Khan prevailed upon him to stay back and begin a home-cooked biryani enterprise, based on a recipe she had learnt from her mother-in-law in Hyderabad. She would cook the biryani at home and her husband was entrusted with the task of selling these in supermarkets. Little by little, they grew their biryani business, moving to a tiny shop with space only for a counter and three tables eight years ago. Over time, the reputation of Noon’s Biryani grew and built for itself a loyal clientele, many of whom would order takeaways. However, the current situation has seen their business dwindle down to less than half, and it was in this context that they reached out to us, seeking assistance to help spread the word. I paid a surprise visit and liked what I tasted, compelling us to return later to film this episode. We visit the elderly couple at their home, watch the making of a chicken and mutton biryani, before making a delicious meal of these at their shop. I hope you enjoy this one, do support enterprises like these. Stay safe and happy eating!

Chicken Kebab 
Moist and juicy, homestyle chicken kebabs that make for a tasty side to the biryani. Seasoned well and encased in a batter with a savoury, light crunch.
Rs. 120/ 220 (usd 1.6/ 2.9) for half/ full portion
8/10

Chicken Biryani
Each grain of rice is separate and every piece of meat is cocooned in the biryani masala, much like how Hyderabadis like their biryanis. The heart of the masala is the brishta, fried onions, and the spices that make their presence felt in the aromatic warmth that wafts through the palate. The meat has a bit of richness thanks to the khoa that goes into the making of the chicken biryani here, and makes for a worthy partner to the rice.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7) per portion; also available by the kilo
8.5/10

Mutton Biryani
Mrs. Mohammed’s mutton biryani benefits from a generous measure, as compared to the chicken biryani, of the fried onions and spices to complement the richness of the mutton on the bone, its meaty flavours fortified by some fat clinging on to the pieces. The rice glistens in its moistness and greets you with a gentle embrace, the edge of the spices tamed by the character of the meat, that also lends the rice depth of flavour. The meat is tender in parts and with a bit of a bite in others, its flavour delicate and warming, shining through the spices. If you are the sort who doesn’t like your biryani to assault your tastebuds with a spicy jhatka, this is certainly a biryani that will please your palate.
Rs. 290 (usd 3.9) per portion; also available by the kilo
9/10

Rasmalai
Rs. 30
8/10

Happy Eating!

Gourmet On The Road,

Hi folks, hope you are doing well. In this throwback takeaway biryani review, we visited Meghana Foods, a establishment that seems to have a formidable following for its biryanis that are mostly made in the Hyderabadi style with loads of masala. Purists may balk at the eatery’s top seller, a boneless chicken biryani that to me seemed like a culinary intersection of Sino-Indian and Hyderabadi fare! Love it or hate it, you certainly can’t ignore Meghana Foods!

And to allay consumer fears in a covid world, they seem to be following many of the practices - temperature checks, hand sanitation, sealed takeaway packs, etc. - that will have to be the norm when it comes to eating out. Hope you enjoy this one, take care and stay safe.

Note: This episode was first released in May 2020 and is being rerun to support local eateries.

Special Veg Biryani
A biryani that panders to a vegetarian’s biryani craving. The rice is flavourful, and the side of tossed vegetables draws clever inspiration from a mirchi ka salan in its flavours. 
Rs. 230 (usd 3) 
8/10

Aloo Dum Biryani
The potatoes are fried to a delicious brown and have absorbed the flavourful character of the fried onions and the spices. With the mildly spiced biryani rice, it makes for a tasty combination.
Rs. 214 (usd 2.8) 
7.5/10

Chicken Biryani
A biryani that is made in the traditional Hyderabadi style with loads of masala, this is the biryani to try here. The meat is juicy, moist and flavourful, cooked perfectly to the bone.
Rs. 242 (usd 3.2) 
8.5/10

Chicken Boneless Biryani
Tender morsels of boneless meat, tossed in a spicy batter are served as an accompaniment to fluffy grains of biryani rice. Though a dish that is far removed from a traditional Hyderabadi biryani, it still commands legions of fans, I suspect partly because the spicy morsels of meat and generous portion of rice served makes it ideal for sharing. 
Rs. 248 (usd 3.3) 
8/10

Mutton Biryani
The meat was a tad chewy and dry and lacking succulence, the rice though had a nice depth of flavour. Not a biryani that I would order again. 
Rs. 301 (usd 4) 
7/10

Mr Venkatesh and Mrs Kamala Iyer serve up Tamil and Kerala Brahmin traditions in their tiny eatery, Iyer Mess, established by the former’s father in 1959. The food is simple, yet delicious, cooked by Mrs Iyer and honestly priced at Rs. 80 for a sumptuous vegetarian banana leaf meal. 
As I catch up with the Iyers when I get this takeaway meal, I can't help but feel sorry for this elderly couple who are trying hard to grasp the realities of business in the new normal. From 200 meals a day, they are now reduced to under 30, and despite the financial hardships that they endure, they have held onto their staff, lodging and boarding them at home to ensure they are safe. Spare a moment for establishments like Iyer Mess even as you watch this episode. Take care and stay safe.

Vegetarian Meal
A simple meal, the Iyer Mess banana leaf is laden with everything that one needs for tasty sustenance. With a menu that changes everyday, the spread - rice, sambar, rasam, kootu, poriyal, thayir, pickle and papad - is nourishing, and of the sort you would relish at a Tamil home blessed with a good cook. And offers great value.
Rs. 80 (usd 0.9) Rs. 100 takeaway

https://goo.gl/maps/JLGgTcL8MC5Pfs7L9.description:
#SouthIndianMeals #Bangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Serving authentic Tamil-Brahmin style meals for close to 60 years now, Iyer Mess is a go-to spot for lunch at Malleshwaram, Bengaluru. 

Founded in 1959, the mess is located in the home of owners, Venkatesh and Kamala Iyer.

The couple who have carried forward the tradition of serving homestyle vegetarian fare, use recipes handed down by Mr Iyer’s father to maintain taste and style of cooking.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the well-known mess to explore its kitchen and taste the ‘veg homely meal’.

The kitchen starts as early as 5:00 am every morning, preparing a standard banana leaf meal, comprising of Rice, Sambar, Rasam, Poriyal, Kootu, Pickle, Yoghurt, Vada and Appalam. On Sundays the menu features a special additions of Payasam and Mor Kuzambu.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Rs 70 for a vegetarian meal

Kose/ Cabbage Poriyal
A fresh, crunchy medley of cabbage and flecks of coconut, simply seasoned with mustard. 8/10


Kumbalakai/ Sweet Pumpkin Kootu
A mildly tempered, delicious preparation. Can taste the sweetness of the pumpkin, a tasty combination with the chapati.
9/10

Paruppu Vada
deep fried yet wholesome because of the lentil or paruppu in the vada. Flecks of onion impart hints of sweetness and the green chillies give it that spicy kick.
8/10


Chapati
Soft and light, a homestyle chapati.
7/10

Thayir Sadam/Curd Rice
thick and creamy, homemade curd. the milk for the curd is cooked on a coal stove!
9/10

Pickle
Spicy, bitter accompaniment called oorukka in Tamil.
7/10

Moolangi/ Radish Sambar
Big in flavour, the spicy, fiery kick from the chilli is very prominent in this sambar. The radish is cooked just right!
10/10

Rasam
a bit mellow. not as robustly flavoured as one would expect.
6/10

Appalam
Crunchy, deep fried, perfect when eaten with rice and rasam or sambar.
8/10

ADDRESS - Iyer Mess, No 4/3, West Park Road Between 7th and 8th Cross, Malleshwaram West, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003; tel: 098860 78290

https://g.page/TheLightHouseBengaluru?sh.title: Homestyle COASTAL FARE At THE LIGHTHOUSE RESTAURANT | A Homemaker’s Expression Of Food & Memories
https://g.page/TheLightHouseBengaluru?sh.description:
#mangaloreancuisine #kundapurcuisine #bangalore

popular coastal restaurant, mangalore, mangalorean, coastal karnataka, kundapur, prawn ghee roast, prawn curry, fish curry, bangude pulli munchi, mackerel, chicken curry, kori rotti, squid koliwada, drumstick koliwada, neer dosa, ragi mani, seafood 

Married into a family of traditional restaurateurs, Prathiksha Nayak sought to create a dining experience that embodied her expression and memories of food growing up. The result is The LightHouse Restaurant, an airy space that is quite un-restaurant-like and more reminiscent of a South Canara home. Here, she serves coastal fare gleaned from family recipes and from her cooks who have worked in kitchens at legendary establishments along the West Coast. Keeping in mind her neighbourhood clientele, there’s a smattering of Chinese and North Indian on the menu too, but it is the dishes from the Kundapur-Mangalore belt that are much in favour here, as I discovered during a recent lunch here. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

Solkadi
Rs. 80 (usd 1.1)
8/10

Drum Stick Koliwada
The robust koliwada masala finds its origins in the fishing community of Maharashtra, and although its combination with the drumstick comes as a bit of a surprise, its flavours seem to find a happy partner in this fibrous vegetable. I only wished the drum stick segments were longer, allowing one to chew on the fry better.
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6)
8/10

Squid Koliwada
The squid holds on to the koliwada masala in a tight embrace, one can taste its spicy notes in every crisp bite. Definitely, a must-order here.
Rs. 300 (usd 4.1)
9/10

Prawn Ghee Roast
The ghee roast masala is modified here to incorporate coconut and some cashew, so the chilli punch is toned down a wee bit, but that doesnt get in the way of an enjoyable ghee roast. One that sits lighter on the stomach as opposed to a traditional ghee roast preparation. The prawns are fresh and cooked right; this is the sort of dish that is begging to be mopped up with a neer dosa.
Rs. 450 (usd 6.1)
9/10

Prawn Hinga Udha
A gentle poached prawn curry, its flavours laced with the edge of hinga (asafoetida) and a lashing of coconut oil. Makes for a comforting combination with the boiled rice, the sort of preparation that you would taste in a Konkani home. 
Rs. 450 (usd 6.1)
8.5/10

Kori Rotti
The chicken curry is robust in its flavours with a savoury onion punch, you can taste the coconut, the coriander, cumin and the slightly bitter edge of the mustard seeds in the seasoning. A delicious combination when ladled over the dry roti. 
Rs. 320 (usd 4.4)
8.5/10

Bangude Pullimunchi
You can taste the sharp tartness of the tamarind (pulli) and the spicy punch of the munchi (chilli) in the gravy. The bangude (mackerel) is fresh, the masala though falls a bit short in steeping into the fish. An enjoyable curry nonetheless, with the appam.
Rs. 250 (usd 3.4)
8/10

Raagi Manni
The raagi manni makes for a soothing and light end to a meal here.
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
8/10

https://goo.gl/maps/JRKuwfs3QxA6rKUGA.description:
#coconutshake #yelneerkatte #bangalore

trending coconut dessert, popular coconut shake, tender coconut shake, ice cream, summer cooler, dessert, milkshake, smoothies, healthy coolers, yelneer katte, basavangudi, bangalore, katte special, ice cream, small business

With the mercury rising, Bengaluru’s denizens seem to be turning to the yelneer or tender coconut water shake, a dessert trend that seems to be the flavour of the season. I ventured out to Yelneer Katte, supposedly the store that began this rage in the city to decipher for myself what the fuss was all about. Hope you enjoy this short and icy-cool episode. Take care, stay safe and happy eating!

Katte Special
Coconut flesh crushed with coconut milk, cream and nuts, this is the one to have if like me you prefer tasting the ‘coconutty’ character. The nuts and raisins also add to the nutty flavor and thick texture of this shake, the pomegranate seeds provide a fruity pop and the swirl of condensed milk a rich, creamy finishing touch. The sweetness is just right.
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
8/10

Yelneer Mango Shake With Vanilla Ice Cream
A loaded shake, coconut flesh ground with coconut water and fresh mango, topped with vanilla ice cream, chocolate syrup, nuts, fresh mango and some condensed milk. A tasty milkshake, but one cannot taste much of the coconut as it is overpowered by the ice cream, chocolate sauce and a copious amount of sugar. 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.3)
6.5/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 11am to 9pm
Note: The place does get crowded especially on weekends. Do plan your visit accordingly. Yelneer Katte also has branches in BTM 2nd Stage, Jayanagar and Malleshwaram, you will find it on google maps.

https://goo.gl/maps/juaSDpVbdQvjvp4w9.description:
#seafood #mangalorean #bengaluru

family eatery, st thomas town, east bangalore, new restaurant, coastal cuisine, fish thali, fish fry, pomfret, mackerel, fish fry, prawn ghee roast, crab masala, chicken curry, small business

Tarayi, a tiny three-table eatery in St. Thomas Town, East Bengaluru, was born of homemaker Freeda Ananth’s desire to share the culinary legacy of her late mother and to set up a small business of her own. So, with the support of her husband, Vijay Ananth, this soft-spoken lady ventured out as a restaurateur just a couple of months ago, and in a relatively short span of time has managed to make an impression on the neighbourhood with her rendition of Mangalorean-Kundapur fare laced with a touch of Kerala influence. I visited Tarayi to taste their limited but tasty homestyle offerings, and to also help share the word on this family enterprise that’s a true labour of love. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care, stay safe and happy eating!

Prawn Ghee Roast
This ghee roast masala exudes a slight sour twang followed by the warmth of the chilli and spices. The prawns are cooked just right, delicately ‘springy’ on the bite, swaddled in the grainy textured masala with the lushness of ghee.  
Rs. 270 (usd 3.6)
9/10

Black Pomfret Fry 
The masala is napped rather lightly on the fish, allowing for the pomfret to shine in its fresh flavours. The skin is cooked to a perfect crisp.
Rs. 250 (usd 3.3)
8.5/10

Seer Fry
Rs. 280 (usd 3.7)
8/10

Crab Masala
Loved the aromatic masala, onions, tomatoes and spices, soaked up by the plump, meaty sea crab. The sweet crab meat contrasts beautifully with the savoury notes of the masala. If you love crab, this is certainly a must-order when here.
Rs. 240 (usd 3.2)
10/10

Fish Thali
A satisfying thali, complete with modest portions of mackerel curry and fry, in addition to sambar, rasam, vegetables, boiled rice… perfect if you’re looking to savour Mangalorean fare on a budget.
Rs. 150 (usd 2)
8/10

Kheema Ball Curry
A pleasing curry, I found the meat ball a tad pasty and giving up the texture of the flour used to bind the mince together.
Rs. 120 (usd 1.6) for half portion
7/10

Chicken Curry
A homestyle curry, thin in its consistency but rich in the flavour of the masala. Goes well with the neer dosae. 
7.5/10


Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: breakfast and lunch - 8am to 430pm; dinner - 630pm to 10pm; closed on Mondays.
Note: This is a tiny eatery with barely three tables; if dining here, be prepared for a bit of a wait. Best perhaps to order in, they are registered on Dunzo for now.
ADDRESS -  Tarayi Coastal Cuisine, #7, 3rd Main Road, karavalli Road, KK Halli, St Thomas Town, Post, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560084; tel: +91 97319 95671/ 96111 02133/ 080 4972 2888

biryani food truck, nrk bamboo biryani, mysuru, bamboo biryani, mutton biryani, chicken biryani, chicken tawa fry, small business

On my last trip to Mysuru, I visited this food truck that cooks an unusual biryani, layered and steamed in bamboo. Helmed by a relatively new food entrepreneur, Ramamurthy, who was left with no option but to move to Mysuru and begin this mobile eatery to support his family after losing his life’s savings, the bamboo biryani is a result of his culinary passion and kitchen experiments. This version of the biryani that is steamed in bamboo for a couple of hours, isn’t what one may traditionally expect, but certainly makes for an interesting dish to taste! Check it out if you find yourself in Mysuru. Hope you enjoy this short and sweet episode, take care, stay safe and happy eating!

Mutton Biryani 
The sort of biryani that tumbles onto the plate when semi-cooked meat masala is placed in the bottom of a bamboo cylinder, topped with aromatic rice and egg,  and steamed for a couple of hours. The thick masala clinging to the meat serves to moisten the rice and the meat, some pieces soft and yet others that warrant a bit of a chew. The bamboo lends its aroma to the preparation.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
7.5/10

https://g.page/ganga-s-mudde-mane?share.title: GANGA’S MUDDE MANE | Homely Gowda Cuisine| This Brave Couple Makes A Fresh Start Despite Challenges!
https://g.page/ganga-s-mudde-mane?share.description:
#traditional #gowdafood #bangalore

new gowda cuisine eatery, vegetarian thali, non veg meal, nalli fry, ragi mudde, kheema unde curry, mutton peas pulav, kaal soup, boti gojju, chicken tava roast, small business

A sudden loss of occupation forced Hemanth Kumar to deploy his life savings and rustle up an eatery to support his family. Seeing her husband struggle, Nalini gave up her teaching job to support him in this enterprise that aspires to serve homestyle Gowda food. I visited Ganga’s Mudde Mane one afternoon to meet and motivate the brave couple, and along the way tasted an elaborate spread. Hope you enjoy this episode; take care, stay safe and happy eating!

Kaal Soup 
An aromatic soup that serves well to whet your palate. The tomato conveys a pulpy texture laden with the meaty broth.
Rs. 40 (usd 0.6)
8/10

Brain Fry
Flavoured with the lightest touch of spice, pepper and curry leaves, the ‘bheja’ is cooked to perfection and melts in its rich buttery lushness when placed in the mouth. If you love the brain, a must-order here!
Rs. 150 (usd 2.1)
10/10

Chicken Tava Roast
Marinated in a green chilli, ginger garlic paste, it is the freshness of the mint that shines through the masala. I found the chicken a tad chewy. 
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6)
7.5/10

Boti Kal Goju 
A thick preparation enlivened with the starchiness of raw banana and nourishment of lentils, the boti is cooked through well. 
Rs. 170 (usd 2.3)
8/10

Mutton Kheema Ball Curry
The kheema unde is rich in its meatiness and is complemented by the green chilli and coriander. Eat this hot to prevent the gram flour, used to bind the meat, from making its presence felt on the palate.
Rs. 180 (usd 2.5)
7.5/10

Chicken Kheema Goju 
Tiny cubes of chicken tossed in a tasty masala. What makes this dish interesting are flecks of yam that bring its earthy flavours. 
Rs. 150 (usd 2.1)
7/10

Nalli Fry 
A weighty lamb shank, some of the meat has a bit of a bite, but as you work your way to the core of the nalli, the meat is tender. There is depth of flavour from the spices and the pepper. 
Rs. 380 (usd 5.2) for two large pieces, the price for this varies by weight. 
9/10

Veg Meals 
A vegetarian will enjoy this simple but homely assemblage with as much gusto as a non vegetarian. From the scrumptious dill fritters to the comforting sprouts saaru and rasam, each dish bears the mark of a talented home cook, in this case, Nalini Hemant Kumar. I would happily order this with a non-vegetarian side.
Rs. 80 (usd 1.1)
8/10

Mutton Peas Pulav 
Made three days a week, this is a pulao that is moist, gentle and aromatic. The aroma of the whole spices is what one tastes on the palate alongside the faint warmth of green chillies whose heat has been toned down by some coconut milk that goes into the pulao just before it is placed on dum. The meat in the pulao is soft and has a bit of fat ribboned through it, the peas are endearing in their soft bite.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.8)
8.5/10


Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

Kaal Soup.summary: An aromatic soup that serves well to whet your palate. The tomato conveys a pulpy texture laden with the meaty broth.

Brain Fry.summary: Flavoured with the lightest touch of spice, pepper and curry leaves, the ‘bheja’ is cooked to perfection and melts in its rich buttery lushness when placed in the mouth. If you love the brain, a must-order here!

Chicken Tava Roast.summary: Marinated in a green chilli, ginger garlic paste, it is the freshness of the mint that shines through the masala.

Boti Kal Goju.summary: A thick preparation enlivened with the starchiness of raw banana and nourishment of lentils, the boti is cooked through well.

Mutton Kheema Ball Curry.summary: The kheema unde is rich in its meatiness and is complemented by the green chilli and coriander. Eat this hot to prevent the gram flour, used to bind the meat, from making its presence felt on the palate.

Chicken Kheema Goju.summary: Tiny cubes of chicken tossed in a tasty masala. What makes this dish interesting are flecks of yam that bring its earthy flavours.

Nalli Fry.summary: A weighty lamb shank, some of the meat has a bit of a bite, but as you work your way to the core of the nalli, the meat is tender. There is depth of flavour from the spices and the pepper.

Veg Meals.summary: A vegetarian will enjoy this simple but homely assemblage with as much gusto as a non vegetarian. From the scrumptious dill fritters to the comforting sprouts saaru and rasam, each dish bears the mark of a talented home cook, in this case, Nalini Hemant Kumar. I would happily order this with a non-vegetarian side.

Mutton Peas Pulav.summary: Made three days a week, this is a pulao that is moist, gentle and aromatic. The aroma of the whole spices is what one tastes on the palate alongside the faint warmth of green chillies whose heat has been toned down by some coconut milk that goes into the pulao just before it is placed on dum. The meat in the pulao is soft and has a bit of fat ribboned through it, the peas are endearing in their soft bite.

https://g.page/ganga-s-mudde-mane?share.summary:
Ganga’s Mudde Mane is a small eatery run by a couple, Hemanth Kumar and Nalini, serving authentic Gowda cuisine.  Hemanth, a seasoned cook with 15 years of experience, and Nalini, a former teacher who joined to support her husband,  prepare each dish with a homely touch. The restaurant offers a diverse menu featuring classics like Kaal Soup, Brain Fry, Chicken Tava Roast, and their signature dish, Mutton Nalli Fry.  A standout feature is their commitment to using fresh, local ingredients, evident in the vibrant flavors and aromas. Despite facing initial challenges, their courage and determination shine through in the delicious, hearty meals they serve.  

Highlight:  A unique aspect of Ganga’s Mudde Mane is their dedication to preserving the authenticity of Gowda cuisine, using traditional recipes and techniques passed down through generations.

Given its modest beginnings as a village eatery in a hut six or seven decades ago in Vijayapura, S. Narayan Rao, the late founder of Nani Hotel may have found it hard to fathom its current immense following that draws Bangaloreans to drive 50 kilometres for breakfast here. Tuppa Masala Dosa
The ghee masala dosa is the top draw with patrons here. Smeared with a spicy chutney as it roasts, the dosa is ladled with a dollop of potato palya and a top-up lashing of ghee to ensure the tuppa is what customers taste in plenty. The result is a golden-brown dosae that is slightly thick and biscuity in its crunch and lush with ghee, cradling within its fold a creamy, flavourful palya. The chutney makes for a spicy accompaniment.

#traditional #keralacuisine #bangalore

best kerala restaurant, bangalore, bengaluru, koramangala, traditional, malayali food, kappa chakka kandhari, appam and stew, karimeen, pearlspot fry, kappa fish curry, pazham kanji, pidi kozhi curry, duck roast, kappa vada, tapioca, ramassery idli, appam and stew, puttu, mutton coconut fry, meen pollichathu, tender coconut pudding, kandhari ice cream, payasam, chef regi mathew

The folks behind Kappa Chakka Kandhari restaurant take their food rather seriously, after all their menu is a showcase of Malayali fare based on their collective memories of growing up in Kerala. And spearheading this unique ‘nostalgic’ culinary initiative is Chef Regi Mathew, who has spent more than a decade extensively touring his home state, exploring recipes and connecting with cooks across homes, community kitchens, and even toddy shops. The resulting food is a labour of love, with ingredients sourced from micro-regions in Kerala to match the provenance of the dish, for instance the rice for the fabled Ramassery Idli comes from Palakkad, the home of the idli, the karimeen (pearl spot fish) from Vaikom, Kottayam, and so on… This fastidious approach to sourcing also seems to extend to the kitchen hands at KCK too, who hail from traditional kitchens and homes in ‘God’s own country’. In this episode, I partake of a lavish lunch that spans across a dozen preparations, made possible by their innovative menu approach that allows for diners to savour a string of delicacies in the course of a meal. Hope you enjoy this one, take care, stay safe and happy eating!

Note:
The set menus at Kappa Chakka Kandhari are priced upwards of Rs. 475 (usd 6.5) and in addition to a tasting of seven preparations, include a beverage and dessert too. Additional add-ons (limited servings), kappa vada, koorka fry, ramassery idli with chicken curry, are priced at Rs. 100 (usd 1.4) per dish.  

Rajayogi Meal
A set menu that’s fit for a king, this smorgasbord of a dozen dishes is sheer indulgence! Begin with juicy prawns in a coconut-kokum masala that is steamed in a petite banana leaf pouch, spicy ‘touchings’ of needle fish, the plumpest soft shell crabs, and a delicately flavoured pearl spot fish draped in a robust, toddy shop masala, amongst other delicacies that include a peppery chicken peralan and a slow-cooked mutton coconut fry. After an interlude of a sweet, sour and spicy, pineapple-nendram relish, the main courses troop out - pidi, tiny rice dumplings steeped in coconut milk and served with a flavourful simple chicken curry, a velvety mutton stew and appam combo, and a prawn puttu biryani that hits the spot. For dessert, there’s much to choose from, we tried the chilli-pricking kandhari ice cream and the luscious tender-coconut cloud pudding.
Rs. 1475 (usd 20.3)       
9/10 (overall) The pearl spot fry, mutton fry, soft shell crab, pineapple nendram relish, mutton fry, appam and stew  - 10/10

Ayakora Nellikai Masala Fry
A fish fry inspired by frugal tribal traditions, the fish is spiced with a paste of sun-dried gooseberries, green peppercorn and kandhari, bird’s eye chilli. Rs. 375 (usd 5.2)

best pizzas, north bangalore, bengaluru, siddys pizza, pizza recipe, pizza, pizzeria, margherita, smoked chicken, garlic bread, pepperoni, handmade pizzas, italian, authentic sicilian style pizzas, siddy, siddhanth sawkar, yelahanka, bangalore

When Siddhanth Sawkar was forced to close his café and home catering-turned-food truck brand, Spitfire Barbeque, owing to the pandemic, he spent a couple of months mulling his next move, making pizzas. Not just a generic version as dished out by fast food chains! Instead, he dug deep into his experience as a culinary student in Southern Italy, to open a pizzeria serving Sicilian style pizzas in his erstwhile North Bengaluru café in Yelahanka New Town. Siddy’s Pizza, as I discovered during a leisurely visit, is a one-man passion enterprise, where Siddy, as Siddhanth is known, does everything from taking the order to putting together the pizzas to serving customers who quite often chat with him as the cheese-laden flavourful pies bake in the oven. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care, stay safe and happy eating!

Garlic Butter Bread
Pillowy soft and gushing with garlic-infused buttery flavour; the butter is molten as the bread comes out of the oven! Changes your perspective of what simple garlic bread can be! The cheddar cheese dip makes for an indulgent accompaniment.
Rs. 140 (usd 1.9)
9/10

Classic Margherita & Cheese - Large
Its dough fermented for a few hours, the pizza is firm and toasty, drooping at the edge, burdened under the weight of a generous topping of cheese. The sharp, spicy notes of the homemade tomato sauce, salsa semplice, is softened by the mozzarella. 
Rs. 350 (usd 4.8)
8/10

Smoked Chicken & Cheese - Large
The juicy personality of the chunky, smoked chicken franks take over the palate the moment you bite into this cracker of a pizza, followed then by the slightly, sweet crunch of the onions. The cheese and tomato sauce play second fiddle to the meat and onions. If you love smoked chicken, this pie is a must-have!
Rs. 420 (usd 5.8)
10/10

Classic Pepperoni & Cheese - Large
Lush in virgin olive oil, this is a classic Sicilian style pizza, its ‘bready’ texture quite similar to a focaccia. There’s plenty of mozzarella that sits atop the pizza, followed by the spicy sauce and onions. But it is the fat-laden savoury fervour of the pepperoni that is the hero of this pizza! This pizza is also the sort that would make for a great midnight snack when left over in the refrigerator.
Rs. 650 (usd 9)
9/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,

Garlic Butter Bread.summary: Pillowy soft and gushing with garlic-infused buttery flavour; the butter is molten as the bread comes out of the oven! Changes your perspective of what simple garlic bread can be! The cheddar cheese dip makes for an indulgent accompaniment.

Classic Margherita & Cheese - Large.summary: Its dough fermented for a few hours, the pizza is firm and toasty, drooping at the edge, burdened under the weight of a generous topping of cheese. The sharp, spicy notes of the homemade tomato sauce, salsa semplice, is softened by the mozzarella.

Smoked Chicken & Cheese - Large.summary: The juicy personality of the chunky, smoked chicken franks take over the palate the moment you bite into this cracker of a pizza, followed then by the slightly, sweet crunch of the onions. The cheese and tomato sauce play second fiddle to the meat and onions. If you love smoked chicken, this pie is a must-have!

Classic Pepperoni & Cheese - Large.summary: Lush in virgin olive oil, this is a classic Sicilian style pizza, its ‘bready’ texture quite similar to a focaccia. There’s plenty of mozzarella that sits atop the pizza, followed by the spicy sauce and onions. But it is the fat-laden savoury fervour of the pepperoni that is the hero of this pizza! This pizza is also the sort that would make for a great midnight snack when left over in the refrigerator.

He especially enjoys the Smoked Chicken & Cheese pizza and the Classic Pepperoni & Cheese pizza. The reviewer also appreciates the restaurant's cozy atmosphere and friendly service. 

Highlight: What makes Siddy’s Pizza unique is that the owner, Siddy, makes everything from scratch, including the dough, sauce, and toppings. He also uses a traditional Sicilian recipe for his pizzas, which gives them a unique flavor and texture.

nellore andhra restaurant, vijay kitchen, brookefield, whitefield, bengaluru, andhra meals, fish curry, chepala pulusu, fish fry, vegetarian bhojanam, rr chilli chicken, mutton pepper ghee roast, biryani, chicken fry biryani, nellore, small business

With a culinary lineage that goes back to Hotel Manju, supposedly the first table-service restaurant in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh in the sixties, Sashidhar Reddy and his wife, Vijayalakshmi, moved to Bengaluru from Nellore little over a year ago to open Vijay Kitchen, to serve dishes made to traditional family recipes. I visited this modest eatery set in the ground floor of their home in the suburb of Brookefield, where I not only savoured a delicious Andhra Bhojanam but also caught the making of an iconic Nellore Chepala Pulusu, a sour and spicy fish curry. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care, stay safe and happy eating. 

Plate Rice Meals
Served on a banana leaf tray, the rice meals is a simple but satisfying affair that consists of two vegetables, one dry and the other moist, a sambar, rasam and a nourishingly tasty pappu to keep company with the anam (steamed rice) and flavoured rice. There is also a sweet to round off the meal.
Rs. 99 (usd 1.4)
8/10 

Chepala Pulusu (Sour and Spicy Fish Curry)
Made by his wife, Vijayalakshmi, to a recipe that goes back to Sasidhar Reddy’s grandmother, the Chepala Pulusu is a must-try here. A sour and spicy affair, the fish curry is made the evening before, thereby allowing for the fish to soak up the vivacious character of the tamarind, raw mangoes, chilli powder and the secret fenugreek spice blend. 
Rs. 180 (usd 2.5)
10/10

Mamdikaya Royyalu (Mango Prawns)
A tangy preparation that juxtaposes fresh flavours of shrimp to the tart fervour of raw mangoes. Taste it with the annam (rice) to tone down some of its tangy flavours.
Rs. 250 (usd 3.4)
9/10

Chepala Fry (Fish Fry)
Chinese pomfret or lake pomfret naped in a pleasant masala; the skin is fried to a crisp.
Rs. 150 (usd 1.4)
7/10
 
Royyalu Avakkai
A spicy, homemade prawn pickle that makes for a great combination with steaming hot rice.
8/10
 
Mutton Pepper Ghee Roast 
The meat is moist and juicy, coated with coarsely ground pepper and tossed in the buttery lushness of ghee. The meat is cooked twice, first a roasted fry with masala, and then tossed around in hot ghee. 
Rs. 250 (usd 3.4)
9/10

RR Chilli Chicken
This dish should come with a ‘chilli hotness’ warning! Not for the faint-hearted, there is little else in this dish other than the chicken and tonnes of green chilli. The result is a unique taste that’s fiery at first but also the sort that endears itself once you get past the ‘suffering’! If you like it toned down, tell them so and they will toss it in some ghee.
Rs. 150 (usd 1.4)
8/10

Chicken Fry Biryani
A dish that was introduced as a means to consume leftover biryani rice, topped with chicken fry, the chicken fry biryani today is more popular than the Nellore biryani here. One can taste the warming flavours of the biryani spices in the kushka, the rice, that makes for a great combination with the robust tomato-onion rich masala of the chicken fry. 
Rs. 180 (usd 2.5)
8.5/10

https://goo.gl/maps/xqwjrMmLnYZCM9Ct8.title: SRI CHIKKAVEERANNA SWEETS | This 72-Year-Old Village Shop Serves PURE GHEE MITHAI & KHAARA Items!
https://goo.gl/maps/xqwjrMmLnYZCM9Ct8.description:
#mysorepak #badamhalwa #vijayapura

popular sweet shop in rural bangalore, vijayapura, bengaluru, sri chikkaveeranna sweets, mysore pak, badam halwa, ghee jilebi, pure ghee sweets, traditional mithai, family run, tuppa, ghee red rice avalakki

In 1948, Chikkaveeranna opened a sweetmeat stall in Vijayapura, then a sleep hamlet located fifty kilometres from Bengaluru. The stall would travel from village fair to village fair selling mithai and khaara made of pure country ghee. 72 years on, village ghee may no longer be easily available, but Suresh Chikkananjundappa, his grandson, tends to the traditions of his ancestors in the ghee sweets and savouries that he personally prepares with his family and dedicated workers. Their mysore pak is hugely popular, made to a special technique where the gram flour is lightly roasted with some ghee, before finding its way into the paaka or sugar mixture. However, the tuppa jilebi, with the batter fermented overnight in clay pots, the rich badam halwa made with homemade khoa, and a seriously addictive red rice avalakki mixture, all made with pure ghee, are also must-haves when at this tiny sweet shop. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care, stay safe and happy eating!

Tuppa Jilebi
Made of a batter that is fermented overnight in a clay pot, and fried in pure ghee, the result is a white jilebi that crackles with a sticky bite and unburdens its ghee-laden sweetness with just a tinge of sourness. 
Rs. 440 (usd 6) per kilo 
9/10 

Tuppa Avalakki
Red rice puffed to a crisp in a bath of boiling ghee, comes together with ghee-roasted cashewnuts, curry leaves, Bengal gram and generous sprinkling of spices to make a seriously addictive khaara or mixture.  
Rs. 560 (usd 7.7) per kilo 
9/10 

Mysore Pak
Soft and crumbly, lush with ghee, this is the sort of Mysore Pak that dissolves on the palate with the light lilt of cardamom, when fresh. You can taste the weight of the gram flour, especially in the tiny clumps that have held on to the ghee as the gram flour is lightly roasted before it finds its way into the sugar syrup or paaka. The hero ingredient in this mithai though is the ghee that makes it Sri Chikkaveerana’s most popular mithai for over seven decades.
Rs. 560 (usd 7.7) per kilo 
10/10 

Bene Murukku
One of the few items here that is made in oil, the murukku though crunchy and flavourful with cumin and carom seeds and the nuttiness of sesame, feels a bit spartan when tasted in the company of the other heavyweights here.
Rs. 280 (usd 3.8) per kilo 
8/10 

Badam Halwa
Garnished with chironji seeds and slivers of pistachio and almonds, the halwa is rich with the reduced milk solid, ghee and the grainy bite of coarsely ground almonds. Although, the Mysore Pak is traditionally more popular here, the badam halwa comes a close second. 
Rs. 640 (usd 8.7) per kilo 
9.5/10 


Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 1030am to 9pm 
Note: They have no branches, to taste what I tasted, visit the original shop located in Vijayapura town by following the google coordinates given below. To ensure their fare is always fresh and given the family-run nature of this sweetshop, Sri Chikkaveeranna Sweets prepares limited quantities each day. It is best to call ahead and ensure you get your quota of the mithai and khaara items here.

https://goo.gl/maps/nbAk8UeeQcvzUvo2A.title: ROYAL MESS | This Couple Serves Memorable Hyderabadi Mughlai Food At Their Mysuru Home Eatery!
https://goo.gl/maps/nbAk8UeeQcvzUvo2A.description:
#restaurantathome #mysore #mughlai

home eatery in mysore, royal mess, mughlai, hyderabadi cuisine, mutton kheema, mutton masala, butter chicken, korma, biryani, kheer, sameena khanum, homestyle food in mysore

When Sameena Khanum’s husband retired from his job overseas, she decided to do something on her own to support the family. Her love for cooking led her to open a tiny eatery at home with two tables only, catering initially to college students yearning for home-cooked meals. Entirely self-taught, Mrs. Khanum serves up a repertoire of Hyderabadi-Mughlai dishes, assisted by her husband and children. A meal here is not just about delicious sustenance but also about the warming hospitality with which one is welcomed and served, as I discovered when I dropped into Royal Mess late one evening. Hope you enjoy this episode; take care, stay safe and happy eating!

Mutton Kheema
The mutton kheema is coarse and grainy, cooked with meat on the bone, that results in a deep-flavoured, warming dish. The sort that makes it a must-try here.
Rs. 350 (usd 4.8) for a large portion.
9/10

Mutton Masala
Flavoured with the gentle sweet flavours of fresh tomato and the savouriness of onions, the masala is tasty. The meat is soft, there’s a bit of fat that one needs to work through. One could request for slightly less fat, makes for an enjoyable dish. 
Rs. 400 (usd 5.5) for a large portion.
8.5/10

Chilli Chicken
A homestyle chilli chicken that is spiced with green chillies and red chilli powder and plenty of garlic. There are onions and capsicum too. A chilli chicken that isn’t as spicy as one would expect it to be. 
Rs. 220 (usd 3) for a large portion.
7.5/10

Butter Chicken
A rich cashew nut gravy that had a tad too much dried fenugreek garnish for my liking, the meat, a bit of a bite. 
Rs. 220 (usd 3) for a large portion.
7/10

Chicken Biryani
Made with long-grained basmati rice, the flavourful masala is an amalgam of fried onions, tomatoes, yoghurt and Mrs. Khanum’s home-blended spice mix. The biryani had cooled down a bit, rendering the rice slightly dry and the meat a fibrous bite. Ensure that you arrive at Royal Mess when the biryani is freshly made to savour this preparation.  
Rs. 175 (usd 2.4) 
7.5/10 

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV
