https://goo.gl/maps/UVjUhU6qW44ZycHAA.title: Traditional Breakfast At New SHIVALLI | Kotte Kadubu, Rajamudi Dosa, Kuchalakki Ganji, Ragi Ambli
https://goo.gl/maps/UVjUhU6qW44ZycHAA.description:
#mysorehighway #vegetarian #breakfast

popular restaurant on mysore highway, shivalli restaurant, mtr shivalli, mudagere, channapatna, bangalore mysore road, kotte kadubu, rajamudi rice, neer dosa, dose, kuchalakki, boiled rice, finger millet, ragi ambli, healthy food, healthy breakfast, highway breakfast, wheelchair accessible

One of the earliest eateries on the Bengaluru - Mysuru route, Shivalli has recently emerged after an extensive renovation that imparts this 20-year-old popular highway destination a breezy, contemporary vibe that comes as a breath of fresh air in current times. It is heartening to note though that the food remains as traditional as ever, in fact, with some ‘new’ additions seeking to convey to diners the wholesome flavours of the good old days. On a recent drive to Mysuru, I stopped by for a delicious breakfast of nourishing porridge, kuchalakki (boiled rice) ganji, tenginkai haalu (coconut milk) ganji, ragi (finger millet) ambli, and also tasted a scrumptious neer dosa made of the very special Rajamudi rice, and their much-favoured kotte kadubu. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care, stay safe and happy eating! 

Kotte Kadubu
Soft and slightly grainy, the kadubu is a much-sought-after breakfast delicacy here; savour it with their flavourful south canara sambar and spicy ‘kai’ chutney
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
8/10

Thenginkai Ganji
Rice soaked in coconut milk and topped with a lashing of ghee. Pleasant in its aroma, flavour and texture, this is a porridge to savour if you’d like something light post a heavy meal the evening before. The cucumber served alongside provides an element of crunch. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
7/10

Kuchalakki Ganji
Boiled rice, sourced from Kundapur, cooked simply with salt and served with a drizzle of hot ghee. Comforting in its nourishing flavours, the rice retains its form and is soft to the bite, having lent some of its starchy heft to the broth. The hand pounded chutney of green chillies, fresh coconut and rock salt provides a spicy edge to the ganji. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
8/10

Ragi Ambli
The cumin is dominant in its flavour in this earthy but sumptuous broth of finger millets. There is also a delicate tinge of green chilli heat and pepper. 
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
7/10

Neer Dosa
The Rajamudi rice lends a brownish tinge to the dose, and also a crusty crunch. The dose is roasted with generous lashings of ghee, ensure you ask for your dose to be kadak. The flavours are quite unlike a traditional neer dose; although enjoyable on its own when hot, the bela kai, jaggery with fresh grated coconut makes for a delicious companion. If you like a touch of spice, there is the chutney too.
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
9/10

Filter coffee
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3)
8/10


Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 7am through 930pm, open all days. 
Note: On google maps, the eatery comes up as MTR SHivalli restaurant, it has no connection to MTR restaurants. Google maps will take you to the eatery on the left hand side of the highway enroute to Mysuru; however the eatery that we visited is on the opposite side a few metres down the road.

https://goo.gl/maps/yiV2cW3wQy3RPDdE9.title: Lunch At LAKSHMAN MESS | Mysore’s Famous Naati (Local) Non Veg Eatery |Mutton Pulav, Curries & Fries
https://goo.gl/maps/yiV2cW3wQy3RPDdE9.description:
#mysuru #lakshmanmess #muttonpulav

popular eatery in mysuru, must-try, non vegetarian, naati style cuisine, local, affordable, mutton pulav, mutton curry, mutton fry, chicken kebab, khaima unde, inspiring story, mysore 

Armed with recipes gleaned from his mother, Lakshman quit his job at a spice shop, to begin a small pushcart operation to serve the non-vegetarian delicacies of his home. Bit by bit, the reputation of his food grew, and after 20 years of eking out a living on the streets, Lakshman was finally able to move into a tiny shop where customers could finally dine away from the bustle of the street. A few years later, the landlord wanted his space back, and faced with no option, he tore down his home to build a permanent space for Lakshman Mess. A eatery that has all of Mysuru thronging here for their honestly-priced limited menu that includes a delicately flavoured pulav, homestyle meaty preparations cooked by Lakshman and his son, Satya, with masalas ground at home. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care, stay safe and happy eating! 

Chicken Kebab
Mild in its flavours, the batter has a flavourful crunch that could have enlivened the taste of the kebab had it seeped all the way into the meat.
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2)
7/10

Mutton Chops
Chunks of meat that have a bit of bite, cooked in a delicious masala that is dominant in the flavour notes of coriander and mint, and the aroma of the special spice blend. The pepper coconut milk adds a layer of creamy warmth. This is the sort of dish that makes for an appropriate side dish to taste with the demure pulav. 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4)
9/10

Mutton Pulav
Delicately flavoured and moist, the Lakshman Mess pulav employs a combination of the long-grained basmati and short-grained rice varieties. You taste the faint edge of the green chili alongside the mint and coriander, the whole spices too aren’t the sort that dominate the palate. The meat is tender and juicy. I loved the pulav as is for its demure character, but if you like yours spicy, savour it with the meaty curries.
Rs. 150 (usd 2.1)
9/10

Kaima
Minced mutton balls simmered in a spicy gravy, spicy when compared to the mutton curry and pulav. 
Rs. 50/ 100 (usd 0.7/ 1.4) for half/ full portion
8/10

Mutton Fry
Curry leaves meet soy sauce in this mutton stir-fry, a dish created for the benefit of locals who wanted something different, I found this a slightly discordant fit on the Lakshman mess menu.
Rs. 105 (usd 1.5) 
7.5/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

Note: The mutton pulav and boti is quite popular and runs out soon, get there early to taste it..

Every city has its popular morning traditions, Mysuru too has its share of them. A delicious one though seems to be that of going for a long walk around Kukkarahalli lake followed by a steaming, hot breakfast at a food rickshaw, Upahara Darshini, popularly known as Deepu Gaadi. The popular draw here is the set masala, smaller than your usual dosa, perhaps to let its fans indulge in more than one of these scrumptious beauties. On a recent dash into Mysuru, I took time out to experience half of this popular tradition, no points for guessing which half, followed by a delicious cup of filter kaapi. Hope you enjoy this breezy watch. Take care, stay safe and happy eating!
 
Breakfast At Upahara Darshini (Deepu Gaadi)
I paid Rs. 70 (usd 1) for a single thatte idli with a vade, and a plate of set masala dose. The thatte idli is soft, a bit pasty, but goes well with the chutney. The set masala dosa though is the dish to try here. The dose is well roasted, crisp and translucent in the centre, revealing flecks of a spicy red chutney smeared within. 
8/10 overall 

Filter Coffee At Mysuru Kaapi
The coffee is thick, strong and just the sort of beverage to wash down an indulgent ghee-laden breakfast.
Rs. 12 (usd 0.2)
8/10

https://g.page/bannurmilitaryhotel?share.title: Tasting Karnataka’s Famous BANNUR MUTTON In Bannur | Bandur Sheep | Lunch At BANNUR MILITARY HOTEL
https://g.page/bannurmilitaryhotel?share.description:
#bannurmutton #biryani #karnataka

bannur mutton explained, bandur sheep, bandur village, malavalli, mandya, bannur, mysore, mutton biryani, mutton fry, mutton kheema, bannur military hotel, ramaswamy hotel, mutton meal

The Bannur mutton, Karnataka’s most prized mutton, isn’t actually from Bannur. It is the meat of an indigenous variety of sheep that hails from Bandur, a village located between Malavalli and Bannur near Mysuru. Prized for its juicy tender meat, the sheep was traditionally sold in village shanties in Bannur, ergo the acquired moniker, Bannur. I drove to Bannur to learn more about this sheep and also catch a mutton meal at a family eatery, Bannur Ramaswami Military Hotel, that showcases this very special meat in its homestyle preparations. Hope you enjoy this episode, stay safe and happy eating! 

Nati Koli Kurma
The chicken has a bit of a chew, a character of the free range chicken, there’s a bit of skin too that adds to the flavourful character of the homestyle curry, which is the sort that goes well with the ragi mudde.
Rs. 110 (usd 1.5) 
8/10

Kaima Sambar
Dumplings of rough-ground mutton simmered in a curry, the meat has a springy bite to it. There is also some dil that lends its aroma to the meat balls. 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4) 
8.5/10

Mutton Fry
The fat of the Bannur mutton is ribonned through the meat that is deep in its slightly salty, savoury flavours. The curry isn't too spicy, and is quite happy playing second fiddle to the flavour of the meat.
Rs. 150 (usd 2.1) 
8.5/10

Bannur Mutton Biryani
You can nose the kasoori methi (dried fenugreek) in the aroma of the biryani, there’s the warming heat of the red chillies and spices that you can taste on the palate, a touch of tang from the tomatoes… the kolam rice is tasty all in itself, also having absorbed the character of the meat. The meat is soft and moist, deep pink in its colour and veined with fat. This is a biryani you should eat hot, do not allow it to cool down for the fat tends to congeal. 
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2) 
9/10 

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

must try idli shop, kote idli, popular village style wood fire idlis, kempu chutney, red chutney, kanakapura, kanakapura road, karnataka, near bengaluru, bangalore, idli chutney, popular breakfast, inspiring story, culinary tradition

After completing the 10th grade, a young lad decided to help his father in their village idli shop in Kanakapura, 60 kilometres from Bengaluru. Half a century on, Mr. Ramchandra has remained steadfast to his father’s culinary tradition, steaming fragrant idlis over a wood fire. A one-man army, he procures the ingredients, prepares the wood to fuel the decades-old stove, soaks the rice and lentils, grinds and carefully ferments the batter, before rising at 4am each morning to make a spicy chutney, and steam over 3000 idlis, 500 in a batch, that run out before noon! Working with the energy and enthusiasm that is hard to imagine in a modern-day sextagenarian, Ramchandra swears by the philosophy of “cheap and best”, in his words, selling four piping-hot idlis for only Rs. 10, or Rs. 2.50 a piece! The quality and appeal of the soft, fluffy idlis are such that patrons don't mind a two-hour drive just to breakfast at this old-fashioned Kote Idli Mane. Hope you enjoy this episode, stay safe and happy eating!

Idlis
The idlis are soft and porous, yielding with a slightly pasty texture in its weight. The size of the idlis are such that you can happily savour about four to six without feeling its burden. The spicy, roasted gram and red chilli chutney makes for a delicious accompaniment to the fragrant idlis. 
Rs. 10 (usd 0.1) for four idlis
9/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 630am to 12noon
Note: Do not be misled by another Kote Idli shop that has opened at the entrance of the street where the original Kote Idli is located. Venture into the lane to find the original Kote Idli, a nondescript village house, where you will find Mr. Ramchandra preparing the idlis.

https://goo.gl/maps/ofKkRxRW9uwhv4XY8.description:
#biryani #jonnebiryani #bangalore

popular jonne biryani shop, donne biryani, bengaluru biryani, jayanagar, mutton biryani, chicken biryani, mutton chops, chilli chicken, chicken curry, leg piece, mutton kheema, inspiring story, jayanagar, bangalore

As the oldest son in his family of modest means, Ningaraju was compelled to look for work as a student. His fondness for food and his ability to recall the flavour of dishes from local eateries led him to set up a pushcart on the outskirts of Bengaluru, serving a self-taught village-style biryani. In the beginning, “things were difficult, sometimes humiliating and marked by periods of self-doubt”, recalls Raju, as he is popularly known. Giving up though wasn’t an option, driven also by the necessity to provide for his family. Slowly, the popularity of his mild-flavoured biryani served in cups of dried banana leaves, jonne, grew, and so did the scale of his enterprise. Today, this resilient entrepreneur’s Halli Jonne Biryani occupies prime real estate in Jayanagar, South Bengaluru, and is frequented by over 500 customers on any given day. I catch up with Raju as he makes the biryani before sitting down to a tasting of most of the dishes on the limited menu here. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay safe and happy eating!

Kaal Soup
The soup is peppery, infused with the freshness of coriander.
Rs. 150 (usd 2.1)
8/10

Khaima Goju
The mutton mince is coarse, there’s a rustic rawness to the masala that is smoothed by the fluffy texture of the idli.
Rs. 130 (usd 1.8)
8.5/10

Chicken Leg Piece
Cooked soft and tender to the bone, you can taste the pungency of ginger garlic that’s softened by the acidity of tomatoes.
Rs. 130 (usd 1.8)
8/10

Mutton Fry
Some of the meat is soft and tender, with a bit of fat, others have a bit of a bite. You can taste the coriander and the pointed heat of green chillies in the masala. The flavours are mild but satisfying.
Rs. 140 (usd 1.9)
9/10

Mutton Liver Fry
The peas make for a nice touch in this gentle gravy; some of the liver pieces though were a bit tough.
Rs. 130 (usd 1.8)
7.5/10

Chilli Chicken
An unusual chilli chicken, you can taste the fresh flavours of the green chilli as opposed to its heat. The mildest chilli chicken I have ever tasted.
Rs. 120 (usd 1.6)
8.5/10

Chicken Kabab
The kabab is scrumptious and flavourful, the chicken is moist and seasoned well, but doesn’t hold on to the spicing of the batter.
Rs. 120 (usd 1.6)
7/10

Chicken Biryani
The seeraga samba rice is stained pastel yellow with a tinge of green, reminding one that this biryani hasn’t borne the brunt of a masala overload. Not the sort of biryani that one will smell from a mile away, the flavours though are the sort that reveal to the palate the ingredients that have gone into its making. You can taste the tingling heat of the green chilli, the freshness of the coriander and mint, the veil of fragrance from the spices register. A biryani that also brings to the fore the flavour of the seeraga samba rice. If you like it spicy, you may need to taste it with the curries that are served alongside the biryani. 
Rs. 140 (usd 1.9)
8.5/10

Mutton Biryani
The mutton has rounded off the flavours of biryani, as opposed to the chicken version. The meat is tender and moist, its fat laden flavours the sort that compels one to draw a bit of the meat in every scoop of the rice. These biryanis are perhaps the lightest donne biryanis one has tasted.
Rs. 180 (usd 2.5)
9/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 730am to 4pm; 6pm to 10pm
Note: Closed on Mondays. This is a rather busy restaurant, prepare to share tables if you get one, there is a stand and eat option too for those in a hurry. If you’d like to savour the Halli Jonne fare in peace, best to takeaway or order in. 
ADDRESS -  Halli Jonne Biryani, #44, 4, 13th Main Rd, opp. BHS College, 4th T Block East, KV Layout, Jayanagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560011; tel: +91 2663 3886/ 96637 11666

#AmmaHotel #Kozhikode #GourmetOnTheRoad

Most Popular Fish Fry and Fish Meal Restaurant in Kozhikode, Amma Hotel, Ayakora (Kingfish) Fry, Chembali (Red Snapper) Fry, Fish Meal

Come lunchtime and locals in Kozhikode (Calicut) flock to this eatery set in a home in the tiny bylanes of Puthiyara. What draws the crowd here is their Ayakora or Kingfish fry and their satisfying fish meal served on a banana leaf.

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna visits this fish fry icon and after a tour of the kitchen where fish are slathered with a secret masala, lashings of coconut oil and fried over a rubber wood fire, sits down for a sumptuous meal.   

AYAKORA (KINGFISH) FRY
a much loved fish in the city, found in almost every eatery. Served here with a thick layer of a spirited masala slathered on a thick slice of kingfish, the bite of the masala has almost tamed the flavour of the fish. Slightly salty and redolent with the aroma of coconut oil, the fish fry masala is also a great accompaniment to be savoured with the rice and lentil curry. 
rs 160. (usd 2.2)
9.5/10

CHEMBALI (RED SNAPPER) FRY
a plump piece of red snapper naped with the Amma Hotel masala. Since this is a meatier fish than the ayakora, the masala doesn’t penetrate all the way in. if you like your fish fry robustly flavoured the ayakora is for you. but if you like it spicy and still want to enjoy the flavour of the fish the red snapper is what you should be trying. 
rs 150. (usd 2.1)
9/10


FISH MEALS
The swollen grains of kuruva rice are the perfect medium to carry the flavours of a tasty vegetable paruppu curry and also tame the aggression of the spices in the fish fry masala. For a mere 50 rupees, this unlimited meal that includes a simple choora (tuna) curry, valakaya (raw banana) upperi and rasam, is a meal that provides nourishment, satisfaction and taste!
rs 50. (usd 0.7)
8.5/10

https://goo.gl/maps/exShmuxjT6EZisK49.description:
#Rahmath Hotel #Gourmet On The Road #Kozhikode

Kozhikode’s Famous Rahmath Hotel Biryani, Chicken, Mutton and Beef Biryani, Mutton Stew, Surprise Collab with Venezuelan-American blogger, Volpe Where Are You

A much-loved biryani destination in Kozhikode is Rahmath Hotel, famous for its meaty biryani, led by beef and mutton. Although they offer many varieties of biryani including chicken, fish, prawns, mussels and squid, it’s the meat biryanis that draw in serpentine queues of people especially on weekends.

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna meets Mohammed Suhail, 2nd generation owner of Rahmath Hotel and explores the making of the biryani before sitting down to a sumptuous biryani meal and a surprise collab with Carlos Volpe, a visiting Venezuelan blogger from Miami who produces insightful destination stories that make for an interesting watch. Do follow his travel vlogs on his channel, Volpe Where Are You https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcPVzEbEIv1GUl_c4owKuhg


Mutton stew 
An aromatic stew, the meat has soaked up the lush creaminess of the coconut milk and the savouriness of the onions which also lend a gentle bite. the potatoes in the stew also add to the body of this dish. The meat pieces are tender and thoughtfully sized small, make this a dish that’s convenient to share. Enjoy this with soft, puffy, rice pathiris. 
rs. 140 (usd 1.8); pathri rs. 9 (usd 0.1 ) for each
8.5/10

Kallumakaya Fry
Cooked in a thick gravy made of onions, tomatoes, green chillies, the kallumakaya or mussels are cooked to the perfect texture that results in a juicy, yielding bite of this mollusc. This preparation displays a harmonious balance of savoury, sweet, sour, the warmth that comes from slivers of ginger, and is perfect to be mopped up with the rice pathiri.
rs. 155 (usd 2.0) 
10/10

Chicken Biryani
A steaming hot biryani, served with lemon and dates pickle, raita and salad, as typical to the region. The white leghorn chicken is cooked twice, first in the masala and next, as the biryani simmers on dum. The bird is juicy and moist. The flavour of the biryani is quite gentle, if you like it spicy, you can always perk things up with the lemon date and chilli pickle.
rs. 155 (usd 2.0 ) 
8.5/10

Mutton Biryani
This one-dish meal is a happy celebration of flavours. the meat, coated in a robust masala, is cooked to perfect doneness and is a juicy pink inside. the tomatoes lend a gentle acidity, thereby a unique to the biryani. you can never tire of a good biryani and this is definitely one of those.
rs. 230 (usd 2.9) 
10/10

Beef Biryani
A flavourful biryani that jolts your senses awake. you can savour the hearty presence of the meat in the rice. the meat is tender, has a salty savouriness that complements the spices in the masala. you definitely taste the fulsome meat broth in every grain of rice. 
rs. 110 (usd 1.4) 
10/10

Armed with the recipe for a crowd-pleasing manchurian sauce that he learnt from a chinese cook, 16 year-old Ravi set out with an auto 21 years ago to serve gobi manchurian in the South Bengaluru neighbourhood of Banashankari. Two decades on, Ravi Gobi seems to rule the heart of gobi manchurian lovers in the city, as evidenced by the number of customers who throng his vegetarian sidewalk eatery each evening. I caught up with Ravi and some of his happy patrons over an extended manchurian tasting session recently, where I savoured not only his popular cauliflower and cabbage versions, but also an equally appetising, babycorn, mushroom and potato variation too. Hope you enjoy this episode, stay safe and happy eating!

Each dish on the Ravi Gobi menu is prepared fresh to order, every plate served piping hot and therefore necessitating a wait of 10 to 15 minutes. The gobi or potato/ mushroom/ baby corn, fried fresh, dressed in a chilli-salt spice mix to make the dry version, or tossed in a savoury manchurian sauce that has the fresh zing of coriander, green chillies, ginger, garlic and onions.

https://goo.gl/maps/s93eS1YseBT6Sdoy7.title: This Man ‘Invented’ The WHITE PAANI PURI! Tasting BANGARPET CHAAT At Ramesh Chit Chat In Bangarapet
https://goo.gl/maps/s93eS1YseBT6Sdoy7.description:
#chaat #bangarapet #karnataka

bangarpet chaat, chaat innovation, white paani, vegetarian, white paani puri, pani puri, masala puri, sev puri, bangarpet tikki, pot gulkand salad, pizza paani puri, street food, pani puri, bangarapet, kolar district, kolar gold fields, kgf, karnataka

Son of R. Panduranga Setty, who is said to have begun the Bangarpet Chaat tradition in 1974 in Bangarapet, named so (Bangar = gold, pete = town) for its importance as a town that connected the erstwhile Kolar gold fields to Bengaluru, 80 kilometres away, young Ramesh, wasn’t happy just continuing with the family legacy. A desire to create something new led to the invention of the ‘white paani’, a clear liquid that though as innocuous-looking as water, packs a potent, spicy punch. And thus began the tradition of the Bangarpet Paani Puri, that has spawned a few hundred namesakes in Karnataka. Ramesh however continues to operate out of his tiny shop in a bylane in Bangarapet, serving customers personally and experimenting constantly to add to his spicy, tangy repertoire. I spend an evening with him, tasting his wares, and return impressed with his childlike enthusiasm that doesn’t seem to have waned in the least despite being in the business for nearly four decades, his latest creation, a pizza inspired paani puri! Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

White Paani Puri
A simple assemblage of green peas, onions, carrots and coriander, stuffed in a semolina and flour puri, topped with the potent ‘white paani’. The spiciness of paani though is toned down by the creaminess of the peas and the crunch of the onions. A simple, clean flavoured paani puri that allows one to appreciate every component singularly, as well as in its completeness. 
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3)
8.5/10

Special Dahi Puri
Embellished with rose petals, this chaat is a riot of flavours and textures. The crispiness of the chaat components and the spice of the masala play second fiddle to the creamy, sweet richness of the yoghurt that is fortified with Horlicks, milk powder and sugar. 
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
10/10

Floating Paani Puri
The floating paani puri is a spicy affair, the spicy white paani goes into the puri and also floats the puri. The moist crispness of the puri is endearing as is the crunch of the spiced peanuts and the sev, despite the fresh crunch of the onion, cucumber and tomato, there is no getting away from the chilli heat of the sea of white paani. 
Rs. 40 (usd 0.6)
9.5/10

Tikki Masala Bangarpet
A take on the Bengaluru masala puri, this is puri topped with spicy chutney, sweet chutney, peas, garam masala, squeeze of lime, onions, carrots, coriander, sev and puffed rice. It has all the components that you would expect to find in a chaat without being overdressed! 
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4)
8.5/10

Special Sev Puri
The flat papdi base for this chaat is fried in ghee which gives it a rich, ‘biscuity’ bite embellished with the nuttiness of sesame seeds. You can taste the edge of garlic in the chutney that the fresh ingredients are tossed in. 
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
9/10

Bhelpuri
A typical bhel but with the addition of the peas gravy that goes into every plat of chaat here, I found this rendered the puffed rice soggy and that didn’t quite work for me.
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3)
7/10

Pizza Paani Puri
I doff my hat to Ramesh on his latest attempt to innovate and bring a foreign flavour to the bylanes of Bangarapet. However, with regards to its taste and appeal, some may fancy it, yet others question its existence. 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4)
7/10

Spiced Amla
Rs. 30
7/10

Pot Gulkand Salad
Rs. 30
8/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

https://goo.gl/maps/omGT3jUSr3BHkeUT6.title: Blockbuster KGF - KAVERI GODAVARI FOODS | Tasty Curries, Dosa, Parotta Cooked In Wood Pressed Oil!
https://goo.gl/maps/omGT3jUSr3BHkeUT6.description:
#foodtruck #tamilnadufood #bangalore

traditional tamil nadu, salem style, non-vegetarian, street fare, food truck, kalakki, mutton kari dosa, nati chicken, mutton chops, brain fry, pepper fry, podi dosa, east bengaluru, bengaluru 

When Prabhu, an automobile engineer with a major car company chose to pursue his entrepreneurial calling in food, a food truck didn't come across as a surprise to his father who encouraged him to pursue his dreams. After getting his hands on a Tempo Traveller, he drove it to Pune to fabricate a food truck that would serve up the meaty cuisine of his Tamil heritage with a smattering of influences from Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka as well. Back in Bengaluru, this culinary enterprise on wheels, Kaveri Godavari Foods, is slowly but surely gaining popularity in the neighbourhood it is parked in. Adding to its appeal is the fact that all dishes here are prepared at Prabhu’s home and cooked in wood-pressed oils extracted in the family’s oil mill. I drive 20 kilometres to East Bengaluru to catch up with this passionate engineer and experience the streetfood vibe here whilst savouring a bunch of tasty preparations - egg kothu parotta, kalakki podi dosa, mutton parotta, chops, nati chicken, brain fry and more. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay safe and happy eating!
 
Mutton Brain Fry
Tava-fried with eggs in an aromatic, homemade masala, this is the dish to taste if you love brain meat; it quite simply melts in the mouth. The eggs also help make more of the dish that is perfect, mopped up with some parotta.
Rs. 150 (usd 2)
9/10

Kuzhambu Kalakki
A Salem egg staple, egg cooked skilfully such that it encloses within its folds a gooey, spicy egg mixture. Traditionally, this is eaten at the end of a non-vegetarian meal in Salem.
Rs. 15 (usd 0.2)
7.5/10

Mutton Kari Dosa
A fluffy dosa topped with coarse mutton mince, eggs and served with a spicy curry, this is the sort that makes for a satisfying one-dish meal or a big late-night snack.
Rs. 140 (usd 1.9)
7.5/10

Mutton Chops
Goat chops cooked in a gravy rich in the flavour of dark-roasted spices, this is a dish that will bring me back to KGF. The meat is the sort that peels away from the bone in a juicy, peppery bite. Order a plain dosa to soak up the curry.
Rs. 150 (usd 2)
10/10

Podi Dosa
One can smell the nutty aroma of the peanut oil that this dose has been roasted in. The dosa is smeared with an Andhra podi whilst being fried to a near crisp. A dose that goes ‘crunch’ from the first bite to the last, with a slightly tangy edge.
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
9/10

Nati Chicken Pepper Fry
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
7.5/10

Chicken Stuffed Parotta
Rs. 100 (usd 1.9)
7.5/10

https://g.page/swad-n-swad?share.title: SWAD - N - SWAD | This RAJASTHANI Couple Is Serving Delicious, HOME-COOKED Traditions Of Their Land!
https://g.page/swad-n-swad?share.description:
#homecooked #rajasthanifood #bangalore

rajasthani food, vegetarian, non vegetarian, besan gatta, sev tamatar, lahsuni bhindi, tangdi kebab, rathodi chicken, junglee maas, laal maas, makki ki roti, roti, kheer,  inspiring story

Hailing originally from Surajpura Lotiyana village in Ajmer district of Rajasthan, Jithender and his wife, Renuka Tak, moved to Bengaluru with their young children having lost their automotive shop in the Ahmedabad earthquake of 2001. Facing financial difficulty, a chance encounter with a visiting relative at an exhibition who was looking for food to be catered led to the couple setting up a home-cooked meal enterprise. A family-run operation, they would shop, cook and deliver the food themselves, with their children lending a hand with the chores too.  However, work from home and the current situation bought their livelihood to a standstill yet again! Not one to give up though, this family has set-up a small one-table eatery in the east Bengaluru neighbourhood of Kaggadasapura, primarily to serve as a takeaway point for their delicious home-cooked Rajasthani fare, both vegetarian and non-vegetarian. I drive here to chat with the couple, watch them cook a laal maas, sev tamatar and other dishes, before tucking into a delicious meal coupled with the warm hospitality of this Rajput family that has an inspiring, never-give-up attitude. Hope you enjoy this episode, stay safe and happy eating!       

Tandoori Chicken Tangdi
Not cooked in a tandoor, but deep-fried and then fire-cooked with some ghee and spices, the chicken legs, marinated for hours in a spice mix, make for a juicy, char-smoked appetiser.
Rs. 120 (usd 1.6) for 2 pieces.
8/10

Lahsuni Bhindi Fry
Cooked with plenty of browned garlic, green chillies, this is a flavourful, though slightly spicy bhindi fry. 
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2)
7.5/10

Sev Tamatar
Spicy sev (chickpea fritters) are cooked in a tangy, thick tomato gravy that tones down the heat of the sev. The sev garnish also adds an element of crunch and spiciness to this simple but tasty preparation.
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2)
8/10

Besan Gatta

https://goo.gl/maps/9DLhEGH91svQpPWc6.title: GOPALJEE CAFÉ | She Quit Her Job To Bring Authentic DELHI Style CHOLE BHATURE To BENGALURU!
https://goo.gl/maps/9DLhEGH91svQpPWc6.description:
#vegetarian #northindianfood #bangalore

gopaljee cafe, delhi chole bhature, delhi style food, north indian, vegetarian, paneer bhaturey, chole, suvigya bansal, passion enterprise, inspiring story

Corporate executive Suvigya Bansal and her entrepreneur husband would scour Bengaluru in search of an authentic Delhi-style chole bhature. When they found none, she decided to quit her job and set up a small eatery that would endeavour to dish out the flavours of their favourite chola bhatura from Delhi. And so seasoned cooks were hired from Delhi, a complex 58-spice masala developed to ensure authenticity of taste, the right size of chickpea sourced to convey the flavour of the spices, et al. Barely had this enterprise found its feet early last year when covid struck! I made a surprise visit to Gopaljee Café one afternoon in response to a plea from the eatery. Suffice to say my conversation with this passionate lady entrepreneur and tasting of the puffy bhature and ‘mazedaar’ chole compelled us to return to film an episode of Gourmet On The Road. Hope you enjoy this one, enough to pay them a visit if possible. Stay safe and happy eating!  

Chole Bhature
The bhatura is light and puffy yet with a bit of strength, to match the tenacity of the 56-spice blend masala that is delicately warming yet has enough depth to linger on the palate. The chickpeas, cocooned in the flavour of the masala, a seasoning of oil, chilli and spices, are stained deep brown by some amla and cooked such that they retain their shape yet yield in a creamy texture to the bite. The mandatory topping of dry, spiced aloo (potatoes) adds a slightly tangy flavour to the dish. If you like it spicy, go for generous bites of the green chilli pickle in between mouthfuls of the chole bhature. If you like paneer, opt for the paneer chole bhature, which arrives with a paneer and coriander mince, stuffed into the bhaturas, and also atop the chole.
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4) per plate, plain 
Rs. 125 (usd 1.7) per plate, with paneer
9/10

Lassi
The lassi is thick and creamy, garnished with nuts, and also provides cooling respite if you have ingested more of the green chilli than you can handle.
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7) 
8/10

Gulab Jamun
The way to end your meal if you have a sweet tooth is with their perfectly browned gulab jamuns.
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8) for two pieces
8/10 

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

Note: The chole bhature are served between 9am and 830pm; the bhaturas are fried fresh upon order, so it may involve a bit of a wait especially if crowded.

https://goo.gl/maps/sSEHEN17cjxtbBZg6.title: Move Over ‘KFC’, Krishnappa Gowda’s Fried Chicken (GFC) Is Here! NEW GOWDA’S FRIED CHICKEN Bangalore
https://goo.gl/maps/sSEHEN17cjxtbBZg6.description:
#friedchicken #biryani #bangalore

gowda fried chicken, fried chicken, gowda fried chicken, gfc chicken, chicken kebab, mandya recipe, mutton biryani, biryani, chicken 65, mysore road, bengaluru, bangalore

Fed up with labour problems in his vegetarian eatery of 35 years, Krishnappa Gowda closed doors 10 years ago to open a shop selling fried chicken, cooked by him to a secret recipe influenced by his Mandya roots. Such is the tantalising taste of this chicken kebab, that its fans drive across the city to stand and eat at this eatery located in a nook of Mysore road! An astute entrepreneur, and mindful of the popularity of his spice mix, Gowda has also developed packaged versions of the masala for those who would like to satisfy their fried chicken cravings at home. I make the trek to GFC and return convinced that this is perhaps the best local fried chicken I have tasted to date. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

Gowda’s Fried Chicken
Tender chicken, marinated for six hours in an aromatic, secret spice mix, Gowda’s Fried Chicken is the sort that is tantalisingly tasty. The masala serves to coat the kebab with a delicately spiced crust and seal its juicy bite; the chicken is cooked perfectly down to the bone. This is the sort of kebab that needs no accompaniment in the form of a chutney or onions.
Rs. 480 per kilo (usd 6.5)
10/10

Chicken 65
A tasty kebab in itself, slightly spicier when compared to the GFC. The masala has formed a bit of a thick crust in parts as the chicken is fried, which lends a spicy kick. And then there are those parts where it is the juiciness of the bird that gushes through the palate. 
Rs. 480 per kilo (usd 6.5)
8.5/10

Mutton Biryani
The biryani here, made of basmati and kollam rice is served in a sumptuous portion, and is rich in the flavour of the masala when hot. Some pieces of the meat are soft and slide off the bone, and ribboned in rich fat, yet others with a bit of bite. As the biryani cools down, the savoury fat-laden flavour of the meat takes over.
Rs. 180 (usd 2.4)
8.5/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 7am to 10pm
Note: Most customers here take away the food, however, we recommend that the Gowda Fried Chicken is best consumed at the eatery, hot off the oil.

popular hassan restaurant, hotel mamatha, gowda food, katla fish fry, mutton biryani, mutton korma, ragi mudde, chicken fry, leg piece, gowda cuisine, naati cuisine, hassan food, mangalore hassan bangalore highway

I often find that the most memorable meals are usually those that happen rather unexpectedly. Like this delicious lunch that we savoured at  this popular eatery in Hassan, 210 kms from Bengaluru, a couple of months ago. Guided by suggestions from our viewers, I didn't quite know what to expect when I walked into a bustling lunch session here late one afternoon on our way back from Mangalore. But the memory of the rustic, homestyle Gowda dishes that I tasted here, lingers to this day. Suffice to say I would happily make the 210 km drive to Mamatha Hotel in a heartbeat just to savour the food all over again. Hope you enjoy the episode. I take this opportunity to wish you and your family a fabulous 2021. Take care and stay safe.

Katla Fry
Coated in a delicious spiced batter that complements the earth flavours of the freshwater fish, the katla fry is a popular dish here for all the right reasons. The crispened skin and the masala work well to cradle the fleshy fish.
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2) for 2 pieces
9/10

Mutton Korma
Notwithstanding bits of fat ribboned through it, the juicy chunks of meat have a bit of a bite. And as you chew on it, you are rewarded with the robust flavours of the curry. Rs. 170 (usd 2.3)

Flecks of fat abound in this biryani, that is redolent with the aroma of mint and coriander, and do well to coat the zesty, hard-spice laced rice with its unctuousness. The meat is mild in its flavour and benefits from being combined with the rice.
Rs. 210 (usd 2.9)

https://goo.gl/maps/nGsLxrfuW4QgLe5W6.title: Flavours of East Godavari At KAKINADA SUBBAIAH GARI HOTEL Bangalore | 30-Dish Vegetarian Andhra Meal
https://goo.gl/maps/nGsLxrfuW4QgLe5W6.description:
#vegetarian #lunch #subbayyagarihotel

popular andhra restaurant, new restaurant, andhra food, subbayya gari hotel, subbaiah gari hotel kakinada, east godavari, kakinada cuisine, andhra sweets, subbaiah hotel hyderabad, subbaiah hotel, banana leaf meal, special lunch, andhra bhojanam, brookefield, whitefield, bangalore, bengaluru

In the year 1950, Subbayya Gaaru opened a small 10-seater mess in Kakinada in the East Godavari region of Andhra Pradesh to serve honestly-priced food of the land. Legend has it that he would treat each customer as a guest visiting his home and leave no stone unturned in feeding them. Tales of his legendary hospitality and traditional fare soon spread far and wide and this tiny eatery evolved into the legendary Subbaiah Gari chain of restaurants. I visit their newly opened Bengaluru outpost where I explore the kitchen and the making of some special dishes before savouring a lavish 30-item banana leaf meal that is served with dollops of neyi (ghee) and old-fashioned hospitality that can leave you bursting at the seams! I also brush up on some Telugu along the way. ;-)  Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe. Happy eating! 

Special Vegetarian Meal
If you’re looking to savour the traditional flavours of the North Godavari region in Andhra Pradesh, look no further than this special 30-dish Andhra Bhojanam. You begin with tantalising sweets like annavaram prasadam, poornam boorelu, junnu, savoury fries like the tamalapaku (betel leaf) bajji, garelu, before moving on to the procession of curries, lentils, tantalising rice preparations like the pullihora (tamarind rice), panasa (raw jackfruit) mukkala biryani and chutneys. The list of dishes served is far too long to be contained within this description, but suffice to say the food prepared by the master cooks who have trained in the original Kakinada Subbayya Gaari Hotel will hold your attention. But then, this is also the sort of meal that you need to savour at leisure, in order to do full justice to the dishes that are served with generous dollops of neyi (ghee) and old-fashioned hospitality. 
Rs. 250 (usd 3.4)
9/10


Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: Lunch - 11am to 4pm; Dinner - 7pm to 10pm 
Note: Note: Subbaiah Gari also serves their famous Butta Bhojanam, a takeaway meal bundle that will feed 4 to 6 diners for Rs. 400. Those with a smaller appetite can consider the ‘single meals’ that are priced at Rs. 150 with a limited selection of dishes. Curries are also available at Rs. 50 per portion.

https://goo.gl/maps/5JCb21ECqN1fkDag6.description:
#bangalore #kebabs #curries

new restaurant, restaurant with a cause, inspiring stories, north west frontier cuisine, kebabs, curries, tandoor, sigri, barbeque, vegetarian, non vegetarian, north indian food, koramangala, bengaluru

In the current climate of gloom and doom, Chefs Sanjay Tyagi and Shyam Sundar Bhaskaran, both seasoned culinary professionals with stints in some top Indian kitchens in the country and overseas, have launched a culinary enterprise to not just serve delicious fare but also, more importantly in our opinion, provide livelihoods to chefs and f&b professionals who have lost their jobs at some of the city’s top hotels. The result is Northwest Kebab & Curryhouse, a breezy casual dining restaurant in Koramangala, that is showcasing an interesting repertoire of dishes from the North West Frontier region. Barely a couple of weeks old, and with not too many customers at present, this is certainly an eatery to pencil into your eating-out plans if you are looking to taste “North Indian-style” of food that goes beyond the ubiquitous palak paneer and butter chicken! Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

Mewe Aur Subz Ki Seekh
A delicately spiced kebab that offers the richness of reduced milk solids, dry fruits and the freshness of vegetables that intermingles with the gentle spice of chillies.
Rs. 289 (usd 3.9)
8/10 

Paneer Parathdar
Marinated paneer, that is soft and creamy to the bite, stuffed with a slightly spicy, tangy paste of sun dried tomatoes. 
Rs. 289 (usd 3.9)
8.5/10 

Teekhi Machli
A dish that is a confluence of the North, in the mustard oil, and the South, toasted curry leaves and tamarind, that go to flavour the masala that the tilapia is tava-fried in. 
Rs. 429 (usd 5.8)
9/10 

Tabak Maaz
Tender lamb that is braised in saffron, spices and milk, and then finished with ghee. At Northwest Kebab & Curry House, the braised meat is then coated in a light batter and fried. The juicy succulence of the fat and the ghee is what one tastes on the palate as the meat peels away from the bone. 
Rs. 439 (usd 6)
9/10

Chicken Behari/ Mutton Behari
A moist and gently flavoured grilled morsel of meat with none of the heavy handed spicing that one would associate with a North Indian Kebab. My vote though goes to the mutton version of this kebab where the tenderiser has imparted a creamy texture to the smokey flavours of the meat.
Rs. 389 (usd 5.3)/ Rs. 439 (usd 6)
8.5/10 / 9.5/10

Bhindi Musallam
Slit and spiced tender ladyfingers that are fried and topped with a rich musallam gravy of almonds and heavy cream, and garnished with beaten silver, rose petals and saffron oil. 
Rs. 289 (usd 3.9)
8/10

Methi Malai Kofta
Paneer and potato dumplings stuffed with prunes and nuts, cooked in a tomato and cream based gravy laced with the slightly bitter edge of fresh fenugreek.  
Rs. 339 (usd 4.6)
8.5/10

Murg Shinwari Karahi
A rustic preparation that one would perhaps encounter on a highway stop in the NorthWest, one tastes the untamed flavours of ginger, green chillies, coriander seeds in this chicken dish that is prepared and served in cast iron karahi
Rs. 429 (usd 5.8)
8.5/10

Nalli Rogan E Nishat
If you are a mutton lover, this is a must-order dish here. The curry bears the lip-smacking goodness of tender meat and bone marrow, the meat the sort that not just slides off the bone but almost melts away when placed in the mouth.

https://g.page/iskconhighertaste?share.title: Exploring SATTVIC Cuisine At THE HIGHER TASTE, ISKCON TEMPLE | Food That Satisfies The Soul!
https://g.page/iskconhighertaste?share.description:
#vegetarian #sattvic #krishnatemple

temple cuisine, sattvic cuisine,  indian food, vegetarian food, krishna temple, iskcon, rajajinagar,  bangalore, bengaluru

Temple food to many isn't about mere nourishment but a blessing from the divine. And when temple fare is presented in a culinary experience that is not only rich in its depth of traditions, but also celebrates diversity to appeal to all humanity, it is elevated to food that truly satisfies the soul. In a first on Gourmet On The Road, I experience the philosophy and flavours of Sattvic cuisine at The Higher Taste, a fine dining restaurant located in the serene environment of ISKCON Temple, Bengaluru. This isn’t a typical episode, but then the experience too isn't! Hope you enjoy this very special presentation, take care and stay safe.

Please note:
As a mark of respect to this meal that is served in a temple complex, I have chosen to not rate the dishes in this episode. Thank you.

Nuggekai Rasam
The rasam is flavourful and aromatic, you can taste the sweet lilt of fennel, the warmth of pepper and the weight of the lentils and drumstick drumstick pulp. The floating drumstick kernels add to the appeal of this nourishing broth.
Rs. 165 (usd 2.2)

Multani Paneer Tikka
The paneer is stuffed with the richness of cream and nuts, marinated in yoghurt, saffron and cooked in the tandoor. The peppers provide for a pleasing crunch, and the chaat masala cuts through the dairy richness and refreshes the palate. 
Rs. 325 (usd 4.4)

Potato Milagu Fry
Baby potatoes that are tossed in a sprightly spice mix, loaded with pepper, chilli flakes, cumin, crunchy, fried curry leaves and the fresh tang of lime juice. 
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1)

Mango Rasgulla Chaat
Visualise a chatpata paapdi chaat where the paapdi is replaced with soft rasgullas immersed in the sweetness of mango pulp. If you want to begin your meal on a sweet and spicy note, this is the dish to try. 
Rs. 250 (usd 3.4)    

Raja Bhojanam
Paneer, peas and nuts cooked in a rich cashew, cream and ghee laden curry, topped with a touch of saffron, this curry is a touch of indulgence befitting a king! The spicing is mellow, barring the tingling prick of heat when one bites into a peppercorn. The soft, layered warki paratha makes for a comforting companion to the Raja Bhojanam. If you’d like to add a touch of spice, savour this gravy with the chilli cheese naan, stuffed with mozzarella that bridges to the creamy flavour of the curry, and topped with finely chopped green chillies.
Rs. 285 (usd 3.9)
Warki Paratha - Rs. 80 (usd 1.1)
Chilli Cheese Naan - Rs. 120 (usd 1.6)

Vazhaipoo Murungakai Kozhambu
A ‘coconutty’ curry with fried banana blossoms and drumstick segments. The drumstick segments are a tad fibrous, the banana blossom, deep-fried, lends a bit of a bite to this dish. The curry is thick, rich in its coconut flavours and does well to smother every grain of the rice.
Rs. 285 (usd 3.9)

Vetrilai Thakkali Satham
An unusual rice preparation that brings together the sharp flavours of betel leaves with tomatoes. Although the paan flavours are quite pronounced on the palate, the pulpy freshness of the fresh tomatoes helps cut the astringency of the former. Rs. 280 (usd 3.8)

Elaneer Payasam
A payasam of tender coconut, coconut milk, thickened milk for sweetening, this payasam makes for a pleasing end to the meal at The Higher Taste.
Rs. 210 (usd 2.9)

Paan Ice Cream
A sweet paan that’s blended into a homemade ice cream, this is a ‘beeda’ the customary sweet paan that concludes a festive meal, in a dessert!
Rs.  165 (usd 2.2)

https://goo.gl/maps/oWc6tRDjuCtFz8Ek7.title: Tasting The Must-Try World Famous Hotel Diana Gadbad & Veg Cutlet In Udupi | A Legacy Of 60 Years!
https://goo.gl/maps/oWc6tRDjuCtFz8Ek7.description:
#gadbad #dianarestaurant #udupi 

most popular vegetarian restaurant in udupi, hotel diana, vegetable cutlet, gadbad, ice cream, udupi ice cream, udupi hotel diana, gadbad ice cream, udupi, karnataka

When this enterprise conjured up the name Diana in the sixties, it was meant to sell cool drinks and ice cream in Udupi, then a sleepy town in South Canara. But because cool drinks and ice creams weren’t popular in this sleepy South Canara town those days, the Pai family decided to diversify into snacks. Their first creation, a vegetable cutlet, then a foreign item to the Udupi populace, took nearly five years to curry favour with the locals. Along the way, they also accidentally conjured up an ice cream concoction, the Diana Gadbad. Whilst the early days may have been tough, these 60-year old timeless classics are the most popular items on the menu today. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

Vegetable Cutlet
A potato and beetroot patty that is flavoured with a seasoning of curry leaves, lentils and spices, this cutlet is a delicious medley of flavours and textures. The accompanying homemade chutney and sauce make for worthy companions to this Diana classic.
Rs. 75 (usd 1)
9/10

Diana Gadbad
An accidental invention of this eatery nearly 60 years ago when the restaurant’s founder, Mohandas Pai, put together a concoction of three ice creams, because he had very little quantity of each, topped with cashew nuts to feed a large group of customers who dropped in unexpectedly for ice cream. And because it was prepared in a ‘gadibidi’ (kannada word for ‘hurry’) it came to be known as the Gadbad. A layered creation with strawberry ice cream, eight types of dry fruits, fresh fruits, a special ‘Horlicks’ cake, vanilla cake, no two spoonfuls of this delicious dessert are the same. 
Rs. 120 (usd 1.6)
10/10

https://goo.gl/maps/oWc6tRDjuCtFz8Ek7.summary: This video is about the legendary Hotel Diana in Udupi, Karnataka, and two of their signature dishes: the Vegetable Cutlet and the Diana Gadbad.  Established over 60 years ago, Hotel Diana has become a beloved institution, renowned for its simple yet incredibly flavorful vegetarian fare. The video begins with the history of the restaurant, which started as a humble shop selling cool drinks and ice cream.  When these items failed to gain traction in the then-sleepy town, the Pai family, the founders, decided to introduce snacks, beginning with their now-iconic vegetable cutlet. This unique dish, a blend of potato and beetroot seasoned with curry leaves, lentils, and spices, took nearly half a decade to win over the local palate, ultimately becoming a testament to the family's perseverance and culinary ingenuity.  The Diana Gadbad, a serendipitous creation, emerged from a happy accident.  When a large group of customers arrived unexpectedly, the restaurant’s founder, Mohandas Pai, improvised a dessert using limited quantities of three different ice creams, topping it with cashew nuts. Named ‘Gadbad,’ meaning ‘hurry’ in Kannada, this delightful concoction, featuring layers of strawberry and vanilla ice cream, a variety of dry and fresh fruits, and a special ‘Horlicks’ cake, has become synonymous with the restaurant itself.  The video provides viewers with a glimpse into the making of both dishes, showcasing the fresh, high-quality ingredients and the care taken in their preparation. The host then indulges in both dishes, vividly describing their flavors and textures. He praises the cutlet for its crispy exterior, its soft, flavorful interior, and the delicious accompaniments of homemade chutney and sauce. He marvels at the Gadbad, highlighting the unique experience of encountering different flavors and textures with every bite, from the sweetness of the fruits to the crunch of the nuts and the creaminess of the ice cream and cake. The video concludes with a heartfelt tribute to the enduring legacy of Hotel Diana. Highlighting that the restaurant's popularity stems not just from the delicious food but also from the warm memories associated with it. The host emphasizes the importance of appreciating the history behind iconic dishes like the Gadbad and the cutlet, acknowledging the effort and innovation that went into their creation. The video is a celebration of simple, well-crafted food and the power of culinary tradition to create lasting memories.

https://goo.gl/maps/brxwTRo7GjvqfpkD8.title: POLAMMA’S MESS | This Eatery Serves Tasty, Affordable ANDHRA FOOD & Memories Of A Grandmother’s Love
https://goo.gl/maps/brxwTRo7GjvqfpkD8.description:
#andhrafood #bangalore #bananaleafmeal 

polamma’s mess, popular andhra eatery for working professionals, students, families, vegetarian andhra meal, banana leaf meal, bhojanam, pappu, sambar, rasam, hyderabadi chicken biryani, chicken roast, mutton pepper fry boneless, chicken polamma, fish fry, bangalore, bengaluru

Every city has its celebrated restaurants, these are the ones that everybody knows. And then there are hundreds of tiny eateries that are almost unknown except to those they quietly provide daily sustenance to - office goers, working professionals, students yearning for a taste of home.... However, in the current scenario of work from home, offices and educational institutions being shut, these establishments that once were the lifeline of the communities they served are now finding it difficult to sustain themselves. 

In this episode, I visit one such Bengaluru eatery, Polamma’s Mess, named so by its owner, Jagadeesh Reddy in memory of his late grandmother who raised him as an orphan in a village near Kalahasti, Andhra Pradesh. I hear his poignant account of how this once bustling eatery is barely getting by, which is rather unfortunate given the simple but delicious Andhra vegetarian bhojanam that Polamma’s serves in addition to other meaty sides. I hope you will find within your heart the desire to support eateries like Polamma’s Mess. These need your support today to help keep them on their feet to continue serving the workforce, students, community at large… when things get back to normal in the future. Take care and stay safe.


Veg Meals
My favourite part of the meal here. Simple but satisfying affair of rice served with a nutritious and creamy ‘thottakoora’ pappu, vegetable for the day, sambar, rasam, yoghurt and the staple condiments of pappula podi, ghee and ghongura chutney. The simplicity of the meal is reminiscent of what you will be served in an Andhra home.
Rs. 100 (usd 1.3)
8/10

Chicken Roast 
The chicken is double cooked, first in a deep-flavoured masala and then roasted in ghee with plenty of curry leaves and spices. Moist inside and with a slight roasted crunch, this is a must-order if you like chicken and prefer it sprightly and spicy.. 
Rs. 150 (usd 2)
9/10

Chicken Polamma
This chicken fry is fortified with the richness of cashew paste and red chilli powder, the sort of preparation that will make you sweat if you aren’t accustomed to chilli heat.
Rs. 150 (usd 2)
8/10

Vanjaram Fry
The fish is fried in a tasty masala, albeit thin sliced, the sort that you would expect to find in a mess.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
7.5/10

Mutton Pepper Fry Boneless
The meat is soft, but the flavours of the masala had settled a tad; I also found the cornstarch a bit overwhelming, especially since we didn’t get to it as soon as it arrived on the table.
Rs. 220 (usd 3)
7/10

Chicken Hyderabadi Biryani
The Friday special at Polamma’s Mess is portioned enough to feed one, or two if you precede it with the Andhra veg bhojanam. There is plenty of masala and the chicken is moist and juicy, made in the kacchi akhni style. A recipe picked up by Jagadeesh during his stint in Hyderabad.
Rs. 150 (usd 2)
8/10

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: lunch - 12pm to 330pm; dinner - 7pm to 1030pm
Note: Only lunch service on Sundays; as you may have seen in the video this is a modest eatery sans any frills. For those looking for takeaways, they are available on Swiggy and Zomato too. Located close to Christ College.

https://goo.gl/maps/kqfWPyHB7dycvZbi6.title: Lunch At Mangalore’s Most Popular SEAFOOD Restaurant, MACHALI | Crab Ghee Roast Prawn Fry Fish Curry
https://goo.gl/maps/kqfWPyHB7dycvZbi6.description:
#seafood #popularrestaurant #mangalore

popular seafood restaurant in mangalore, machali restaurant mangalore, manguluru, fish curry, fish fry, ghee roast, fish thaali, crab ghee roast, pomfret masala fry, anjal tava fry, squid ghee roast, alle piao, sardine fry, prawn fry, koliwada, kingfish, top seafood in mangalore

Given its incredible popularity with hundreds of seafood lovers who visit here for the meals, fries and curries everyday, it’s hard to believe that this restaurant is only six years old. I visit this eatery that has the vibe of a busy dining hall to indulge in a humongous meal, and along the way also catch up with its unassuming owner, Vicky Pai, who says his trying experiences as a young executive looking for affordable, homestyle food in a new city, spurred him to open Machali - to serve tasty, homestyle food at affordable prices. And going by my meals at this eatery, I have visited thrice already, and watching fastidious Mangalorans relish the seafood here, Machali certainly delivers, whether one wants to enjoy a sumptuous fish meal and fry for Rs. 150 or splurge Rs. 300. Truly, a democratic seafood restaurant that caters to all.

Fish Thaali
A standard Mangalore fish meal experience, on the plate there is a fish curry with a small piece of fish, some dry vegetables on the side, boiled rice, shrimp chutney, fried sandige and pickle. Servers walk along ladling more fish curry, a simple Konkani style lentil preparation, daali thove, and rasam out of buckets. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
8/10

Taru Buthai
Tiny sardines, fried to delicious scrumptiousness, the sort that you eat whole. Quite tasty!
Rs. 100 (usd 1.3)
8.5/10

Prawn Fry
A robustly-flavoured fresh prawn preparation crusted in a Konkan koliwada masala. Once you get past the spices, you can taste the sweet lilt of the prawns.
Rs. 230
8.5/10

Boneless Crab Ghee Roast
Perfect for those who love crab but don’t want to go through the hassle of de-shelling one. The lush ghee roast masala packs a punch more so against the mild flavours of the crab, the buttery fervour of the ghee brings the spices and the crabmeat together. 
Rs. 280 (usd 3.8)
10/10

Squid Ghee Roast
The squid was cooked to the texture that yielded quite gently to the bite, the masala though, seemed a tad salty to my taste. Perhaps a bit lacking in the ghee. 
Rs. 180 (usd 2.4) 
7.5/10

Alle Piyao
A flavourful Konkani curry made of ginger, onions and fresh coconut. The onions, starring both in the masala and the seasoning, are quite pronounced on the palate, as is a tinge of turmeric and the warmth of the ginger.   
Rs. 130 (usd 1.8)
10/10

Anjal Tava Fry
A plump piece of fish, flakey and pristine in its freshness, crusted with a punchy masala. You can taste the red chilli spice the moment you place the fish in your mouth, but the meaty character of the anjal balances against the spicy hit.  
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
9/10

Pomfret Tava Masala
The pomfret is burdened under the weight of a flavourful masala that has notes of savouriness, heat and sourness, owing to the onions, curry leaves, chillies and tamarind. The fish is moist, poached in a turmeric curry first, before being slathered with the masala in a pan. 
Rs. 300 (usd 4)
9/10

Happy Eating!

https://goo.gl/maps/ufXbWexTE2wEo1Ct7.description:
#popularhighwayrestaurant #mangalorehighway #koppa 

popular restaurant for vegetarian breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner on the bangalore mangalore highway, kunigal, koppa, south indian, breakfast, tiffin, thaali, north indian, sandwich, idli, vada, dosa, dose, coffee, vegetarian

When on the highway, you want to stop for a meal at a place where you will not only get your food piping hot, consistently tasty and sumptuous enough to keep you fortified for the journey, but also in an environment that is clean and hygienic. Swathi Delicacy, located 100 kilometres from Bengaluru on the Mangalore Highway seems to have built a massive following doing precisely that. In a short span of 8 years, this eatery has come to be the preferred dining spot on the route. On a recent trip to Mangalore, I stopped for breakfast here and also caught up with co-owner, Ram Prasad Bhat to find out that his family has a legacy of being in the food service space for nearly half a century. Hope you enjoy the episode, take care and stay safe.


Idli Vada
Idlis served steaming hot, the sort of welcome that would please a traveller. The texture of the idli is grainy, and comes alive when drowned in the deliciously flavourful sambar. The vada is crisp and crunchy, soft and airy inside. The chutney is green-chilli-hot and balances against the slightly sweet notes of the sambar. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
9/10

Kesari Baath
Not decadently burdened with ghee, the kesari baath served here is relatively austere. On the palate, one can taste the comforting, toasty notes of the semolina, mingled with pineapple flecks, fried cashew and raisins.
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4)
8/10

Butter Masala Dose
The masala dose is crisp and kadak, smeared with a spicy red chutney inside and served, topped with a generous dollop of butter. The dose is thick and filling, the sort that would keep one sated for a few hours. The coriander freshness of the potato palya takes centerstage in this masala dose. 
Rs. 80 (usd 1.1)
9/10

Open Butter Masala Dose
A fluffy open dose, thick and ‘spongy’ in its texture, with a generous sprinkling of a sweet and spicy, powdery-crunchy podi that assumes a caramelised note when the dosa is flipped over on the tava. Contrasts playfully with the creamy potato topping. The butter seems like an over the top indulgence. 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.3)
8.5/10

Grilled Vegetable Cheese Sandwich
The crunch of fresh veggies smothered with plenty of cheese in between toasted slices of bread. 
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2)
7.5/10

Coffee 
An exceptional filter coffee, the sort that lures travellers to drive on kilometres more, just to stop at Swathi Delicacy for a steaming hot cup of Joe!
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4)
10/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 630am to 1030pm on all days.
Note: Weekends may be a bit crowded, but the service here is the sort that is quite efficient and quick.

https://goo.gl/maps/D75HLQzFVW6VBtgz9.description:
popular vegetarian lunch, baale ele oota, vegetarian lunch, thaali, udupi sri krishna bhavan, gandhi bazar, basavangudi, south bangalore, poori saagu, kadubu, palya, vegetable, sambar, tilli saaru, rasam, hollige, south canara meal, udupi meal, south indian,, vegetarian, traditional south indian lunch

When it comes to festive vegetarian indulgence here in Namma Bengaluru, one looks forward to a good baale ele oota,  a meal that is served on a banana leaf. And a popular one at that is the 20-dish special lunch served at the Gandhi Bazaar, Basavanagudi outpost of Udupi Sri Krishna Bhavan, a vegetarian eatery that first opened doors in 1926. In this episode, I not only savour this special lunch but also step into their kitchen to catch the making of a steamed ‘kadubu’ and the South Canara style rasam, known as the Tilli Saaru, by Ganesh, their ‘adige bhatru’, or chief cook, who has been cooking here for over 40 years. There is something truly auspicious about eating off a banana leaf. I hope you enjoy this episode. 

Special Banana Leaf Lunch
This is an indulgent lunch affair representative of the flavours of the Udupi-Kundapura region in most of the 20-dishes that make for a typical baale ele oota offering here. The food is served hot and fresh, and conveys a wholesomeness that is pleasing and satisfying. One begins with a traditional grape juice and mosaru vade, menasinkai bhajji, kosambari, kadubu-chutney, couple of coconut-rich vegetables before proceeding to the substantial mains of poori-saagu, anna (rice) served with tilli saaru and sambar. Servings are unlimited, and the servers are quick and efficient in dispensing refills. Make sure you save space for the desserts, a payasa and hollige, before you close with curd rice, banana and beeda, in true South Canara style.
Rs. 220 (usd 2.9) 
9/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 12pm to 330pm on all days.
Note: They also offer a limited lunch option should one not be feeling indulgent enough to try the special banana leaf lunch.

Established in 1926, Sri Janardhan Hotel has a history that spans nearly a century, and of its many delicious offerings, one rules supreme, the Mysore Pak. Such is its popularity, that this eatery in Ramnagar, a 60-kilometre drive from Bengaluru enroute to Mysuru, is called the Mysore Pak hotel. Made to a recipe tradition that hasn't wavered for decades, each batch of the famed sweet is made by third generation owners, Prashant and his wife, Gayathry. I catch up with them to find out what makes the Mysore Pak sold here supremely addictive and with a following that stretches far beyond the borders of Karnataka. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

Mysore Pak
Drenched in ghee, the mysore pak is meltingly soft, and dissolved when placed in the mouth. The sweetness of the sugar is balanced by the weight of the gram flour and the buttery fervour of the tuppa in this dessert! A mysore pak worth its weight in gold!

https://goo.gl/maps/cPJQWVaGVcHF2DYp7.description:
#mulbagal #dosa #vegetarian 

popular mulbagal dosa, prasad hotel, mulbagal, karnataka, masala dosa, dose, plain dosa, chutney, masala vada, onion dosa, popular traveller breakfast spot, highway breakfasts, madras highway, old madras road, tirupati highway, breakfast, snack

When friends encouraged Rajendra Prasad to begin a home-eatery in 1979 in Mulbagal, then a sleepy village 100 kms away from Bangalore on the Tirupati - Madras highway, he set out to make a dose that hadn’t been seen in commercial kitchens before. Borrowing a homestyle tradition of cooking dosas on individual tawas, “he pioneered” the technique of making a dose that was both roasted and steamed. And thus began the tradition of a scrumptiously delicious, crisp and fluffy breakfast treat, now known as the Mulbagal Dosa, that has put this temple town on the map for every dose aficionado. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe. 

Special Masala Dosa
Roasted first and then steamed, the form of the Mulbagal Dosa with its upturned edges mirrors the shape of the individual cast iron pans it is cooked in. Crusty and crisp on the outset, soft and spongy within, this dose comes across as a cross between a traditional version and an appam. Oozing ghee, the dose breaks in a crisp crackle that belies its thick and fluffy body. The chilli-warming, slightly sour notes of the red onion chutney smeared within complements the palya. For a spicier bite, taste the dose with the lentil chutney.  
Rs. 45 (usd 0.6)
10/10

Masala Vada
Crisp and flavourful, makes for a tasty sidekick to the dosa.
Rs. 6 (usd 0.1)
8/10  

Special Plain Dosa
The unique texture of the dose is heightened because there is none of the potato stuffing (palya) to moisten the dose; taste it before the masala dose to savour completely the texture of this unique creation.
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5)
9/10

Onion Dosa
More like a thick, fluffy uthappam. The hero here is the texture and flavour of the onion; you can taste the near caramelised, sweet notes of the fried onions, and also the moist bite of the translucent onions that haven’t been roasted to a crisp. A dose that can get heavy, the chutneys provide respite. 
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5)
8.5/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: Breakfast 730am to 12noon, Evening tiffin 6pm to 8pm
Note: Get there early, they run out quick, much before closing time, especially on weekends. If arriving by four wheeler, park near the bus stand in Mulbagal, it’s a few minutes walk from there.

https://goo.gl/maps/iteU7UmSF12AR7kF6.title: Tasting INDIAN CHINESE Traditions At HAO HAO, Mangalore’s Oldest & Most Popular Chinese Restaurant
https://goo.gl/maps/iteU7UmSF12AR7kF6.description:
popular chinese restaurant, oldest chinese restaurant, hao hao, manguluru, chinese family restaurant, mangalore, hongkong soup, crunchy fried chicken, chicken, mushrooms and bamboo shoots stir fry, honey spiced chicken wings, roasted and fried chilli chicken, shin min rice, dragon noodles, karnataka

When I moved to Bengaluru nearly 25 years ago, Chinese family-run restaurants formed a significant part of the dining landscape. Run by second and third generation immigrants who were shipped to India by the British over a century ago, the cuisine in these restaurants had evolved to integrate Indian influences, much like how the entrepreneurs of Chinese descent, now Indian citizens, had adapted to the tastes and traditions of the land. Since then, most of these restaurants have closed doors. However during my recent visit to Mangalore, I came upon one such establishment that has stood the test of time for nearly half a century. I caught up with Louis and Rosy Wong to find out more about the Indian Chinese culinary phenomenon, and to also savour some of the dishes on offer at their restaurant, Hao Hao, Manguluru’s most popular Chinese dining spot.

Crunchy Fried Chicken
A tasty duet of spicy chicken supremes encased in crisp, crunchy threads. Alongside a tangy, piquant dipping sauce, this makes for an interesting play of flavours and textures on the palate, not surprising then that this is “the most ordered dish” here.
Rs. 220 (usd 3)
8/10

HongKong Soup
A nourishing, delicately flavoured chicken broth that is topped with ‘clouds’ of eggs whipped into a soft meringue. There’s tiny diced of vegetables to give the chicken company with some soft noodles.
Rs. 180 (usd 2.4)
9/10

Chicken, Mushrooms & Bamboo Shoots Stir Fry
A wholesome assemblage of veggies - chinese cabbage, peppers, beans, onions, bamboo shoots - tossed with chicken in a light soya sauce. The garlic is quite pronounced, in the flavour of the dish, and also on the bite with whole cloves that are stir-fried into the noodles. 
Rs. 220 (usd 3)
8/10

Honey Spiced Chicken WIngs
Fried chicken wings, tossed with a potent dark honey-soy-chilli-garlic sauce and sprinkled over with toasted sesame and spring onions. The chicken is crunchy and moist, only wish the sauce had seeped all the way into the wings.
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1)
8/10

Roasted & Fried Chilli Chicken
The chicken is cooked twice, first roasted, allowed to rest before being tossed in a hot wok with soy, chillies, ginger, garlic, spring onions… rendering the meat the sort that pulls away from the bone effortlessly. Although spicy, the chilli heat is balanced against the umami flavours of the dish. There are also bits of chicken skin in the dish that provides a lovely flavour burst. 
Rs. 220 (usd 3)
10/10

Shin Min Rice
A one-dish meal of soy prawns, sweet garlic chicken, fried rice topped with an egg sauce that coats every grain of rice in its moist custardy texture. The chicken is slightly sweetesh with a prick of pungency from the garlic, the shrimps are a tad overwhelmed by the soy and batter.
Rs. 220 (usd 3)
7.5/10

Dragon Noodles
My favourite of the two main courses, this has chicken in a savoury sauce tossed with plenty of veggies, served with noodles - fried and soft, topped with an egg sauce.
Rs. 210 (usd 2.8)
8.5/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

Note: Open all days.

https://g.page/Thimmappa-fish-hotel?shar.title: HOTEL THIMMAPPA, Udupi’s Most Popular FISH FRY & Meals | A 50-Year Tradition That Began In A Home
https://g.page/Thimmappa-fish-hotel?shar.description:
#seafood #fishfry #udupi

popular seafood restaurant, affordable seafood, fish meals served on banana leaf, affordable seafood, udupi, malpe road, south canara, mangalore, mangalorean food, fish thali, fish curry, fish fry, kane rava fry, lady fish, pomfret, prawns, crabs, disco fish, karnataka

50 years ago, Thimmappa and his wife set up three tables in a rented outhouse in Udupi that they called home, to earn a livelihood by serving a simple meal of fish fry, curry and rice. Over the years, the fish fry, slathered in a secret masala made by the couple, and their sons thereafter, gained favour with locals who would flock to this home that carried no name. Five years ago, his son, Sathish Kotian finally put up a nameboard as a tribute to his late father’s culinary legacy that has endured decades since the eatery’s modest beginnings. In this episode, I visit Hotel Thimmappa Fish Meals to chat with Kotian and also taste some of the seafood delicacies here. Hope you enjoy this one. Take care and stay safe.

Fish Meal
The fish meal is a simple affair here, there’s rice, a tasty curry made with small-sized, inexpensive fish, a vegetable for the day and some pickle. And to complete this, one picks from the selection of fish fry (charged extra) proffered by attendants who scurry between the tables and the kitchen. Whether one has a budget of under Rs. 100 or 300, one is assured of a satisfying fish meal at Thimmappa.
Rs 40 (usd 0.5)
8/10

Kane Rava Fry
This was a plump lady fish, the semolina forming the perfect crunchy crumb over a veil of perfectly spiced masala encasing the flakey delicate flesh of the fish. One of the best kane rava fry preparations that I have tasted.
Rs. 100 - 250 (usd 1.3 to 2.7) depending on size
10/10

Disco Fish
The perfect fish fry for those on a budget. The fish is meaty, it is mild in its flavours and readily embraces the vivacious strength of the masala. 
Rs. 40 - 50 (usd 0.5 to 0.7) depending on size
8.5/10

Prawn Ghee Roast
The prawns are swathed in a robust masala, the flavour of the ghee complements the slight hint of sweetness in the prawns. 
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7) 
8.5/10

Fish Kebab
Kingfish deep fried in a spicy Koliwada batter, a touch of the Konkan coast in Udupi.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7) 
8/10

Pomfret Fry
The pomfret exemplifies the fish fry preparation at Hotel Thimmappa. Aided by the sizzling hot tawa and lashings of coconut oil, the fish has the perfect masala crust encasing its moist and meaty flesh. If you are lucky to find it on the fish fry tray, go for the biggest pomfret. 
Rs. 200 - 300 (usd 2.7 to 4) depending on size
10/10

Prawn Pepper Fry
The pepper intensifies the sweetness of the prawns, and the toasted flavour of curry leaf lends a savoury note to the delightful crunch of this deep-fry.
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2) for a full portion, I tasted a sample portion of this dish.
9/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS:  Lunch from 12pm to 4pm; Dinner from 7pm to 10pm
Note: Get here early, the eatery tends to get quite busy, especially on weekends.

https://goo.gl/maps/cWa1KURs9zBMn9mt7.title: Tasty VILLAGE MEALS Cooked Over A Wood Fire At This FARMER’S AKKI ROTI HOTEL | Needs No Sign Board!
https://goo.gl/maps/cWa1KURs9zBMn9mt7.description:
#villagefood #vegetarian #sakleshpur 

simple village style akki rotti and vegetarian lunch outside sakleshpur, village food, vegetarian, highway eatery, bangalore mangalore highway, akki rotti, vegetarian meal, thaali, raagi mudde, sambar, highway dining, highway meal, karnataka

Sixteen years ago, Balwant and his wife, Girija decided to open a tea shop on the fringe of their small farm abutting the highway at the foothills of the Western ghats just outside Sakleshpur, to augment their income. The tea shop soon began offering Malenadu style akki rotti to hungry travellers. And then meals followed, fuelled by Girija’s recipes and a wood fire, a simple affair, rice, rotti or raagi mudde, served with homely preparations of sambar, rasam, vegetable, pickle, papad, buttermilk and curd. Their following may have grown over the years, but the eatery remains as basic as it was when they first opened; I asked Balwant why he didn’t have a name board, and he modestly replied, “I thought I would put up a board when I improved the hotel,” meaning the interiors.

His son, Prashant interrupts to say “we are on google maps and customers find us so we don’t need a signpost anymore.” And that’s true, it’s the simple yet tasty village style food served in a rustic setting here that’s a big draw for locals and travellers alike and earned for the establishment the moniker, Akki Roti Hotel Anemahal.

Akki Rotti
The Malenadu style akki rotties are served hot and puffy with homemade butter that makes for a simple yet delicious accompaniment to the toasty crackle of the rotti. A tasty vegetable saagu, curry made of raw banana and bengal gram, helps one make a sumptuous meal of these rotties. There’s a spicy green chilli chutney completes the plate.
Rs. 50 (usd ) 
9/10

Meals 
Choose from rice or raagi mudde served with a delicious homestyle sambar and a fingerlicking rasam that’s a flavourful play of spicy, sour and sweet on the palate. A dry vegetable for the day adds to the tasty nutrition of this meal, and there’s some homemade curd, buttermilk, happala and pickle to round off the meal.
Rs. 60
8/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS:  Breakfast from 7am to 11am; Lunch from 12pm to 4pm.
Note: Open all days of the week; they only close on Sundays during heavy monsoons. The eatery has no signboard and is at a slightly lower position than the road. If driving from Bengaluru, look to your left when you arrive at the location and you should find it. Opp Canara Bank ATM.
ADDRESS -  Akki Roti Hotel Anemahal,, NH-48, Bengaluru-Mangaluru Highway, Anemahal, Sakleshpur, Rural, Mangalore, Karnataka 573134; tel: +91 73376 43313
