https://g.page/malgudi-mylari-mane.title: MALGUDI MYLARI MANE Combines An Iconic Mysore Dosa Style With Local Curries & Palav | Highway Dining
https://g.page/malgudi-mylari-mane.description:
#nelamangala #bangalore #mangalorehighway

highway eatery in nelamangala, bangalore mangalore highway, mylari dose, akki rotti, mutton fry, mutton chops, chicken palav, mutton palav,  akki rotti, highway dining, karnataka

This highway eatery in Nelamangala, 40 kilometres from Bengaluru, is a passion enterprise of young entrepreneurs seeking to combine an iconic dosa style with local curries, palavs and more. Their conviction in the dosa, and a dosa cook with credentials apparently in the kitchen of the legendary Vinayaka Mylari, Mysuru, is even stamped in the name of this culinary venture, Malgudi Mylari Mane. I venture out for breakfast one early morning to taste the dose and other meaty offerings here, and return convinced that MMM certainly offers a refreshing change-from-the-usual offering for travellers on this stretch of the road. Hope you enjoy this episode, stay safe and happy eating!

Mylari Dosa
Topped with some village butter, the Mylari Dose here served with a herb-enriched green saagu and coconut chutney. Its fluffy, porous texture also makes it a willing accomplice to be dunked in the curries. However, in comparison to the iconic Mysuru Vinayaka Mylari Dose that it seeks to emulate, it doesn’t quite manage the melt-in-the-mouth fragility of the original offering. But it is a tasty dose on its own.
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5)
8/10

Paaya
This broth typically consumed in the morning is the sort that jolts your senses awake with its spicing. Would make for a perfect medium to dunk some hot thatte idlis in here.
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7) soup only; Rs. 100 (usd 1.4) with one trotter
8/10

Koli Kara
A Sino-Indian inspired creation of MMM, the chicken is juicy down to the bone. You can taste the heat of the fresh green chillies, the slight sweetness of some tomato sauce and the lingering warmth of red chillies combined with the umami punch of some soy. 
Rs. 70 (usd 0.9) per leg piece
8.5/10

Chicken Pepper Fry 
You can taste the grainy bite of the pepper alongside some garam masala and coriander in this preparation. 
Rs. 140 (usd 1.9)
7.5/10

Naati Koli Fry
Loved the coriander freshness of this preparation made of free range chicken that is deep in its flavours, fortified also by bits of skin clinging on to the meat. 
Rs. 180 (usd 2.4)
9/10

Mutton Fry
A rustic-style dish, the meat is soft in parts and a tad chewy otherwise. The masala seemed a bit heavy on the salt though, thankfully one could dunk the fluffy dose in to tone it down. 
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
7/10

Mutton Chops
The meat is juicy and pink with a bit of fat, and the sort that peels away from the bone. The curry is thick and flavourful, redolent of coriander and fenugreek. Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
9/10

Akki Rotti
Rs. 20 (usd 0.3) 
8/10

Chicken Palav
The rice is a bit starchy to the touch, the punch of the spices quite pronounced in the rice. The meat is moist and juicy, savour it with the rice to taste the complete flavours of this tasty palav.
Rs. 140 (usd 1.9)
7.5/10

Mutton Palav 
Although the composition of the spicing is similar to the chicken palav, one can taste the flavour and aroma of the meat in the rice as opposed to the accent of spices in the former. The spice in this version is subservient to the flavours of the goat meat, thereby making this a palav that is gentle and rounded on the palate.
Rs. 220 (usd 3)
8/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 730am to 1030pm.
Note: Closed on Mondays

popular highway eatery in bidadi, bangalore mysore highway, bengaluru mysuru, idli, thatte idli, masala vada, chutney, vegetarian, breakfast, snack, karnataka

The origin of this iconic Bidadi thatte idli shop dates back to the 1950s when it came into existence as a tiny village eatery in the middle of nowhere (then), steaming and serving large plates of the acrey idli, an early precursor to the modern day thatte idli.  What makes Sri Shiva Darshana Shashi Thatte Idli Hotel the most popular stop on the Bengaluru-Mysuru highway today though is the owning family’s commitment to its culinary legacy over five generations. I stop by for a chat and to taste the idli that in a manner of speaking has put Bidadi on the food lovers’ map.

Thatte Idli
The thatte idli is pillowy, it is as “soft as air” and breaks under the effect of gravity! Definitely order the butter with the idli, it’s a premium worth paying. The butter seeps through the porous structure of the fragile idli and makes for a bite that melts the moment you place it in your mouth. The chutney delivers a potent chilli punch, the potato saagu is creamy and provides for respite from the spicy yet addictive red chutney. The masala vada makes for a savoury interlude whilst tasting the idli. On the whole, this is an idli that is worth driving 50 kilometres for! 
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7) for two idlis, two masala vada. Extra butter Rs. 25 (usd 0.3)
10/10 

Happy Eating!

https://goo.gl/maps/ue6vNnDDgiRnnZhx5.title: Exploring 25 Years And 3 Generations Of RURAL Culinary Traditions At SVS MESS, Kolar
https://goo.gl/maps/ue6vNnDDgiRnnZhx5.description:
SVS MESS, Kolar | 25 Years And 3 Generations Of RURAL NON VEG Traditions! Biryani, Chops, Kheema Fry

#ruralfood #kolar #karnataka 

popular rustic eatery in kolar for non vegetarian food served by a family, svs mess, mutton dishes, sheep, mutton biryani, chicken biryani, mutton chops, boti fry, fish kebab, paya soup, mutton fry, kheema, kolar food, non vegetarian food, biryani, non veg in kolar, kolar hotels, karnataka

This rustic eatery, located in Kolar, the milk and silk center of Karnataka, and within a two-hour driving distance from Bengaluru, is a labour of love spanning three generations of a family who come together every morning to serve up a meaty repast of traditional dishes that over the years has found much favour with the locals. I catch up with the family in their kitchen where the food is cooked as it was 25 years ago, on an ingeniously designed wood-fired stove. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

Paya Soup
The paya is gentle and nourishing with the warming touch of pepper, an appetising start to the meal here.
Rs. 10 (usd 0.1) for a cup of soup; Rs. 180 (usd 2.5) with two trotters
8/10

Fish Kebab
A fish fry that’s best savoured hot, the flesh is moist with the skin crispened. The masala is flavourful and thankfully does not overpower the earthy flavours of the fish, I suspect this is a kaatla or a variant thereof, although locally it is referred to as silver pomfret. 
Rs. 140 (usd 1.9)
7.5/10

Mutton Biryani
A biryani that is mellow in flavours, subtle nuances of the aromatic spices are all that one detects in the rice, a combination of seeraga samba and the bullet variety. The meat is tender and moist, effusive in its flavour with a slightly salty edge of sheep meat. The meat combined with the rice makes for a flavourful mouthful, combine with the sherva to add a bit of a punch, the biryani is definitely a must order here if you come on one of the days they make it.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7)
9/10

Mutton Kheema Unde
Handground by the ladies of the house, one can discern the grainy texture of the coarse kheema on the bite and the warming notes of inger. The kheema unde is soft and flavourful, there is some egg that’s used to bring the roundels together with a bit of gram flour, but is barely discernible. Loaded with fresh pepper spice, 
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2)
8.5/10

Boti Fry
The boti is cleaned well and cooked with tender hithikabele (peeled hyacinth beans) which helps in toning down some of the ‘funky’ flavours of the boti. If you love your boti, you will enjoy it.
Rs. 120 (usd 1.6)
7/10

Mutton Chops
A loaded chop, plenty of meat and some fat, that stands testament to the fact that SVS knows how to cook its meat. Absolutely delicious, the meat peels away from the bone, yet has a bit of a bite. There’s bits of fat floating in the gravy, that also adds to the rich, unctuous flavours of the curry. Savour this with some plain steamed rice.
Rs. 160 (usd 1.6)
9/10


Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: Full menu is available for lunch from 12pm to 4pm only; they are open in the evenings but only serve kebabs. Saturdays closed.
Note: Biryani is available on Tuesday, Friday and Sunday only. Raagi Mudde available on other days.

https://goo.gl/maps/JxBsqNtjYG3xwkro7.title: This Humble FAMILY Eatery Is Serving Honestly-Priced, Delicious COASTAL MANGALORE Food | FISH N DISH
https://goo.gl/maps/JxBsqNtjYG3xwkro7.description:
#mangaloreanfood #seafood #bangalore

family run mangalorean coastal restaurant, neighbourhood restaurant, jp nagar, south bengaluru, fish n dish, fresh seafood, fish fry, fish curry, prawn fry, prawn curry, prawn sukka, ghee roast, kane, lady fish rawa fry, mackerel tawa fry, silver fish curry, curry, spicy mangalorean curry, fish meal, fish thaali

Harish Shetty, a native of Puttur, and his wife, Prema, uprooted themselves from their life in Mangalore five years to move to Bengaluru with their only son, Shaman, for his higher education. To earn a livelihood, they set up a small eatery in a corner of the city, with absolutely no experience but compelled by necessity and their love for cooking the food of their native land. Despite all odds, their tiny shop, Fish N Dish, prospered modestly over the years. The current situation brought all that to nought as they lost their meagre staff, most of their business, and were forced to fend for themselves to stay afloat. Alerted by our viewers of their plight, I paid an impromptu visit to find the couple cooking in the kitchen, serving customers and also cleaning up after them, assisted by their son. The delicious homestyle Mangalorean food that I tasted fuelled by Harish and Prema Shetty’s motivation to provide for their son a better life inspired this episode. Hope you enjoy this one, please support them and neighbourhood eateries like these if you can. 

Lady Fish Rawa Fry
A delicate crust conceals the lady fish, smeared with a gentle masala that’s seasoned to perfection. The fish is fresh and flakey, the perfect size to peel away at its flesh, definitely a fry to order when here
Rs. 200 (usd 2.7) for one fish
9/10

Prawn Sukka
The coconut is the perfect sponge to soak up the flavours of the masala and also the slight sweetness of the prawns. The coconut masala, toasted curry leaves, ginger garlic and green chilli combine supremely with the prawns that have been cooked to just the right texture. 
Rs. 300 (usd 4.1) 
9/10

Squid Ghee Roast
The ghee roast masala is warming and ‘kadak’ in its punch and laced with the generous ‘butteriness’ of ghee. Would order the ghee roast here again, but perhaps with fish or chicken. 
Rs. 220 (usd 3) 
8/10

Mackerel Fry (Green Masala)
You can taste the fresh herbaceousness of coriander combined with the zing of mint and the spicy heat of green chillies. It’s a masala that’s robust enough to take on the strong flavours of the mackerel.
Rs. 130 (usd 1.8) per fish
8/10

Mackerel Tava Fry (Red Masala)
A deep-coloured masala that greets you with its spicy punch and has seeped into the core of the fish.
Rs. 130 (usd 1.8) per fish
8.5/10

Fish Thaali
A complete meal that includes a mackerel curry, mackerel fry, some vegetable, pickle, rice and neer dosa, guaranteed to satisfy, taste-wise and also fill you up.
Rs. 150 (usd 2)
9/10

Silverfish Curry
A gentle curry with the creaminess of coconut milk and mild flavours of the fish, the fish is the sort that one can devour completely, bone and all. A traditional silver fish curry would also have a bit of tartness that I missed in this preparation. 
Rs. 150 (usd 2) 
7.5/10

Mackerel Pullimunchi
The curry is nice and thick, however to a Mangalorean, it may seem a trifle compromised on the chilli and tamarind punch that one would expect to find in a traditional Puli (sour) Munchi (chilli). 
Rs. 150 (usd 2) 
8/10


Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: lunch 12noon to 330pm, dinner 630 to 10pm; Monday holiday
ADDRESS -  Fish ‘N’ Dish, Jambunagar 1st cross. Jambusavari dhinne, Near Bus Stand, J P Nagar 8th Phase, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560 076; tel: +91 99453 81372 
LOCATION TAG - https://goo.gl/maps/JxBsqNtjYG3xwkro7
NOTE: Fish N Dish is a small family run set-up with only four tables. If possible, do call them ahead, and also be a little patient in case you need to wait. Thank you.

https://goo.gl/maps/LLzVZDKGAPpt5AD37.title: Famous RAMANAGARA Biryani Ritual | TAJ BIRYANI PARADISE | Mysore Highway Mutton Biryani, Chicken
https://goo.gl/maps/LLzVZDKGAPpt5AD37.description:
#biryani #mysorehighway #ramnagar 

popular biryani stop on bangalore mysore highway, ramanagara, bengaluru mysuru highway, mutton biryani, biryani trail, mutton biryani, chicken biryani, chicken grill, chicken al faham

For travellers on the Bengaluru Mysuru highway craving a quick biryani fix, Taj Biryani Paradise has been a popular pitstop for years. Located bang on the highway, it’s the sort of place that’s hard to miss with a number of vehicles parked out front alluding to its crowd-pleasing appeal. Curious to taste this much-sought after biryani, we stopped by impromptu on a recent expedition to the area. Watch the episode to know what we thought of the offerings here. Stay safe and happy eating!

Chicken Al Faham
The meat, especially the leg piece, is moist and juicy, the masala has permeated all the way into the meat. The chaat masala sprinkled over the bird is a tad overpowering, all in all a tasty preparation, provided it’s served hot.
Rs. 220 (usd 3) for half a chicken
7/10

Mutton Biryani
The biryani is stained saffron yellow, the rice fluffy, moist and flavourful and seemingly mellow when it greets your palate first with the aromas of the seasoning spices like cardamom. Golden fried onions, brishta, lend to the flavour of the biryani, however a few bites in one can detect the mild burn of red chilli spice on the lips. But that’s quickly assuaged when the rice is tasted with the juicy, fat-lined plump pieces of meat in the biryani. The meat is intense in its ‘meaty’ flavour, slides off the bone, and definitely the sort that leaves an impression on the palate.
Rs. 270 (usd 3.7)
8/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

TIMINGS: 12pm to 12am on most days. 
ADDRESS - Taj Biryani Express, B.M. Road, National Highway 275, Ramanagara, Karnataka 562159; tel: +91 98447 87860

https://goo.gl/maps/GcVv3J8dBmkfZR4V6.title: Tasty, Traditional Fare Served By VILLAGE HOUSEWIVES | THOTADA MANE | FARM DINING At Srirangapatna
https://goo.gl/maps/GcVv3J8dBmkfZR4V6.description:
#vegetarian #traditional #villagefood 

a unique farm garden dining experience in srirangapatna, close to mysore, mysuru, village tradition thotada mane, guru dutt bharadwaj, mint lime, akki rotti, spinach rotti, raagi rotti, millets, vegetarian meal, thaali,  sambar, rasam, bangalore mysore highway, bengaluru mysuru highway, mandya district

Guru Dutt Bharadwaj quit his IT job in Bengaluru five years ago to move into the tiny village of Darasaguppe in Srirangapatna to look after his aging parents. With his parent’s traditional home as backdrop, his fondness for cooking led to the creation of Thotada Mane, rustic vegetarian dining amidst a verdant garden setting, that seeks to offer not just mere sustenance but also a refreshing glimpse into an alternate way of life. In doing so, he employed an all-women team of housewives from the neighbouring villages, working alongside them in the kitchen to serve up traditional family recipes, some tweaked with playful twists to ensure there is something for everyone who arrives here. I drive the 130 kilometres from Bengaluru to savour this unique experience that literally comes across as a breath of fresh air in the current circumstances. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

Mint Lime
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
8/10

Special Bhajji 
A tasty bhajji platter, the crunch of tomatoes, onions and coriander add an element of ‘freshness’ to a deep-fried indulgent snack. Order for one of these as soon as you arrive at Thotada Mane.
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2)
8/10

Rotti Platter
A wholesome plate of three rotties, rice, spinach and raagi, topped with a generous dollop of butter and served with a niger seed chutney, uchilu pudi and curd combo, and a knock-your-socks-off spicy village condiment of green chillies, mensu. The rotties are ‘kadak’, crisp around the edges, and loaded with flavour. The akki rotti, infused with onions, dill, green chillies, cumin and more, was my favourite. The spinach rotti is a rice rotti infused with the ‘dulling’ green notes of spinach, the raagi rotti on the other hand is quite earthy in its flavour. The uchila pudi, with its fibrous nuttiness, tart fervour of tamarind and slight sweetness of jaggery makes for a great combination with the rotties, especially when combined with the yoghurt. And for those with a festish for spicy heat, the mensu will be most appealing!
Rs. 80 (usd 1.1)
Akki Rotti 9/10; Spinach Rotti 8/10; Raagi Rotti 8/10

Meals
The sort of traditional meal you would taste perhaps if you were invited to a home in Srirangapatna. A sumptuous thaali weighed down by a dry palya for the day, saagu, sambhar, rasam, puri, homemade yoghurt and rice. You also have the option of opting for chapattis or parottas. The vegetables are fresh and crunchy, sourced from the nearby villages, the preparations tasty and comforting in their flavours. The Maddur vade makes for a nice, crisp touch, and the kai obbattu, served for dessert, helps round up this indulgent meal. The sort of satisfying meal that will lull you into a quick catnap in the lush green setting of Thotada Mane before you set out on the road again.
Rs. 130 (usd 1.8)
9/10


Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,

https://goo.gl/maps/ufeyT7ANncwiSgwJ6.title: Delicious VILLAGE Tradition, CHIBLU IDLIS Steamed In Bamboo Over Wood Fire | BABU HOTEL Halaguru
https://goo.gl/maps/ufeyT7ANncwiSgwJ6.description:
#villagefood #idlichutney #vegetarian 

ancient village tradition idli, halaguru, 80 kms from bangalore, bengaluru, idli chutney, butter, bene dose, dosa, tuppa dose, ghee dosa, red chilli chutney, kempu chutney, babu hotel, halaguru, bangalore kanakapura road, kanakapura road, bengaluru, mandya district 

The chiblu idli dates back to an era when modern kitchen conveniences of utensils weren’t easily available in villages, and so people would fashion cooking vessels out of resources handy. In the absence of present day idli steamers, village folk would steam idlis in baskets, known as ‘chiblus’ in kannada, made of bamboo, over a wood fire. And thus, these soft, aromatic chiblu idlis came into being. The painstaking effort required to steam idlis using this old-fashioned approach has caused this ancient practice to all but disappear. We travel 80 kilometres to Halaguru to savour this delicious tradition at Babu Hotel, a tiny village eatery that has been serving up the chiblu idli for over half a century now. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

Chiblu Idli
The chiblu idli is aromatic and steaming hot, served with a dollop of butter and alongside palya and red chilli chutney. The idli is soft, porous and carries a tart edge from the fermentation, that the butter helps balance against. The kempu chutney has a good balance of spice, and the crunch of the coconut complements the grainy bite of the hurigadale (roasted gram). The palya is savoury with the flavour of the onions.
Rs. 10 (usd 0.1) per idli; Rs. 5 for butter
9/10

Tuppa Dose/ Bene Dose/ Masala Dose
The dose is crisp to the touch and fried to an appealing golden brown. Makes for a simple but satisfying tiffin with the palya and chutney. The masala dose is similar but stuffed with palya and larger in size, with twice the amount of butter. 
Rs. 10/ 25 (usd 0.1/ 0.3) for bene/ masala dose
8/10

Chitranna
A pleasing lemon rice preparation should you wish to round off your breakfast at Babu Hotel. 
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) 
7/10


Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

https://goo.gl/maps/AfA4MVarv3VVA3qp9.title: Tasting The HINDUPUR Sandwich Tradition At HARI SUPER SANDWICH | Secret Recipes, Cheese & Chocolate!
https://goo.gl/maps/AfA4MVarv3VVA3qp9.description:
#bangalore #sandwich #streetfood 

popular vegetarian sandwich shop, hari super sandwich, street food, bread, vegetables, american corn sandwich, chilli cheese toast sandwich, chocolate and cheese sandwich, hari special sandwich, capsicum sandwich, local eatery, jayanagar, bengaluru, snack

Hindupur, a town 100kms from Bengaluru, in Andhra Pradesh, dotes on its sandwich, a derivative of the Mumbai bread and veggies affair. In Bengaluru, Hari Super Sandwich, has adapted the Hindupur sandwich to its own style with customised breads, a special spicy chutney and secret spice mix, the recipe for which is zealously guarded, in a medley of combinations that range from the expected chilli cheese toast to eclectic american sweet corn, chipotle mayo, and the wacky but popular chocolate sandwich! I taste five of their sandwiches to find out what makes this chain of sandwich shops such a rage in the city. 

American Corn Sandwich 
A texture-rich sandwich, with the sweet pop of the corn and the moist crunch of capsicum and onion. The bread is toasted just right to hold within it the creaminess of the cheese and the stuffing. You can taste the aromatic flavour of the spice powder mix and the fervour of garlic.
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5)
8.5/10

Chilli Cheese Toast Sandwich
Fresh green chillies are grated onto a bed of cheese, the cheese helps tone down the chilli kick for sure.
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5)
8/10

Chocolate Cheese Sandwich 
A combination that sounds unusual to the ear, but works well on the palate. The chocolate is not as smooth as silk, but is complemented by the creamy saltiness of the cheese and butter. It tastes almost like a chocolate waffle.
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5)
8/10

Hari Special Sandwich 
A loaded vegetable sandwich, inspired by the Bombay sandwich. You bite into the crispness of the vegetables, onion, tomato and cucumber, and taste the warmth of the chipotle laced mayo.
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5)
8.5/10

Capsicum Onion Sandwich 
You can taste the full-on vegetal notes of capsicum in this one, appealing if you like peppers, not otherwise. 
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5)
7/10

Happy Eating!

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road,
Food Lovers TV

https://goo.gl/maps/TQphTrun1to6tRoJ6.title: Authentic KODAVA Fare At THE COORG FOOD COMPANY | A Kodava Couple Share Their Culinary Heritage
https://goo.gl/maps/TQphTrun1to6tRoJ6.description:
#kodavacuisine #coorgfood #bangalore

authentic kodava, coorg cuisine, bengaluru, chicken curry, pandi curry, kadambuttu, akki otti, pork curry, koli bhartad, chicken fry, kaima unde, meatball fry, onake erachi, spicy smoked pork, veg curry,  tender coconut pudding

The Coorg Food Company is Pavith Ponnappa and Pavitha Poonacha’s culinary ode to their Kodava heritage and ancestry, a labour of love with recipes gleaned from family and ingredients sourced from their estates in Coorg. The result, not surprisingly, are dishes brimming with authenticity and flavour. I catch up with them at their cosy restaurant and also savour many of the dishes that offer a stellar showcase of Kodagu’s rich culinary traditions. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe.

Kripal Amanna,
Gourmet On The Road

Crispy Bhendi Fry 
Juliennes of ladies finger coated in a simply flavoured rice flour batter. 
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6) for a full portion, roughly twice my tasting portion
7/10

Vegetable Cutlets
You bite through the soft crunch of the crust into a tasty vegetable mash, one can detect the savoury sweetness of some fried onions in the mix.
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6) for 5 cutlets
7.5/10

Kaipake Fry 
The bitter gourd is fried to minimise its bitter edge and then tossed in a mix of sliced onions, green chillies, chilli powder and fresh coriander with a heavy-handed drizzle of lemon juice that balances against the bitterness of the bitter gourd.  
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6) for a full portion, roughly twice my tasting portion
8/10

Kodava Koli Bhartad  
The chicken, cooked on the bone, is moist and flavourful with a potent peppery punch counterpointed with the tartness of the kachampuli, Coorg vinegar. 
Rs. 240 (usd 3.3) for a full portion, roughly twice my tasting portion
8.5/10

Kaima Unde Bhartad
Crisp outside and juicy within, all that one tastes in these roundels is the flavour of the meat and the lush mouthfeel of the ghee. There is spicing, but subdued to celebrate the richness of the coarse meat.
Rs. 275 (usd 3.7) for 8 roundels
8.5/10

Onake Erachi 
A traditional Kodava preparation of smoked pork, shredded and tossed with onions, chillies, spices and kachampuli. One can detect a faint ‘smokey’ veil on the bite. 
Rs. 350 (usd 4.8) for a full portion, roughly twice my tasting portion
8.5/10

Pandi  Bhartad 
A preparation that breaks down readily in the mouth, releasing the flavours of the deep roasted Kodava ‘kartha’ masala. The fat has a deliciously jammy, sticky texture and has rendered well into the dish. 
Rs. 285 (usd 3.9) for a full portion, roughly twice my tasting portion
9/10

Thith Pandi  
A simple dish that draws inspiration from the erstwhile Kodava tradition of hunting, the meat is tossed simply in some paringe molu (bird eye chillies) and rock salt.
Rs. 335 (usd 4.6) for a full portion, roughly twice my tasting portion
8.5/10

Kootu Curry 
A warming preparation of lentils and vegetables, wholesome and simple. Best mopped up with akki otti.
Rs. 195 (usd 2.7) combo with a choice of staple
8/10

Koli Curry 
A delicious, homestyle chicken curry, the coconut milk in this preparation ensures the flavours are gentle and calming, quite unlike the robust pork dishes. 
Rs. 235 (usd 3.2) combo with a choice of staple
9/10

Pandhi Curry 
The signature dish here, the pandhi curry is stained dark with the kartha masala and the kachampuli, and the sort that breaks down in a hurry the moment you bite on it releasing the flavours of the masala laden with the fat of the meat. 
Rs. 245 (usd 3.3) combo with a choice of staple
10/10

Puttu Platter 
Rs. 155 (usd 2.1)
8/10

Tender Coconut Pudding 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4)
10/10

Gasagase Payasa 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4)
8/10

Lazy Daisy 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4)
8/10

Belgian Chocolate Mousse 
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4)
7/10

https://g.page/NaidusChats?share.title: NAIDUS ‘Hygienic’ CHAATS | An Engineer & Accountant Transform Their Father’s 35-Year-Old CHAAT Cart!
https://g.page/NaidusChats?share.description:
#naiduschats #foodtruck #bangalore

clean, hygienic, chaat, naidus chats, food truck, paani puri, pani puri, masala puri, sev puri, dahi puri, street food, chat, inspiring stories

After years of working for a paani-puri vendor, Kuppuram Naidu saved enough to set up a chaat cart in the eighties in the far flung suburb of Basaveshwar Nagar in Bengaluru. His sons, Gokul and Sarvan, would turn up at the cart after school to help their father, and in between preparing chaat, serving customers and doing the dishes, catch up on their homework under street lights. The years passed, Gokul became an engineer, his brother a cost accountant. Unable to find a suitable job though, Gokul turned back to his father’s trade, and aided by his brother, has transformed the cart to a food truck. And not just any food truck, this engineer and cost accountant duo have aspirations to be the most hygienic street food operation serving authentic chaats! Made to the age-old recipes of their father who has since retired to farming, and with almost every component of the chaat prepared by them with the assistance of their mother, Shanthi Kuppuram. 
I drive up to Naidus Chats to see this for myself and also savour a few of their popular offerings made to that has made them the cynosure of their neighbourhood. 


Masala Puri 
Bengaluru’s popular ‘local’ chaat offering is served in an avatar that is spicy but doesn't subdue the aroma and warming spices of the ‘masala’ that is at the heart of this concoction. The masala has depth of flavour, this chaat can be a filling snack with the white peas.
Rs 30 (usd 0.4)
8.5/10

Sev Puri 
Not a Mumbai version with potatoes, but topped with onions, spiced peanuts, chilli powder, seasoning, chutneys and sev, this chaat is a riot of textures. From the crispy crunch of the papri to the moist crunch of the onions and the spicy nutty bite of the peanuts, laced with the chilli-coriander-mint green chutney balanced with the tangy sweetness of the jaggery-tamarind chutney.
Rs 30 (usd 0.4)
9/10

Dahi Puri 
The dahi puri is burdened with potatoes, white peas, peanuts, chutneys and the aromatic masala before being topped with yoghurt, sev and boondi. A sumptuous chaat if you are looking for one. 
Rs 30 (usd 0.4)
7/10

Paani Puri 
The paani puri is light and chatpata, not too spicy or the sort that will singe your palate. The potatoes and chickpeas, just enough to give it a creamy bite.
Rs 30 (usd 0.4)
8/10

https://goo.gl/maps/7tR4BBYWUQEFksKW7.title: Bengaluru's Favourite KHAALI DOSA At 50-Year HOTEL DWARKA | The Dosa That Changed An Eatery’s Name
https://goo.gl/maps/7tR4BBYWUQEFksKW7.description:
#khaalidose #hoteldwarka #bangalore

south bangalore’s popular hotel dwarka, popular breakfast, vegetarian, khali dosa, tomato dosa, dose, carrot halwa, basavangudi, bengaluru

For nearly half a century Hotel Dwarka has ruled the South Bengaluru palate, when it comes to the Khaali Dose, that though not as popular as the ubiquitous masala dose, is much revered by dosa aficionados. Intrigued, I visit this eatery to taste their khaali dose, and also discover that though its name may mean ‘empty’ in Kannada, there’s much that goes into its making that has earned for Dwarka the moniker, Khaali Dose Hotel. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care and stay safe.

Khaali Dosa
The khaali dose, served in a pair, is soft and spongy, topped with mini-dollops of butter. When eaten piping hot with a generous smear of the butter, it’s the sort that when placed in the mouth dissolves little effort. The chutney served alongside is the right consistency to impregnate the porous dose with its spicy fervour. The potato palya is flavourful, but the main act here is the dose, butter and chutney.
Rs 50 (usd 0.7)
9/10

https://goo.gl/maps/BGiyFiR9qPqM1ECg9.description:
#vegetarian #northkarnatakacuisine #bangalore

original north karnataka restaurant from dharwad, north karnataka, jollada rotti meals jowar rotti, maddike kaalu, moth beans, badanekayi ennegayi, eggplant, hesarukaalu, sprouted mung beans, sprouts, donne menasinakai, gurelu, shenga, chutney, jhunka, shenga obbatu, hollige, malleswaram, bengaluru, 

Kudlayya Karbasaiyya Ganachari and his wife, Susheela, opened a tiny student mess, Basaveshwara Khanavali, in their home in Dharwad in 1963. Soon, the delicious reputation of their home-cooked jolada rotti oota or meal spread far beyond the student community, compelling them to open an eatery in the town’s main market. 50 years on, this North Karnataka khanavali or eating house, has expanded to 12 locations, including two in Bengaluru, but the family’s personal touch remains with the founder’s sons involved in the cooking of the meals. In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, I catch up with the youngest son, Ravi Shivappa Ganachari, at their newest eatery in Malleswaram, and savour a satisfying jolada rotti oota. Hope you enjoy the watch, stay safe and happy eating!

Jollada Rotti Meal
This is a meal that is high in nutrition, taste and variety. The jolada rottis are light and fluffy, the sort that when smeared with some butter, marry well with everything on the leaf, especially the chutneys, kempu chutney, shenga chutney and guralu, with some yoghurt. The rotti wrapped with the jhunka, salad and the gravy of the eggplant preparation, is a riot of flavours and textures. The pulses, the moth bean and sprouted mung, are satisfying, the badanekayi enngayi and dhonne menasinkayi, the sort that will have you calling for second helpings. Certainly a meal that extols the vegetarian flavours of North Karnataka. 
Rs 150 (usd 2) per meal
9/10

Shenga Hollige
Served with a generous drizzle of ghee, the hollige is sticky in its texture and carries the nutty crunch of the peanuts. 
Rs 30 (usd 0.4)
7/10

https://g.page/EatRaja?share.description:
#zerowaste #freshfruitjuice #bangalore 

india’s first zero waste, juice bar, eco-friendly, bengaluru, eat raja, popular juice shop, malleswaram, anand raj, raja, watermelon juice, chilli guava shots, muskmelon banana juice, banana beetroot juice, cucumber lime wellness drink, juices, smoothies, healthy drink

Eat Raja is the fascinating story of an engineer turned radio jockey who gave up his career to help his mother look after the family juice shop upon the untimely passing of his father a couple of years ago. And along the way, elevated it from a mere juice shop to the country’s first zero waste juice bar. Where there is no plastic, no paper used, where imaginative juice concoctions are served in vestibules fashioned out of fruit shells, highly instagrammable, that after serving their purpose are then gathered to be fed to cows. I catch up with zero-waste evangelist, Anand Raj aka Raja, taste six of his slurp-worthy creations, and leave with the one thought that we must all pay heed to what we waste. Take care and stay safe.

Waterless Watermelon Juice
Refreshingly thick juice, unfiltered and sweetened with the natural sugars of the fruit. 
Rs 50 (usd 0.7) 
8/10

Chilli Guava Juice Shots
The best seller at Eat Raja, pink guava that’s juiced and served in its shell with a chilli-salt rim that contrasts sharply against the sweetness of the fruit. You are served five shots to a portion, and the bonus here, you get to relish the juice and eat the fruit too! 
Rs 50 (usd 0.7) 
10/10

Muskmelon Banana Juice
Served in a muskmelon cup, the tropical notes of the muskmelon pairs deliciously with the ripe sweet ripeness of the Chandrabaley banana. The flavours of this delightful combination linger long on the palate even after you have finished drinking the juice. 
Rs 50 (usd 0.7) 
10/10

Cucumber Lime Detox
Raja’s “inside the fruit” thinking manifests itself in a “healthy-tasting” puree of cucumber spiked with lime that’s served in the shell with a chilli-salt rim. Whilst the salty rim didn’t appeal to my palate in this combination, this certainly is a juice that would be great on a hot summer’s day.
Rs 50 (usd 0.7) 
7/10

Banana Beetroot Juice
A thick and creamy concoction that’s served in a banana skill shell! The banana dominates on the palate, with a touch of sugar, the beetroot whispers its faint earthiness. 
Rs 50 (usd 0.7) 
8/10

popular punjabi restaurant, vegetarian and non-vegetarian, indiranagar, bangalore, kebabs, curries, butter chicken, tandoori chicken, paneer tikka, machhi tikka, fish tikka, dal makhani, butter chicken, seekh kebab, baingan bartha, palak, paneer, mutton barra kebab, mutton rogan josh, rasmalai, moong dal halwa, gulab jamoon  

The year was 1993. A Punjabi from Delhi with a young family, hotel management degree from the US and a stint with a leading hospitality chain, landed in Bengaluru on business. Taken in by the city’s salubrious weather, he set up a tiny 400 sq. ft. restaurant called Treat to serve up "Saddi Dilli" style Punjabi food. 27 years on, Treat has integrated well into Indiranagar, Bengaluru’s culinary landscape with a loyal following in the area and beyond. Its founder, Pramod Chaudhry is now joined by his son and daughter, as they look to take on the challenges brought on by the current pandemic. I visit them, and savour many of the hearty Punjabi kebabs and curries, vegetarian and non-vegetarian, that helped this neighbourhood eatery make it to many a Bangalorean’s speed-dial way before delivery apps appeared on the scene! Hope you enjoy this one, take care and stay safe.

Bharwan Tandoor Aloo
Potato stuffed with paneer and veggies, cooked in a tandoor and then sliced pinwheel style. 
Rs. 240 (usd 3.2) for 6 pcs

This paneer is soft and creamy, well marinated in the tikka masala and cooked in the tandoor with delicious charred edges. On the palate, it is the flavour of the ajwain, carom seed, that shines. 
Rs. 255 (usd 3.4) for 6 pcs

The seer fish kebab is fresh and flakey to the touch, and despite being cooked in the searing heat of the tandoor, is moist and juicy. The seasoning has penetrated all the way in, making for a flavourful tikka till the very last bite.

Mutton Seekh Kebab

Mutton Barra Kebab

https://goo.gl/maps/x3KdAFXHnNDm1u6VA.description:
#roomaliroll #kabab #bangalore

popular drive-in, car service eatery, kabab korner, rolls, kebabs, roomali roti, curries, north indian, chicken roomali roll, paneer, malai kabab, hariyali kabab, st marks road, bangalore

When it came to grabbing a quick bite of mostly kebabs and rolls, Kabab Korner, located in what was once upon a time the heart of Bangalore’s nightlife and entertainment action, ruled. One pulled up at the eatery, placed an order and would be relishing piping hot food served in the car a few minutes later. Over the years the action moved elsewhere, the number of vehicles on the city’s roads exploded manifold making it difficult to park, and ergo, Kabab Korner seems to have all but dropped from radar. In this short episode, I take advantage of the current lull in traffic and head back here after many years to relive old memories of their chicken roomali roll and a couple of kebabs. Hope you enjoy this one, stay safe and happy eating!

Chicken Roomali Roll
Served in a soft roomali roti with enough shredded chicken tikka and plenty of onions tossed with spices, the kabab korner chicken roomali roti still makes for a satisfying snack. 
Rs. 210 (usd 2.8)
8/10

Malai Kebab
The kebab is moist and juicy, when savoured steaming hot.
Rs. 365 (usd 4.9)
7/10

Hariyali Kebab
You can taste the freshness of the coriander and mint in the green marinade, and the spicy kick of chilli too. The marinade though hasn't penetrated into the meat, making for a bland third or fourth chew of the kebab. 
Rs. 365 (usd 4.9)
6/10

https://goo.gl/maps/9Bn528LKAHCqPbZcA.title: PURNABRAMHA Maharashtrian Vegetarian Cuisine| A Woman’s Tribute To Authentic Flavours Of Her Land
https://goo.gl/maps/9Bn528LKAHCqPbZcA.description:
#vegetarian #jayantikathale #bangalore

purnabramha, popular maharashtrian restaurant, jayanti kathale, lady entrepreneur, woman enterprise, maharashtrian vegetarian cuisine, bangalore, vada pav, sabudana vada, kothmir vadi, vada, maaswadi rasa, narayangaon, maharashtra, pune, bharleli vaangi, eggplant, varan bhaat, dal rice, modak, ganesh chaturthi, puran poli, shirval, 

A 27-hour flight from Australia to Bengaluru sans any vegetarian food for her husband and child spurred Jayanti Kathale to give up her career as an IT professional and set up an enterprise fuelled by the mission of propagating vegetarian Maharashtrian cuisine across the globe. With a humble beginning, selling modaks online, Purnabramha has evolved into a full-fledged restaurant offering with multiple centres in India and overseas. I catch up with this firebrand entrepreneur at one of her restaurants in Bengaluru, watch the making of a unique maaswadi rassa, a dish from Narayangaon, before sitting down to a satisfying Maharashtrian meal that begins with an expected vada pav and sabudana vada but travels far beyond. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay safe and happy eating!


Solkadi
An appetising start to the milk, sour kokum extract infused in spiced coconut milk.
Rs. 150 (usd 2)
8/10

Vada Pav
The vada pav here is served in the traditional Maharashtrian style, a lightly flavoured batata vada in a laadi pav with a generous rub of kanda-lehsun chutney, choora, fried batter pearls for crunch, and lavangi, salted and fried green chillies. 
Rs. 35 (usd 0.5)
8.5/10

Sabudana Vada
A textbook sabudana vada, crisp and crunchy on the outside and moist and yielding inside. The spicing is minimal in keeping with its reputation as a ‘upavaschi faraal’ or fasting snack. The sweet and sour yoghurt dip is a perky accompaniment to the vada.
Rs. 154 (usd 2) for 6 pieces.
8/10

Kothmir Vadi
The sort of snack that you would find in a Maharashtrian home. Generous amounts of coriander (kothmir, in Marathi) combine with spices and chickpea flour in two versions, steamed and fried. I preferred the fried version. 
Rs. 176 (usd 2.3)
7/10

Combo Main Course Platter
A great plate to taste the depth and variety of Maharashtrian cuisine in dishes that aren’t commonplace. The spicy rasa grips you by the throat, the soft and wholesome tandala chi bhakri (rice rotti) helps tone down the spicy fervour of the rasa. The maaswadi, a vegetarian’s imaginative take on the bone and marrow concept, is an interesting play of flavours and textures - smooth, spicy chickpea paste that’s stuffed with a mixture that comprises sesame seeds, coconut, peanuts, etc. if you like it spicy, combine the bhakri with the chilli thecha and onions. The bharleli vangi offers a flavourful bite, swathed in a nutty peanut based gravy,
Rs. 280 (usd 3.7)
9/10

Thup Varan Bhat Nimbu 
A simple, soul-pleasing plate of mildly flavoured daal (varan) seasoned with toasted thup (ghee), served with rice. There’s some methkut, a five-lentil, spice and asafoetida concoction, on the plate for added punch.
Rs. 110 (usd 1.5)
8.5/10

Shirval
A vegan-friendly, low on sweetness dessert, made of rice flour that’s collected into a dough, poached, before being pressed into noodles that are then steamed. The steamed noodles, combined with coconut cream, a touch of jaggery and almond flakes, is the delicate sort that dissolves when placed in the mouth. 
Rs. 350 (usd 4.7)
8/10

Modak
Lord Ganesha’s favourite sweet, Purnabramha’s modak is a must-order. Within the austere exterior of the modak lurks a caramelised, coconutty mixture, fortified with reduced milk, that will sing to your palate. 
Rs. 150 (usd 2) for 4 pieces.
10/10

Puran Poli
Purnabramha has sold 750,000 of these, and for good reason. Jaggery-sweetened chickpea paste flavoured with a touch of nutmeg and rolled in a wheat dough, this is the sort of dessert that’s best enjoyed with plenty of thup (ghee)! 
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2) 
9/10

ADDRESS -  Purnabramha, VCR Stone Corner, 780, 17th Cross Road, Opp Pappu Chaywala, 1st Sector, HSR Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560102; tel +91 81056 45499

https://goo.gl/maps/Sd6x5FcdckcF2xvt7.title: Tasting East Bengaluru’s Insanely Popular  MALLIKA WOOD-FIRED BIRYANI | Mutton Curry, Chicken Fry
https://goo.gl/maps/Sd6x5FcdckcF2xvt7.description:
#mallikabiriyani #muttonbiryani #bangalore

Bengaluru’s Newest Biryani Craze, Mallika Biriyani, sells over 500 kilos of meat biryanis every weekend! Mutton biryani, chicken biryani, homestyle mutton curry, chicken fry, liver fry, boti fry, raagi mudde, kothanur, east bangalore

Mallika Biriyani is the fascinating story of a computer engineer who began a biryani shop six years ago with an investment of Rs. 10,000 after a string of failed ventures. In the early days, he would procure a kilo of mutton each day, today the shop has evolved to a bustling biryani destination which procures over 500 kilos of meat on weekends to cater to the thronging crowds here. I make a 20-km trek through town to the far flung suburb of Kothanur in East Bengaluru to catch up with Venkatesh for a close look at his enterprise, and also taste the five or six dishes on offer here including his unique wood-fired biryani creation which comes across as a delicious confluence of various styles. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay safe and happy eating!

Mutton Curry
A pleasing homestyle mutton preparation that’s cooked slowly on a wood fire, the fat in the meat renders into the gravy giving the curry a lip-smacking unctuous richness. The meat slides off the bone, the curry is a great combination with the rice and raagi mudde. If you need one reason to make the trip to Mallika, this would be it!
Rs. 180 (usd 2.4)
10/10

Chicken Fry
Made in a flavour coriander-greenchilli-coriander masala, this is a zesty chicken dish. The meat is cooked perfectly down to the bone. 
Rs. 80 (usd 1.1)
8/10

Boti Fry
The boti is soft, cooked well and spiked with loads of pepper. Its only fault however, its sandy griminess on the bite, which can be difficult to get past when you are eating offal.
Rs. 100 (usd 1.3)
6/10

Liver Fry
A preparation, identical to the pepper-laced boti fry, it’s a pity the flavourful warmth of the masala could not penetrate the ‘tough-on-the-bite liver.
Rs. 100 (usd 1.3)
7/10

Chicken Biryani
The biryanis are served in large portions, there’s plenty of rice, and 5 or 6 pieces of chicken, which makes it a great biryani to share. On the nose, there’s the smokey character from the wood-fire, you can taste the depth of flavour in the rice from the spices. The meat is moist, though mellow in its flavours and benefits from being eaten with the flavourful rice, that is a mixture of two varietals, the ‘starchy’ short-grained seeraga samba and the ‘low on starch’ medium-sized-grain, bullet variety.
Rs. 130 (usd 1.7)
8.5/10

Mutton Biryani
Seven or eight pieces of meat in a mutton biryani at Rs. 230 makes it great in terms of value, and perhaps also lends to its mass appeal. The spicing and masala is identical to the chicken version, but the character of the mutton, with a bit of fat, imbues the biryani with a mellow, warming flavour note that’s more rounded on the palate. The meat is juicy, and has a bit of a bite. If you like your flavours a bit punchy, taste it with the sherva, the gravy of the mutton curry.
Rs. 230 (usd 3.1)
9/10

https://goo.gl/maps/N8rjbD3qRNwwdu8x8.title: MY LAST MEAL At KOSHY’S BENGALURU | Fish Biryani, Kerala Prawn, Tomato Cheese Toast, Mutton Omelette
https://goo.gl/maps/N8rjbD3qRNwwdu8x8.description:
#koshys #bangalore #popularrestaurant 

popular bangalore restaurant, bengaluru, koshys cafe, koshys bakery, jewel box, popular breakfast in bangalore, popular lunch, coffee shop, bakery, all day breakfast, mutton omelette, tomato cheese toast, fish biryani, kerala prawn fry, chilli chicken, plum cake, coffee

Most of my visits to Bengaluru’s iconic Koshy’s, an eatery that dates back to pre-independence times, have almost always been for their all-day breakfast. Simple omelettes, comforting toasts made with wholesome bread from their bakery, old-fashioned cutlets and sandwiches, the sort that can brighten up a dull day. In this episode, filmed just before they closed doors owing to the current crisis, I partake of a couple of their breakfast must-haves, their crowd-pleasing fish biriyani and a prawn fry that pays ode to the establishment’s Keralan roots, and also take a look at how they tried their their best to keep serving customers in these trying times. I hope this landmark cafe, an indelible part of the city’s history, emerges stronger in due course. Take care and stay safe.

Do catch our previous Koshy’s episode for an in-depth look at their history and the must-have breakfast dishes here:
KOSHY’S BEST BREAKFAST DISHES| Mutton Cutlet, Appam Stew, English Brekkie... Exclusive KITCHEN TOUR https://youtu.be/YCMp44D6jak

Tomato Cheese Toast
This dish celebrates the sweet tartness and textures of tomato - crisp dices, sauteed near pulpy bits and thick sauce slathered over thick toast of Koshy’s homemade bread. Shavings of cheese round off the flavours with savoury notes. 
Rs. 170 (usd 2.3) 
8/10

Mutton Omelette
Food doesn’t have to be complicated, but the sort where it touches your soul. Like this simple omelette, beaten egg rolled around mutton mince that seasoned sparingly, sings the flavor of the meat. Savoured with some toast and butter, this is the breakfast of Koshy’s champions!
Rs. 240 (usd 3.2) 
8/10

Chilli Chicken
Koshy’s version of this Sino-Indian staple that one will only find in India is generous in the peppers and onions, but lacking in some chilli punch one would expect. I also wish the sauce had permeated the chicken better. 
Rs. 360 (usd 4.8) 
6/10

Fish Biriyani
This fish biriyani has been on Koshy’s menu for decades and is the sort that requires one to redefine the notions of a biryani. Composed of plump steaks of kingfish, fried, cooked in a gravy and then topped with basmati rice, it isn’t one for the biryani purist, but certainly makes an impression on the palate.
Rs. 430 (usd 5.8) 
7/10

Kerala Prawn Fry
A delicious preparation of tiny fried chemmeen, prawns. One can taste the sweetness of the prawns juxtaposed against the toasty herbaceousness of the curry leaves, the singe of pepper, the lilt of coriander and other spices.
Rs. 500 (usd 6.7) 
9/10

Plum Cake
Koshy’s plum cake has legions of fans not just in Bengaluru and the country but across the world. The fruits are macerated, rendering a slightly bitter edge against the sweetness and subtle spicing of this plum cake that is not as heady and alcohol-laced as some traditional cakes can be. It makes for the perfect sweet close to a meal here with some coffee.
Rs. 40 (usd 0.5) 
9/10

Koshy’s Special Coffee
Rs. 52 (usd 0.7) 
8/10

https://goo.gl/maps/N8rjbD3qRNwwdu8x8.description:
#Breakfast #KoshysParadeCafe #GourmetOnTheRoad
 Koshy’s is a landmark establishment in Bengaluru that has been around since the 1950s, popular for its old world charm and vintage decor. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna, meets with Mr. Prem Koshy, third generation co-owner of this hallowed institution to discover its surprisingly humble origins. 

He savours some of the most popular breakfast items from their expansive menu, including the homemade Baked Beans on Toast, Chicken Liver on Toast, Club Sandwich and of course, their signature Appam and Stew, a signature dish that is served only on Sunday!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD 
BAKED BEANS ON TOAST
Homemade baked beans generously slathered on a thick slice of Koshy’s bread. The earthy flavours of the beans and tangy tomato, make this dish very comforting. 
Rs. 130
7/10

MUSHROOM ON TOAST
A simple dish of mushrooms sauteed in some garlic and pepper, spread over buttered toast. The earthiness of the mushroom is what’s most prominent. A must-try for every mushroom lover. 
Rs. 130
7.5/10

TOMATO AND CHEESE ON TOAST
A beautiful plate popping with contrasting colours of the sauteed tomatoes and cheese. The jammy flavours of the tomatoes are delicious. Acidic and salty flavours, yum!
Rs. 130
8/10

VEGETABLE CUTLET
An old fashioned cutlet made from a medley of veggies, peas, carrots and potatoes, spiced delicately. There's a certain creaminess that takes over the palate.
Rs. 75
8/10

MUTTON CUTLET 
Hot and crisp to the touch. A delicious mutton cutlet, the crumbed exterior holds that flavourful spiced mutton mince. A textbook mutton cutlet. Old fashioned, like mum would make.
Rs.100
9/10
 
MR. K's BIG EASY ENGLISH BREAKFAST
Tawa toast slathered with baked beans and fried sunny side up eggs, crisp, plump pork sausage, fries, and a side of veggies. Layered with flavours, this is definitely an indulgent breakfast. 
Rs. 450 
7.5/10

SPANISH OMELETTE.
This old-fashioned omelette is a big, protein-packed meal in itself, especially with the fries. This is a loaded omelette. It's cheesy; it has the meaty bite of the chicken, a salty hit from the bacon, and a crunch from the peppers.
Rs.300
9/10

MR K'S GINGER FRUIT PUNCH
You can taste an assortment of fruits like papaya, apple, banana, and grape. You get the mellow spike of ginger and its wellness boost. Quite a filling drink. 
Rs. 75
8/10

CHICKEN LIVER TOAST 
A must-try dish for liver lovers! There’s very little that gets in the way of the rich deep flavour of the liver. The peppers pick up the flavour. The thick soft bread has absorbed liver gravy.
Rs.130
9/10

CLUB SANDWICH
Fried egg, slice of ham. roast lamb, chicken, tomatoes, onions, and some lettuce all encased in that soft bread from Koshy's bakery. You get the flavour of the roast meat, the pungent bite of onions. There’s the creaminess of the egg enveloping it. 
Rs. 190
8.5/10


APPAM AND MUTTON STEW 
Traditionally only served on a Sunday. The mellow, creamy coconut milk has a hint of whole spices. The meat has soaked in the flavours of the stew but the flavour of the meat itself shines through. 
Rs.170
10/10

COFFEE
Nice and strong with a robust hit. Just the thing you need to pick you up after a big heavy breakfast here.
Rs. 39
8/10 

ADDRESS- Koshy’s Parade Cafe, No. 39, St Marks Road, Shanthala Nagar, Ashok Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560001

https://goo.gl/maps/ppE2Pvju9zW368W47.title: Exploring Bengaluru’s Timeless IYENGAR BAKERY Tradition At 60-Year-Old Sri Jayalakshmi Bakery
https://goo.gl/maps/ppE2Pvju9zW368W47.description:
#iyengarbakery #traditionalbakery #bangalore 

popular bakery, traditional bakery, bengaluru, iyengar bakery, benne biscuit, vegetable puff, egg puff, aloo bun congress, khara bun, bun butter jam, dilpasand, honey cake, almond biscuit, salt biscuit, khara biscuit

The Iyengar Bakery is an integral part of Bengaluru’s culinary landscape. Located in almost every neighbourhood of the city, these traditional bakeries date back to the turn of the last century when two Iyengar brothers from the Ashtagrama (a cluster of eight villages) area in Hassan made their way to Bengaluru in search of livelihoods, and built on the legacy of British bakeries with their own customs and flavours. Over the years, more from the community followed in their footsteps, a trend exacerbated by the famine of the 50s which rendered agriculture in the villages unviable, leading to the rapid growth of Iyengar bakeries in Bengaluru, Mysuru and elsewhere in the South.  In this episode, I visit Sri Jayalakshmi Bakery, a 60-year old bakery that though rooted in its traditions has made space to evolve with the times. Needless to say, I also taste many of the calorie-laden but deliciously addictive goodies that have built for these time-honoured establishments a loyal fan following over the years. Hope you enjoy this one, stay safe and happy eating!

Benne (butter) Biscuit
The sort of cookie that’s crumbly, fragile and almost melts in the mouth. 
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4) per 100 gm 
8/10

Vegetable Puff
Bite into the airy crunch of layers of pastry that traps within its folds a flavourful vegetable stuffing. A popular snack anytime of the day. 
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) 
8/10

Egg Puff
One you get past the airy crunch of the pastry layers, you taste the creamy egg bhurji that's fortified with half a boiled egg. Reason why these outsell the vegetable puff in a traditionally vegetarian establishment.
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) 
9/10

Khara Bun
A generous hit of curry leaf and green chilli in a spice mix stains this popular bun a yellowish green and also gives it a spicy bite. The savoury notes of toasted onions and a smidgen of sugar rounds off the flavours on the palate.
Rs. 15 (usd 0.2) 
9/10

Aloo Bun Congress
Picture a soft bun stuffed with a creamy, lightly tempered potato mash. Slice it open and slather on a generous helping of spiced peanuts. That’s the ABC for you. Soft and creamy with the toasty, spicy crunch of peanuts, delicious down to the last bite.
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4) 
9/10

Bun Butter Jam
A sweet, raisin speckled bun sandwich slathered with salted butter and Sri Jayalakshmi’s homemade mixed fruit jam, on the palate it evokes memories of a comforting bread, butter jam sandwich packed in a school snack box.
Rs. 32 (usd 0.4) 
8/10

Dilpasand
Sri Jayalakshmi Bakery’s most popular sweet offering is the sort of calorie-laden indulgence that helps you get past a bad day, if you are having one.Puff pastry stuffed with freshly grated coconut, raisins, glazed cherries, tutti frutti, cashew nuts and scented with cardamom! Sweet Bliss!
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) 
10/10

Honey Cake
Another one for the sweet tooth, a butter sponge cake dipped in a sugary syrup and rolled over in desiccated coconut. The sweetness, though is cut, thankfully, by the acidity of the jam that’s smeared on top.
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) 
7/10

Almond Biscuit
The sort that breaks off in a crisp, soft, crunch.
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4) per 100 gm 
8/10

Salt Biscuit
Initially, you taste almost nothing, but then you are surprised by its salty spike that makes a late appearance on the palate. 
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4) per 100 gm 
8/10

Khara Biscuit
Flavours of the khara bun - curry leaf, chillies, onions and jeera - but in a biscuit form.
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4) per 100 gm 
8/10

ADDRESS -  Sri Jayalakshmi Bakery, No.1, Lal Bagh Main Rd, Srinivas Colony, Sudhama Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560027; tel +91 99458 89911

https://goo.gl/maps/Fk6wWYRuefqdQ4Si8.title: Making The Nellore-Style ANDHRA BIRYANI At Most Popular NANDHANA PALACE | Tasting 13 Iconic Dishes
https://goo.gl/maps/Fk6wWYRuefqdQ4Si8.description:
#nandhanapalace #andhracuisine #bangalore

andhra cuisine, meal, andhra biryani, nellore biryani, nandhana palace, bangalore’s largest andhra restaurant chain, sholay kebab, drumstick soup, mutton bone soup, chilli chicken, chicken kshatriya, chicken amravati, nellore mutton biryani, mati kodi biryani, chicken biryani

In good times or bad, Bengaluru loves its biryani and the one biryani that is perhaps most favoured here is the Andhra biryani. A biryani that’s nuanced in its depth of flavour and finds its roots in the Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh. In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, I catch the making of this traditional biryani from start to finish at the newest outpost of Bengaluru’s largest chain of Andhra restaurants, Nandhana Palace. In doing so, I chat with second generation owner, Shweta Ravi, and learn of her family’s commitment to culinary traditions over three decades, and also savour the many creations of the kitchens here that are now synonymous with Andhra cuisine. Hope you enjoy this one. Stay safe and happy eating!


Drumstick Soup
Made of drumstick marrow and leaves, this is a soup that’s warming and rich in nutrients.
Rs. 95 (usd 1.3) 
8/10

Mutton Bone Soup
Mutton bones simmered over hours into a spicy broth, served with a tender piece of meat that offers a juicy bite of this soup. 
Rs. 120 (usd 1.6) 
9/10

Carrot 65
There’s little in the flavour of the reddish-orange batter-fried discs tossed in garlic, curry leaves and spices that reveals it’s made of carrots! If you are a vegetarian looking to savour the flavour of the legendary chicken 65, this Nandhana Palace invention is perhaps the closest you can get.
Rs. 185 (usd 2.5) 
8/10

Sholay Kebab
This invention of the kitchens at Nandhana Palace is now synonymous with fried chicken Andhra style. Marinated in a yoghurt and spice masala and deep-fried, the result is a kebab that’s moist to the core and seriously addictive.
Rs. 270 (usd 3.6) 
9/10

Chilli Chicken
The chicken is coated in a sauce of naati (local) green chillies that packs a ferocious, palate-numbing punch. If you have a high tolerance for chilli heat, do pop a few of the whole chillies floating in the dish to derive the painful yet satisfying pleasure of indulging in the Andhra chilli chicken. 
Rs. 240 (usd 3.2) 
8/10

Chicken Kshatriya
This dish is an ode to the family’s Kshatriya lineage. Stained bright yellow with turmeric, the fresh flavours of the masala hold to the chicken leg, making for a flavourful bite. A touch of cashew nut also renders a rich note to the sauce alongside the pungency of garlic. 
Rs. 270 (usd 3.6) 
9/10

Amravati Chicken
Boneless morsels of chicken cooked in a semi-gravy rich in the savoury flavours of fried onions, curry leaves and hint of fennel. 
Rs. 280 (usd 3.7) 
8/10

Mutton Pepper Fry
The meat is cooked to pink tenderness and its flavour reigns supreme beyond the pepper-rich masala. The cooks at Nandhana Palace certainly know how to treat the meat right. 
Rs. 290 (usd 3.9) 
9/10

Bamboo Chicken
A tribal dish that finds its provenance in the Araku valley of Andhra Pradesh, it features chicken that’s marinated in green and red chillies, ginger, garlic and other fresh ingredients, and then poached in its juices in a sealed bamboo cross section over fire.  
Rs. 299 (usd 4) 
8/10

Nellore Mutton Biryani
Layers of flavour from the spices - cloves, cinnamon, marat moggu, bayleaf, etc., waft through your palate when you place a morsel of the basmati rice in your mouth. You can also taste the underlying sweet acidity of the pineapple, a unique ingredient of the Nellore biryani. The meat has a bit of a bite, and is flavourful. 
Rs. 290 (usd 3.9) 
10/10

Nati Kodi Biryani
Made with short-grained seeraga samba rice, the nati kodi biryani takes over the palate with its spicy, green chilli laden flavours laced with the freshness of coriander and mint, and the toasty savouriness of fried onions. The rice when tasted on its own has a salty edge which complements the feisty character of the country chicken. 
Rs. 270 (usd 3.6) 
8.5/10

Takeaway available at all Nandhana palace outlets. To order across Bengaluru, call +91 80 4613 1111

https://g.page/ebony-restaurant?share.title: LAST LUNCH At EBONY, Bengaluru’s Most Popular Multi-Cuisine Restaurant | Arcot Chops, Butter Chicken
https://g.page/ebony-restaurant?share.description:
#ebony #bangalore #multicuisine

popular bangalore restaurant, bengaluru, ebony, 13th floor, asean on the edge, popular multicuisine restaurant, popular lunch, pan indian, asian, arcot lamb chop, kakori kebab, thai crisp vegetables, nonya prawns, dal makhni, butter chicken, diwani handi

My first meal in Bengaluru when I moved here 25 years ago was at Ebony, a restaurant perched on the 13th floor of one of the city’s earliest highrises. Dining under the stars, I distinctly remember the food, a smattering of Parsi, Pan Indian and Continental, dished up, simply minus any pretence yet solid in its flavours, much like the character of the city I now call home. I learnt later that the restaurant came into being quite by accident, born out of a crisis after its owner, Rajesh Rajaram, having bought the property as an investment was unable to flip it owing to the adverse fall out of the first Gulf war. Over the years, Ebony has successfully weathered many crises, evolving multiple avatars, the city’s most ‘democratic’ bar and more recently, an Asian restaurant. But sadly, the economic brunt of the current situation seems to have gotten the better of this Bengaluru bellwether. I visit Ebony for their last lunch service as they close shop to emerge stronger in a couple of months. Take care and stay safe. Happy eating!

Do catch our wine tasting table at Ebony here:
A Tasting Of Indian Wines From SULA & KRSMA|TASTING TABLE|Pairing Food & Wine|White Wines For Summer  https://youtu.be/p7TDogoQWok

Nonya Crunchy Butter Prawns
Despite being crumbed in a flavoursome buttery crunch that resonates the toasty herbaceousness of crispened curry leaves and the tingling heat of red chillies, the faint sweetness of the prawns shines through. 
Rs. 495 (usd 6.6) 
8.5/10

Thai Crispy Vegetables
Vegetables served up in a crispy batter with a honey-chilli combination, this was a vegetarian favourite at 13th Floor. The peppery notes of basil accents this appetiser.
Rs. 355 (usd 4.7) 
8/10

Salonee Broccoli
Moistened in a saffron-mustard marinade, the grilled broccoli florets unburden the punchy mustard flavours on the palate. The processed cheese rounds off flavours of this tasty appetiser. 
Rs. 320 (usd 4.3) 
8/10

Arcot Mutton Chops
A ghee laden lamb chop that is slow-cooked to juicy doneness, and then charred on a grill to form a delicious masala crust. A traditional Mudaliar dish, the ghee in this heroes the juicy bite of the meat. A must-have when at Ebony. 
Rs. 545 (usd 7.3) 
10/10

Kakori Kebab
Tender, rich in fat, lamb mince that is massaged with gentle spices and grilled on a skewer, these fragile kebabs leave a warming smokey, decadent impression as they melt away when placed in the mouth.
Rs. 525 (usd 6.7) 
9/10

Ebony’s Ultimate Butter Chicken
Rich in the tart sweetness of the tomatoes that cradles the tandoori spiced, grilled chicken, this is a dish that is supposedly a popular order here. I would have enjoyed a bit more kasoori methi punch in this makhan-laden dish. Having said that, it’s a dish that is comforting with a hot roti.
Rs. 495 (usd 6.7) 
8/10

Hyderabadi Deewan E Handi
Vegetables cooked in a rich cashew and onion gravy, the softened shallots add a punch of demure sweetness. 
Rs. 385 (usd 6.7) 
8/10

Malaidar Dal Makhni
Loved the smokey, buttery flavours of the dal makhni that has been cooked slowly allowing for the flavours to develop. This is a dal that I would happily return for. 
Rs. 325 (usd 6.7) 
9/10

https://goo.gl/maps/LzMQgsjySnPaw3Cg9.description:
#MarataDarshan #NonVegetarian #MarathaCuisine

popular non vegetarian lunch, maratha cuisine, marata darshan, military hotels, bengaluru, bangalore popular lunch spot, mutton korma, chilli chicken, ragi, raagi mudde, kheema unde, mince ball, curry, mutton liver fry, chicken biryani

Maratha warriors entered Karnataka over a couple of centuries ago, drawn to battle, but were eventually disarmed by the people, customs and traditions of the land. And so they stayed back integrating into the local community, adopting culinary practices along the way. And thus was born Karnataka style Maratha fare, distinctly different from that found in the neighbouring state. I revisit Marata Darshan, a family-run eatery that though immensely popular today had rather humble beginnings on a pushcart nearly 30 years ago. Hope you enjoy this episode, take care and stay safe. Happy eating.

Do catch our previous Marata Darshan episode for an in-depth look at the kitchen, meet the family, and savour many other dishes:
MARATHA STYLE NON-VEGETARIAN Food | MARATA DARSHAN | Naati Koli Saaru, Mutton Chops & More! https://youtu.be/WF5Yb2q-0VA

Kheema Unde
These mutton mince roundels, floating in a spicy broth are soft to the touch and on the palate exude only the flavour of meat punctuated with spices. 
Rs. 200 (usd 2.6) 
9/10

Chilli Chicken
The Maratha version, rich in tomatoes, green chilli and pepper; the chicken is moist and juicy, cooked perfectly down to the bone.
Rs. 150 (usd 2) 
9/10

Mutton Liver Fry
The liver has bite but is still creamy, any gaminess is offset by the flavours of the pepper that the liver is roasted in. It makes for a delicious meal with the thin chapatis served here. 
Rs. 200 (usd 2.6) 
8.5/10

Mutton Korma
Meat that is swathed in a generous amount of fat, the meat is cooked long until soft and tender. Barring the initial bite, it breaks down in the mouth instantly. The rice and korma are the perfect match, the rice doing well to absorb the deep unctuous flavours of the curry.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.6) 
10/10

Chicken Biryani
A local Karnataka style biryani, the rice is moist and redolent with the flavour of mint and coriander, the meat peels away from the bone and exudes a smokey aroma. It’s the sort of biryani that works well when you taste the rice and meat together, add some if you need a spicier punch.
Rs. 180 (usd 2.4) 
8/10

https://goo.gl/maps/LzMQgsjySnPaw3Cg9.description:
#MilitaryHotelsInBangalore #NonVegetarianFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

Maratha Cuisine In Bengaluru. Military Style Food In Bangalore. Ragi Mudde and Mutton Chops Thali.

Gorge on mouthwatering military-style food, especially robust mutton dishes at Marata Darshan in Bengaluru. Established by Shantharaj Lad back in 1989, this humble eatery is known for its wholesome military style meals served for breakfast and lunch. Presently run by the father, mother and son trio, the reason behind the restaurant’s success are traditional recipes by the mother, Hemavathi Bai.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna meets the family in this episode of Gourmet On The Road. He unveils the secret behind the eatery’s success and explores the must eat dishes here through a short kitchen tour. He then sit downs for a meal tasting the Mutton Chops Thali served with either rice and the restaurant’s signature Ragi Mudde, Koli Saaru, Mutton Kheema Curry and a bowl of Soppina Saaru. He also tastes must-try sides, a peppery Mutton Liver Fry, a flavourful Chilli Chicken, a wet Chicken 65 made with a yoghurt gravy and Mutton Korma.

NAATI KOLI SAARU
the gravy of this naati koli saaru certainly has some chilli kick to it. one can also taste layers of spice and the garam masala. the soft, pasty ragi mudde is perfect to be dunked into this flavourful saaru.
rs 200. (2.80 usd)
9/10

MUTTON CHOPS
the meat in this hearty curry has a good distribution of fat and the mutton still has its bite intact. the masala has a mellow lingering heat perhaps from some warm spices like cloves and cinnamon. the mutton with the gravy makes for a juicy bite.
rs 170 (2.40 usd)
9/10

CHICKEN PEPPER
this chicken is liberally spiced with pepper that gives it a delicious, toasty flavour note. you taste the juiciness of the chicken that has been cooked to perfection and the freshness of coarse ground pepper and a slight savouriness perhaps from some onion.
rs 140 (2 usd)
9/10

CHILLI CHICKEN
easily one of the best ‘local-style’ chilli chicken I have tasted! the chicken just yields, and parts effortlessly from the bone. the masala made with plenty of tomatoes and green chilli is fingerlicking good! the chilli heat isn’t palate-numbing like other versions of its ilk.
rs 130. (1.80 usd)
9.5/10

CHICKEN 65
the chicken 65 here is a wet gravy of chicken kebab tossed in a thick gravy of yoghurt, curry leaves, dry red chillies and spices. the flavour of the dish is a little too tart, an interesting take on the 65, but plays a distant second fiddle to the other dishes.
rs 140 (2 usd)
7/10

KHEEMA UNDE GRAVY
love the rogan or thin veil of fat floating over this thick, lush gravy that is perfect to be ladelled over the unde or meatball. all you taste is the meat and the gentle spicing. the gravy merely straddles the unde without overpowering its nuanced flavour. the quality of meat in this dish is just brilliant!
rs 170 (2.40 usd)
9.5/10

MUTTON LIVER PEPPER FRY
mutton liver can usually be tough when cooked this way but in this dish, the meaty liver is quite yielding to the bite. there's none of the gamey meatiness. you taste the roasted pepper.  to hold itself up to the meatiness of the liver, the strength of the pepper is a lot more apparent in this preparation.
rs 170 (2.40 usd)
8.5/10

SOPPINA SAARU
love the earthy flavours of this soppina saaru that is made with a bunch of different greens. you can sense the nourishment you get from every scoop of rice that's soaked in the soppina saaru!
8.5/10

RASAM 
this almost clear rasam has an apparent tartness from some tamarind and you can definitely taste prominent notes of cumin or jeera. 
7/10

ADDRESS - Marata Darshan, Kaverappa Layout, Vasanth Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560051; tel: 9902021970

https://goo.gl/maps/e4voDdkbLHrnzpaW7.title: AIRLINES HOTEL | Bengaluru’s Most Popular Outdoor Eatery | Butter Masala Dosa, Mangalore Buns & More
https://goo.gl/maps/e4voDdkbLHrnzpaW7.description:
#AirlinesHotel #ButterMasalaDosa #DriveInRestaurant

bengaluru, bangalore popular breakfast, drive-in restaurant, garden restaurant, pure vegetarian, south indian, mangalore buns, sambar vada, medu vada, butter masala dosa, dose, akki rotti, channa bhatura, south indian snack, sambar, chutney, kesari bath, basundi, lavelle road, state bank of india road, coffee 

Named simply for the reason that an airline office was located down the road when it first opened its doors as Bengaluru’s first drive-in restaurant in 1968, Airlines Hotel harks back to a time when life was uncomplicated. As evident in its non-pretentious South Canara fare headlined by the wafer-crisp butter masala dose, that has won it legions of fans over the years, served under the magnificent verdant canopy of ancient banyan trees. Some may say the restaurant is a relic of the past, but then life has a way of coming full circle, the restaurant’s garden eating providing a much-needed social-distanced setting with the bonus of Bengaluru’s glorious outdoorsy weather. Enjoy this video. Stay safe and happy eating!

Mangalore Buns
A puffed deep-fried pastry made of maida dough that’s fortified with ripe banana, yoghurt, cumin seeds, and left to ferment. The bun is a tad chewy, the banana making its presence felt on the palate and also aiding in its subtle sweetness.
Rs. 65 (usd 0.9) 
8/10

Sambar Vada
The sort of vada that one should perhaps be tasting with steaming hot idlis if one is looking for a substantial snack. The vada isn’t crisp, but then that makes it of the perfect sponge to soak up the delicious Airlines Hotel sambar!
Rs. 65 (usd 0.9) 
7/10

Butter Masala Dosa
Loaded with butter and the resulting calories, the dose is crackling crisp and ironically a hit with Bangaloreans for whom savouring this is a ritual after an early morning walk or jog in nearby Cubbon Park! But then, to be fair this certainly a dose that can make anyone weak. Lined with a red chutney and bearing a potato stuffing that also employs the crunch of carrots and beans, this is a dose you will love if you like it crisp. 
Rs. 130 (usd 1.7) 
9/10

Akki Rotti
The akki rotti is crisp around the edges and a tad dry on the bite. However, this filling snack is redeemed by the moistness of the gentle coconut-urugadle chutney, to take the spice quotient a few notches higher, taste it with the pungent byadgi chilli-garlic chutney. 
Rs. 115 (usd 1.5) 
7/10

Channa Bhatura
A popular lunch order, this isn't your typical NorthIndian style dark-coloured and deep-flavoured chole. Get over that and you will be rewarded by a tasty combination of the chickpea with a steaming hot bhatura.
Rs. 155 (usd 2.05) 
7.5/10

Kesari Bath
Not a lush ghee-laden version of a popular Bengaluru tiffin, the version here is rich in pineapple flavours. 
Rs. 90 (usd 1.2) 
7/10

Basundi
If you enjoy dairy-richness, you will dig the lushness of this dessert, milk thickened in a pan slowly and then fortified with nuts, cardamom powder and served chilled. 
Rs. 120 (usd 1.6) 
8/10

Coffee
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7) 
8/10

https://www.google.com/maps/search/Bheem.title: Full-On ANDHRA NON-VEG Meal At BHEEMA’S | Biryani, Mutton Pepper Fry, Guntur Chicken, Chilli Chicken
https://www.google.com/maps/search/Bheem.description:
#Bheemas #AndhraFood #Bangalore

andhra cuisine, bheema’s, bengaluru, non vegetarian meal, lunch, fish fry, chilli chicken, mutton pepper fry, guntur chicken, mutton seeraga samba biryani, chicken biryani, nellore biryani, popular bengaluru lunch spot

After many a vegetarian reviews over the last few weeks, I was craving the comfort of some hearty non vegetarian fare. And so we landed at Bheema’s to savour a spicy Andhra bhojanam of fish fry, chilli chicken, mutton pepper fry, Guntur chicken, and a couple of biryanis, their staple Nellore version in addition to their ode to Bengaluru’s dhonne style biryani! And needless to say, we also took a quick look behind the scenes to see how this popular restaurant is gearing up to serve customers in these challenging times. Enjoy and stay safe. 

Fish Fry 
A tasty fry, though not the sort that will blow your socks off! It’s a thin slice of fish, napped in a sprightly masala and fried crisp around the edges.
Rs. 370 (usd 4.9) 
7/10

Chilli Chicken
No Andhra non-vegetarian meal can be complete without a chilli chicken, rich in copious amounts of green chilli and pepper. The spice hit is tongue-numbing, but one that’s vicariously addictive. The chicken is nice and juicy all the way down to the bone. 
Rs. 270 (usd 3.6) 
8/10

Mutton Pepper Fry 
The mutton is soft and yields to a gentle bite, draped in a pepper-onion masala. The meat is sheathed in some fat, which lends it its fulsome flavour. At Bheema’s they pick their meat cuts well and certainly know how to cook it well too.
Rs. 350 (usd 4.6) 
9/10

Guntur Chicken
A chicken preparation that heroes the Guntur chilli.The creaminess of the coconut though and the acidity of tomatoes in this dish balances against the heat of this otherwise spicy Andhra chilli.
Rs. 305 (usd 4) 
8/10

Mutton Jeera Rice Biryani
Bheema’s ode to the local Bengaluru biryani, this one is made with the short-grained seeraga samba rice. You can taste the fervour of coriander, mint and green chillies alongside other ingredients like the marat moggu, cloves that are typically used in this one-pot rice and meat preparation. The meat slides off the bone, it is cooked as well as that! 
Rs. 295 (usd 3.9) 
8/10

Chicken Biryani 
Bheema’s most popular dish, this traditional Nellore-style biryani is made with basmati rice. There’s flecks of pineapple that go into this biryani and you taste its acidity juxtaposed against the aromatic flavours of cloves, cinnamon and other warming spices that the chicken and rice are cooked in. The meat is soft and juicy, however it is the delicate spicing of the biryani that makes an impression on the palate and lingers long after one has finished eating.
Rs. 260 (usd 3.4) 
9/10

best_dishes.name: Fish Fry
best_dishes.summary: A tasty fry, though not the sort that will blow your socks off! It’s a thin slice of fish, napped in a sprightly masala and fried crisp around the edges.

best_dishes.name: Chilli Chicken
best_dishes.summary: No Andhra non-vegetarian meal can be complete without a chilli chicken, rich in copious amounts of green chilli and pepper. The spice hit is tongue-numbing, but one that’s vicariously addictive. The chicken is nice and juicy all the way down to the bone.

best_dishes.name: Mutton Pepper Fry
best_dishes.summary: The mutton is soft and yields to a gentle bite, draped in a pepper-onion masala. The meat is sheathed in some fat, which lends it its fulsome flavour. At Bheema’s they pick their meat cuts well and certainly know how to cook it well too.

best_dishes.name: Guntur Chicken
best_dishes.summary: A chicken preparation that heroes the Guntur chilli.The creaminess of the coconut though and the acidity of tomatoes in this dish balances against the heat of this otherwise spicy Andhra chilli.

best_dishes.name: Mutton Jeera Rice Biryani
best_dishes.summary: Bheema’s ode to the local Bengaluru biryani, this one is made with the short-grained seeraga samba rice. You can taste the fervour of coriander, mint and green chillies alongside other ingredients like the marat moggu, cloves that are typically used in this one-pot rice and meat preparation. The meat slides off the bone, it is cooked as well as that!

best_dishes.name: Chicken Biryani
best_dishes.summary: Bheema’s most popular dish, this traditional Nellore-style biryani is made with basmati rice. There’s flecks of pineapple that go into this biryani and you taste its acidity juxtaposed against the aromatic flavours of cloves, cinnamon and other warming spices that the chicken and rice are cooked in. The meat is soft and juicy, however it is the delicate spicing of the biryani that makes an impression on the palate and lingers long after one has finished eating.

South Bengaluru’s popular vegetarian restaurant, Maiyas prides itself on serving the “purest, cleanest and tastiest food”, says 72 year-old Sadananda Maiya whose family has a legacy in food for nearly a century beginning with Mavalli Tiffin Rooms in 1924. Next troops in a flavourful pulao, followed by anna (rice), sambar and rasam with a sweet payasam thrown in. Best to linger over this meal, nice and slow.
Rs. 150 (usd 2) 
9/10

Coffee
Rs. 25 (usd 0.3) 
9/10
