https://goo.gl/maps/YEA7v5D3nxKAf9i5A.title: Tasting Famous Podi Idli At MURUGAN IDLI SHOP | Krishnagiri | GHEE MASALA DOSA | PONGAL |JIGARTHANDA
https://goo.gl/maps/YEA7v5D3nxKAf9i5A.description:
#TamilBreakfast #HighwayRestaurants #GourmetOnTheRoad

An iconic breakfast spot in Tamil Nadu, Murugan Idli Shop that first began in Madurai, today, has scores of branches in Chennai. The restaurant’s latest outlet in Krishnagiri, has turned into the place to stop at for patrons driving from Bengaluru either towards Salem, Madurai or Chennai.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna makes a quick stop at the eatery for a late breakfast, tasting some of the must-tries on the menu. This includes the restaurant’s signature Podi Idli, a paper-thin Masala Dosa, a ghee-laden Pongal, the Jigarthanda and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
PLAIN IDLI
not the softest idli you will come across, this one borders on being slightly firm. you taste the tart fermented edge of the batter. the idli is best enjoyed with the chutneys. the coriander chutney has a fresh flavour while the mint chutney makes for a zesty bite. my favourite accompaniment is the nourishing sambar fortified with lentils. the texture of the idli makes it perfect to be dunked in the sambar. 
rs 20. (0.30 usd)
7.5/10

GHEE PODI IDLI
this idli is a lot more softer and has a certain springiness to it. Slathered with ghee and doused in a spirited, spicy podi, its texture is a lot more pleasing to the palate. the heat of the podi is tamed when eaten with the creamy lentils in the sambar. this is a delicious idli!
rs 32. (0.45 usd)
9/10

SPECIAL SWEET PONGAL 
this dish is laden with ghee, so much so that it feels like you aren’t just eating the pongal but the ghee too! the dish isn’t cloying sweet, the amount of jaggery used is just right. the addition of toasted cashews gives it a nice bite and also helps cut through that dairy richness of the ghee. 
rs 58. (0.80 usd)
8/10

GHEE MASALA DOSA
the dosa is crisp and translucent. you can hear it go crunch as you break into it. the potato filling is creamy, almost pate-like. a bit excessive on the salt but flavourful nonetheless. the dosa batter in no way interferes with the flavours of this soft mash. the dosa surprisingly manages to retain its crunch despite being dunked into the sambar. it's almost like biting into a puff pastry, that's how delicately crunchy this dosa is!
rs 108. (1.50 usd)
9/10

ONION UTHAPPAM
love the way this uthappam is loaded with onions! the onion has been roasted to a deep brown. you taste the delicious caramelised notes of the almost burnt onion on the top layer followed by the sweet crunch of the lightly sauteed onions below it. the thick uthappam just cradles all these delicious textures and flavours! the chutney provides for a nice break, if it gets too onion-y.
rs 89. (1.25 usd)
8.5/10

JIGARTHANDA
literally translating to ‘cool the heart’ the jigarthanda is a very popular cooler on the menu here. the orange flavoured ice cream made in-house has a texture that’s somewhere in between a gelato and sorbet. the jelly has almond essence in it, you can also taste the dairy from the basundi. if you like something cooling and refreshing, settle for this drink.
rs 70. (1 usd)
7/10

FILTER COFFEE
my choice of drink after a south indian breakfast! the sweet bitterness of the filter coffee is the right way to end a slightly over indulgent breakfast here at murugan idli shop. 
rs 32. (0.45 usd)
8/10

https://goo.gl/maps/2FMuVqHjJtJyUs4M6.title: Tasting 14 COASTAL DELICACIES At KARAVALLI Bengaluru |LOBSTER, CRAB, PRAWN, OCTOPUS, POMFRET & More!
https://goo.gl/maps/2FMuVqHjJtJyUs4M6.description:
#GourmetOnTheRoad #RestaurantsInBangalore #Seafood 

Best Seafood Dishes In Bengaluru, Coastal Restaurant At The Gateway Hotel Bengaluru, Top Rated Seafood Dishes at Karavalli. Aquafest 
 
In nearly three decades of its existence, Karavalli at The Gateway Hotel Bengaluru has distinguished itself as an establishment that serves the country's finest South West Coastal cuisine. This has made the speciality fine dining restaurant an absolute must-visit in the city with patrons highly recommending a meal here.

What patrons also await is a much loved, annual seafood festival that the restaurant has been hosting since its existence. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits Karavalli to savour all the dishes on offer as part of this very special Aquafest menu. He meets with Executive Chef of The Gateway Hotel, Naren Thimmaiah to understand what makes this festival as popular. He then sits down to enjoy a whopping 14-dish meal.

BABY LOBSTER JIREM MIREM
chunky baby lobster meat marinated and cooked in a cumin (jirem) and fresh pepper (mirem) masala. you taste the byadgi chilli as opposed to the pepper in this warming masala. 
rs 1850. (25.80 usd)
9/10

GOAN OCTOPUS CHILLI FRY
i love the sweetness of the tomato in this preparation, the octopus however, has a bite that borders on being chewy. the flavours of this dish is one you would enjoy in a shack somewhere on the beaches of goa.
rs 1200. (16.75 usd)
7/10

KOONDAL PORICHATU
the batter-fried masala coated squid is cooked to springy perfection and the masala has penetrated all the way through. the fresh acidity of a squeeze of lime cradles that gentle spicing of the squid. this is the sort of dish that would make for a very happy bar snack.
rs 1200. (16.75 usd)
9/10

WHOLE SILVER POMFRET RECHEADO
this dish of whole fried silver pomfret is a taste of goa! liberally coated in the sweet, tart and hot goan recheado masala, both inside and out, you taste notes of the goan palm vinegar and the aggressive punch of chilli as you devour the dish. 
rs 1200. (16.75 usd)
8.5/10

TIGER PRAWN MALABAR STYLE
a signature dish at karavalli i keep returning for! these meaty tiger prawns are first fried to perfect scrumptiousness and then tossed in a vivacious masala of shallots, tomatoes and pepper.
rs 1800. (25.10 usd)
10/10
SEA CRAB GHEE ROAST
these meaty sea crabs, cooked in a ghee roast masala are divine! i love the mild sweetness of that crab meat (tastes just like the ocean!). the butteriness of that well rounded masala embraces the natural flavours of the crab.
rs 1450. (20.20 usd)
9/10
KOLI BARTHAD
a speciality here on the menu, this is a dish that hails from coorg. pieces of chicken are pan fried in a bunch of spices and kachampuli. the deeply roasted spices that have melded together as one.
rs 995. (13.88 usd)
8.5/10

MUTTON STEW
this is a textbook syrian christian stew with the mellow coconut base carrying just the subtlest hint of spicing. the meat is soft, you taste its nourishment in every strand. 
rs 1150. (16.05 usd)
10/10

PRAWN CALDEEN 
this goan-style curry is a pleasant melange of flavours. you taste the freshness of the coriander, the spice of the green chilli, raspy bite of the ginger and the creaminess of the coconut in the sauce. the prawns are juicy having absorbed all that goodness. 
rs 1450. (20.20 usd)
9/10
ALAPPUZHA MEEN CURRY
the deep, spice notes in this alleppey fish curry catches hold of your palate from the first bite. the seer, a meaty fish, is the right medium to convey and carry these bold flavours of coconut, ginger and raw mango. 
rs 1150. (16.05 usd)
9.5/10


DODOL
my favourite way to end a meal at karavalli is with the dodol, a goan dessert made with rice flour that has been well roasted with palm jaggery and loads of butter! it is rich and dark, each bite is lush, buttery yet dry. 
rs 475. (6.60 usd)
9/10
KASHI HALWA
the ghee glistens in this translucent kashi halwa. the ash gourd is flavoured with saffron, you also sense a hint of acidity in this dessert. 
rs 475. (6.60 usd)
7/10

ADDRESS- Ground Floor, The Gateway Hotel, Residency Rd, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560025

Some say it is a sin to visit Mysuru and skip out on eating the famous Mylari Dosa. But what is it about this dish that demands such reverence? Food Lovers pays a visit to Hotel Original Vinayaka Mylari to find out! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna gets a close look at the making of these soft, melt-in-the-mouth dosas and discovers that they are cooked on a massive iron tawa over a searing hot wood fire! GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Idli 
These woodfire steamed idlis are soft, fluffy, aromatic and slightly tart. saagu is robustly flavoured,  with a coriander accent. the vegetables still have their crunch intact.
9/10
Rs. 30 

Masala dosa  
This dosa is unbelievably soft and fragile. Holds together just enough to contain the vegetable saagu. After the initial crunch, the dosa dissolves in the mouth! The chutney adds a touch of freshness and spice. 
10/10
Rs. 40 

Kashi Halwa 
it's not overly sweet and is cooked down just right to a jammy consistency with an endearing stickiness
8/10
Rs. 25

https://goo.gl/maps/YevqsyLMv6SUhko79.description:
#Biryani #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad
This biryani establishment has been in existence for 40 odd years and the citizens of Mysuru swear by their biryani! 

Hotel RRR serves up classic Andhra-style fare with a menu that is limited to about 15 items only! They are most popularly known for their biryani and Andhra style starters that do not skimp on flavour. From robust whole spiced preparations, to an almost numbing but heavenly chilli kick to moist, aromatic biryani, this restaurant serves it all!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna starts his meal here with the Chilli Chicken and Mutton Pepper Fry. He also savours both the Chicken and Mutton Biryani here.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Chilli chicken
The chicken is tender and juicy, having soaked up that fiery chilli gravy. A squeeze of lemon helps tone down the spice slightly. 
8.5/10
Rs. 181.

Mutton pepper fry
This masala is well-roasted, with toasty notes of onion and pepper. The meat has its bite intact. there’s bits of organ meat, and the kidney especially has a nice, briny, meaty flavour that goes well with the masala. 
9/10 
Rs. 190.

Chicken biryani 
Fragrant biryani studded with flecks of tomato and chilli slices. every grain of the basmati rice has soaked in the spice and flavour of the chicken. the slightly tart gravy on the side helps transform the flavours of this mellow biryani.
8.5/10 
Rs. 176.

Mutton biryani
Has similar spicing to the chicken biryani but feels a little more moist thanks to the juices of  the mutton! every bite is flavourful. You can taste the flavour of the tender meat and the fat that has rendered into the rice. 
9.5/10
Rs. 195.

https://goo.gl/maps/k3BkbUi2VyKVCLQQA.description:
#BestRestaurantsInMysore #NonVegetarian #GourmetOnTheRoad
When in Mysore, head to Tegu Mess for local-style non-vegetarian fare! This hole-in-the-wall eatery began as an establishment to cater to the needs of students in the area nearly 50 years ago! 

Known especially for its wholesome, hearty, meat dishes, each item on offer has its own unique masala ground in-house by the family. Open through the day for breakfast, lunch and dinner, the fare here is sure to remind one of home.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits this humble eatery and meets second generation owner, Mr. Tegoji Rao and his son Shyam. He takes a look at the open kitchen, right next to the dining area and samples the Idlis with Gravy which is offered during breakfast hours. He also tries a nourishing Paya soup, a flavourful Pepper Chicken, a gently spiced Mutton Curry and much more as part of his lunch meal.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
IDLI WITH GRAVY
Steaming hot and fluffy idlis. can be savoured with a chicken gravy or a robust mutton gravy that packs heaps of flavour. 
8/10
Rs 30

PAYA
Has a nourishing, delicate flavour with a hint of pepper and fresh herby zing of coriander. the gelatinous trotter just melts in your mouth! 
8.5/10
Rs. 130

MUTTON CHOPS
A light, delicate stew cooked with mild spices allowing the meat flavour to be most dominant. The mutton is soft and peels effortlessly off the bone!
9/10
Rs. 130.

PEPPER CHICKEN
This is a delicious gravy. notes of pepper and fenugreek give it a deep flavour. the chicken is lushly flavoured with that masala, and is tender and juicy in every bite.
9/10 
Rs. 130.

GHEE RICE
A staple here made with long grain rice. it’s aromatic on its own but can also be paired with the delicious meaty sides!
7.5/10
Rs. 60.

CHILLI CHICKEN
Loaded with tomatoes and coriander this gravy has a gentle, roasted red chilli heat. it is very different from the green chilli heat that one is used to. the curry also has a certain smokiness to it. 
7/10
Rs. 130.

MUTTON LIVER
Made in green masala made that is loaded with fresh coriander. works well with the earthy, meaty, irony notes of the liver. the liver has a slight bite but yields quickly.  
9/10
Rs. 130.

MUTTON CURRY
A superb curry! The mellow spicing allows the meat to shine. all the flavour of the meat is in the gravy. the sort of dish your grandmother would cook for you.
9/10
Rs. 140.

ADDRESS- Tegu Mess, Adipampa Road, 6th Cross Rd, Vani Vilas Mohalla, Mysuru, Karnataka 570 002

#MysoreFoodTrail #MuttonPulav #GourmetOnTheRoad

The iconic Hanumanthu Hotel in Mysuru is famous for its mutton pulav that patrons relish from six am each morning! The restaurant, now looked after by the second and third generation, father-son duo of, Parmesh and Vishal  cooks all its food on firewood.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, we get an exclusive insider access to the kitchens of this legendary establishment and a closer look at how their iconic mutton pulav is made. Aside from the generous serving of Mutton Pulav, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna samples some Mutton Boti and a plate of Mutton Chops. 

This restaurant, part of Mysore’s rich culinary history is a must-visit!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
mutton pulav
the gentle masala spicing makes this a fragrant biryani. perfectly cooked pieces of mutton, with a slight bite. the organ meat and fat of the mutton intensifies the meaty flavours in this biryani. 
10/10
Rs. 200 for full plate. Rs 160 for half a plate.

mutton chops 
The gravy carries the flavour of the fat and meat. This style of preparation highlights the flavour of the meat through and through.
9/10
Rs.120 

mutton boti 
The liver, intestines and other offal meat are flavourful, perfectly tender, not leathery or rubbery! The gravy is thick, almost creamy and unctuous. The masala does not overpower the meat. 
8/10
Rs 120

#Breakfast #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

Visit Gayathri Tiffin Room or popularly called GTR in Mysore for a variety of dosas or tiffin time snacks like idli ! Breakfast or Tiffin Spots In Mysuru.

Gayathri Tiffin Room, widely known as GTR in the city of Mysuru, is a destination loved for its tiffin items, especially a variety of dosas! This over half a century old establishment serves up tongue-tickling dosa, the favourite being the Gayatri Masala Dosa here, not the typical Mysore Masala with red chutney, but a thick roast with a soft underbelly. 

Customers who patronise this restaurant have grown in number over the years and often frequent the place for breakfast or tea-time tiffin.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the eatery for tiffin in the evening and savours three dosas, the GTR Masala Dose of course, along with an unusual Green Dosa and an Open Butter Masala Dose. He also tastes one of the best Kesari Baths he has ever eaten!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
GTR masala dosa
a delightful crunchy dosa with a soft interior. has a nice buttery flavour. the potatoes are soft, creamy and have a generous amount of onion and fresh coriander for that sprightly freshness. the dosa itself is quite thick. served with a fresh spicy chutney. 
8.5/10
Rs. 45 

idli 
the idli has a grainy texture and a mildly vegetal flavour that suggests it may have been steamed in a leaf. the spicy chutney has the fresh flavour of coconut and body from the ground lentils. the sambar has a gentle sweetness typical of a south canara sambar. 
8.5/10
Rs. 30 

green dosa 
the heavy texture and thickness is reminiscent of an uthappam. nicely roasted at the bottom. served with a tasty vegetable saagu and a spicy chutney to lift all the flavours. there’s a mild lingering flavour of dill. 
7.5/10
Rs. 50 

open butter masala dosa
slightly thick, well-roasted dosa. the podi has a hint of sweetness and a bit of spice that is mellowed out by the butter. the palya is creamy and soft. the chutney helps lift the flavours of everything on the plate. 
9/10
Rs. 52
 
Uppitu
very gentle delicate flavour of tomato, fried lentils, and curry leaves. there’s the soft grainy texture of semolina with a hint of spice and onion for crunch. 
7.5/10

kesari bath
reminiscent of a badam halwa in terms of texture. silky, velvety with barely any graininess. restrained sweetness with the occasional gentle pop of raisins. the ghee makes it lush and seductively delicious. kesari bath at a whole new level! definitely one of the best I’ve tasted.
10/10
Chow chow bath price 
Rs. 50 

filter coffee 
nice and frothy on top. sort of coffee that makes you happy! 
8/10
Rs. 10

https://g.page/mangalorepearlblr?share.title: Affordable, Fresh & Delicious SEAFOOD At MANGALORE PEARL | PRAWN GHEE ROAST | KANE FRY | CRAB & More
https://g.page/mangalorepearlblr?share.description:
#Seafood #SeafoodRestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Best Seafood Restaurants In Bangalore. Mangalorean Food In Bangalore. Authentic Mangalorean Food In Bengaluru. 

A favourite for Mangalorean fare in Bengaluru, Mangalore Pearl is always bustling with patrons who visit this spot for their taste of coastal Karnataka, more specifically the Mangalorean Catholic-style of seafood food.

Set up by Steven Pinto who left behind a lucrative career in the IT sector to pursue his dream of sharing the food he grew up with, this 15-year old restaurant rose to fame thanks to its spiced filled seafood dishes and Mangalorean classics.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the Ulsoor outlet and meets with the brother duo that run the restaurant. He discusses the procurement of fresh seafood, the variety of curries on offer and also witnesses the making of two most popular fries, the Bangude and the Kane Fry.

He then sits down to a feast, tasting a bevy of coastal dishes, from a Pomfret Curry, Crab Masala, Khoobey Mootlien, Chicken Roce Curry and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

RAGI MANNI 
the manni has a lush, creamy texture that takes over your palate! you taste the caramel notes of the jaggery. this mangalorean dessert resembles the Italian panacotta minus the cream. definitely a delicious way to end your meal here.
rs 60 (0.90 usd)
8/10

KHUBEY MOOTLIEN
this dish deserves attention when being savoured, especially when picking on the tiny yet sweet and mildly briny clam flesh. the rice dumpling has a sticky, slightly slimy texture that goes very well with the thick, velvety coconut based gravy. the flavour of the clams in this dish is reminiscent of the ocean.
rs 170 (2.40 usd)
8.5/10

CRAB MASALA
tossed in a semi-dry onion and tomato masala that complements the mildly sweet, flesh of this dotted sea crab don’t forget to suck on the crab meat!
rs 310 (4.30 usd)
8.5/10

POMFRET STEW CURRY
the spicing in this masala is mellow and refreshing and just right, allowing the flavours of the pristine, fresh pomfret to shine. this stew curry goes deliciously well with mangalore rice.
rs 480 (6.70 usd)
9/10

KANE TAWA FRY
this fish is as fresh as it gets! so delicates that the meat just flakes apart effortlessly. the pullimunchi masala gives off a warming note o f the byadgi chilli and also a slight tartness from vinegar. the fish has absorbed the masala, yet retains its unique flavour. be mindful of the tiny pin bones though!
rs 280. (4 usd)
9/10

BANGUDE FRY
the butterflied mackerel allows for the masala to penetrate the deep flavours of this fish. notwithstanding this, the mackerel asserts its strong flavour from the word go despite being fried in a spicy masala.
rs 120 (1.70 usd)
9/10

CHICKEN ROCE CURRY
a popular choice of chicken curry at mangalore pearl made with coconut milk, fried onions and gentle spices. best savoured with the soft, spongy sannas that disintegrate as it absorbs this flavourful curry. the chicken though, tastes better when in the company of the creamy curry.
rs 220. (3 usd)
8.5/10

PRAWN GHEE ROAST
soaking in oodles of ghee this is one of the best prawn ghee roasts i’ve tasted! the prawns are plump and fresh, being coated in all that roasted masala that does not overpower its sweet flavour. the neer dosa serves as the perfect combination to this dish. the beautiful balance of spice, toasty flavour notes of coconut oil, rich ghee and divine prawns will keep you coming back for this dish!
rs 295 (4.10 usd)
10/10

FRIED POTRADAY
this dish starts off as a rice cake steamed with spinach, coriander, cumin seeds and red chill that is then sliced, battered in a light spice mix and deep fried. it makes for an appetising start to a meal.
rs 120. (1.70 usd)
7.5/10

SOLKADI
this drink made of coconut milk, kokum juice, ginger, garlic and chilli certainly awakens the senses and the palate. a refresher with a bite.
rs 50 (0.70 usd)
7.5/10

Mangalore Pearl, 2nd Floor, 5/1, Assaye Road, Skywalk Building, Assaye Rd, next to YMIA or BodyCraft, Ulsoor, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560042

https://goo.gl/maps/uomXAuRpAYo2oi447.title: Tasting SOUTH CANARA VEGETARIAN THALI At NEW MODERN HOTEL Bengaluru | Making Of BADAM HALWA |Chiroti
https://goo.gl/maps/uomXAuRpAYo2oi447.description:
#VegetarianMeals #RestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Most Popular Vegetarian Restaurants In Bengaluru. Masala Dosa At New Modern Hotel VV Puram Bangalore. South Indian Vegetarian Meals 

Located at VV Puram in South Bengaluru, New Modern Hotel is one of those rare, iconic establishments that has stood the test of time retaining it’s old world charm be it in its space and ambiance or in its recipes and way of cooking, simple honest homestyle fare.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna, visits the eatery to escape the hustle and bustle of the city meeting with 3 generations of the family that has been running the restaurant for over 60 years. He then gets special access into the kitchen and to a step-by-step making of the most popular sweetmeat on their menu, the Badam Halwa. Following this he tastes the Thatte Idli, a wholesome South Canara-style Thali and the ghee laden Badam Halwa and another favourite dessert in the region called Chiroti Milk.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

THATTE IDLI
generously smeared with ghee and served with a side of sambar and chutney, the thatte idli here is soft, almost breaking under its own weight. the chutney is rich in coconut with a mild chilli flavour while the sambar is thick, one in which you taste the hing and jaggery.
rs 30. (0.40 usd)
8/10

VEG MEALS
this vegetarian meal at NMH is a wholesome, south canara-style thali that is sure to remind you of home. this plate comes to you with a poori/ chapathi, vegetable of the day, sambar, saagu, tilisaaru, mosaru, rice, papad, pickle and majjige. a complete meal that’s honestly priced and delicious!
rs 80. (1.15 usd)
8.5/10

CHIROTI MILK
this popular dessert in the region is a puri made of semolina and maida that is crumbled and topped with sugar, badam powder and hot milk. the result is a sort of dessert that can bring a smile to anyone’s face. you taste the rich badam milk and occasionally crunchy bits of the ‘indian’ puff pastry.
rs 42. (0.60 usd)
8.5/10

BADAM HALWA
lusciously velvety, this dessert fill every pore of your palate with joy. served in small portions because it is super rich (1 part badam, 2 parts khova, 3 parts sugar and 6 parts ghee!) you can taste the granular texture of the almond and the fragrant flavour of cardamom.
rs 50. (0.70 usd)
9/10

FILTER COFFEE
Strong, piping hot filter coffee. just the sort you need after a meal here. order this with a side of the badam halwa. 
rs 23. (0.30 usd)
8/10

Street Food In Bengaluru. Best Street Food In Bangalore. VV Puram Food Street. Thindi Beedi. Vegetarian Street Food.

In part two, the final part of our street food trail at Thindi Beedi, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna tastes some of the more traditional and popular recommendations at VV Puram. He begins by tasting a super scrumptious Avarekalu Vada served piping hot, followed by a wholesome Avarebele Akki Rotti served with an saaru and crusty, Paddus. He then visits over 45 year old Guru Idlis to try their Mini Idlis. Rounding off the trail on a sweet note, he tastes two types of Holiges, a glass of nutritious Badam Milk and the super popular Gulcan Ice Cream. To help digest the 21-dishes he savours, he ends with a Fire Paan!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 

SRI VASAVI VAISISTA THINDI
AVAREKALU VADA 
this vada is every fried food lovers delight! made using a mixture of water hyacinth bean, dill, gram flour and aromats like onion, ginger, garlic, chilli and coriander this is as delicious and nutritious as a vada can get. in short, hot, crunchy and mouthwatering!
Rs 20 for two vadas. (0.30 USD)
9/10

SRI VASAVI MANE THINDI
AVEREBELE AKKI ROTTI 
this dish is a full meal. the akki roti has a crunchy crust and a soft inside. the gravy however, is quite tame. the avarekalu in the rotti makes for a tasty textural relief.
Rs 40. (0.56 USD)
7.5/10

PADDU
an enriched dosa batter that is cooked on a tava speckled with spherical cavities. it has a slight sour twang coupled with the crunch of the onions and freshness of the dill. delicious when eaten with coconut, chana dal and green chilli chutney.
Rs 20. (0.30 USD)
8/10

SRI GURU DEV IDLI MANE
MINI IDLIS
porous, soft fluffy idlis. the chutneys however are a little watery. the green chutney with gram flour is diluted in flavours. the idli though is the hero of this dish! 
Rs 10 for 3. (0.15 USD)
8/10

IDLI MANE
PLAIN OBBATTU 
a flaky, sweet paratha stuffed with lentil, cardamom and jaggery. the liberally slathered buttery ghee and that mild jaggery sweetness make this a delicious holige.
Rs 20 (0.30 USD)
8.5/10

KAI OBBATTU
much more weightier, this version of the obbattu has a rich, sticky, sweet coconut filling that lends a great bite to this obbattu.
Rs 20 (0.30 USD)
8.5/10


MUMBAI BADAM MILK AND LASSI CENTER
BADAM MILK
a rich, thick and nourishing badam milk flavoured with pista, kesar and cardamom. the super thick cream on top tastes almost like khova. one can run a mile after drinking this!
Rs 40. (0.40 USD)
9/10

SHIVANNA GULCAN ICE CREAM CENTER
GULKAND ICE CREAM
a crowd pleaser of a dessert here at vv puram. a mixture of gulkand or rose jam and butter topped butterscotch ice cream and mixture of fruits. the fruit helps cut through the sweetness of the ice cream and jam.
Rs 100. (1.40 USD)
8/10

PAAN POINT
FIRE PAAN
this unique version of the popular digestive, paan left me speechless, quite literally! you can absurdly taste the fire for a fraction of a second, followed by the cool ice and a mish mash of flavours from all the components inside!
Rs 50. (0.70 USA)
7/10

#ThindiBeedi #VegetarianFood #GourmetOnTheRoad
Street Food In Bengaluru. Best Street Food In Bangalore. VV Puram Food Street. Thindi Beedi. Vegetarian Street Food.
Bangaloreans love eating out and one spot every one frequents is VV Puram for its delicious vegetarian street food that can leave you spoilt for choice!

In part one of this two-part street food trail at Thindi Beedi, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna begins his trail at the legendary VB Bakery to taste three recommended treats, starting with the signature KBC or Khara Butter Bun Congress, a butter jam bun and the honey cake. Following this, he makes a trip to Shree Swamy Bajji Center to taste five scrumptious bajjis! Next on the list is a unique, smokey Tandoori Chai, special chaats from Chandra Chaat Center and highly recommended street snack, the Mosaru Kodubale or the Curd Kodubale.
Stay tuned to the final part of this trail coming up, this one covers some traditional snacks and tiffin and something sweet to seal the deal!
GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
VB BAKERY
KHARA BUTTER AND CONGRESS KADLEKAI BUN 
the first flavour to hit your palate is the savouriness of the curry leaves. you taste the buttery goodness, followed by the chilli and the crunch of the peanuts! this could very well be the Iyengar version of the peanut butter sandwich!
Rs 26. (0.40 USD)
9/10

BUN BUTTER JAM
This special bun is made with milk powder and has some raisins in it too. slathered with a generous lashing of butter and mixed fruit jam, this dish is a slice of nostalgia packed in a bun! 
Rs 27. (0.40 USD)
8/10

HONEYCAKE
made with pure coorg honey, this honeycake is dense and sticky. the top is light, airy and spongy but the bottom is where the sugary attack of the honey hits you. 
Rs 28. (0.40 USD)
8/10

SHREE SWAMY BAJJI CENTER
OOTY MENASINAKAI BAJJI
the ooty pepper in itself does not have too much heat but that raw chilli powder sprinkled on top certainly has a kick to it. this bajji will be a treat on a rainy day!
Rs 10 for a bajji. (0.15 USD)
8/10

CAPSICUM BAJJI
a whole capsicum fried to scrumptiousness. the capsicum still retains its fresh crunch despite being fried. ticks all the boxes if you are considering a nice evening snack.
Rs 20 for a bajji. (0.30 USD)
8/10

ALU BONDA
delightful fried snack that is super hot and made fresh. an absolute steal for a tasty snack! 
Rs 10 for 3 bondas. (0.15 USD)
8/10

BANANA BAJJI
love how the raw, starchy banana tones down the spice in that chutney and chilli powder sprinkled on top. the bajji is deliciously crisp when eaten seconds after it is fried!
Rs 20 for 2 bajjis. (0.30 USD)
8.5/10

PINEAPPLE BAJJI
a large slice of pineapple battered fried and then sliced and topped with a chutney and a garnish of onions and carrots! a definite first for me. Rs 20 for a bajji. (0.30 USD)
7/10

NAMMA KITCHEN
TANDOORI CHAI
certainly a tasty tea spiced with cinnamon and ginger. what makes this a tandoori chai is that smokey flavour present in every sip! perfect for a nippy evening. 
Rs 20. (0.30 USD)
8/10

CHANDRA CHAAT CENTER AND PAV BHAJI
MASALA PURI
this masala puri isn’t too spicy as one would expect. what you really taste is the fragrant spicing in the masala base and the slight sweet pop of the peas. 
Rs 30. (0.40 USD)
7/10

DAHI PURI
a loaded dahi puri. one bite and the puri just oozes all the delicious dahi with the stuffing of the boiled potatoes. you can also taste the spice of the garam masala. 
Rs 40. (0.56 USD)
9/10

GULAB JAMUN
this gulab jamun made using a special recipe is soft, creamy and perfectly sweet. the richness from the khova makes you want to keep going back for seconds.
Rs 20. (0.30 USD)
8/10

ARYA VYSYA
MOSARU KODUBALE
the mosaru kodubale was a scrumptious discovery. the crunchy exterior gives way to the gooey, porous inside. there’s a hint of chilli and cumin flavour. 
9/10

https://g.page/new-govindarao-hotel-main.description:
#NonVegetarian #RestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

New Govind Rao Military Hotel, Bangalore serves up popular local style non vegetarian fare, and has amassed a loyal following drawing from its 110 year-old legacy. Customers flood the establishment as early as 6am for their steaming hot pulav that is prepared in an interesting fashion. The rice here is cooked in a meaty stock and not with the meat itself! One can order a Mutton/Chicken Pulav or a khaali (plain) pulav. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna samples a meaty spread that includes the mutton pulav, Kheema Unde, a Mutton Liver Fry and a couple of robust chicken sides. He also gives viewers an inside look at the kitchens of New Govind Rao Military Hotel to discover the making of these popular dishes.
 
GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
KHEEMA UNDE
The unde or meat ball is made of finely minced mutton mixed with a bit of fat and sinew. you can taste the roasted gram flour/ binder in the mixture too. this takes away from the meat flavour but a tasty dish nonetheless. 
Rs 100.
7/10

 MUTTON LIVER FRY
The liver itself tastes fine, but with topped with that well roasted masala, this dish tastes robust and complete!
Rs 100
8/10

CHICKEN PEPPER DRY 
Chicken that is big in flavour! the pepper and roasted spice masala coating is fingerlicking good.
Rs 90.
9/10

CHILLI CHICKEN
This chicken is cooked tender with a nice chilli heat that’s not overpowering. a great combo with the mellow pulao.
Rs 90.
8/10

https://goo.gl/maps/iWJx7MCjucNvpCUX7.description:
#GoaFood #BestBreakfastInGoa #GourmetOnTheRoad

Goa Food Vlog. Best Dishes For Breakfast In Goa. Exploring Goan Food. Goan Cuisine. Top Goan Breakfast Dishes.Top 4 Goan Breakfast Dishes 

This episode of Gourmet On The Road is one that was shot by Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna during his holiday in Goa! In this laid-back video he shares with viewers his favourite dishes to eat for breakfast when in Goa.

He meets with Chef Anthony Vaz, who makes him a lavish Goan breakfast spread with dishes from the staple Ros Omelette, an egg dish served with the classic xacuti gravy, the must-have spicy Goan Sausage, fish croquettes and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
ROS OMELETTE
Signature Goan breakfast of a fluffy masala omelette served in a flavourful, spicy xacuti gravy. A wonderful way to enjoy your eggs. Best eaten with the dry yet pillowy poi.

MOOGACHI GAATI
this Goan style sprouted moong curry is a great vegetarian breakfast option. Perfect to be mopped with some poi. 

GOAN SAUSAGE CHILLI FRY
gently sauteed with onions a copious amount of capsicum and chilli, this Goan sausage preparation is delicious. You taste the mellow tartness of the vinegar in this dish.

FISH CROQUETTES
a happy surprise for breakfast, these croquettes are made with King fish that imparts a lovely flavour together with the chilli and coriander! Not greasy at all. 

ADDRESS - Holiday Inn Resort Goa, Mobor Beach, Cavelossim, Goa 403731

https://goo.gl/maps/suj7zrhPWC7YRzXG6.description:
#BakeriesOfHyderabad #HyderabadFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

Best Bakeries Of Hyderabad. Popular Bakery In Old City Hyderabad. Tasting Muharram Special Hyderabadi Dum Ke Roat.


A huge part of Hyderabad’s dining culture is of course, snacking on popular bakes at some of the city’s most popular bakeries. This tradition of savouring biscuits with Irani Chai or even presenting biscuits as gifts when visiting someone’s home was what brought us to Subhan Bakery located at Old City, Hyderabad to taste some of their very special offerings in this episode of Gourmet On The Road.


Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna, meets with Mr Syed Imran, the owner of Subhan Bakery to taste a Muharram delicacy, the Dum Ke Roat made especially during the holy month of Muharram. He also tastes the Hyderabadi essential, Osmania Biscuits, and a cardamom flavoured Chand or Moon Biscuit. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
SPECIAL DUM KA ROAT    
this rich cookie is a muharram specialty at subaan. it is soft and chewy on the inside. you taste the delicious richness of the ghee right away followed by the crunch of nuts. this is one decadent cookie!
rs 600/ kg.
10/10

OSMANIA BISCUITS    
a popular chai time snack, especially with the irani chai, osmania biscuits have a distinct salty-sweet flavour. the delicate crust melts on the palate giving way to buttery notes that linger.
rs 125/ half a kg box.
9/10    

MOON/ CHAND BISCUITS
this cookie is as crumbly as it gets. the cardamom aroma is so gentle yet so effusive on the palate.
rs 130/ 400gm pack.
8/10

Hotel Nayaab Old City Hyderabad, Restaurants Of Old City Hyderabad, Muslim-Style Hyderabadi Cuisine

In this episode of Gourmet On The road we set out in search for some delicious Hyderabadi fare. This culinary conquest led us to the Old City, an area that boasts of some of the most iconic, traditional Hyderabadi eateries. 

Hotel Nayaab, an establishment over three decades old, located right at the entrance of bustling Chatta Bazaar, Nayapul Road, Charminar, is a favourite amongst locals and tourists. Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna catches up with Omer Aziz of Hotel Nayaab to understand the typical Hyderabadi fare served here. He explains how the Nihari, a broth that makes for the Paya Soup is slowly simmered over hours and also steps into the kitchen to discover the making of two extremely popular dishes.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

NIHARI  
this is a comforting dish perfect to be enjoyed on a nippy evening! you taste the nourishing goodness of the juices from meat bones and the warm spices. the thin veil of fat on top rounds off all flavours. the deep savouriness of fried onion and the fresh hit of coriander adds another layer to the nihari.
rs 100.
9/10

MALAI PAYA/ PAYA MASALA 
definitely an indulgent take on the austere paya! the gravy is enriched with thick cream. the trotter itself is melt-in-the-mouth. Perhaps not for the purist.
rs 240.
8/10

BHEJA MASALA 
this bheja preparation is as light as air! it melts away leaving behind the delicious, custardy flavour of the brain. the masala is unctuous, smoky yet delicate in flavour.
rs 160.
9/10

BHEJA PEPPER FRY
the gentle heat of the pepper creeps up the back of your throat. the bheja is cooked beautifully and the masala, heavy on pepper and coriander balances against the intense creamy bite of the brain.. 
rs 160.
9/10

MUTTON TALAHUA
the masala is reminiscent of an achari masala with its tart edge. it’s perfect to mop up with a piece of roti. the boneless mutton chunks are well cooked and have absorbed that masala.
rs 220.
8/10

DAL FRY 
this nourishing lentil curry is thick and rich. it is more of a south indian style dal that is slightly tart, tempered with curry leaves and mustard. 
rs 150.
8/10

MUTTON BIRYANI
every grain of rice is separate and has absorbed the flavour of the meat. the meat itself has its flavour and a bit of its bite intact. one can also taste the robustness of the spices that have gone into this biryani. the salan has a mild pickling flavour note that helps break the rich spice notes of the biryani. 
rs 200.
8/10

QUBANI KA MEETHA 
this dessert is a tad syrupy. the malai with its richness helps balance out the overwhelming sweetness. the nuttiness from the apricot kernels pack twice the flavour of almonds and breaks the monotony of flavours. 
rs 100.
8/10

#BiryaniLovers #HyderabadFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Andhra,Telangana, Rayalseema food at Ulavacharu, Hyderabad. Pulao and biryanis in Hyderabad. Pulao restaurants in Hyderabad. Raju Gari Pulao, Rayala Vari Kodi Pulao.

This hugely popular establishment in Hyderabad is famous for its unique takes on traditional recipes. Their specialties are their biryanis or rather, their pulaos, of which they make 18 varieties! And each of them has its own unique flavour and character.
Food Lovers' Editor, Kripal Amanna joins Ravitej Ravuri of StreetByte on an epic pulao tasting session. He tastes a couple of unconventional starters namely, the Bamboo Chicken, an appetiser of chicken cooked in a bamboo stalk in a tandoor, and the Bangla Kodi. From their wide menu of pulaos, he tries the unique Raju Gari Pulao, a vegetarian Guthivankaya Pulao with eggplant, as well as the Rayala Vary Kodi Pulao with gongura leaves. He rounds off the meal with an indulgent rose milk and a sweet pudding called Junnu made from colostrum. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 

BAMBOO CHICKEN
this chicken is cooked in a fresh, tangy herb marinade and steamed in a bamboo shell. the masala has penetrated all the way into the chicken. the meat is juicy but a wee bit powdery in its texture. 
rs. 445
8/10

BANGLA KODI 
an interesting appetiser of chicken encased in a thick slice of potato that is marinated in a red spice paste and deep fried. almost resembles a mini taco! the slightly underdone potato adds a textural crunch.
rs. 399
8.5/10

RAJU GARI KODI PULAO 
this is unlike any biryani/ pulao i have ever tasted! the consistency is that of a khichdi or rice and gravy mixed together. the pulao is flavoured with pepper, whole spices and green chilli takes some getting used to, the chicken is here just to support the flavourful rice.
rs 335
9/10

GUTHIVANKAYA PULAO
a refreshing take on a vegetarian pulao or biryani. this masaledar pulao has an eggplant gravy ladled on the rice. the eggplant adds a meaty bite to the dish.
rs 285
8/10

RAYALA VARI KODI PULAO
cooked with a masala made of sorrel leaves/ sour spinach or gongura as it is popularly known in the region, this pulao is unique in its flavours. you taste the sour notes in the rich masala and chicken.
rs 345
8.5/10

RAJAHMUNDRY ROSE MILK
thick, rich milk infused with a sweet rose syrup. difficult to down an entire glass!
rs 125
8/10

JUNNU
this milk pudding is rich and creamy. visualise lightly sweetened khova in a custard form. 
rs 95
8/10

ADDRESS: Ulavacharu, 2-1/6 & 2-1/6/A, 1st Floor, 133, Fantasy Square Building, Old Mumbai Highway, Opposite Nissan Showroom, Biodiversity Circle, Gachibowli, Jayabheri Pine Valley, Gachibowli, Hyderabad, Telangana 500032

#MealsInBangalore #NaatiFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

For a taste of Karnataka or for local non-vegetarian meals visit Naati Sogadu, Sahakar Nagar, Bengaluru. Non-Vegetarian Restaurants In Bangalore.

Heroing flavours of the land, this desi hotel, Naati Sogaadu serves homestyle fare and is especially known for its non-vegetarian offerings. 

Run by a family of four, the food here is made using family recipes, a reason why this spot is gaining popularity despite being less than a year old. The women of the house supervise the making of the base masalas to every dish on the menu. These distinctive masalas result in dishes that remind one of home. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna makes a trip from the South to the North of the city to indulge in a hearty non-vegetarian lunch here. He also interacts with the family and watches the making of a popular dish on the menu!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
KHEEMA BALL PEPPER DRY
The mutton mince ball is soft and meaty, with intense flavours and a prominent pepper kick! the healthy smattering of curry leaves adds a deep herbaceous note. A tasty dish! 
Rs 200.
9/10

CHICKEN LOLLIPOP
Crunchy outside, juicy, soft chicken inside. a tasty appetizer but seems a little out of place in a naati or local meal.
Rs 200
7/10

CHILLI CHICKEN
This masala has heaps of sauteed onions, that lends a savoury flavour and a slight sweetness. the chilli heat is mellow, not the kind that will not leave you in agony!
Rs 180
7.5/10

NAATI CHICKEN LIVER FRY
This naati chicken liver is firm, not powdery. the masala of pepper, coriander and onions perfectly complements the meaty flavours of the liver.
Rs 180
8.5/10

BOTI GOJJU
The boti here is cooked in a gojju, a semi dry gravy. the flavour is intensely gamey, not for the faint hearted.
Rs 180
7/10

MUTTON CURRY 
A curry flavoured with roasted spices. the meat is pink and succulent with a slight bite and some fat. perfect when savoured with the dry, spongy dosa.
Rs 220 
9/10

NAATI KOLI BASAARU
The thin gravy or saaru has the goodness of the chicken, bones, marrow, gelatin and all in a grainy masala. The chicken, cooked twice, in the saaru and as a dry preparation is flavourful and almost melt-in-the-mouth in its texture.
Rs 220
10/10

MUTTON BIRYANI
Made with short grain rice, this pulao has the gentle aroma and zing of the herbs - coriander, ginger, garlic and chillies, and the mellow, lilting sweetness of fennel or star anise. 
7.5/10

#IndianSweets #HyderabadFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

G Pulla Reddy Pure Ghee Sweets Top Sweet Shop In Hyderabad and all of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Famous Indian Sweets.

If you’re looking for great sweets in Andhra Pradesh, look no further than G Pulla Reddy Sweet Shops. The company now has a presence all over Andhra Pradesh and Telengana. Established in 1948, the original owner set up shop in Kurnool. He insisted on making sweets of the highest quality which meant using pure ghee!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the original establishment set up by G Pulla Reddy himself. Here he samples a smattering of their most popular offerings including, a delicious Khova Puri, the ghee laden Mysore Pak and Badusha, as well as the paper thin, melt-in-your-mouth Sugar Pootharekulu. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
KHOVA PURI
this puri is flaky with layers of dough stuffed with creamy khova or cooked milk solids. the buttery goodness of the ghee makes you want to keep going back for a bite.
rs 580/ kilo
 8.5/10

BADUSHA
a crusty maida cookie. the texture is crumbly on the outside and gooey inside. you can taste the doughy goodness in every mouthful.
rs 540/ kilo
8/10

SPECIAL MYSORE PAK 
this version of the mysore pak is unbelievably soft! just melts on the palate leaving the delicious aftertaste of ghee!
rs 580/ kilo
8/10

MYSORE PAK
the older, original version. harder in texture and lighter in colour. It has a crumbly bite. this mysore pak lingers on the bite. 
rs 580/ kilo
7/10

SONA PATTI 
also called the gatti mithai, this one’s an interesting indian sweetmeat made of germinated wheat sprout flour, sugar and ghee. Has the texture of a hard candy and a mellow toffee-like sweetness. What you really taste is the ghee.
rs 620/ kilo
7.5/10

SUGAR POOTHAREKULU 
there’s nothing quite like this sweet creation that resembles and feels exactly like paper! These thin sheets are made of rice flour and ghee is stuffed with sugar. it disappears the minute it hits your palate!
Rs 30/ piece
 9/10

JAGGERY POOTHAREKULU
this version of the paper sweet is lined with bits of jaggery. its taste has much more of an earthy sweetness. a delightful find at g pullareddy!
Rs 32/ piece
10/10

KHOVA
can taste light, toasty caramelised notes in the milk of the khova or reduced milk solids. a simply yet soul satisfying dessert.
rs 540/ kilo
9/10

KAJU BARFI
Looks similar to a kaju katli but much thicker. You taste the richness of kaju and the subtle hint of cardamom and other sweet spices. garnished with the signature varak or silver leaf.
rs 1200/ kilo
8.5/10

#BestAndhraBiryani #Bangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Most Popular Biryani Restaurants In Namma Bengaluru. Best Restaurants For Spicy Andhra Biryani In Bangalore.

Widely famous for their Andhra & Hyderabadi style of biryanis, Nagarjuna and Meghana Foods are often pitted against each other. Without surprise both these eateries have a devoted following, most who swear-by the biryanis.

Nagarjuna, an establishment that was set up in the early 1980s serves two Andhra-style, dum biryanis, a Mutton and a Chicken while Meghana Foods, a relatively new eatery serves an array of biryani to choose from, the most popular of which is a spicy, Chicken Boneless Biryani.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna, tastes both biryanis at Nagarjuna and three of the crowd favourites at Meghana Foods, reviewing what makes each of these biryanis special.

In conclusion, he tells viewers what could be the biryani for them based on their preferences!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

CHICKEN BIRYANI
studded with a fair bit of whole spices - cloves, cardamom and cinnamon, which gives the biryani rice a fulsome flavour that serves well to embrace the chicken.
rs 265
8/10

MUTTON BIRYANI
the rice is similar in flavour to the chicken biryani, but the spices here seem more accentuated. The meat is soft, you can taste the gamey flavours of the fat. 
rs 305
8.5/10

CHICKEN BONELESS BIRYANI
made with long grain basmati rice, each grain is separate. topped with boneless chicken morsels coated in a thick, spirited masala, this is a biryani you can definitely share.
rs 248
8/10

CHICKEN DUM BIRYANI
served with a leg of chicken that is coated in a savoury, caramelised onion masala that threads through the long grained rice. the meat is cooked to the bone and is flavourful. a biryani that leaves you more than satisfied!
rs 242 
8.5/10

MUTTON BIRYANI
the spicing in meghana biryanis is apparent on the palate, but absent on the plate. one sees no hint of any of the spices that have gone into the dish, but you can taste its presence. the masala in the mutton biryani is mellower than in the chicken version, allowing the flavour of the meat to take precedence. 
rs 301
8/10

https://goo.gl/maps/vNcyHVMAAhZagSXd7.description:
#Kodava #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad
Authentic Kodava Food In Mysore Only At Simply Kodavas!

Finding authentic Kodava food outside Coorg can be quite the task but for the citizens of Mysuru however, Simply Kodavas is the place to go! This family-run restaurant features traditional Kodava art and serves up classic Kodava dishes.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna pays a visit to this restaurant and chats with the owner and his son about this distinct cuisine. He samples the quintessential Kodava Pandi Curry a flavourful Pork Chilli, both finished with kachampuli. He also tastes a robust chicken curry and couple of unconventional dishes namely, the Pork Biryani and Pork Kebab. He savours all of this with some traditional Kodava rice-based staples like Kadamputtu, Noolputtu and Paaputtu. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 
Pandi curry
you can taste roasted spices, fresh coriander, the tartness of the kachampuli and a peppery heat. A finger-lickingly good pork dish!
9/10
Rs. 160.

Pork chilli
the fat in this is spicy and flavourful! pork melts in your mouth and the delicious fat coats your palate. You have the deep brown roasted spices, a slight tartness from the kachampuli or coorgi vinegar, and the spice of the green chilli that lingers on the palate. a satisfying preparation!
9/10
Rs. 190.

Chicken curry
This curry definitely holds its own against the pork items in terms of flavour. Made with a spicy coconut base, the gravy has certainly been cooked for a while for the flavours to deepen!
9/10
Rs. 160.

Pork biryani
made more in the pulao style of cooking. The tiny morsels of tender pork have a certain smokiness that takes over your palate. Can also detect a hint of pickling spices. This is very different from a typical biryani. 
7/10
Rs. 180.

Pork kebab
The meat definitely has a bit of bite to it and the fat hasn't rendered down. Innovative dish but I’m not a fan. 
6/10
Rs. 200.

#LocalFlavours #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

Must-visit restaurant for the best, traditional vegetarian and non-vegetarian thalis in Mysore! Restaurants To Lunch At In Mysore.

Karnataka has some delicious fare on offer and these iconic dishes can be savoured as a whole in its Thalis. To experience these traditional flavours Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits La Uppu, the all-day dining restaurant at Grand Mercure Mysore for not just one, but two thalis for lunch.

He interacts with local chef, Vijay in the kitchen understanding what goes into some of the dishes on the thali. At the table he begins lunch with the Mysuru Thali, a vegetarian thali featuring dishes such as Bisi Bele Bath, Mysore Bonda, Chitranna, Thilisaaru, Mysore Pak and Godhi Halwa. He then tastes the non-vegetarian Karnataka Thali that comes with a Donne Biryani, Gorikayi Kara and Koli Saaru among other dishes.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
Mysore Thali
MYSORE BONDA 
mildly seasoned bonda. dunk it into the thili saaru to perk up its flavours

THILI SAARU
there’s a puckering tartness in this rasam, gentle spice and slight, soothing sweetness in its flavours. 

BALEKAI FRY
raw banana fry with a nice masala coating. no-fuss, tasty, fried goodness.

BELE TAWE
Thick, creamy lentil preparation with chilli, mustard and curry leaves. the kind that would perhaps be served in a typical Mysuru kitchen.

GORIKAYI PALYA
Lightly tempered, this cluster bean preparation is delicious, savour it with the akki rotti.

BADNEKAYI GOJJU
loaded with onions, the flavours of the masala make this brinjal dish shine!

CHITRANA
a satisfying rice preparation, flavoured with tumeric, onions and lemon juice.

BISI BELE BATH
a tasty bisi bele bath! the rice is fortified with lentils and a gentle warmth from the red chilli. the ghee on top makes this dish all the more irresistible!

KOSAMBARI
the kosambari is quite generous in its use of grated coconut. perfect palate refresher in between tasting all the dishes on the thali.

MOSARANNA
the cool yoghurt and mild tempering makes the mosaranna the best way to end an all vegetarian meal.

MYSORE PAK
all the ghee makes this mysore pak melt in the mouth!

GODHI PAYASAM
the best part to this wheat payasam is that it isn’t very sweet. it’s a light dish for a dessert, not leaving you feeling too heavy!

The Mysore Thali is priced at Rs 999 +taxes per person.
9/10

Karnataka Thali

GORIKAYI PALYA
this version of the palya or veggie preparation is spicy and uses a mint, green coriander and chilli paste!

KOLI SAARU
a rich, thick gravy that is flavoured with methi or fenugreek. there’s also some chilli and whole spices that have been ground and added to the masala.

MUTTON DONNE BIRYANI
the rice in this biryani is very mellow in its flavours. you taste the signature donne masala or spicing but this isn’t overly powerful. the meat is soft and tender, cooked really well!

The Karnataka Thali is priced at Rs 999 +taxes per person.
8.5/10

The Bengaluru Mysuru Highway is a busy one! And thanks to all that footfall, there’s definitely some great eateries that have popped up along the way. If you’re setting out early in the morning, these three eateries make for the ideal breakfast spots.

THATTE IDLI

9/10

7.5/10

UDDINA VADA
crispy and very lightly seasoned. 
7/10

Plate of Idli Vada 
Rs. 50

SPECIAL MADDUR VADA 
this feels and tastes like a scrumptious savoury cookie. there’s a prominent flavour of caramelized onions, curry leaves and cashew. rava in the batter gives it that grainy bite. it can feel dry after a few bites and needs that minty spicy chutney to moisten it.
Rs. 23
9/10

this is a frothy, well made coffee. it has the right amount of decoction and milk,  and is served at just the right temperature. 
Rs. 26
8.5/10

RICE KADUBU 
the batter is steamed in jackfruit leaves. this imparts a mild fragrance to the dish. the kadubu dissolves in your mouth. it pairs well with the tart sambar and is delicious with the coconut chutney too. 
Rs 50.
8.5/10

FILTER COFFEE
frothy and strong, just the way coffee should be. make sure to pull it to cool the coffee down.
Rs. 25.
8/10

#CoffeeShop #Dessert #GourmetOnTheRoad

Looking for a scenic cafe in Mysuru? The Malgudi Coffee Shop located at Green Hotel (formerly the Chittaranjan Princess Palace) is the place to visit!

This cafe set in a covered courtyard, surrounded by nature and natural interiors is the perfect spot to unwind with a cup of coffee and some scrumptious cakes or sandwiches.

The unique aspect of this culinary enterprise is that it seeks to employ and empower women who come from less privileged backgrounds, offering them a means of livelihood. All treats on the cafe’s menu is all made by the staff who run the show here! Their delicious coffee is also sourced from local farmers, supporting fair trade in the area. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna, visits the coffee shop, interacts with a member of the staff and orders himself some of the must-tries on the menu. He tastes a highly recommended Lemon Drizzle Cake, Walnut and Date Cake, and gooey Chocolate Cake together with a cup of strong Mysore Filter Coffee.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
LEMON DRIZZLE CAKE 
buttery with the citrusy edge of the lemon. slightly crumbly texture. an old fashioned cake that's comforting and delicately flavoured.
7.5/10

DATE AND WALNUT CAKE
this cake slices clean and holds together. one can taste the full-on nutty flavours of the walnut and the natural sugars of the date.
7.5/10

dense and gooey! the sort of chocolate cake that a good home chef would bake using locally available  ingredients. 
7.5/10

this coffee has a strong, heady aroma and some terrific body! you get the fullness of the coffee in the first sip. it works well when relished with sweet cakes. 
8/10

Indulge in their must-try Lemon Drizzle Cake, Date and Walnut Cake, and gooey Chocolate Cake. Each bite is a testament to the dedication and passion of the all-women staff. Malgudi Coffee Shop truly embodies a cafe with a cause, where every cup of coffee and slice of cake contributes to a greater good

https://g.page/the-paul-bangalore?share.title: Tasting 28 dishes! KERALA SADHYA at Vembanad, Bangalore|Vegetarian Malayalee Food|4 TYPES OF PAYASAM
https://g.page/the-paul-bangalore?share.description:
#Onam #VegetarianFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

The Kerala sadhya meal is an essential part of Malayalee cuisine. Traditionally served at festive occasions like Onam, Vishu, weddings and the likes, the sadhya on average consists of 25-28 dishes! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna, samples the sadhya at Vembanad, the Keralan Hotel at The Paul. He savours this lavish meal of 28 dishes, each with its own unique character and flavour. The meal celebrates the use of vegetables, fruits, various lentils, spices, yogurt and of course coconut in various forms! He wraps up the meal with 4 varieties of payasams, a traditional dessert from Kerala. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD
NEI PARIPPU
very mildly flavoured. this lentil dish is meant to be eaten at the beginning of a sadhya.

SAMBAR 
slightly tangy with the nourishing feel of the vegetables. quite a satisfying sambar! 

INJI PULI
the sour hit of the tamarind and warm heat of the ginger in this pickle awakens your palate!

ULLI THEEYAL
the delicious savouriness from the onions plays off the sweetness from the jaggery. 

KOOTU CURRY
there’s the earthy texture of the yam with bite of the bengal gram and the slight crunch of the coconut. these veggies are coated in an aromatic, roasted masala. 

BEANS MEZHUKUPURRATI
this poriyal of sorts has a nice crunch of the beans with the mild sweetness and gentle crunch from the onions. 

OLAN
the coconut milk in this soothes and refreshes your palate. best eaten in between tasting the spicy dishes.

VENDAKYA MORRU CURRY
this yoghurt based gravy has a pleasant crunch from the sauteed okra and the savoury pop of the mustard seeds.

AVIAL
a lovely union of veggies. this avial has the gentle flavour of yoghurt, sweetness of the grated coconut and the crunch of the vegetables. you can taste that drizzle of coconut oil used to finish the dish.

CABBAGE THORAN
this cabbage thoran has a prominent sweetness from the copious amounts of fresh grated coconut. It’s mild tempering allows the cabbage to shine!

KAALAN 
the unctuous ripeness of the banana imparts a surprising sweetness to this dish. delicious!

RASAM
you can taste the tartness of the tamarind and tomato and the gentle heat of the peppercorn at the back of your throat in this rasam.

PACCHA MORRU
this buttermilk is thick unlike regular buttermilk. savour this combination of the buttermilk with the rice with kondattam or yoghurt-soaked, sundried and fried chilli!

PARIPPU PAYASAM 
the sweetness of this lentil payasam pairs well with the fruity flavours of the banana. the pappadam adds weight and body to your bite.

SEMIYA PAYASAM
this semiya payasam has the toasty notes of the fried cashews and the sweet jammy pop of the sauteed raisins.

PAAL ADA
a traditional malayalee dessert made with rice flakes, has a delicious, mild caramel flavour. 

JACKFRUIT PAYASAM
this payasam has the intense, pungent sweet flavour of ripe jackfruit. you also taste the lingering note of ground cumin with each bite.

SADHYA
This vegetarian meal gives one a delicious taste of Kerala, each dish unique and pleasing to the palate. a highly-recommended experience to savour!
10/10
This traditional sadhya is priced at Rs 1350 +taxes per person.

ADDRESS -  Vembanad, The Paul, 139/28, Domlur Layout Opp. Embassy Golf Links, Off, Intermediate Ring Rd, Krishna Reddy Layout, Amarjyoti Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560071

https://goo.gl/maps/hmbwNq4oydb7Nf9W8.title: PAN ASIAN Lunch At BIG WONG XL | Chinese Dim Sum | Japanese Sushi | Cambodian Lamb Curry | Stir Fry
https://goo.gl/maps/hmbwNq4oydb7Nf9W8.description:
#AsianCuisine #LunchInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad
Big Wong XL, a Pan Asian restaurant serving up interesting dimsum and sushi, is just a stone’s throw away from the Food Lovers office, in 5th Block Koramangala. 

Exuding a laid back vibe, with contemporary decor together with oriental accents, this eatery features an extensive Asian menu, from Indonesian curries to Japanese Ramen Bowls and everything in between!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Ammana decides to check out Big Wong XL for some steamed dim sums, a variety of sushi as well as a couple of appetisers and a recommended Cambodian Style Lamb Curry. 

He books his table using Eatigo, a restaurant booking app now available in Bengaluru, through which he avails of 50% discount on the bill.  To avail of attractive discounts at interesting restaurants, download the Eatigo app at https://bit.ly/343K1XZ

Note: Although we have been invited by Eatigo to use the app in this episode, this is an independent review of the restaurant and its food as in all Gourmet On The Road episodes.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
RAINBOW SUSHI 
This one’s a colourful seafood sushi but the pieces topped with tuna is where the flavour is!
7/10
Rs. 650 for 8 pieces.

CALIFORNIA ROLL
the california roll is stuffed with crab stick, avocado, and mayo. the salty pop of the tobiko (flying fish roe) livens up its flavours. eat it with a touch of wasabi!
8/10
Rs. 650 for 8 pieces.

VEG TEMPURA 
well wrapped sushi with the right balance of rice and filling. there’s a pleasing crunch to the fried vegetable tempura. 
7/10
Rs. 550 for 8 pieces.

ASPARAGUS TEMPURA
with this sushi, you first experience the crunch of the asparagus followed by the creaminess of the mayo. the perfectly seasoned, vinegar rice is the ideal vehicle to carry these flavours and textures. 
8/10
Rs. 550 for 8 pieces.

CRYSTAL VEG DIMSUM
a delightful ‘money bag’ dumpling stuffed with peppers and mushrooms. the skin is translucent and skillfully made. definitely a dimsum to try if you like robust, spicy flavours.
7.5/10
Rs 220 for 4 pieces.

VEG THAI HERBS DIMSUM
plump, flavourful dumpling. the filling is soft barring the bite of the water chestnuts. The accompanying chilli peanut sauce provides a spicy kick!
8/10
Rs. 220 for 4 pieces.

CHICKEN CHILLI FLAKE DIMSUM
served with a cheung fun sauce, this dumpling has a filling that does not hold back in its flavours but the wrapper however, feels a little doughy on the palate.
6/10
Rs 290 for 4 pieces.

PAK CHOY WRAPPED CHICKEN DUMPLING
well marinated chicken with great umami flavours and the herbaceous crunch of the wrapper/ pak choy. a delicious dumpling!
8.5/10
Rs 290 for 4 pieces.

THAI STYLE COCONUT PRAWN
there’s an appetising sweetness from the coconut milk, and a mellow warmth from the spicy chilli glaze. the curry leaves give it an unexpected herbaceous lift. The prawns are cooked perfectly and embrace the unctuous thickness of the sauce!
9/10
380 small/ 650 sharing.

CAMBODIAN STYLE LAMB CURRY WITH JASMINE STICKY RICE 
this delicious curry is fortified with coconut and shrimp paste. the lamb is tender, flavoured with the aromats in the curry.
9/10
Rs 500.

CRISPY SPINACH AND CORN 
the veggies are dusted in cornstarch and flash fried to help retain their crunch. the spinach is left whole as opposed to being shredded, this allows you to still taste its flavour. a simple yet tasty appetiser.
7/10
Rs 220.

https://goo.gl/maps/kfv5seio9Tp5YvJb8.title: MYSORE PAK TRAIL IN MYSURU | Guru Sweet Mart | Shree Mahalakshmi Sweets | 5 Varieties Of Mysore Pak
https://goo.gl/maps/kfv5seio9Tp5YvJb8.description:
#IndianSweets #Desserts #GourmetOnTheRoad
No visit to Mysore is complete without tasting the city’s most popular sweetmeat, the Mysore Pak! This concoction, born in the royal palaces of Mysore, takes only 4 ingredients to make, namely, gram flour, sugar, turmeric, and plenty of ghee! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna samples various versions of the Mysore Pak across the city. The first Mysore Pak he samples is at Guru Sweet Mart. This sweet shop is run by the fifth generation of the family descended from Kakkasura Madappa, the chef at the royal palace, widely regarded as the inventor of the Mysore Pak. He then moves on to Shree Mahalakshmi Sweets, a sweet shop that specializes in varieties of Mysore Pak. Here he samples the Milk Mysore Pak, the Badam (Almond) Mysore Pak and the Kaju (Cashew) Mysore Pak. 

GURU SWEETS 
Vanaspati Mysore pak
made with vanaspati or vegetable oil. It has a hard, crumbly texture.
7/10
Rs 280/ kg

Special Mysore pak
made with pure ghee. Has a luscious, dissolve-in-the-mouth texture. You can feel the rich ghee coat your palate!
10/10
Rs. 400/ kg

SHREE MAHALAKSHMI SWEETS

Ghee mysore pak
It’s soft to the touch. Beautiful, luscious melt in the mouth quality! 
9/10
Rs. 483/ kg 

Milk mysore pak
Texture-wise, very similar to the ghee mysore pak. You have the flavour of khova or milk solids running through every bite.
8/10
Rs. 504/Kilo 

Badam mysore pak
You definitely taste the almond. Almost feels like a drier badam halwa. You have the grainy bite from the almonds, but this still is a buttery, luscious mysore pak!
10/10
Rs. 670/Kilo 

Kaju mysore pak
you can taste the slight nuttiness of cashew and slight graininess in texture. This mysore pak has more of a bite. 
9/10
Rs. 650/Kilo 

Vanaspati mysore pak
This mysore pak is hard and crumbly. it doesn't have the richness of the ghee but it certainly has the flavour of the besan and sugar. 
7/10
Rs. 294/Kilo 

GURU SWEETS ADDRESS - Shop No: 1, Devaraja Market Building, Near K.R. Circle, Sayyaji Rao Rd, Devaraja Mohalla, Mysuru, Karnataka 570001; Location Tag: https://goo.gl/maps/kfv5seio9Tp5YvJb8

SHREE MAHALAKSHMI SWEETS ADDRESS - No 997, Near Chamundipurum Circle, 3rd Main Road, Vidyaranyapuram, Vijayanagar 2nd Stage, Vidyaranyapura, Mysuru, Karnataka 570008; Location Tag: https://goo.gl/maps/izWCtN6BYzvEtLSj8

https://maps.app.goo.gl/hEELRpRd79nxk9Ym.title: Traditional GOWDA & MANGALOREAN Cuisine At Bengaluru Oota Company |Kane Fry |Kaima Unde |Badam Halwa
https://maps.app.goo.gl/hEELRpRd79nxk9Ym.description:
#HomeDining #Communal #GourmetOnTheRoad
Bengaluru Oota Company is a unique dining experience run by two lady entrepreneurs Divya Prabhakar and Vishal Shetty. Divya is a Gowda, and Vishal is from the Bunt community of Mangalore. They bring together their respective cuisines in a marriage of flavours, represented in their customizable tasting menus. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, we learn how the two women started this enterprise. Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna sits down to sample their menu for the day which includes a Kane Rava Fry, Pelata Gatti (steamed jackfruit dumplings) with Kori Ajadina, a Bannur Mamsa Pulav. He rounds off the meal in true South Indian fashion with curd rice, rasam and a badam halwa. 

KOSAMBARI 
This cucumber based traditional salad has just the right amount of tempering to give it that savoury lift. A great start to a meal here. 
7/10

GARLIC SANDIGE 
scrumptious crunch with a strong garlick-y flavour.
7/10

GOLI BAJJI 
hot and freshly made! crisp, crunchy outside with a yielding inside. Makes for a spirited bite with the coconut chutney, owing to the green chilli heat in the chutney!
7.5/10

KANE RAVA FRY 
this rava-fried kane is just the right size. Ticks the right boxes - the flaky freshness of the fish, well- balanced masala and the perfect semolina crumb. 
9/10

KAIMA UNDE 
soft to the touch and literally melts in your mouth! you don't have to chew on it at all. A tava fried crust yields to the moist coriander flavoured mutton mince on the palate. 
9/10

PELATA GATTI 
similar in texture to an idli but with the mellow sweetness that emanates from flecks of ripe jackfruit. A happy discovery! 
9/10

KORI AJADINA 
the chicken has absorbed the savoury, creamy, coconut-ty flavours of this curry. when eaten with the pelata gatti, it is a divine combination. 
9/10

BANNUR MAMSA PULAV
the rice has all of the flavours of the meat, spices, and herbs, with a subtle citrusy twang. With a bite to it, the meat makes for a happy union with the flavourful rice, the pulav takes a zesty turn when eaten with the piquant pudina chutney. 
8/10

MUNCHI KORI (CHILLI CHICKEN)
served as a side to the pulav here. the chicken is braised in a lovely, savoury, onion masala with mild heat. 
8/10

AVAREKAI PALYA
the vegetable still has its crunch and fibre. the bite of the coconut gives it that added texture.
7/10

RASAM 
tangy rasam that’s low on spice. 
7/10

MOSARANNA (CURD RICE)
cool and refreshing with the sweet pop of the pomegranate seeds. lightly tempered with that roasted curry leaf flavor. the pineapple in the mensakai made for sweet and sour  combination with the curd rice.
8/10

ANANNAS (PINEAPPLE) MENSAKAI
more sour than spicy, with a mellow heat that stays on the palate. 
8/10

BADAM HALWA
made of almonds, cashew nuts, ghee, and khova this is a decadent, thick halwa.

https://goo.gl/maps/cdMGLk1GaGQbT1xc6.title: Tasting Muslim-Style MUTTON DUM BIRYANI At Chichaba’s Taj | Bheja Fry | Barrah Chops | Seekh Kebab
https://goo.gl/maps/cdMGLk1GaGQbT1xc6.description:
An offshoot of the restaurant that claims to be the only muslim restaurant in Bangalore to have been around since 1935, Chichaba’s Taj is known for serving up traditional muslim-style dum biriyani, kebabs and curries

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Ammana visits the crowd favourite at Frazer Town, Bengaluru, to quell his craving for a good biryani, and along the way also tastes some of the highly recommended kebabs, paya and a peppery bheja fry!

MUTTON SEEKH KEBAB
The right proportion of meat to fat makes this succulent kebab. The outer crust envelopes a flavourful mutton mince. This kebab is gentle on the palate despite its fiery red colour. Best eaten hot off the sigri! 
Rs.160.
7/10

MUTTON BHEJA FRY
Its unctuous bite coats the palate with its creamy texture. It's delicious, loaded with pepper, roasted onions, curry leaves and chillies. A must-try here!
Rs. 190
9/10

MUTTON PAYA
The paya or trotter is gelatinous and has rendered well into the aromatic broth. There’s a mild meatiness to this nourishing soup. 
Rs. 200
8/10

BARRAH CHOPS 
The meat peels away from the bone but still retains its bite. This dish is cooked to textbook perfection with the right amount of spicing that allows the meat to shine through. 
Rs. 400.
9/10

MUTTON DUM BIRYANI
This biriyani is aromatic with smoky undertones and gently spiced with whole spices. The mutton pieces are moist and succulent with pockets of fat! The baigan ka salan accompaniment with its tartness, adds a whole new dimension, making the biryani livelier!
Rs. 260.
8.5/10

CHICKEN DUM BIRYANI
Each grain of rice is separate. It has a nice gentle aroma, a hint of tartness from the tomatoes and fresh flavour of herbs. A mild biriyani that will not necessarily jolt your taste buds.
Rs. 200
7/10

CHICHABAS FRIED CHICKEN
Well marinated, succulent fried chicken that’s not dry. It has a pleasant spice marinade and gentle flavouring.
Rs. 200
7.5/10

Address - Chichabas Taj; 50, Madhavaraya Mudaliar Road, Frazer Town, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560005; 
Location- https://goo.gl/maps/cdMGLk1GaGQbT1xc6

https://goo.gl/maps/Q7XjR5wdmMGNsUas8.title: Mumbai Vada Pav & Maharashtrian Street Food In Namma Bengaluru |Rajvardhan Foods |Dabeli |Misal Pav
https://goo.gl/maps/Q7XjR5wdmMGNsUas8.description:
#StreetFood #MumbaiStreetFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

Nothing quite like Maharashtrian street fare and Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna who spent his early in the city of Mumbai absolutely agrees!

In this Gourmet On The Road episode, he visits Rajvardhan Foods, to take a trip back to Mumbai, tasting an authentic Vada Pav, spicy Misal Pav, Poori Bhaji with some lusciously thick shrikhand and some upvaas chi faraal or fasting foods such as Thalipeeth and Sabudana Vada. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

VADA PAV
The pav is perfect in its taste and texture. the plump batata vada, with a thin casing is stuffed with an appetising potato mix. The garlic chutney and customary fried chilli makes every bite an explosion of flavours! 
Rs 35
8.5/10

KUTCHI DABELI 
a riot of flavours and textures. sweet, spicy, tangy potato patty, topped with the crunch of peanuts and fruity pop of the pomegranate seeds. the pav is toasted to perfect scrumptiousness. the fried sev adds another layer of texture. 
Rs 50
7/10

KANDA POHA
maharashtrian breakfast special made with beaten rice. tempered with onions, mustard, chilli, peanuts and topped with generous amounts of sev. a very simple flavoured dish that needs that twist of lemon to amp up flavours. the thick, slightly sweet yoghurt with the poha is delicious! 
Rs 65
7/10

SHRIKHAND POORI BHAJI 
fluffy pooris but the bhaji is a little low on flavour. best way to savour this is with the lusciously thick, sweet, cardamom flavoured shrikhand.
Rs 115
7/10

KOLHAPURI MISAL PAV
spicy rassa cooked with moth beans and topped with crunchy sev and mixture. a hearty dish to be enjoyed with the pav. the lemon helps tone down the heat. 
Rs 90
7.5/10

SABUDANA KHICHDI
a wholesome dish prepared with minimal fuss. Simply seasoned with flecks of chilli and ajwain seeds.
Rs 90
8/10

SABUDANA VADA
crunchy outside and soft inside. generous flecks of green chilli. minimally seasoned. enjoy this with mint chutney.
Rs 55
8.5/10

ONION THALIPEETH
the almost burnt onions gives this filling pancakes a strong onion-y flavour and bite. 
Rs 90
7/10

UPVAAS THAALIPEETH
made with tapioca flour and rajgira this is a high on nutrition pancake. it’s slightly dry. the butter and the sweet and bitter lemon pickle helps add flavour to this fasting snack.
Rs 95
6.5/10

CHAAS/ MASALA BUTTERMILK
just the drink you need to help you settle your stomach after eating all the spicy street fare served here!
Rs 25
6/10

ADDRESS - 1291, 25th Main Rd, Putlanpalya, Jayanagara 9th Block, Jayanagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560069

LOCATION TAG - https://goo.gl/maps/Q7XjR5wdmMGNsUas8

https://maps.app.goo.gl/hdJWku2LcF4TGLcB.title: Epic Bangalore DOSA TRAIL Part 2 |CTR |Hanchina Mane|Airlines|Umesh Dosa|Chikkanna Tiffin|99 Variety
https://maps.app.goo.gl/hdJWku2LcF4TGLcB.description:
#Dosas #BangaloreFoodTour #GourmetOnTheRoad 

In this exciting Gourmet On The Road episode, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna takes off on a trip across Namma Bengaluru exploring the city’s most popular dosa destinations!

The second and final part to this dosa trail begins at Shri Sagar - CTR, an establishment with legions of loyal fans. Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna tastes a Benne Masala Dose and the Set Dosa here. He then relishes a unique dill flavoured dosa at a streetside dosa haunt in the bylanes of Basavanagudi. He then tastes a smashing Podi Dosa at Umesh Dosa Point, and a Bath Masala and Khaali Dosa at Chikkanna Tiffin Room located in the narrow bylanes of Cubbonpet.

He finally rounds off this dosa trail in the evening with the famous Pav Bhaji Dosa at Shree Balaji 99 Variety Dosa. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

CENTRAL TIFFIN ROOM 
BENNE MASALA DOSA 
Love the texture of this thick yet crisp dosa roasted with oodles of ghee. it takes skill to roast a dosa like this. the chutney is fresh while the ghatti chutney is nice and spicy.
Rs 52.
10/10

SET DOSA
Fluffy yet crisp set dosa. the saagu here is unlike any other loaded with a bunch of seasonal veggies. An absolute find here!
Rs 47.
9/10

GOLI BAJJI 
The ultimate tea or coffee time snack! crisp and stretchy outside, soft and porous inside.
Rs 32.
9/10
7th Cross Rd, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003
080 2331 7531
https://maps.app.goo.gl/hdJWku2LcF4TGLcBA

HANCHINA MANE 
SABAKKI DOSA 
An aromatic dosa, made with a batter infused with dill. very different in flavour. The freshness of the dill takes over the palate.
Rs 20.
6/10
Netkalappa Circle
Subram Chetty Rd, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004
https://maps.app.goo.gl/2AR4518mGf72T7RDA

AIRLINES HOTEL 
BUTTER MASALA DOSA 
Crisp buttery dosa, stuffed with loads of potato. dining here is more about the experience than it is about the actual dosa.
Rs 120.
7/10
No 4, State Bank of India Rd, Shanthala Nagar, Ashok Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560001
080 2227 3783
https://maps.app.goo.gl/qS8RE3mKTaqKQFwM7

UMESH DOSA POINT
PODI PLAIN DOSA 
Smeared with a homemade podi, made of gram flour, spices, and jaggery. love this dosa it’s got the sweet, spice and the crunch! Perfect balance of flavours. Certainly a discovery for me.
Rs 65.
9/10
21, 1st Main Rd, 4th Block, Kumara Park West, Seshadripuram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560020
098454 15768
https://maps.google.com/?cid=12853698143630628717

CHIKKANNA TIFFIN ROOM
KHAALI DOSA
Order this with the extra ghee. the dosa just by itself is absolutely dry. You need to mix the chutney, aloo gadde palya and the tuppa to enjoy this dosa melt in your mouth.
Rs 54.
8/10

BATH MASALA DOSA
Plain dosa topped with ghee, pulao, chutney, palya and ghee. a loaded dosa! Personally a little too much for me. But if you're looking for something filling this is your dosa. 
Rs 70.
7/10
#32, 30th Cross Rd, Kanchan Nagar, Cubbonpete, Nagarathpete, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560002
098459 17991
https://maps.app.goo.gl/NoVFKn28eRSzFfM38

SHREE BALAJI 99 VARIETY DOSA
PAV BHAJI DOSA
This dosa is where the story of the 99 variety dosa began. bite into this and you could well be biting into a pav bhaji. A chatpata, butter laden, spicy dosa for the adventurous. 
Rs 60.
7/10

DIL KHUSH DOSA
Loaded with cabbage, spring onions, paneer and schezwan chutney. you taste all the salty cheese and then you taste the schezwan chutney. a whole new concept on dosa, a tasty one but not for the purist. 
Rs 120.
5/10
Police Station Road, Koramangala 5th Block, Near Ganesh Temple and Opposite Bajaj Storeroom, Bangalore 560 034; tel 81470 48251
