https://maps.app.goo.gl/JfzrF2A9ypAUQCzr.title: Exploring Traditions & Tasting the VEGETARIAN LUNCH THALI At Mavalli Tiffin Rooms | MTR | Bangalore
https://maps.app.goo.gl/JfzrF2A9ypAUQCzr.description:
#VegetarianRestaurants #IconicEateriesInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

One of Bengaluru’s most iconic restaurants for traditional South Indian breakfast and meals, Mavalli Tiffin Rooms or MTR is a culinary institution.
 
Nearly 100 years old, located in a quaint double-storey building with halls packed full of patrons, both old and new, Mavalli Tiffin Rooms, Lalbagh is part of the history of Bengaluru.
 
The eatery today is known for its rich culinary traditions, that has struck a chord with people not just in the country, but across the world! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor visits the iconic eatery to lunch with Hema Malini Maiya, Managing Partner. He explores the nuances of what makes MTR so special over a traditional lunch.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Lunch Thali - Rs 270

Black grape juice
No lunch at mtr has begun without this refreshing drink, that is served no matter grape season or not!
7/10

Kosambari
Fresh, crunchy salad. Typically to be eaten at the start of the meal.
7/10

Raw banana palya/ balekai palya
tasty fibre. coconut adds a nice texture. made with a south canara masala, that is very gentle. Looks spicy but isn’t!
8/10

Poori Sagu
Fluffy pooris best eaten with the sweet and tangy saagu and thick chutney. the savoury and slight sweetness from the potatoes are balanced with the spice hit from the chutney.  
8/10

Sabbakki kadle bele payasam
Perfectly sweet dessert. has some chana dal that adds texture and breaks the gluten and the sweetness. helps you refresh your palate in between all the food.
8/10

Mini masala dosa
dosa has a slight tartness from the batter. can taste the masala in every bite. the chutney adds flavour and spice. the slightly grainy bite of fried gram in the chutney makes it the perfect accompaniment to the dosa.
10/10

Rave vade
a delicious, crunchy fritter. this accompaniment on the thali is different everyday.
6/10

Bisibelebath
a flavourful bisibelebath. the bite of the vegetables is what makes this dish. it is robustly spiced. Best eaten with the raita.
10/10

Kara pongal with hunase hannu gojju
A Thursday special. This flavourful dish sings on your palate. the tangy tamarind chutney helps cut through the spice from the ginger and peppercorns in the dish. 
9/10

White rice and bendekai huli with ghee
typical south Canara Style huli/ sambar. super tasty! Slightly tart in flavour, you can taste the spices and the crunch of the vegetable. Best eaten with ghee to round off all its flavours.
9/10

Rice and rasam 
piping hot rasam/ saaru! can taste the spices that are well balanced. sourness from tomato and tamarind is balanced with a slight sweetness from the jaggery. The spice comes from the red byadgi chilli. great when eaten with the appala and uppinakayi or pickle.
9/10

Curd rice 
lightly seasoned. curd rice helps settle your tummy. makes for a lovely end to the rice courses. 
7/10 

Ice cream and fruit mixture 
this ice cream, made in house and with very little fat - almost like a rich sorbet -  is only available at mtr and is called the american ice cream. served with a ‘french fruit mixture’ as they call it. 
8/10

Gulab jamoon
Flat, oblong jamoon. Light, not cloyingly sweet, a bit of camphor traditionally added for flavour.
8/10

Beeda or pan 
Stuffed with fennel, gulkand and betel nut to refresh your mouth. a perfect digestive. rounds up a perfectly satisfying and happy lunch here. 
7/10

ADDRESS - MTR, #14, Lal Bagh Main Road, Doddamavalli, Sudhama Nagar, Bengaluru 560 027; tel +91 80 2222 0022

#Seafood #FishMarket #Fishing

Bunder or the Old Port, is a landmark in the city of Mangalore with dozens of trawl boats bringing in marine wealth of all kinds. Heaps of freshly caught prawns, clams, crabs, squid, an abode of different varieties of fish is up for auction day in and day out. 

Locals including vendors of hotels and restaurants flock to this forever bustling market to purchase seafood at affordable prices. In this episode, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna explores all kinds of seafood at the Bunder while he discovers the means of livelihood of fishermen and vendors who strive hard so that we can enjoy the bounty of the sea! 

Fresh stocks of tiger and zebra prawns, seer fish, octopus, blue sea crab, prawns, lizard fish, pomfret, and other fishes locally called batfish, madmal, and a type of green lipped mussel were on sale on this day.

A name that is highly familiar among the locals of Mangalore, Giri Manja’s is a landmark restaurant known for its mouthwatering and fingerlicking seafood specialities! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits this forever bustling eatery on recommendation, to try some of its best known dishes, the anjal tawa fry, prawn golden fry, sardine hing fry, squid fry and more!

A wholesome meal that is also unlimited, slightly stingy on the fish, but at just Rs. 50 you can’t complain! 7/10

Flakey, meaty piece of fish best eaten with a squeeze of lemon on the top to help sober down the chilli! Rs 220. 9/10

https://maps.app.goo.gl/MEjL2L9G3xp6WNHA.title: NORTH KARNATAKA DELICACIES In Mangalore |HALLI MANE ROTTIES| Must Visit FOOD Truck | Food Lovers
https://maps.app.goo.gl/MEjL2L9G3xp6WNHA.description:
#MangaloreFoodTour #StreetFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

This mobile eatery that exclusively serves North Karnataka delicacies is a raging hit in the city of Mangalore!

Run by Shilpa, a homemaker turned entrepreneur, Halli Mane Rotties was set up to introduce a different style of cuisine to Mangaloreans, especially when it came to street food. On their daily menu, the canteen offers three types of Rottis made of Ragi, Jowar and Rice, along with Thatte Idli, rice based dishes, a special Chicken Leg Masala or veg accompaniments.

In this episode, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna makes a quick stop at the joint to savour some of the must-haves!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD 
AKKI ROTI 
Light as air! Made with zero oil, this is the healthiest thing you can eat if you love your rice. Rs 30 for 2 Rotis. 10/10

RAGI ROTTI
Ragi in its fluffiest avatar. Nonetheless two of these wholesome rotis will fill you up. Rs.30 for 2 Rotis. 9/10

CHICKEN LEG MASALA 
The meat is slow cooked in a rich, flavourful gravy. The best chicken leg in all of Mangalore.  Rs 120. 10/10

VEG CURRY 
Packed with veggies, including the delicious, local ‘Mattu’ gulla (eggplant), served with the rottis. 8/10
    
Chutney
Made with local green chillies. The spice hit is sure to clear up your sinuses. 8/10

BASIL SEED DRINK  
A refreshing accompaniment, to wash down the spicy flavours. Rs 10. 7/10

ADDRESS - Halli Mane Rotties, Pentland Pet Road, Gandhinagar, Mangaluru 575 003; tel +91 80504 56379

https://maps.app.goo.gl/tLwaoLXjEwSysQAa.description:
#MangaloreFoodTour #StreetFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

Mangalore is full of delicious street treats, perfect to snack on anytime of the day.

A favourite with the locals, Seetharam’s is the place to visit for Mangalorean chaat. This van that has been converted into a chaat counter, is a hangout for not just the college students but also hungry customers from all over the city. The mainstay here is the charmuri, a puffed rice mixture that will set your mouth on fire. What gives Mangalorean charmuri its characteristic flavour is the coconut oil used!

Another hotspot is The Balli Shop located on Carstreet is known for its crispy, crunchy and tongue tickling fritters! 

Tag along as Food Lovers’ Editor, explores these institutions in the city, telling you what you can expect. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 
CABBAGE VADA PODI 
Big, large cabbage fritter! Perfect for a big appetite. Rs 10. 8/10

VEGETABLE CUTLET 
Potato and cauliflower crumbed in rava for a crisp bite. The cauliflower adds a new touch! Rs 12. 9/10

MEDU VADA 
Roundels of deliciousness studded with curry leaves and chilli. Can definitely feel the kick of the chilli. Rs 10. 10/10

BATTATA AMBADE 
The casing is just enough to contain the potato filling without interfering with the flavors. Bright in colour and bright in flavours. Rs 10. 10/10

https://maps.app.goo.gl/24YwTcG8qpEhM15F.title: Enjoy Vegetarian MANGALOREAN BREAKFAST At 96-Year-Old Taj Mahal Restaurant | Mangalore | Food Lovers
https://maps.app.goo.gl/24YwTcG8qpEhM15F.description:
#Breakfast #GourmetOnTheRoad #MangaloreanCuisine
Although popular for its seafood delicacies, Mangalore is also home to some of the oldest culinary institutions that serve up traditional vegetarian fare. 

The Taj Mahal Veg Restaurant is one such establishment that is nearly a 100 years old. In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna enjoys Mangalorean breakfast classics at the restaurant, with dishes like the tuppa dosa, biscuit roti, kashi halwa and more!

He also interacts with co-owner, Vishnu Shenoy, discovering how the restaurant and the kitchen functions.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 
TUPPA DOSA 
Crisp yet soft, slightly tart and loaded with the goodness of ghee! Delicious breakfast choice! Rs 40. 10/10

TEEK ROTI 
Subtle chilli hit. Not as spicy as the name suggest. Rs 20. 7/10

BISCUIT ROTI
Deep fried wheat flour roti stuffed with coconut and spices. Best eaten with chutney. Rs 25. 8/10

GOLI BAJJI
Crisp on the outside and airy inside, with a hint of sweetness that complements the chutney. Rs 25. 9/10

BUNS
Flavoured with ripe banana and fried! Great for a snack! Rs 25. 8/10

GODHI HALWA
An over 90-year-old dessert made with wheat and pure ghee! Sticky, sweet and seriously addictive! Rs 25 per piece. 9/10

BAALE HALWA
Intense caramel flavour and not overly sweet! A halwa you can go back to! Rs 25 per piece. 9/10

FILTER COFFEE
Strong like a filter coffee should be with a nice roast on the beans! Rs 27. 10/10

SAATHU 
Crumbly texture and perfectly sweet! Comfort snack! Rs 280 per kilo. 10/10

KASHI HALWA
Won’t be able to tell that this dessert is made with a vegetable! Delicious! Rs 30. 10/10

Taj Mahal Veg Restaurant, Mangalore Railway Station Road, opposite government wenlock, hospital, Hampankatta, Mangaluru 575 001; tel +91 82424 23195

https://maps.app.goo.gl/LXvoGiHfuRv9zjB4.title: Must-have BREAKFAST Delights At HOTEL JANATHA| Mangalore Food Trail |NEER DOSA| KHOTTIGE|KASHI HALWA
https://maps.app.goo.gl/LXvoGiHfuRv9zjB4.description:
#Breakfast #GourmetOnTheRoad #MangaloreanCuisine

A favourite among the residents of Mangalore, Hotel Janatha Deluxe is over two decades old and is preferred by the masses for its hearty breakfast options.

What’s special on the menu is an array of Mangalorean breakfast specials such as Khottige served with a dal or Tove, Neer Dosa and Bella, Buns, Sheera and Kashi Halwa, among others. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna revisits his childhood whilst he tastes and reviews these must-tries at Hotel Janatha Deluxe. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 
SHEERA 
Not too sweet and studded with the right amount of nuts and raisins! A great way to begin breakfast! Rs 32. 8/10

KASHI HALWA
A rich, decadent dessert with the right touch of sweetness. Best way to make use of ash gourd! Rs 32. 9/10

KOTIGE AND DAALI TOVE
Fragrant cousin of the idli steamed in jackfruit leaves. Much coarser yet light, served with a daali tove or daal seasoned with coconut and local, spicy chillies.
Rs 30. 9/10

BUNS
Fluffy, airy texture! A dish exclusive to Mangalore! Rs 26. 8/10

NEER DOSA WITH COCONUT BELLA
Light dosa, the perfect accompaniment to the coconut and jaggery! My childhood happy meal! Rs 36. 10/10

FILTER COFFEE
A deliciously strong coffee buzz rounds off this breakfast meal. Rs 25. 9/10

ADDRESS - Hotel Janatha Deluxe, Shan Plaza Building, K.S. RAO Road, Mangaluru 575 001; tel + 91 82424 26889

https://maps.app.goo.gl/3sKkHUEFtfT8ENzr.title: Tasting Enormous SEAFOOD THALI At Shetty Lunch Home JUICY CHICKEN GHEE ROAST| KANE FRY | Food Lovers
https://maps.app.goo.gl/3sKkHUEFtfT8ENzr.description:
#Seafood #Mangalore #ShettyLunchHome
 Food Lovers’ Founder & Editor, Kripal Amanna stops by Shetty Lunch Home for the perfect Mangalorean lunch. 
Tasting dishes that the restaurant is said to have invented - Chicken Ghee Roast and Kane Masala Fry together with a sumptuous Seafood Thali, he tells viewers why a meal at this place is a must when in Mangalore!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 
CHICKEN GHEE ROAST - 
Copious amounts of ghee and the original ghee roast masala! The one dish you must definitely try in Mangalore! Spices are smooth and balanced by the ghee. Rs 500 for a whole chicken. 10/10

KANE MASALA FRY -
The spices sing on the palate! Flaky yet firm with the goodness of the secret masala! Rs 300 per fish. 10/10

SPECIAL FISH THALI 
A plate of ten absolutely fresh and delicious seafood dishes! Worth the price! Rs 380. 8/10

Bondas Ghee Roast -
Beautifully cooked, soft textured squid!
Marwai Sukka 
These tiny clams roasted in coconut and dry spices are a flavour bomb! 
Prawn Curry 
Flavourful curry made with the small variety of prawn.
Anjal Fish Fry 
The flavour of the fish overpowers the masala slightly. Pick the kane fry over this!
Yetti Chutney 
Pungent, salty, delicious!
Buttermilk 
Perfect drink to wash down all the heavy spices used in the thali! 

ADDRESS - Shetty Lunch Home, Don Bosco Hall Cross Road, Hampankatta, Mangaluru 575 001; tel +91 99456 18222

https://maps.app.goo.gl/mPbLcFErANKmEi5Q.title: Home Cooked Christian Food At MARYBAI’S Mangalore| MEATY DELIGHTS!|PORK BAFAT|FISH FRIES|Food Lovers
https://maps.app.goo.gl/mPbLcFErANKmEi5Q.description:
#NonVegetarian #MangaloreanCuisine #GourmetOnTheRoad

If one is looking for a simple yet sumptuous home-cooked meal, Marybai’s in Valencia, Mangalore is the place to visit! 

Located in a small home, this eatery has been making its patrons happy with authentic Mangalore Christian cuisine since 1984, when Marybai, the founder set up the restaurant.

Dishes that have been coined to be delicacies at Marybai’s are its meat preparations such as pork chilli, chicken pepper, beef bafat and pork bafat. These dishes are meant to be eaten with a humble thali to enjoy a complete experience here.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna, digs into this delicious spread together with some local, tasty fish fries!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
BOILED RICE AND PICKLE MEALS 
A nourishing, home cooked meal worth its price. Rs 40. 7/10

SARDINE FISH CURRY 
A curry with a tart edge, made with the humble boothai or sardine. Perfect when eaten with boiled rice. 7/10

CHICKEN PEPPER 
This dry preparation is loaded with coriander and pepper. Rs 70 9/10

PORK PEPPER 
Fat has rendered down beautifully. meat is unctuous with a smokey flavour. A must-try here! Rs 80 10/10

BEEF BAFAT  
The meat and masala sing in unison. Very unique in its style and preparation. Rs 90 9/10

PORK BAFAT 
Pork heaven! The meat is well roasted in the bafat masala. Every bite is delicious! Rs 80 10/10

MACKEREL FRY 
Fleshy and coated with the perfect crust. Skin almost fried to a crisp. Rs 70 10/10

SARDINE FRY 
Lightly battered, flavour of the sardine is prominent. Rs 60 8/10

MOORI MEEN FRY
Pungent notes of the fish is balanced with a robustly spiced masala crumbing. Rs 70 7/10

ADDRESS - Marybai’s, 17-7-412, Silva Cross Road, Valencia, Kankanady, Mangalore 575 002; tel +91 99457 36146

#IceCream #MangaloreFoodTour #GourmetOnTheRoad

Mangalore’s favourite spot to hangout at, Pabba’s and Ideal Ice Creams is ‘the’ place to flock to if one wants to relish rich flavoured ice creams! 

While locals swear by the hugely popular Gadbad, this ice cream house also creates inspired and innovative ice creams, made just cream, sugar, fruits and nut! All vegetarian!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits Pabba’s, to indulge in this delicious summer treat and be transported to ice cream heaven! 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 
DIL KHUSH ICE CREAM 
3 flavours for the value of one! Rs 110.  8/10

GADBAD 
Secret proportions and the layering makes this ‘confusion’ of an ice cream a delight! No surprise that this is Mangalore's favorite dessert, it's a happy dessert and will brighten anyone's day! Rs.100.  10/10

TIRAMISU
The coffee hit! A wake-me-up sort of a dessert! Rs 120. 9/10

BELLA CANDY
Jaggery popsicle with a cardamom coconut hit! Like a sorbet! Rs 10. 8/10

AAMBULI CANDY 
Raw mango popsicle with jeera ginger pepper black salt! Great local flavoured candy! 
Rs 10. 8/10

https://goo.gl/maps/LFd5HgUE37J76oPn8.title: BIG FAT MEDDITERANEAN Lunch At Fava Bistro | Salads | Mezze | Burgers |Peri Peri Chicken |Bangalore
https://goo.gl/maps/LFd5HgUE37J76oPn8.description:
#Lunch #Mezze #GourmetOnTheRoad
Fava Bistro, a laidback Mediterranean restaurant in the suburb of Koramangla is Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna’s go-to spot for lunch, on the rare work day that he is not shooting or producing a Gourmet On The Road segment. 

Unfortunately, however, Fava Bistro is set to soon close doors. In this episode, he shares a final lunch at the bistro, tasting dishes he would typically order including a selection of mezzes, a filling wrap, a faultless burger, and a fruity salad!

He also briefly touches upon the challenges involved in running a restaurant.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Organic chickpea hummus
Spiced with paprika, light and creamy. the tahini or sesame paste balances the prominent chickpea flavour. the pita with hummus makes for a great bite. 
Rs 200
8/10

Multigrain fava bistro hamburger with grilled bacon 
A loaded burger that you should dig into when you're really hungry.  multigrain bun, juicy patty, bacon, gherkins, coleslaw, caramelized onions and salty cheddar make this a super delicious burger! can't fault this one!
Rs 395
10/10

Mango caesar salad 
Dressed just enough enough to moisten the salad and your palate. the mango, the Mallika mango in this case  is nice and sweet. eating this salad will not leave you feeling guilty!
Rs 295
8/10

Lamb kebab and avocado wrap
The weight of the wrap gets your palate going. a wholesome, whole wheat wrap loaded with hummus, labneh and avocado salsa. the lamb is spiced just right. 
Rs 375
8/10

Peri peri grill chicken 
A flavourful dish that will fill you up yet leave you feeling light. The chicken is juicy and the spice of the peri peri marinade asserts itself in every bite. the sweetness of the barbecue sauce keeps the chilli heat down.
Rs 375
9/10

Labneh with spinach 
You can taste the perfect balance of sour and a hint of sweet from the honey in the this yoghurt mezze. the wilted garlic seasoned spinach provides a slightly bitter edge making it a great amalgam of flavours!
Rs 300
10/10

Fava Bistro, No.8 Jailakshmi Nivas, 1st Cross Rd, 5th Block, Koramangala, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560095; tel: +91 077600 18751

https://goo.gl/maps/DLEdQ8Y4fKB6zYzq7.title: Non Vegetarian FEAST At RANGANNA MILITARY HOTEL|Famous Mutton Pulao, Kheema Gojju, Mudde |Bangalore
https://goo.gl/maps/DLEdQ8Y4fKB6zYzq7.description:
#MilitaryHotel #RestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad


Drop in at Ranganna Military Hotel for breakfast, lunch or dinner to chow down on rustic meaty dishes full of flavour. 


Established way back in 1964, this eatery swears by its food and so do its patrons. Presently run by a husband-wife duo and their sons, the USP of the restaurant lies in the functioning of its kitchen. 


In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the 60-year-old establishment to explore its kitchen with third generation Co-owner, Sendil Kumar. He discovers that the prep here begins as early as 7am, and every dish is prepared using secret recipes and local ingredients!

He also relishes a meaty spread for lunch, tasting from a hearty mutton leg broth, to steaming hot mutton pulao, kheema gojju, ragi mudde and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Bannur Mutton chops
Mutton has a decent amount of bite. Most of the fat from the meat has rendered into the gravy enhancing the meaty flavours of this dish.
Rs 150
9/10

Bangude fry
Love the masala coating on this deep fried mackerel! The crunch, spice from the batter and prominent fish flavours make this a tasty fish fry!
Rs 150
8/10

Mutton head
a strong, deep flavoured dish, definitely for a hardcore carnivore to savour! Not my cup of tea though. 
Rs 125
7/10

Chicken leg masala
spicy leg of chicken cooked with the skin on. The gravy is robust and rich and the meat is cooked right down to the bone yet juicy!
Rs 80
9/10

Raagi mudde and saaru
Wholesome, filling mudde served with a spicy saaru or meat gravy.
Rs 36
7/10

Goat leg soup
A hearty broth that can make a sick man walk! Mellow in flavours, one can taste the intense flavours of the bones that’s extracted into the broth.
Rs 150
8/10

mutton pulao 
An aromatic pulao, where the meat is cooked with the short grain jeeraga samba rice. The rice is intense in its meaty flavour and studded with flecks of coriander and chilli. 
Rs 190
9/10

Mutton Kheema Gojju
Coarse mince, with flecks of fat, fresh peas and coriander. the kheema is coarsely ground, soaking up the masala. the peas pop in the mouth and the fat adds a burst of savouriness.
10/10
Rs 130

Kheema unde 
Very different from the gojju, the meat here is more finely ground and comes together as a ball or unde. The springy texture gives this meatball a chewy bite. The gravy, is lighter, with flavours of coriander. 
Rs 190
7/10

ADDRESS - Ranganna Military Hotel, New 61, 1st floor, opp to Indian oil petroleum, Krishna Rajendra Road, 7th Block, Jayanagar, Bangalore 560 070; tel +91 80 4302 7346

https://g.page/THITWC?share.title: Eating An Enormous Breakfast At HOLE IN THE WALL CAFÉ|Bangalore’s MOST Popular Eggs Breakfast Spot!
https://g.page/THITWC?share.description:
#AllDayBreakFast #Cafes #GourmetOnTheRoad

Popularly known for its breakfast options, mouthwatering egg creations (an omelette pizza too!), fluffy pancakes, loaded burgers and loaded toasts, The Hole In The Wall Café is perfect for lazy mornings and mid day brunches when in the city of Bengaluru!

In this episode of Hole In The Wall, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna meets proud owner, Nathan Harris, and shares  exclusive details on how the café  actually started out as a literal “hole in the wall”.
 
He also tucks into a large breakfast spread, tasting everything from a scrumptious English Breakfast, perfectly cooked Skillet Eggs, an all-time favourite Chicken Liver on Toast and sweet decadent waffles and pancakes!
  
The Hole In The Wall Café, No 4, 8th Main Road, Koramangala 4th Block, Koramangala, Bangalore 560 047; tel + 91 80 4094 9490

LOCATION TAG - https://g.page/THITWC?share


GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

English breakfast
a hearty breakfast platter of eggs, juicy bacon, cooked just right and juicy, crunchy bacon! Not a big fan of the texture and flavour of the chicken sausage, the mash however, was seasoned well. 
Rs 320
8/10

Skillet eggs with chicken pepperoni and cheese
perfectly cooked eggs with the yolk still runny, savoury chicken pepperoni and slivers of chilli make for a creamy, meaty, spicy mouthful. easy to miss out on the flavour of the cheese, so make sure to order with extra cheese!
Rs 175
7/10

Meaty beef cheeseburger 
the juicy tenderloin patty, topped with fried egg, lettuce, tomato and cheese makes this a rustic burger that will leave you satisfied! The crumbly bun however,struggles to hold the burger together.
Rs 265
8/10

Chicken Liver On Toast
Love the savoury, deep flavour of the liver and its soft yielding texture. Cooked simply with lightly caramelised onions this is a dish every liver lover must try!
Rs 170
9/10

Veggie pizza Omelette
An interesting discovery, this pizza with an ‘eggy’ twist is tangy, savoury and has a nice crunch, thanks to the veggies. Order this dish when out with a bunch of friends.
Rs 165
7/10

Guava Juice
Surprisingly available all year round here, this pink guava juice is nourishingly tasty. The grainy texture of the guava is a great indicator of its freshness! 
Rs 75
8/10

Triple Chocolate pancakes
Chocolate nirvana! The chocolate pancakes, chocolate sauce and chocolate shavings ensure that every bite is decadent and super chocolatey!
Rs 220
8/10

Apple pie waffles
Two thick slices of perfectly cooked waffle topped with caramelised, cinnamon apples, caramel sauce and ice cream. The doughy texture of the waffle makes you want to keep eating! Look out for the slightly burnt edges, they are the best bits!
Rs 240
9/10

https://maps.app.goo.gl/P6nsuk2JZUWM7vms.title: Tasting the BEST Chicken and Mutton BIRYANI In Vellore! Making of Famous JOTHIE BIRIYANI
https://maps.app.goo.gl/P6nsuk2JZUWM7vms.description:
#Biryani #BiryaniInIndia #GourmetOnTheRoad

Gorge on mouthwatering biryani at Jothie Biriyani in Vellore, a 37-year-old establishment that has stood the test of time in the city.

This humble eatery has held onto a traditional recipe and way of making, for nearly four decades. Skilled cooks recreate this recipe by layering meat, rice and a rich, flavourful stock to make some of the most deliciously moist biryani. 

Large deghs fired using tamarind wood charcoal are used to make batches of Mutton and Chicken biryani at different times in day.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the kitchen to understand what goes into making this extraordinary dish!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Mutton biryani
Fingerlicking rice! taste it just by itself and you are hit with a savoury kick of the meat that gets to your palate. the meat makes its presence felt even without it being your mouth! such a find. 
Rs 120
10/10

Chicken biryani 
Mildly coloured rice, flavours of the stock layered into it while cooking takes over the palate! flavours of the chicken biryani is in the rice and not the meat. just eat the rice to be totally happy and totally satisfied! the enne katrikai has a crunch,  sour edge, but this biryani rice needs no accompaniment. not even the meat! it's moist light leaving you wanting another bite. 
Rs 100
10/10

Chicken varuval
An appetising preparation. flavoured with onion, tomato also the curry leaf.skin on the chicken also gives it that flavour burst. 
Rs 90.
6/10

ADDRESS - Jothie Biriyani, CMC Hospital, 65, Bangalore Road, Near Old Bus Stand , Near, Balaji Nagar, Vellore, Tamil Nadu 632004; 098846 42297

https://maps.app.goo.gl/78BKZtkbZtb1mZRV.title: The Perfect FAMILY BREAKFAST Stop | Sai Sangeet, Vaniyambadi | South Indian VEGETARIAN | TamilNadu
https://maps.app.goo.gl/78BKZtkbZtb1mZRV.description:
#Breakfast #HighwayFoodSpots #GourmetOnTheRoad

Sai Sangeet located between Vaniyambadi - Ambur NH 48, On Bangalore-Chennai highway is a delightful spot to stop over for breakfast!

More than any typical highway eatery, this restaurant has an interesting store out front that sells everything from windchimes, to clay pots and pans and also has animals and birds for entertainment!

The fare here is South Indian, with typical, Tamil Nadu breakfast dishes such as the podi uthappam, idli vada and ragi poori. 

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna relishes some delicious highly recommended.
 breakfast staples in this episode of Gourmet On The Road also sharing a quick review on each dish!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

Idli & chutneys

light and fluffy idli with a perfect wobble. a beautiful combination with the sweetness of coconut chutney. The podi with idli hits you right in the throat!
Rs 25.
8/10

Vada & chutneys
Nourishing vada with the bite of the lentil intact. vada is crisp, studded with onions chillies and peppercorns. crunchy on the outside, soft and coarse within. a seriously delicious vada!  
Rs 35.
10/10

Ragi poori
only place where I've tasted a ragi poori. can feel the weight and the bite of the ragi millet. filling and nourishing, two of these with some lightly spiced sagu and chutney and you're good to go!
Rs 65.
7/10

Podi uthappam
a specialty here. podi is completely smeared on the soft, fluffy texture of the dosa. the crunch of the podi and spices together with chutney rounds off all the sharp flavours. the sambar is a nourishing accompaniment. 
Rs 75.
10/10

Black jaggery halwa/ karupatti halwa
nice and warm on the palate. Toasty, intense jaggery flavours. copious amount of ghee makes this a super-rich halwa. a halwa you can't finish on your own!
Rs 70.
8/10

Milk and date halwa 
can taste the milk solids and flecks of date in the halwa. not too sweet, not too rich. A dessert I can finish entirely on my own. 
Rs 40.
9/10

Filter coffee
nice, thick and strong! don't forget to pull your coffee to cool it down and for that extra froth. 
Rs 30.
8/10

ADDRESS - Sai Sangeet Vegetarian Restaurant, Banglore to Chennai Highway, Between Vaniyambadi - Ambur, NH 48, Chengilkuppam, Vellore, Tamil Nadu 635 807; 099418 99099

https://maps.app.goo.gl/rhEktWnTVXjprXKM.title: Exploring the Vaniyambadi BIRYANI at 40-year AHMEDIA HOTEL| Mutton Biryani | Chicken | Quail Masala
https://maps.app.goo.gl/rhEktWnTVXjprXKM.description:
#Biryani #TamilNadu #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Established in 1975, Ahmedia Hotel, a name highly familiar with the locals of Vaniyambadi is the quintessential non-vegetarian lunch stopover in town!

Especially known for its aromatic Biryani made using long grain basmati rice, unlike the typical jeeraga samba rice used in biryanis elsewhere in Tamilnadu, this restaurant claims that its biryani is what brings patrons back each time. 

Aside from the biryani, the mutton and quail preparations here are what one should definitely indulge in here. In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the kitchen to discover what makes this biryani great and also orders a full lunch meal complete with piping hot Mutton Biryani, Mutton Chukka, Chicken Chukka, Teetar Pepper Masala, Chicken Kebab and more to savour the whole experience of dining here.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Mutton chukka
meat is roasted superbly well. not your typical Chettinad/ Kongu chukka. very mild and gentle, allows you to enjoy the flavours of the meat. deep brown on the outside and moist and pink on the inside. 
Rs 150.
8/10

Chicken chukka
crisped curry leaves add an extra dimension to the dish. excellent dish for a chicken lover!
8/10

Quail pepper dry
Cooked well although quail is tough to get right. Prominent pepper flavours together with the characteristic crispy curry leaves makes this an intense dish.
Rs 130
9/10


Quail phaal/masala
thick gravy with the quail having soaked in all the masala. delicious! a dish to definitely order here! all you need is a piece if parota to mop up all the goodness. 
Rs 150.
10/10


Bheja/brain pepper fry
in-your-face pepper hit with underlying flavours of curry leaves, onion and tomato.  Can be enjoyed both with roti and biryani.
Rs 140
8/10


Vanjaram fish fry 
Fish tastes fine but doesn't really make the cut. slightly overcooked. the masala hasn't penetrated inside. I prefer the meat dishes here. 
Rs 160.
5/10


Chicken kebab
Tastes like a regular kebab. A tad bit dry. if you love your kebab, this dish is worth trying. 
Rs 140.
6/10


Mutton Biryani
certainly an aromatic biryani! made with the long grain basmati. very delicate in it's flavours. pink juicy pieces of mutton, you can taste the pure flavour of the meat. no heavy spices weighing down the meat. this is a delicious biryani!
Rs 200.
10/10

ADDRESS - Ahmedia Hotel™️ Since 1975
3/7, CN Annadurai Road, Near Bus Stop, Vaniyambadi, Tamil Nadu 635751; tel: +91 97893 29139

https://maps.app.goo.gl/Cypw9n7cnCpiBSBh.title: Desi Gourmet OMELETTES! Streetfood Eggs Taken To A Whole New Level| Egg Factor! Bangalore Food Tour!
https://maps.app.goo.gl/Cypw9n7cnCpiBSBh.description:
#Eggs #StreetFoodInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Egg Factor – Street House, a street kiosk whips ups gourmet-style omelettes that are a far cry from the regular masala or cheese versions.

Using ingredients such as chicken, prawn, grilled fish, goat brain and even fruits such as pineapples or strawberries, ex-cruise line chef, Kumar is dishing up fancy, exotic and unheard of toppings and fillings to go with the humble omelette, in a street shop setting.

In this Gourmet On The Road video, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna discovers what inspired this well-travelled, ex-cruise line chef’s vision, the incidents that led to the creation of offbeat toppings and fillings, the delectable omelettes you can try here and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

Chicken and Cheese Omelette
A loaded omelette! chicken is well marinated. The crunchy veggies complement the gooey savouriness of the cheese. Can definitely feel the chilli kick in the seasoning!
Rs 150.
8/10

Pepper Prawn Omelette
You smell the inviting aromas of freshly ground spices and fresh herbs. This makes all the difference! the prawns are torched, cooked just right, can taste the sweetness. The use of desi eggs gives this omelette a wholesome touch!
Rs 200
8/10

Goat Brain Omelette
Luscious, creamy, custardy! The heavy masalas balance the rich flavours of the brain. The lush buttery texture of the brain with the fluffy egg is a delightful mouthful.
Rs 200
10/10

Pineapple And Cheese Omelette
A sweet, hot and sour medley on the palate! The garlic and chilli in the pineapple is a surprising touch. a tart zingy acidity and a chilli heat in the back of your throat. A savoury fruit omelette. This is definitely a first for me!
Rs 130
6/10

ADDRESS - Eggfactor, # 367, 80th feet road, 17th Main Road, HSR Layout, Sector 3, Opposite to Sri Muneshwara Swamy Temple, Bengaluru 560102; Tel: +91 82484 54360/ 99028 05592

https://maps.app.goo.gl/7Mra39VE7Jf7Rvj9.description:
#DonneBiryani #MilitaryHotelsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

An age-old, iconic establishment in the city of Bengaluru, Shivaji Military Hotel is renowned for its Maratha cuisine.

The crowd favourite, “donne-style” biryani here is cooked on dum using coal and robustly flavoured with stock, chunks of meat and a secret masala blend all made in-house. The biryani can be enjoyed with other meat heavy preparations like Mutton Dry, Chicken Kalmi, Liver Fry and more.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits this bustling eatery to discover what makes it popular with the locals while he indulges in a full-fledged meal!

GOTR RATING
Chicken Dry
the chicken is smothered in masala, making every bite flavourful. Chicken cooked just right. 
Rs 160
8/10

Mutton Dry
great quality meat. cooked dry with fat trimmings that imparts a deep savouriness, a meaty bite. So good!
Rs 190
9/10

Chicken Leg/ Kalmi Masala
plump, spicy chicken thighs. it's juicy, succulent inside and has a peppery bite.
Rs 160
8/10

Mutton Donne Biryani
piping hot biryani with gentle inviting aromas. the rice has all the flavours of the biryani, is cooked perfectly well and even has a bite to it. the meat is soft, juicy, fatty, all things you want in a piece of meat! a seriously tasty biryani!
Rs 220
10/10

Mutton Liver
cooked in a green chilli, coriander and mint masala that has a freshness to it. meaty piece of liver. a tad dry for my liking.
Rs 150
6/10

Chicken Donne Biryani
pleasantly surprised with the flavours for a chicken biryani. lightly spiced with a chilli kick that you feel at the back of your throat. chicken with the rice makes for a lovely mouthful. the pachadi (yoghurt salad) helps cool off the heat.
Rs 180
8/10

Chilli Chicken
not your typical chinese-style chilli chicken. this maratha chilli chicken uses tons of green chilli. if you love your food spicy then this dish is for you.
Rs 160
7/10

ADDRESS- Shivaji Military Hotel, No. 718, 1st C Main, 45th Cross, 8th Block, Jayanagar, Bangalore 560 082; tel: +91 98451 49217

#ChettinadCuisine #Salem #GourmetOnTheRoad

Hotel Rajaganapathy, a tiny eatery located at Arthanari Nagar, Salem is frequented by locals for its non-vegetarian meals and Chettinad style meat fries. 

Carrying forward its 40-year old legacy is owner, Vaidyanathan, a gentleman who has been working the stove since he was a 7-year-old.

In this episode of Gourmet Of On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, tastes a lavish non-vegetarian meal with a variety of dishes as interacts with the owner and his sons to find what makes this spot special!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Mutton Chukka
Roasted with a bunch of spices and cooked on the bone with the marrow rendered into the gravy.  The meat definitely has a bite to it. Rs 200. 9/10

Natti chicken fry
pieces of shredded country chicken roasted in a dry masala with loads of curry leaves. Rs 200. 7/10

Mutton boti
boti cooked to perfection, almost melts in the mouth. Rs 150. 8/10

Pigeon roast 
Intense, gamey flavours. The curry masala made using hard spices complements the meat. 
Have to wrestle with tiny bones to get to the meat! Rs 200. 9/10

Natti Chicken biryani
The flavour in this biryani runs deep. the country chicken has a chewy texture but the flavourful rice makes up for this. pairs well with the special, rich chicken gravy. Rs 200. 9/10

Country chicken pepper chukka
very distinctive, peppery taste. Rs 200. 7/10

Chicken chintamani fry
Simple preparation of chicken tossed with shallots and red chillies. A bit on the salty side. Rs 150. 5/10

#ChettinadCuisine #Salem #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Selvi Mess, in Salem, Tamil Nadu, known for its Chettinad-style fare dishes out specials in true country style. Although a tiny eatery, this spot is unmissable to the traveller’s eye owing to the clamour coming from a full house of diners. In nearly 35 years of its existence, the iconic mess called a ‘mess’ has amassed a devoted audience, turning into the perfect pit stop for a delicious meal!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna tastes a full meal of the most highly recommended dishes here including a piping hot Catla Fry, robust Mutton Chukka and the signature Turkey Chukka, the special for the day. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Prawn fry 
A semi dry preparation of tiny prawns cooked in roasted spices and onions. the tiny prawns add flavour and punch to the dish.
Rs. 210  
9/10

Turkey chukka
Cooked just right although turkey is a tough meat to nail. The deeply roasted masala adds an extra dimension to the dish.
Rs. 200
8/10

Mutton chukka
A true blue Chettinad preparation made with tiny bits of meat cooked on the bone. You can taste the signature spice mix and pepper with every bite. 
Rs 200
10 /10

Goat Head Curry
Delicious! The meat and fat melts in your mouth with each morsel.  
Rs 180
8 /10

Country chicken chukka
Naati style chicken cooked with the skin, deep flavour. Rs 215
7/10

Mutton biryani
Served with a customary egg, this biryani is made with the short grain jeerga samba rice. This style of making a biryani uses copious amounts of tomato that lends a tart flavour to the dish.
Rs 210
8/10

Mutton gravy
The mutton gravy is a delicious side to the biryani. The spices are raw and coarse, with the fat perfectly rendered into the gravy.
 8/10

Catla fry
Caught in the Mettur dam, a specialty of the region. Lightly coated in masala and deep fried, it makes for a scrumptious, mildly spicy dish..
Rs 110
9 /10

Rice & Rasam 
The unlimited rice and rasam are perfect to be eaten with the robust meat fries. The tangy rasam is a great wash down to a non-vegetarian meal! 
Rs. 100
 8/10

https://maps.app.goo.gl/yAVBZrdm1aWMV8VU.description:
#RamadanFeast #Haleem #GourmetOnTheRoad

Haleem, a delicacy especially during the month of Ramadan is a filling, wholesome meal  packed with essential nutrients. Made with ingredients like lentils, spices and broken wheat, along with spices, ghee, dry fruits, and saffron, the haleem is said to be easy on the stomach but also full of nourishment that helps restore energy. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna indulges in seven variations of the haleem at Punjab Bistro to celebrate this holy month in full swing! From a Vegetable Haleem made with over five kinds of veggies, Raw Jackfruit Haleem, to Prawn, Duck and even Turkey Haleem, this haleem festival has something for everyone! 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

Vegetable Haleem
Great choice for vegetarians on the lookout to try haleem, its texture mimics a meat haleem! The fried veggies as a garnish adds a beautiful crunch.
Rs 275 for a full portion. 8/10

Kathal Haleem
meaty bite for a vegetarian haleem. can taste the subtle sweetness of the raw jackfruit.
Rs 295 for a full portion. 7/10

Prawn haleem
Light in its flavours. Definitely needed the birista and coriander for added depth. The spicy prawn chutney accompaniment is overpowering.  
Rs 475 for a full portion. 6/10

Chicken haleem
mellow flavours with a bit of an underlying tartness. a great combination with the sheermal.
Rs 340 for a full portion. 8/10

Turkey haleem
light in colour but deep and bright in flavours! the fried turkey is a little salty perfect to cut through the monotony of flavours. Rs 575 for a full portion. 9/10

Duck haleem
The haleem for duck lovers. deep flavours of the duck are balanced when eaten with birista and coriander. Personally, a bit strong for my liking. Rs 450 for a full portion. 6/10

Mutton haleem
Classic, textbook haleem. Its rich, meaty savouriness shines in every bite. piece of ghee fried mutton on top makes for a wonderful bonus! Rs 400 for a full portion. 10/10



Punjab Bistro, SJR Primus Ground Floor Opposite Forum Mall, 20th Main Rd, 7th Block, Koramangala, Banaglore 560 095; tel +91 80 4090 2161; Location Tag - https://maps.app.goo.gl/yAVBZrdm1aWMV8VU8

https://maps.app.goo.gl/4bEbeBGCpeupr5ZX.title: Breakfast at the Original Krishnagiri SREE SARAVANA BHAVAN, Tamil Nadu |PODI DOSA |PONGAL |IDLI VADA
https://maps.app.goo.gl/4bEbeBGCpeupr5ZX.description:
#Breakfast #SouthIndianBreakfast #GourmetOnTheRoad 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the Krishnagiri outpost of Sree Saravana Bhavan that has spawned several other restaurants trying to imitate its menu under its name. 

Savouring some of Tamil Nadu’s breakfast staples, the idli vada, masala dosa including a fiery podi dosa, catch Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna’s full review in this video.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

Idli Vada
Soft, almost-pillowy idlis served with an assortment of chutneys, leaving you spoilt for choice. Vadas are perfectly crunchy. Rs 60. 10/10 


Pongal
Lightly spiced, mellow pongal that is delicately tempered with ghee and studded with cashews. The peppercorns help cut through the richness! Rs 62. 8/10

Masala Dosa
A thin, crisp dosa, surprisingly light on oil! Each bite with the spiced mash potato is super satisfying! Rs 71. 9/10

Podi dosa
You can taste the fire of the podi. This spirited condiment is a Tamil Nadu staple made with lentils, chillies and garlic. Rs 76. 7/10

Idiyappam
A simple dish but delicious! The steamed rice flour noodles are best when lapped up with the sweet coconut milk flavoured with cardamom. Rs 55. 10/10

Filter coffee
Dark, deep-roasted coffee topped with a frothy foam. Rs 25. 8/10


Sree Sarvana Bhavan, Vangli Towers National Highway 7, Avathanapatti 635 101; 94437 66655

https://maps.app.goo.gl/44crqhUcfLi9AZnU.title: Mosque Road BANGALORE FOOD TRAIL | Albert Bakery, Pista House | KHEEMA SAMOSAS| HALEEM| NALLI NIHARI
https://maps.app.goo.gl/44crqhUcfLi9AZnU.description:
#RamadanFoodTrail #FrazerTown #GourmetOnTheRoad

Frazer town located in the heart of Bangalore is nothing less than a food lovers heaven! 

With streets like Mosque Road and MM Road lined with restaurants and eateries dishing out some of the most delicious non vegetarian fare, this spot in the city is a must-visit.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna takes off on this busy street, during the month of Ramadan together with a friend to taste and review much loved dishes such as the Haleem, Kheema Samosa, a delectable Nalli Nihari and more! 

Gourmet On The Road Ratings
MUTTON KHEEMA MINI SAMOSA 
a speciality at Albert, he thin skin is fried to a crisp with a moist kheema filling. Delicious! Rs 480 a kilo. 10 /10

BRAIN PUFF
piping hot, flaky puff stuffed with a custardy mutton brain that dissolves in your mouth!  Rs 35 per puff. 
9/10

KHEEMA NAAN
prominent taste of onions and a meaty savouriness makes the kheema naan a tasty, filling indulgence! Rs120 6/10

KHOVA NAAN 
the filling of the khova or reduced milk solids shine in this dessert puff that isn’t overly sweet. Rs100 7/10

HYDERABADI MUTTON HALEEM 
A wholesome dish, this haleem is velvety, gooey and is crowned with fried onions, mint and lemon juice. The twang of the lemon and texture from the onion helps cut through the richness. Rs 250 8/10

QUBANI KI MEETHA
This Hyderabadi speciality is a rich and pulpy apricot dessert laced with a  hint of saffron. The sugary goodness makes the perfect accompaniment to the haleem. Rs 190. 7/10

PAYA WITH NAAN
This gelatinous, warm and nourishing stew made with lamb trotters is to be enjoyed steaming hot with some naan! Rs150. 8/10

NALLI NIHARI
The slow cooked, rich nihari is superbly flavourful. You can tell that the gravy has been cooked for hours to intensify the deliciousness! Rs 350. 10/10

KARACHI NAAN 
The Karachi naan is a light yet dry making it the right accompaniment to soak up all the gravy and its unctuous goodness. Rs 45 for 2. 9/10

https://maps.app.goo.gl/2fFeNiangGP3sKZM.description:
#MilitaryHotel #NonVegetarian #GourmetOnTheRoad

Murli Miltry Hotel on Bellur Cross is the quintessential non-vegetarian lunch stopover on Bangalore-Mangalore highway.

The mutton preparations here are what one should definitely indulge in here. In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna orders a full Mutton Thali served 
with chapathi, Mutton Chops, Mutton Kurma, Rice and Buttermilk including a Mutton Pepper Dry and A naati-style Mutton Biryani, to savour the whole experience of dining here. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Mutton Meal 
A delicious thali of Mudde/ Rice/ Chapathi served with Mutton Chops, Mutton Korma, Egg, Rasam and Butter Milk. Rs 240.  8/10

Mutton Chops
A spirited naati style curry made in a delicious green masala. The mutton is melt-in-the-mouth and flavoured with cardamom, coriander and green chilli. 8/10

Mutton Pepper Dry
The roast and the pepperiness is what makes this dish shine. Mutton is braised well with a crisp outside and juicy, soft inside. The dish to order here! Rs 160. 10/10

Fish Fry Mackerel
Butterflied fish, layered with masala. Not high on appeal to the fish purist, but okay otherwise. Rs 200. 5 /10

Chicken Kebab
a typical kebab, good but not brilliant. the meat is a bit dry and stringy.. Rs 140. 5/10

Mutton Dum Biryani
Crowned with some kurma gravy on top. Tasty but not what I would order here. Found the meat a bit chewy. Rs 180. 6/10

How do biryanis become iconic? Well, most begin as tentative experiments and over a period of time endear themselves to the palate of the locals. So much so that the denizens of the place become vocal ambassadors for the biryani. And when it comes to Belagavi (Belgaum), the Niyaaz biryani is one such icon. Made in the kacchi akhni style, in which semi-cooked rice is layered over twice-marinated meat and cooked on dum, the Niyaaz biryani is subtle in its character, owing to a unique blend of spices, and the light fragrance of a short-grain locally grown rice that is used in combination with the more typical long grain basmati rice. What began as a family’s endeavour to create a unique biryani 30 years ago is now unarguably one of Belagavi’s most popular dishes. In this episode, I drive to Belgaum to meet co-owner, Niyaaz Abdussalam Saudagar, and explore in depth the making of both the chicken and mutton biryani, before proceeding to make a meal of these distinct Belagavi culinary signatures. Hope you enjoy this one; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

https://maps.app.goo.gl/gaDweeSNAwped....description:
#Bheemas #AndhraFood #Bangalore

andhra cuisine, bheema’s, bengaluru, non vegetarian meal, lunch, fish fry, chilli chicken, mutton pepper fry, guntur chicken, mutton seeraga samba biryani, chicken biryani, nellore biryani, popular bengaluru lunch spot

After many a vegetarian reviews over the last few weeks, I was craving the comfort of some hearty non vegetarian fare. And so we landed at Bheema’s to savour a spicy Andhra bhojanam of fish fry, chilli chicken, mutton pepper fry, Guntur chicken, and a couple of biryanis, their staple Nellore version in addition to their ode to Bengaluru’s dhonne style biryani! And needless to say, we also took a quick look behind the scenes to see how this popular restaurant is gearing up to serve customers in these challenging times. Enjoy and stay safe. 

Fish Fry 
A tasty fry, though not the sort that will blow your socks off! It’s a thin slice of fish, napped in a sprightly masala and fried crisp around the edges.
Rs. 370 (usd 4.9) 
7/10

Chilli Chicken
No Andhra non-vegetarian meal can be complete without a chilli chicken, rich in copious amounts of green chilli and pepper. The spice hit is tongue-numbing, but one that’s vicariously addictive. The chicken is nice and juicy all the way down to the bone. 
Rs. 270 (usd 3.6) 
8/10

Mutton Pepper Fry 
The mutton is soft and yields to a gentle bite, draped in a pepper-onion masala. The meat is sheathed in some fat, which lends it its fulsome flavour. At Bheema’s they pick their meat cuts well and certainly know how to cook it well too.
Rs. 350 (usd 4.6) 
9/10

Guntur Chicken
A chicken preparation that heroes the Guntur chilli.The creaminess of the coconut though and the acidity of tomatoes in this dish balances against the heat of this otherwise spicy Andhra chilli.
Rs. 305 (usd 4) 
8/10

Mutton Jeera Rice Biryani
Bheema’s ode to the local Bengaluru biryani, this one is made with the short-grained seeraga samba rice. You can taste the fervour of coriander, mint and green chillies alongside other ingredients like the marat moggu, cloves that are typically used in this one-pot rice and meat preparation. The meat slides off the bone, it is cooked as well as that! 
Rs. 295 (usd 3.9) 
8/10

Chicken Biryani 
Bheema’s most popular dish, this traditional Nellore-style biryani is made with basmati rice. There’s flecks of pineapple that go into this biryani and you taste its acidity juxtaposed against the aromatic flavours of cloves, cinnamon and other warming spices that the chicken and rice are cooked in. The meat is soft and juicy, however it is the delicate spicing of the biryani that makes an impression on the palate and lingers long after one has finished eating.
Rs. 260 (usd 3.4) 
9/10

ADDRESS - Bheema's, 31, Asha Building, Ground Floor, Church Street, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560001; tell: 080 2558 7389

#Dosas #BangaloreFoodTour #GourmetOnTheRoad 

In this exciting Gourmet On The Road episode, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna takes off on a trip across Namma Bengaluru exploring the city’s most popular dosa destinations!

The second and final part to this dosa trail begins at Shri Sagar - CTR, an establishment with legions of loyal fans. Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna tastes a Benne Masala Dose and the Set Dosa here. He then relishes a unique dill flavoured dosa at a streetside dosa haunt in the bylanes of Basavanagudi. He then tastes a smashing Podi Dosa at Umesh Dosa Point, and a Bath Masala and Khaali Dosa at Chikkanna Tiffin Room located in the narrow bylanes of Cubbonpet.

He finally rounds off this dosa trail in the evening with the famous Pav Bhaji Dosa at Shree Balaji 99 Variety Dosa. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

CENTRAL TIFFIN ROOM 
BENNE MASALA DOSA 
Love the texture of this thick yet crisp dosa roasted with oodles of ghee. it takes skill to roast a dosa like this. the chutney is fresh while the ghatti chutney is nice and spicy.
Rs 52.
10/10

SET DOSA
Fluffy yet crisp set dosa. the saagu here is unlike any other loaded with a bunch of seasonal veggies. An absolute find here!
Rs 47.
9/10

GOLI BAJJI 
The ultimate tea or coffee time snack! crisp and stretchy outside, soft and porous inside.
Rs 32.
9/10
7th Cross Rd, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

SABAKKI DOSA

https://goo.gl/maps/Mfcwwje694kJvdYeA.title: Desi Gourmet OMELETTES! Streetfood Eggs Taken To A Whole New Level| Egg Factor! Bangalore Food Tour!
https://goo.gl/maps/Mfcwwje694kJvdYeA.description:
#Eggs #StreetFoodInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Egg Factor – Street House, a street kiosk whips ups gourmet-style omelettes that are a far cry from the regular masala or cheese versions.

Using ingredients such as chicken, prawn, grilled fish, goat brain and even fruits such as pineapples or strawberries, ex-cruise line chef, Kumar is dishing up fancy, exotic and unheard of toppings and fillings to go with the humble omelette, in a street shop setting.

In this Gourmet On The Road video, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna discovers what inspired this well-travelled, ex-cruise line chef’s vision, the incidents that led to the creation of offbeat toppings and fillings, the delectable omelettes you can try here and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

Chicken and Cheese Omelette
A loaded omelette! chicken is well marinated. The crunchy veggies complement the gooey savouriness of the cheese. Can definitely feel the chilli kick in the seasoning!
Rs 150.
8/10

Pepper Prawn Omelette
You smell the inviting aromas of freshly ground spices and fresh herbs. This makes all the difference! the prawns are torched, cooked just right, can taste the sweetness. The use of desi eggs gives this omelette a wholesome touch!
Rs 200
8/10

Goat Brain Omelette
Luscious, creamy, custardy! The heavy masalas balance the rich flavours of the brain. The lush buttery texture of the brain with the fluffy egg is a delightful mouthful.
Rs 200
10/10

Pineapple And Cheese Omelette
A sweet, hot and sour medley on the palate! The garlic and chilli in the pineapple is a surprising touch. a tart zingy acidity and a chilli heat in the back of your throat. A savoury fruit omelette. This is definitely a first for me!
Rs 130
6/10

https://maps.app.goo.gl/GF1UawDxiLD58dfi.description:
#RamadanFoodTrail #FrazerTown #GourmetOnTheRoad

Frazer town located in the heart of Bangalore is nothing less than a food lovers heaven! 

With streets like Mosque Road and MM Road lined with restaurants and eateries dishing out some of the most delicious non vegetarian fare, this spot in the city is a must-visit.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna takes off on this busy street, during the month of Ramadan together with a friend to taste and review much loved dishes such as the Haleem, Kheema Samosa, a delectable Nalli Nihari and more! 

Gourmet On The Road Ratings
MUTTON KHEEMA MINI SAMOSA 
a speciality at Albert, he thin skin is fried to a crisp with a moist kheema filling. Delicious! Rs 480 a kilo. 10 /10

BRAIN PUFF
piping hot, flaky puff stuffed with a custardy mutton brain that dissolves in your mouth!  Rs 35 per puff. 
9/10

KHEEMA NAAN
prominent taste of onions and a meaty savouriness makes the kheema naan a tasty, filling indulgence! Rs120 6/10

KHOVA NAAN 
the filling of the khova or reduced milk solids shine in this dessert puff that isn’t overly sweet. Rs100 7/10

HYDERABADI MUTTON HALEEM 
A wholesome dish, this haleem is velvety, gooey and is crowned with fried onions, mint and lemon juice. The twang of the lemon and texture from the onion helps cut through the richness. Rs 250 8/10

QUBANI KI MEETHA
This Hyderabadi speciality is a rich and pulpy apricot dessert laced with a  hint of saffron. The sugary goodness makes the perfect accompaniment to the haleem. Rs 190. 7/10

PAYA WITH NAAN
This gelatinous, warm and nourishing stew made with lamb trotters is to be enjoyed steaming hot with some naan! Rs150. 8/10

NALLI NIHARI
The slow cooked, rich nihari is superbly flavourful. You can tell that the gravy has been cooked for hours to intensify the deliciousness! Rs 350. 10/10

KARACHI NAAN 
The Karachi naan is a light yet dry making it the right accompaniment to soak up all the gravy and its unctuous goodness. Rs 45 for 2. 9/10

In a small village in Kundapur taluk, sits a nondescript eatery by the wayside. If you step in, you will find Mr. Subramanya Holla hunched over a large cast iron pan, ladling batter, smearing masala, lashing streams of ghee and throwing in chunks of butter to make a special benne masala dosae. It’s a craft that he has mastered over 43 years, and he serves only the dosae and a sajjige vade alongside, that too for only four hours each evening! But such is the popularity of Guru Canteen, Halady that people don't mind changing their travel routes just to get a taste of his dosae. On my recent visit to South Kanara, I too made a 100-kilometer return trip to experience this dosae at this family-run eatery. Was it worth the effort? Well, I polished two butter laden, utterly scrumptious, flavourful dosae back to back! 
Hope you enjoy this one. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Originally from Chikmagalur, Lijjo Joy Kasper was introduced to the world of pizzas a decade ago during a stint in an Italian kitchen. Since then, pizzas have become centrestage for this young chef, obsessing over the right mix of flour, fermentation techniques, a zesty tomato sauce that employs both Italian and naati (country) tomatoes in a sweet, spicy and sour mix, to topping combinations that are rooted in the classic but have flavourful tweaks. A year ago, his pizza passion found home in a tiny 300 s.ft. pizzeria in Koramangala, South Bengaluru where he alongside his brother and wife dish out, through a curbside store window, an impressive range of sourdough pizzas and sandwiches. 64 Mutton Pulav began as a Sunday experiment five years ago for Goutham and his cousin Abhishek to cook an old-style pulav in their home kitchen to serve neighbours and friends. Enthused by the positive response of early customers to their woodfire cooked pulav, they bootstrapped an eatery in an open plot in the North Bengaluru suburb of Yelahanka. It’s been four years since and the space has evolved to evoke a rustic, airy vibe that is popular with locals. What hasn’t changed though is the brothers’ commitment to the food, preparing the dishes personally sans any hired cooks. I dropped in unannounced one afternoon to find Goutham applying the finishing touches to the mutton pulav. What impressed me also was the fact that they only serve five or six dishes; I spent time observing them and left only after tasting some of their popular fare.

Hope you enjoy this one too. Do support small enterprises like 64 Mutton Pulav for the delicious work that they do. Happy eating!

Eight years ago, two IT professionals, Vikas Subramani and Varun Timmegowda ventured out to do something on their own. A culinary enterprise wasn’t on these engineers' minds, but their limited cumulative savings ruled out most other options. And so, they ventured into the food business with a small ‘stand-and-eat’ darshini style South Indian vegetarian tiffin eatery. With no background in the space, they invested nearly a year in learning basic recipes, honing them before opening in Jayanagar, South Bengaluru. Cut to the present, and Bengaluru Café has emerged as a hugely popular neighbourhood tiffin stop. I visited them recently to see how they operate and also to taste most of their evening tiffin menu. And in the course of doing so, also learnt of their plans to open one of Bengaluru’s largest tiffin eateries shortly.

I hope you enjoy this inspiring and tasty watch. Happy eating!

Needless to say, I stayed for both breakfast and the biryani. Another must-visit eatery if you find yourself in this part of Coorg!

Before exploring two coffee shops, one that is almost hidden in a palace that few know of! And the second, the harbinger of a new wave of coffee spots that are extremely serious about their coffee. We also visit a chocolate studio and café in a heritage bungalow that dates back to the 19th century, a must-visit if you’re a chocolate lover, before settling for the evening at a revolving restaurant that commands a bird’s eye view over this palace city. Every evening Rohan leaves home in Rayasandra with a bag full of hot vada pavs cooked fresh and packed with care by his Mom, Mrs. Hema Birajdar, for a street corner in HSR Layout, South Bengaluru, where he stands patiently for four hours to sell his wares. Not your typical-sized batata (potato) vada, these are humungous therefore deserving of its moniker XXL vada pav. I visited him on a drizzly evening recently to taste a simple but tasty vadapav, which prompted a visit to his home to meet his mother and find out more about his heartening ‘Mom & Son’ enterprise. An incentive when you visit them, you can taste their food piping hot, and also a very special masala vada pav that will surely have me revisiting them more than once.

I hope you enjoy this watch, and that it also encourages you to support small enterprises like this that are doing honest, delicious work.

Every evening Rohan leaves home in Rayasandra with a bag full of hot vada pavs cooked fresh and packed with care by his Mom, Mrs. Hema Birajdar, for a street corner in HSR Layout, South Bengaluru, where he stands patiently for four hours to sell his wares. Not your typical-sized batata (potato) vada, these are humungous therefore deserving of its moniker XXL vada pav. I visited him on a drizzly evening recently to taste a simple but tasty vadapav, which prompted a visit to his home to meet his mother and find out more about his heartening ‘Mom & Son’ enterprise. An incentive when you visit them, you can taste their food piping hot, and also a very special masala vada pav that will surely have me revisiting them more than once.

I hope you enjoy this watch, and that it also encourages you to support small enterprises like this that are doing honest, delicious work.

Namaskara folks! Welcome to a new show on Food Lovers TV, where we seek to explore diverse strands of a city’s culinary landscape in a single episode. In our first tour, we visit Mysuru, a city that has always held an allure for travellers, for its majestic charm steeped in royal heritage, architecture and its proud traditions. Alongside its fabled eateries and shops that have stood the test of time, the city has also witnessed the birth of new age bakeries, cafes and food concepts. Set in a beautiful bungalow that dates back to the last century, Raya is easily the most popular restaurant in Old Phuket town. Known for its traditional recipes that span across Thai, Malay and Chinese influences, the food here is the sort that brings people back over and over again “for its consistency”, avered my friend Mark Wiens. And so it was only appropriate that we experienced the must-try dishes here with him and his family. Definitely make note of this spot for a meal when you are in Phuket next.

We commence part two of our Mysuru food tour at a legendary dosae destination that has ruled Mysuru’s palate for over 80 years, and then stop at a breakfast food truck that has grown in popularity over the last couple of years. Before exploring two coffee shops, one that is almost hidden in a palace that few know of! And the second, the harbinger of a new wave of coffee spots that are extremely serious about their coffee. We also visit a chocolate studio and café in a heritage bungalow that dates back to the 19th century, a must-visit if you’re a chocolate lover, before settling for the evening at a revolving restaurant that commands a bird’s eye view over this palace city. Hope you enjoy this one.

Before exploring two coffee shops, one that is almost hidden in a palace that few know of! And the second, the harbinger of a new wave of coffee spots that are extremely serious about their coffee. We also visit a chocolate studio and café in a heritage bungalow that dates back to the 19th century, a must-visit if you’re a chocolate lover, before settling for the evening at a revolving restaurant that commands a bird’s eye view over this palace city. We commence part two of our Mysuru food tour at a legendary dosae destination that has ruled Mysuru’s palate for over 80 years, and then stop at a breakfast food truck that has grown in popularity over the last couple of years. Before exploring two coffee shops, one that is almost hidden in a palace that few know of! And the second, the harbinger of a new wave of coffee spots that are extremely serious about their coffee. We also visit a chocolate studio and café in a heritage bungalow that dates back to the 19th century, a must-visit if you’re a chocolate lover, before settling for the evening at a revolving restaurant that commands a bird’s eye view over this palace city. Hope you enjoy this one. 

If you haven't caught the previous episode in this Mysuru food tour, watch at:

Namaskara folks! Welcome to a new show on Food Lovers TV, where we seek to explore diverse strands of a city’s culinary landscape in a single episode. In our first tour, we visit Mysuru, a city that has always held an allure for travellers, for its majestic charm steeped in royal heritage, architecture and its proud traditions. Alongside its fabled eateries and shops that have stood the test of time, the city has also witnessed the birth of new age bakeries, cafes and food concepts. In the first show in this series, we explore a decades old popular biryani at RRR followed by a visit to SAPA Bakery that in a short span of only four years has endeared itself to the hearts of locals and travellers alike. A trip to Mysuru is incomplete without a taste of the Mysuru Pak, and we explore myriad flavours of this mithai at its source, Guru Sweets. Followed by a market outing to taste bananas including one that enjoys a GI tg. There’s more in this episode, hope you enjoy it.

Namaskara folks! Welcome to a new show on Food Lovers TV, where we seek to explore diverse strands of a city’s culinary landscape in a single episode. In our first tour, we visit Mysuru, a city that has always held an allure for travellers, for its majestic charm steeped in royal heritage, architecture and its proud traditions. Alongside its fabled eateries and shops that have stood the test of time, the city has also witnessed the birth of new age bakeries, cafes and food concepts. In the first show in this series, we explore a decades old popular biryani at RRR followed by a visit to SAPA Bakery that in a short span of only four years has endeared itself to the hearts of locals and travellers alike. A trip to Mysuru is incomplete without a taste of the Mysuru Pak, and we explore myriad flavours of this mithai at its source, Guru Sweets. Followed by a market outing to taste bananas including one that enjoys a GI tg. There’s more in this episode, hope you enjoy it.

Do let us know your thoughts in the comments. Stay tuned for more in this series.

Namaskara folks! Welcome to a new show on Food Lovers TV, where we seek to explore diverse strands of a city’s culinary landscape in a single episode. In our first tour, we visit Mysuru, a city that has always held an allure for travellers, for its majestic charm steeped in royal heritage, architecture and its proud traditions. Alongside its fabled eateries and shops that have stood the test of time, the city has also witnessed the birth of new age bakeries, cafes and food concepts. In the first show in this series, we explore a decades old popular biryani at RRR followed by a visit to SAPA Bakery that in a short span of only four years has endeared itself to the hearts of locals and travellers alike. A trip to Mysuru is incomplete without a taste of the Mysuru Pak, and we explore myriad flavours of this mithai at its source, Guru Sweets. Followed by a market outing to taste bananas including one that enjoys a GI tg. There’s more in this episode, hope you enjoy it.

Do let us know your thoughts in the comments. Stay tuned for more in this series.

The universe conspired yet again to bring Mark Wiens and me together, this time for a supremely delicious, robustly flavoured Thai meal at his favourite restaurant in Phuket. A 30-minute drive from Phuket town, Krua Pailin is not on the typical tourist trail, but serves wholesome, honestly priced Southern Thai dishes from a menu that is replete with exotic vegetables and greens, seafood and also some game meat. If you’re looking to taste authentic flavours, this is where to go when you are in Phuket.

Hope you enjoy this special episode with my friend, Mark Wiens. Stay tuned for the other Thailand episodes on Food Lovers TV, and also subscribe to our second channel, Kripal Amanna vlogs for more from this epic food and travel adventure.

I stepped out of my hotel to find some good coffee when I discovered this low profile 30-year-old eatery in Kottara, an area that’s off the beaten track for most visitors to Mangalore. Whilst I enjoyed the coffee, ambode and buns, what stole my heart here were the dosae, a butter-laden one, and then, an old school version sans any butter or ghee that took me back nearly half a century to the way masala dosa was made back in the day. Check out Hotel Karthik to taste some flavours of yesteryear.

Every Sunday evening, the main street in Old Phuket town transforms into a pedestrian-only zone with hundreds of stalls that sell all sorts of food and bric-a-brac. The aroma of delicious preparations wafts through the air beckoning visitors by the thousands. If you’re a food lover, you’ve got to be here, and no matter what dish you crave, chances are you will find it here. The only downside though, there’s far far more to savour than you can manage on one visit here, as Sree and I discovered!

On my return trip from Udupi, I stopped at this rustic eatery just outside the foothills of Agumbe and made a light breakfast of a delicious neer dosae and chutney. The most impression-able aspect of Sri Sathyanarayana hotel, Seethanadi, though is its owner Mr. Anil Kumar Shenoy, whose sincere and infectious enthusiasm lingers long beyond the fleeting minutes one spends here. Also, noteworthy are the cottage industry preparations and edible knick knacks one can carry from the store. Definitely an interesting stop to pencil into your itinerary if you find yourself on the road here.

Hope you enjoy this one. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

21 years ago, long before Coorg saw the number of travellers it receives these days, Mr Girish and his wife, Pushpa set up an eatery out of their home to serve the cuisine of their land. Disregarding the safe multi-cuisine approach of most highway eateries to cater to each and everyone, the couple focused only on Kodava dishes, a cuisine that not too many knew of outside Coorg back then. This gutsy gamble seems to have paid off, for today Coorg Cuisine is ‘the stop’ for its namesake cuisine for travelers (in the know) in Madikeri. I dropped in for an impromptu lunch and was pleasantly surprised to find some delicious vegetarian dishes too, like a top notch baby brinjal fry, a mellow bamboo shoot curry, in addition to the usual non veg fare - pandi curry, mutton fry, etc. that one expects to find in this part of the state.

Definitely an eatery to visit when you are in Coorg. Hope you enjoy this watch. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

#hotelvanishree #udupi #breakfast
 
hotel vanishree, udupi, home eatery, 30-year-old eatery, vegetarian breakfast, traditional breakfast, jackfruit mulaka, fritters, sajjige bajil, avalakki uppittu, mangalore buns, ambode, coffee, where to eat in udupi, restaurants in udupi, udupi food trail, udupi food tour, karnataka food tour, support local, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food 

I found my way to this 30-year-old home eatery on a rainy morning in Udupi,  where I was rewarded with a satisfying breakfast prepared by the lady of the house, Mrs. Sanjeevini Bhat, who also doubles up as the only cook in the kitchen. I tried a scrumptiously delicious jackfruit ‘mulaka’ that I instantly fell in love with and some more of the fare at this tiny eatery that though known to the locals is perhaps not as known (yet) to travellers yet. When in Udupi next, do check out Hotel Vanishree, and by the way, they are perhaps also the first eatery to open doors here at 615 every morning. Hope you enjoy this one as much as I did.

Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Jackfruit Mulaka
10/10

Idli Sambar Chutney
8/10

Biscuit Ambode
8.5/10

Buns
8/10

Avalakki Uppittu
avalakki 9/10, uppittu 7/10

Coffee 
7.5/10

Note: I paid Rs. 250 for all the dishes I tasted, including some for my crew. Prices are low, for instance a idli is Rs. 10, two buns are for Rs. 30, jackfruit mulaka Rs. 30 for a plate of 6 to 8, coffee Rs. 10.

As you approach Hunsur en route to Coorg, you will find many coffee stops along the state highway. But should you fancy a taste of some delicious old-world, take a minor detour to drive towards Hunsur town. There you will find Hotel Sabari Prasad, an eatery that first opened as Mangalore Cafe nearly 70 years ago, and to this day holds on to that era in its old world (read as extremely spartan and rustic!) decor and a wood fired dosa tava that dishes out the popular benne masala set and a unique jeera (cumin) dosae. Pradeep moved from his hometown in Nepal to Bengaluru over 40 years ago to seek employment in Chinese owned kitchens. SInce then, he has worked in some of the top Chinese restaurants in the city and also in Mumbai. Joined by his brother, also a service staff veteran in Chinese restaurants, the duo opened My Little China, a modest restaurant in Kothanur, East Bengaluru nine years ago. I dropped into their restaurant impromptu one afternoon and tasted a range of their dishes. The food here, I found light, flavourful and bereft of the chilli-garlic stodginess that passes off for the cuisine in the mainstream segment. Definitely a must visit if you enjoy Chinese food.

Pushparaj and his wife, Sachita moved to Bengaluru from Malpe a couple of years ago to begin life afresh after facing an economic downturn owing to the pandemic. A seafood tradesman since the age of 16, Pushparaj knows his seafood well, and so armed with this insight, a regular supply of the freshest catch from Malpe fishing harbour, and the recipes of his mother and mother-in-law, the couple opened Shoaling Fish Mangalore Lunch Home, a tiny 12-seater eatery in a quiet bylane of BTM 2nd Stage to serve delicious Udupi style coastal preparations. I visited them twice, the first time unannounced, and relished a range of their seafood fare - fish, prawns, crabs - cooked by the couple with care, and at prices that offer great value for money. It quite reminded me of an eatery in Kudla, such is the authenticity of the food and hospitality one encounters here. If you love seafood, definitely make tracks here.

A native of Kodagu, Manoj Thammaiah missed the authentic meaty flavours of Coorg in Bengaluru. And so he set up a street cart to cook and sell pork based dishes in the evenings, whilst holding a job in an export firm during the day. That was seven years ago. Encouraged by the steady, encouraging response of customers over the years, he has now given up his job and expanded to a tiny shop, Coorg Style Pork Corner, in BTM 2nd Stage, Bengaluru where he and his wife cook delicious preparations to recipes from their home. I dropped in impromptu one afternoon to taste most of what they have to offer. If you love pork, certainly a place to visit someday. Hope you enjoy this episode, part of our special initiative to shine a bit of light on unsung eateries that are doing good work.

Venkatesh and his parents began Sri Vinayaka Condiments, a small tiffin eatery, 24 years ago. His father fell ill and they were forced to relocate to the garage of their home nine years ago to tend to him and to also run their store in whatever little manner they could. The first few years were tough, with customers far and few in their neighbourhood located in the farthest corner of Banashankari, South Bengaluru, Venkatesh says, “sales were hardly a few rupees.” However, over time the soft, melt-in-the-mouth quality of their idli, their crunchy vada and khaara bath, the only three dishes they serve here, have acquired quite a following. I dropped in impromptu one evening for a light tiffin and chat with the family.

Hope you enjoy this episode, part of our special initiative to shine a bit of light on unsung eateries that are doing good work.

Three years ago, Subbanna and  his wife, Jamuna began a small biryani eatery in the ground floor of their home in Wilson Garden, a neighbourhood near Lalbagh in Bengaluru. In the construction business by profession, but passionate about cooking from an early age, Subbanna wanted to serve a homely chicken biryani cooked to his mother's recipe to patrons. The menu at Subbanna’s Biryani includes only a chicken kabab, chicken fry and the chicken biryani, sold at only Rs. 100 for a fairly adequate portion. Just because it is priced low doesn’t take away from the care that the couple shower upon their dishes, with the husband making the trek to the market every morning to procure the ingredients before returning to the kitchen to cook. I fell in love with the honest, homely appeal of this modest eatery, and am sure you will like it too. 

Hope you enjoy this episode, part of our special initiative to shine a bit of light on unsung eateries that are doing good work.
